attorneys.name: Brian Adams
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Brian Adams, the founding partner of Adams Law Firm, has a passionate commitment to both his clients and the practice of law. A third-generation Macon attorney, Brian’s inherent legal savvy teamed with his drive to help others has paved a successful path to representing seriously injured individuals in a wide range of litigation matters. Brian strongly believes in the right to trial and has experience in both the trial and appellate courts throughout the state of Georgia.

Throughout Brian Adams’ career, he has unmercifully fought both insurance companies and large corporations responsible for harming innocent victims through negligent business practices. As a result, he has recovered millions of dollars for his clients. Brian fully dedicates himself to each case and ensures that each client gets the care and attention they deserve.

A dedicated conservationist and outdoor enthusiast, Brian Adams is heavily involved in multiple community organizations concentrating on the protection of our environment. As Founder of the Ocmulgee National Park & Preserve Initiative, he is a driving force in bringing Georgia’s first National Park to his community. Additionally, he has served on the Board of Directors for the Altamaha RiverKeeper, Keep Macon-Bibb Beautiful Commission, and the Ocmulgee Water Trail Partnership. His involvement in these influential organizations, among other environmental groups, further champions his efforts to hold powerful corporations accountable for various mistreatments to both individuals and communities.

In 2023, Brian was named Lawyer of the year for the Macon Bar Association. For three consecutive years, Brian has been named a Super Lawyers “Rising Star” in personal injury. This prestigious distinction is awarded to no more than 2.5% of the attorneys in Georgia, based on Super Lawyers’ determination of the state’s elite up-and-coming attorneys who have attained both a high-level of professional achievement and positive peer recognition. Brian has also received the “Client’s Choice Award” through Avvo, was named one of the “Top 100 Lawyers” through the National Trial Lawyers Association, and was named “Best Attorney” in 2018 by The Macon Telegraph.

Brian’s demanding schedule is rewarded with time spent with his daughter and son, making memories with family and friends, traveling, reading, skiing, hiking, and canoeing. With a true “carpe diem” spirit, you can trust that when practicing law and enriching his community, Brian’s passion for results is guaranteed.

attorneys.name: Judge Bill Adams
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Judge Bill Adams joined Adams Law Firm in July 2017 following nearly 19 successful years serving as Judge of the State Court of Bibb County. Judge Adams’ love for both the legal field and the Macon community has spanned his adult life, and his leadership in both has spanned almost as long.

The eldest son of Middle Georgia “legal legend” Charles Adams, Judge Bill Adams grew up with a plan to practice law. He joined his father’s law firm in 1977 upon graduating cum laude from Mercer University’s Walter F. George School of Law. In 1978, he went on to serve as an Assistant United States Attorney in the United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Georgia. There, he prosecuted a wide array of federal crimes and served on the Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Force. In 1986, he rejoined Adams, Hemingway and Hemingway as partner, engaging in a varied practice of civil and criminal litigation in state and federal courts.

In 1998, Judge Bill Adams ran unopposed for an open seat on the State Court bench after the retirement of Judge Taylor Phillips. Adams was re-elected (unopposed) four more times. While serving on the bench, he gained expert legal knowledge in all aspects of civil trials from a perspective that few attain and even fewer take back to private practice.

As Adams Law Firm’s “Of Counsel” attorney, Judge Adams applies his decades of legal knowledge to fight for justice for our personal injury and wrongful death clients, considering the nuances involved in each individual case. Judge Adams is also a registered mediator and arbitrator. He is a member of the panel of neutrals at Adams ADR Services. Judge Adams is President of Middle Georgia Justice, a local non-profit dedicated to closing the justice gap in Middle Georgia.

A dedicated family man, community member, and baseball lover, Judge Bill Adams has served in many volunteer roles at Vineville United Methodist Church, Vine Ingle Little League, and the Kiwanis Club of Macon. He enjoys spending time with his wife, children, and grandchildren, especially at the lake.

Chris is proud to be among the seventh generation of his family to live and work in Gwinnett County. Committed to professional growth and community service, Chris actively participates in continuing legal education and various service organizations. attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Cumming, GA
attorneys.bio:
Danielle earned her Bachelor of Business Administration in Management from the University of Georgia, where she also completed a minor in Spanish. She went on to attend Mercer University School of Law, graduating cum laude and earning a Certificate in Advanced Legal Writing, Research, and Drafting. This distinction reflects her strong analytical abilities and exceptional skill in legal research and written advocacy.

Danielle began her legal career practicing medical malpractice litigation, where she handled complex and high-stakes matters. Through this experience, she developed a disciplined and detail-oriented approach to case preparation, along with the ability to analyze complicated factual and legal issues and advocate effectively in challenging disputes.

Danielle later transitioned her practice to family law to work more closely with individuals and families navigating some of the most important and difficult moments of their lives. She represents clients in divorce, child custody, child support, and other domestic relations matters. Danielle is committed to providing thoughtful guidance, strategic advocacy, and clear communication to help clients navigate the legal process with confidence while pursuing the best possible outcome for their families.

Outside of the office, Danielle enjoys hiking, cooking, and spending time with her dog, Olive.

attorneys.name: Stephen G. Adkins
attorneys.firm_name: Stephen G. Adkins, Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Valdosta, GA
attorneys.bio: Stephen (Steve) G. Adkins is an aggressive trial lawyer focusing his practice in criminal defense and personal injury. A skilled courtroom advocate, Steve has close to twenty years of legal experience representing clients charged with felony and misdemeanor crimes, Driving Under the Influence (DUI), serious traffic violations, and plaintiff injury cases. Steve practices in over forty different courts in the South Georgia area. Steve is highly skilled in DUI law and is certified in Standard Field Sobriety Testing and DUI Detection. He also is certified on the breath testing machines (Intoxilyzer 9000 and Alco-Sensor) used by law enforcement, and he represented more than 500 clients charged with DUI in his career. Steve is a member of the Georgia Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers. He is also a past president of the Valdosta Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers. He taught as an adjunct professor in the Political Science Department at Valdosta State University from 2008 to 2012. Steve is a native of Valdosta, Georgia, and attended public schools. A 1989 Valdosta High School graduate, Steve was a member of the Wildcat football team that compiled a 39-2 record and won a National Championship. He is a former past president of the Kiwanis Club of Valdosta. Steve and his family attend St. John the Evangelist Catholic Church in Valdosta. Away from the office, Steve enjoys fishing and hunting.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Richard Aime, Esq., joined Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele as an associate attorney in 2023. His current practice area focuses primarily on Workers’ Compensation.

Originally from California, Richard earned his bachelor’s degree in political science from Gettysburg College in 2012. He went on to graduate cum laude from the University of Massachusetts School of Law in 2016. While in law school, Richard worked for a criminal defense attorney in New Bedford, Massachusetts.

After law school, Richard worked for several years in Massachusetts before returning to Pennsylvania to work as a prosecutor for 4 years. He was an Assistant District Attorney in Northumberland and Adams Counties in Pennsylvania, where he tried numerous jury trials and argued before the Pennsylvania Superior Court. Richard is currently licensed to practice law in Pennsylvania and Massachusetts.

Outside of work, Richard enjoys hiking with his wife and their two dogs, playing golf, as well as rooting on Bay Area sports teams.

attorneys.name: Morgan Akin
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Cartersville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Morgan Akin is a trial lawyer and is co-owner Akin & Tate, P.C., one of the oldest continuous family practices in the United States. The firm was established in 1836 by Morgan's great grandfather. Morgan and his five ancestors have provided legal advice and counsel to citizens of Bartow County and northwest Georgia for over 170 years. Morgan and his father Warren Akin joined with Lester Tate to form the firm Akin & Tate, P.C. in 1996.

Morgan is a veteran trial lawyer who practices primarily in the areas of plaintiff's personal injury, business and commercial litigation, estate litigation, and real estate litigation. A former special assistant Attorney General representing the Georgia Department of Transportation. Morgan now represents landowners against the DOT and other condemning authorities in eminent domain cases. He also does business formations, wills and estates, and adoptions.

Morgan is a member of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association and the Association of Trial Lawyers of America. He served on the Board of Governors of the State Bar of Georgia from 1994 through 1996. He has been appointed by the Georgia Supreme Court to be a Special Master in disciplinary proceedings and by superior courts to serve as Special Master in a number of real estate litigation eases.

Born in Cartersville in 1949, Morgan graduated with high honors and as star student at Cartersville High School in 1967. He received a BA in English from Emory University in 1971 where he was a member of Phi Beta Kappa. He attended the University of Georgia School of Law on a full scholarship, served as member and associate editor of the Georgia Law Review, and graduated in 1974 with high honors. On his graduation from college, Morgan was commissioned as second lieutenant in the United States Air Force and was named a distinguished military graduate. He served in the Air Force reserve following law school, attaining the rank of captain.

After graduating from law school and a brief tour in the Air Force, Morgan returned to Cartersville in 1974 where he has been in the active practice of law since. Active in community affairs, Morgan has headed the United Way campaign, the Heart Association campaign, was named Jaycee's Young Man of the Year, and was president of the Cartersville/Bartow County Chamber of Commerce in 1988. He is Chairman of the Board of Directors of Bartow County Bank. Akin & Tate, P.C. (and its predecessor) serves as general counsel for that bank.

Morgan is married to the former Deborah Hogg of Greenville, South Carolina. Between them they have five adult children and three grandchildren. Morgan's daughter Peggy joined the firm in 2007, and is the fifth generation of Akins to practice law.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Jaycee’s Young Man of the Year

attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning: Wills, Trusts, Powers of Attorney, Advance Directives Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Jonathan A. Alderman is managing partner at the Anderson, Walker & Reichert, LLP, in Macon, Georgia. Estate planning, estate administration, will and trust drafting, contract and prenuptial agreement drafting, adoption, incorporation, business guidance, and charitable organization representation are all within Mr. Alderman's scope of practice. He has also handled cases involving commercial/contract law, real estate, insurance defense, and personal injury.

Born in Evansville, Indiana, Jonathan spent his formative years in Cochran, Georgia, where his father served as president of Middle Georgia College and his grandfather, Lucian A. Whipple, practiced law for 75 years before retiring at age 97. In 1981, he graduated with an associate's degree from Middle Georgia College, and in 1983, he graduated with a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Georgia with highest honors and membership in Phi Beta Kappa. In 1986, he graduated with a Juris Doctor from the University of Georgia with honors, and he started working with Anderson, Walker & Reichert in 1986.

Mr. Alderman married a Georgia educator; Amy Holland, formerly of Dexter, GA who spent the past four decades instructing students in Jones, Twiggs, Ben Hill, Walton, Baldwin, Bibb and Clarke counties. His daughter Kim works as a nurse practitioner in Columbus, Georgia.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Alfred obtained her Bachelor of Arts degree from Hamilton College located in Clinton, NY in 1998. After graduating from college, she worked as a paralegal supervisor for Lane & Mittendorf (now known as Windels, Marx, Lane & Mittendorf) until May of 2000, when she enrolled at New York Law School.

​In 2002, Ms. Alfred became an editor of the New York Law School Journal of Human Rights and published a note titled "Denial of the American Dream: The Plight of Undocumented High School Students Within the U.S. Educational System" and an article titled "The 4th Session of the Commission on the Status of Women: Gender Discrimination and the AIDS pandemic". After graduating from law school, Ms. Alfred moved to Atlanta, Georgia and subsequently became admitted to the Georgia Bar. Thereafter, she worked in-house at two telecommunication companies prior to going into private practice.

attorneys.name: Justyn D. Alioto
attorneys.practice_type: Civil and Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Lawrenceville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Alioto represents clients throughout the United States, litigating in both state and federal courts. Justyn's practice involves civil and commercial litigation, including the areas of business/corporate law, contract law, and landlord/tenant law.

After years of dedicating a portion of his practice to legal issues involving coin operated amusement machines, Mr. Alioto has emerged as one of the preeminent authorities on the subject. Justyn currently devotes his practice almost entirely to the representation of COAM licensees. In doing so, Mr. Alioto counsels both master and location licensees in both the civil and regulatory arenas, litigating at the trial and appellate levels.

Justyn is one of the only attorneys in the State who routinely represents individuals and companies for claims involving the Georgia Lottery Corporation, COAM arbitration, and criminal offenses relating to COAM operations, including RICO offenses. Mr. Alioto has represented license holders throughout Georgia, and he understands the importance of helping license holders navigate the highly regulated COAM industry.

Because of the constant attention Justyn gives to COAM cases, he is able to provide clients with valuable insight on the ever-changing laws related to the amusement machines industry, as well as the complicated procedural processes associated with those laws. Mr. Alioto's extensive experience affords his clients a significant advantage when tackling legal issues involving COAMs.

Finally, Justyn also represents clients for various criminal matters, including an array of misdemeanor offenses such as DUI and other traffic violations. Mr. Alioto also represents clients accused of various felonies, including drug possession, aggravated assault/battery, burglary, and fraud.

Awards and Honors

attorneys.name: Cody M. Allen
attorneys.practice_type: Premises Liability Lawyers in Columbus, GA
attorneys.bio:
Cody uses his background in communications, public service, and experiences as a reformed defense attorney to benefit his clients in premises liability actions. Cody is admitted to practice law in both Georgia and Alabama and is driven by the opportunity to help those who have been injured and need assistance negotiating and fighting for the best possible recovery.

Born and raised in Gwinnett County, Georgia, Cody obtained his undergraduate degree from Georgia College and State University in Milledgeville, Georgia. He served as President of both the Student Body and Student Government Association, and a Student Ambassador. In recognition of his efforts to better the Georgia College community, Cody received the 2013 Georgia College Transformational Leader Award, named to Who's Who in American Colleges & Universities, and inducted into Omicron Delta Kappa, the National Leadership Honors Society.

Cody attended Georgia State University College of Law, where he graduated with honors. While in law school, Cody worked at two law firms specializing in civil litigation. In addition, he served as the Deputy Director of Communications for the Democratic Leader of the Georgia State Senate and clerked for Judge Goger of the Fulton County Superior Court.

Cody began his career defending many of the largest hospital systems in Georgia. After spending three years on the defense side of these actions, Cody decided to follow his passion and use his knowledge and experience to be a fight for those who have been injured due to the negligence of others.

attorneys.name: Lauren Antonino
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Lauren Antonino has over 30 years of complex litigation experience. At The Antonino Firm, Ms. Antonino focuses on business litigation, real estate litigation, and trust and probate litigation. She also selectively handles insurance coverage disputes, personal injury claims, and employment law matters.

Antonino is a Phi Beta Kappa graduate of Duke University, earning an A.B. degree with magna cum laude honors in 1984. She is a 1987 graduate of the University of Virginia School of Law where she served on the managing board of the Virginia Tax Review and as a defense counsel for the University Honor System. Following law school, she clerked for the late Honorable M. Oliver Koelsch of the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit in Seattle, Washington.

Antonino has been a featured speaker on securities litigation, employment law, alternative dispute resolution and product liability issues. She has served as a presenter for public pension fund conferences, the American Bar Association Convention, the Alternative Dispute Resolution Convention and ICLE. In July 2000, her article entitled ""The Seven Steps of Effective Workplace Investigations (with Sample Questions)' was published in The Practical Litigator. Her article ""Fast Companies Need Fast Lawyers; Speeding Up Dispute Resolutions,' was published in Competitive Edge. Antonino has been published in Mealey's Litigation Reports, Drugs and Medical Devices, and has been quoted in numerous publications, including Business Week.

She is a member of the American Mensa Society and has been listed in the National Registry of Who's Who, Who's Who in American Law, the National Trial Lawyers Top 100, Georgia's Super Lawyers, and Lawyers of Distinction. Antonino is admitted to practice before all Georgia state trial and appellate courts, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia and the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals.

Antonino is a Past President and a former member of the Board of Directors for the Legal Clinic for the Homeless and of the Atlanta Legal Aid Advisory Board. In honor of a former client, Ms. Antonino has co-chaired the MDA Night of Hope and has served on its Executive Committee for fifteen years. The Night of Hope has raised over eleven millions of dollars for research to find a cure for Lou Gehrig’s Disease/ALS.

attorneys.name: Jonathan Apolinario
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Johns Creek, GA
attorneys.bio:
Jonathan Apolinario joined Meriwether & Tharp, LLC, as an Associate Attorney in 2026. Born and raised in Florida, Jonathan relocated to Valdosta, GA, in 2020 and brings an outsider perspective to his practice serving clients in South Georgia and across the state.

Jonathan earned his undergraduate degree from the University of Florida in 2010, where he studied Journalism & Communications with intentional focus on developing the skills necessary to provide a strong and effective voice of advocacy for his future clients. Thereafter, Jonathan attended the Florida State University College of Law where he earned his law degree and graduated with a Certificate of Distinction in Pro Bono Service, working at the Florida Innocence Project on behalf of the wrongfully convicted.

Since his admission to the Georgia Bar in 2016, Jonathan has gone to bat for his clients as a plaintiff's attorney in the realm of personal injury and in criminal defense, developing a strong sense of successful negotiation and trial strategies. Jonathan is a qualified Guardian Ad Litem with a personal passion for protecting the best interests of children and helping families navigate the very difficult divorce and custody process.

Away from the courtroom, Jonathan puts family first always and enjoys spending time with his wife, her three children, and his daughter. Having been through the Family Court system himself, Jonathan understands very well what you are going through and how best to ensure you are not alone in navigating your case.

attorneys.name: Sergio Ardila
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Sergio Ardila was born and raised in Colombia before moving to the United States at age 11. He attended the University of Georgia where he graduated Cum Laude before earning his Juris Doctorate in 2015 from The University of Georgia School of Law. He began working for Morgan & Morgan Atlanta, PPLC in the summer of 2015, and currently represents the Hispanic community across the state of Georgia.

Since 2015, Sergio has recovered over 14 million dollars for injured Georgia workers. Sergio has won cases at both the trial and appellate levels including having a 2019 undefeated court appearance record of 4-0. Sergio is also a court-certified mediator under the Georgia Office of Dispute Resolution.

Sergio was a member of the Georgia Association of Latino Elected Officials' 2016 Institute for Leadership. During law school, Sergio had a wide range of experiences including working for Fortune 100 companies such as The Coca Cola Company & First American Corporation, working for U.S. government organizations such as the Securities Exchange Commission & the Public Defender's office, and working for international organizations such as Melo Pimenetel - a midsize law firm in Recife, Brazil - & the Colombian Consulate in Orlando.

Sergio was an All-American on the NCWA wrestling team for the University of Georgia and is a Black Belt World Champion in Jiu-Jitsu. During his free time, he enjoys training and competing in JiuJitsu around the world.

attorneys.name: Yoko Ariza
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Yoko Ariza-Diaz is an Associate Attorney at Briskin, Cross & Sanford, LLC, where she assists clients with corporate and real estate transactional matters. Her practice includes commercial real estate transactions, corporate formation and governance, and contract drafting and negotiation. Yoko works closely with business owners, entrepreneurs, and individuals to provide practical and efficient legal solutions tailored to their goals.

A proud graduate of Georgia State University College of Law, Yoko earned her dual J.D./M.B.A. in 2022 after completing her B.S. in Criminal Justice (2018). During law school, she served as President of the Latinx and Caribbean Law Student Association and competed on the Environmental Moot Court Team. She also volunteered with the Atlanta Legal Aid Society and the Atlanta Volunteer Lawyers Foundation, assisting attorneys with landlord-tenant disputes and housing matters.

Yoko is a registered civil mediator, certified through Georgia State University Law’s landlord-tenant mediation clinic, and has successfully mediated more than 50 cases in the Magistrate Court of Fulton County. Her background in mediation reinforces her client-centered approach that focuses on clear communication, balanced advocacy, and practical problem-solving.

As an active member of the Georgia Bar Association’s Business Law Section, the Georgia Hispanic Bar Association, and the Hispanic National Bar Association, Yoko is passionate about expanding access to legal representation and supporting diverse voices in the legal community.

Outside of work, Yoko enjoys traveling, playing soccer and tennis, and spending time with her family.

attorneys.bio:
Jeffery L. Arnold has more than 39 years of legal experience representing individuals, small businesses, large corporations and municipal governments. He also has more than 38 years of distinguished service in the United States Army and Army Reserves earning the rank of major general.

Honored as an AV-Preeminent* attorney, Mr. Arnold is the senior partner of Arnold & Stafford, a Georgia law firm dedicated to representing clients in a wide range of practice areas. With offices in Hinesville, Richmond Hill and Ludowici, Mr. Arnold’s firm handles cases involving personal injury, criminal defense, family law, military law, real estate, municipal law and much more.

Mr. Arnold graduated with his J.D. in 1976 from the McGeorge College of Law, University of the Pacific. He is admitted to practice in Georgia, Iowa, California, Florida and Hawaii. He also is privileged to serve as the State Court Judge for Long County, Georgia.

Mr. Arnold is a member of the State Bar of Georgia; the Florida Bar; the Hawaii State, Iowa State and American Bar Associations; the Atlantic Judicial Circuit; the State Bar of California; the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association; the Georgia Municipal Association; and the American Association for Justice.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Jeffery L. Arnold has more than 39 years of legal experience representing individuals, small businesses, large corporations and municipal governments. He also has more than 38 years of distinguished service in the United States Army and Army Reserves earning the rank of major general.

Honored as an AV-Preeminent* attorney, Mr. Arnold is the senior partner of Arnold & Stafford, a Georgia law firm dedicated to representing clients in a wide range of practice areas. With offices in Hinesville, Richmond Hill and Ludowici, Mr. Arnold’s firm handles cases involving personal injury, criminal defense, family law, military law, real estate, municipal law and much more.

Mr. Arnold graduated with his J.D. in 1976 from the McGeorge College of Law, University of the Pacific. He is admitted to practice in Georgia, Iowa, California, Florida and Hawaii. He also is privileged to serve as the State Court Judge for Long County, Georgia.

Mr. Arnold is a member of the State Bar of Georgia; the Florida Bar; the Hawaii State, Iowa State and American Bar Associations; the Atlantic Judicial Circuit; the State Bar of California; the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association; the Georgia Municipal Association; and the American Association for Justice.

attorneys.name: Lee S. Ashmore
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Lee S. Ashmore
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Brunswick, GA
attorneys.bio:
Lee S. Ashmore is a Brunswick divorce attorney whose practice has been devoted to family law for 20 years. He is a family law specialist who has developed his expertise in family law by litigating over 500 family law cases in the courts, as well as negotiating and drafting hundreds of settlement agreements.

A Military Veteran born in Brunswick

Mr. Ashmore was born in Brunswick, Georgia, on March 9, 1960. He served in the United States Army, graduating from the United States Military's Foreign Language School in Monterey, California, and serving as a Signals Intelligence Analyst in Augsburg, Germany.

A Graduate of the University of Virginia School of Law

He graduated Magna Cum Laude from Virginia Tech in 1989 with a B.A. in history. At Virginia Tech he was inducted into Phi Beta Kappa, the most prestigious undergraduate honor society in the United States. While at Virginia Tech he served on the Montgomery County Central Committee.

Mr. Ashmore received his J.D. from the University of Virginia School of Law in 1992. He served as president of both the Virginia Employment and Labor Law Association and the Law Student Advocacy Project. He was a board member of the Legal Aid Association. He participated in the Family Law Clinic and Moot Court. He was selected to advise incoming law students as a peer advisor.

20 Years of Experience as a Family Law Specialist

He has practiced family law from 1993 to the present, litigating over 500 family law cases in the courts. He has completed the 40 hour mediator training program and the 20 hour family law mediator training program. He has served as an instructor in the mediator training program and the family law mediator training program. He has served as a mediator for the EEOC, mediating 74 cases.

Former Chair of the American Bar Association's Family Law Litigation Committee

On a national level, Mr. Ashmore has served as chair of the American Bar Association's Domestic Relations and Family Law Litigation Committee. He has also served as editor of the American Bar Association's Family Law Litigation Newsletter. He has been awarded the American Bar Association's Section of Litigation's prestigious Star Award.

He is a member of the State Bar of Georgia, as well as the Family Law Section of the State Bar. He is also a member of the Glynn County Bar Association, the American Bar Association's Family Law Section, and the Association of Family and Conciliation Courts. He is a current member of the American Bar Association's Marital Property Committee.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Section of Litigation's Prestigious Star Award, American Bar Association's

attorneys.name: William J. Atkins
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Bill is a founding member of Atkins & Fife, LLC. He is a seasoned trial lawyer with a strong record of success on behalf of his clients in criminal and civil matters. Bill concentrates his civil practice in the areas of wrongful death, catastrophic personal injury, false arrest, sexual harassment, and civil rights matters involving law enforcement officials.

Bill earned his undergraduate degree from Vassar College in 1991 (B.A. History). He earned his Juris Doctor degree from Emory University School of Law in 1994. He was named Best Oralist in the 1992 Emory Moot Court Competition, and competed on the Georgia Intrastate and National Moot Court teams.

His career as a trial lawyer began as a prosecutor in the Douglas County District Attorney’s office. He tried over twenty felony and misdemeanor jury trials to "guilty" verdicts, all of which were affirmed on appeal. He entered private practice more than a decade ago and has secured significant jury verdicts and settlements in a broad range of cases including serious personal injury, intentional torts, employment discrimination and police misconduct.

Bill is admitted to practice in the Georgia Supreme Court, the Georgia Court of Appeals, the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals, and the Northern and Middle Districts of Georgia. He is a member of the State Bar of Georgia, the Atlanta Bar Association, the Cobb County Bar Association and the Lawyers Club of Atlanta. He is a Master member of the Order of Barristers.

attorneys.name: Meredith Atwood
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Woodstock, GA
attorneys.bio:
Meredith Atwood is a Senior Attorney at Oliver Hughes LLC and is the Firm’s Director of Client Engagement.

Prior to starting with the Firm, Meredith worked for several Atlanta-area firms specializing in Real Estate, Litigation and Compliance. She has extensive experience in client and customer service and project management. She, over the course of her legal career, has represented clients in complex real estate and title matters, civil litigation, business disputes, family law and probate. She has successfully argued before the Georgia Court of Appeals.

Meredith received her JD from University of Georgia, where she served on the Journal of Intellectual Property Law. She graduated Phi Beta Kappy with a Bachelor of Arts in English, also from the University of Georgia.

In addition to her legal background, Meredith is the author of three traditionally-published books, including Hope Fights Back, co-written with her friend, Andrea Lytle Peet—who is fighting a battle with ALS (Lou Gehrig’s Disease). She is also four-time Ironman triathlete who now enjoys lifting weights more than riding a bike.

attorneys.name: Jessica Autry
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Jessica Autry has been committed to learning the skills of a trial attorney ever since she decided to go to law school. She was in the Honors Program at John Marshall Law School, which allowed her the unique opportunity to specialize in litigation of cases. Jessica graduated in the top 10% of her class, then began practicing law as an attorney in 2014. She has represented clients in a variety of criminal defense, contract dispute, personal injury, and landlord-tenant cases.

Prior to going to law school, Jessica worked as an Emergency Medical Technician. Her education in emergency medicine allows Jessica specialized insight into personal injury cases, and her experience as a trial attorney makes her a zealous advocate for the rights of her clients.

Jessica is a native to Georgia and currently lives in Cobb County with her husband, two sons, two dogs, and cat. She volunteers as Treasurer for the non-profit group Friends of Price Park, which oversees the development and preservation of a local 243-acre park. In her free time, she enjoys hiking, backpacking, and reading novels.

attorneys.name: A. Bryan Baer Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney A. Bryan Baer is the founder and owner of The Baer Law Firm in Atlanta, Georgia. Recognized as one of the leading trial advocates in the state as well as the entire country, Mr. Baer provides exceptional representation to clients throughout the greater Atlanta Metro who have suffered injuries or loss as the result of someone else's negligence or wrongdoing.

A lawyer since 2002, Mr. Baer once worked as an insurance defense attorney, so he has a wealth of insight into the industry that enables him to devise the most effective strategies possible for injury victims and their families. Focusing on plaintiff representation since 2011, he has recovered millions of dollars in total compensation for his clients, earning his membership in the Million Dollar Advocates Forum.

Among his other notable accolades, Mr. Baer has received a Top 40 Under 40 designation from The National Trial Lawyers as well as designation as among America's Top 100 High Stakes Litigators. He also holds a Lawyers of Distinction rating, and the American Institute of Legal Advocates voted him a Top 100 in 2019.

Furthermore, the American Institute of Personal Injury Attorneys voted him one of the 10 Best Attorneys High Verdict and Settlement Winner in Georgia and one of the 10 Best Attorneys in Client Satisfaction in Georgia. He has also received a Legal Elite designation from Georgia Trends magazine and other top rankings from his peers along with "Superb" client ratings on Avvo and the site's Clients' Choice Award.

After earning his undergraduate degree cum laude in economics from the University of Georgia, Mr. Baer returned to his alma mater and obtained his Juris Doctor from the University of Georgia School of Law in 2002. He has established himself as a leader in his legal community by conducting numerous continuing legal education seminars across his region on a variety of legal topics.

She enjoys meeting individual and family legal obligations in areas like separation and divorce, marriage agreements, child custody and adoptions, estate planning, trust and probate administration, administration and business formation, and civil case litigation.

Ms. Bafas earned a law doctorate with Pro Bono Distinction from Georgia State University College of Law in 2012. In 2012, Georgia licensed her to practice. Moreover, Georgia Tech awarded Ms. Bafas a Bachelor of Science with top honors in 2009. The President's Scholarship Alumni Society and Georgia Tech Bar Association keep her connected at Georgia Tech, where she received the Stamps President's Scholarship Award. She participated in many Georgia Tech student organizations and serves on the President's Alumni Society Board.

A distinguished member of the Rotary Club of Dunwoody, Ms. Bafas serves on its District 6900 Committee for Global Grant Scholarships, as a trustee for the Georgia Rotary Student Program, and as a board member and Secretary of the Foundation. She is also the CEO of the accredited, nonprofit adoption agency St. Nick's Kids and an American Legion Auxiliary member. As founder and CEO of The Atlanta Social Club, Ms. Bafas connects young professional women in Atlanta. Her services to these organizations are well-regarded.

attorneys.name: Laura Johnson Bailey
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Laura Johnson Bailey was born and raised in Charleston, South Carolina. She attended the University of Alabama to obtain her Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice. While there, she was the president of Alpha Phi Sigma and received the Department of Criminal Justice Chairperson's Award of Merit. Ms. Bailey then obtained her Juris Doctor from the Florida State University College of Law. During law school, she obtained her Certificate of Comparative International Law from Oxford University in Oxford, England, and was awarded the Certificate for Distinguished Pro Bono Service for serving as a pro bono law clerk to the Honorable Judge Kathleen F. Dekker in the Felony Division of the Circuit Court for the Second Judicial Circuit of Florida.

Upon graduating from law school, Ms. Bailey spent 12 years defending corporations and insurance companies in personal injury matters ranging from car accidents, dog bites, and premises liability, to wrongful death, in Florida and Georgia. She has repeatedly lectured on new developments in insurance and tort law for the Tort and Insurance Practice Section of the State Bar of Georgia. In 2017, she joined Morgan & Morgan to pursue a more meaningful career as a zealous advocate for those injured by the negligence of others. Ms. Bailey is honored to have the opportunity to use her technical knowledge of the law, and her insight into how corporations and insurance companies defend injury claims, for the benefit of her clients.

Outside of the practice of law, Ms. Bailey is passionate about animal rescue and welfare, and volunteers with several rescue groups throughout Georgia. She is a member of Buckhead Church.

attorneys.name: Nick M. Bajalia Sr.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Valdosta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Nick M. Bajalia, Sr. is a native of Valdosta, Georgia. He attended Valdosta State College between 1971 and 1973. In 1972, during his sophomore year at Valdosta State College, he joined Tau Kappa Epsilon Social Fraternity. After completing his sophomore year at Valdosta State College, he transferred to the University of Georgia in 1973, and enrolled in the Terry School of Business Administration.

While attending the University of Georgia, Mr. Bajalia founded and formed "Communiversity", which is the equivalent of the Big Brother - Little Brother Program on the University of Georgia Campus. He served as a Big Brother to a needy youth during his entire time as a student at the University of Georgia. He graduated, with honors, from the Terry School of Business Administration at the University of Georgia with a Bachelor of Business Administration degree in 1975.

After graduating from UGA, Mr. Bajalia attended the Cumberland School of Law of Samford University, from where he graduated with a Doctor of Jurisprudence degree in 1979. During his third year of law school, he was asked to serve as the personal Law Clerk for the Honorable R. Macey Taylor, United States Magistrate, United States District Court, Northern District of Alabama.

Mr. Bajalia became a member of the State Bar of Georgia in 1979 and The Florida Bar in 1981. He first worked as an associate for the law firm of Coleman & Kitchens in Valdosta, Georgia. In 1980, he became a partner, and the law firm became known as Coleman, Kitchens & Bajalia. Later, he became associated with the law firm of Blackburn, Bright, Edwards and Dodd in Valdosta, Georgia. Mr. Bajalia founded and opened Bajalia Law Firm on May 3, 1982.

Mr. Bajalia is a member of the Episcopal Church. He is married to the former Monique Andrews. They have six (6) children and several grandchildren.

attorneys.name: A. J. Balbo Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: Balbo & Gregg, Attorneys at Law, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Hinesville, GA
attorneys.bio:
A. J. Balbo's practice focuses exclusively on the area of Criminal Defense. Mr. Balbo handles felonies and misdemeanors in Federal, State, and Military Courts. He has defended clients charged with Murder, Rape, Sexual Assault, Drug Distribution, Molestation, Child Pornography, White Collar Fraud, Driving Under the Influence (DUI), and Domestic Violence. Several of his cases have garnered national medial attention, including federal death penalty and hate crimes cases. He has also defended a person accused of Impeding Congress and Seditious Conspiracy on January 6, 2021 at the U.S. Captiol. He is certified in the mentods of Standardized Field Sobriety Testing and was the first attorney in Georgia to voluntarily install a Smart Start Ignition Interlock Device into his vehicle to learn about its use firsthand. When defending a client, knowledge of the law and mastery of the facts are critical for success. Every client deserves an attorney who will aggressively fight for them every step of the way.

Born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, Mr. Balbo attended Duquesne University and Fordham University School of Law. He entered the Army's Judge Advocate General's Corp and was an Honor Graduate of the 157th JAG Basic Course. After being assigned to the 3rd Infantry Division at Fort Stewart, Georgia, Mr. Balbo deployed first to Kuwait before "crossing the berm" into Iraq in March 2003 with Operation Iraqi Freedom, earning a Bronze Star. Upon his return to the United States, Mr. Balbo continued to act as a military prosecutor until leaving the service in 2006. While in uniform, Mr. Balbo prosecuted a high-profile desertion case, arguing against former Attorney General of the United States Ramsey Clark.

Mr. Balbo has presented courses on the Servicemember's Civil Relief Act on behalf of the American Bar Association and on Federal and State Law on behalf of the American Board of Trial Advocates. He has been selected Bryan County's Favorite Lawyer multiple times.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Bronze Star Medal

attorneys.practice_type: Constitutional Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Anita Kumar, a member of Gregory Doyle's Education Law practice group, specializes in matters involving civil litigation, special education and employment law.

Ms. Kumar has successfully represented school district clients in various matters of civil litigation, including First Amendment claims, torts, and Fair Dismissal Act cases. She also maintains a busy special education practice, counseling clients at IEP meetings and in due process proceedings. Her transactional experience includes contract review for school district procurements. She also regularly assists clients in governance matters and board policy review.

Prior to joining the firm, Ms. Kumar worked for the City of New York Department of Social Services as a special assistant civil prosecutor for matters involving child abuse and neglect. She has extensive experience representing public agencies in litigation involving services for children with special needs.

During law school, Ms. Kumar published and presented a law journal article on the federal No Child Left Behind Act of 2001 at a national education law conference. During the summers, she focused her work on municipal legal issues and interned at both the City of Atlanta Law Department and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. Her other legal experience includes criminal litigation work in both prosecution and defense offices.

Before law school, Ms. Kumar studied International Affairs at Emory University and the London School of Economics.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Lithonia, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney E. Noreen Banks-Ware is a Georgia native. Born just south of the Atlanta metro area in Barnesville, she is proud to give back to the local communities she grew up in.

Educational Background & Experience

While working towards her undergraduate degree in Business Administration at the University of Georgia, Noreen had to take a business law course that sparked her interest in the legal profession. After completing her bachelor's program, she went on to pursue her J.D. at UGA law school.

Founding the Firm

Upon graduating with her law degree, she spent a couple of years working for a larger firm that initially led her to practice in the area of family law. Feeling like she was teaching herself how to be successful, Noreen decided she could do more for her clients by running her own firm.

Since 1991, E.N. Banks-Ware Law Firm, LLC has specialized primarily in family law. From handling uncontested to complex divorces, custody and child support cases, fathers' rights, and probate matters, Noreen has garnered a reputation as a skilled trial attorney that has professionally provided excellent representation to clients. In 2006, she became certified in Collaborative Law to better serve her clients' needs. Her firm has provided high-quality legal services for individuals and families in the Metro Atlanta and DeKalb County community for nearly thirty (30) years.

"My style of counsel is very personable. I genuinely care about helping you work through these difficult times and finding a way to start fresh."

Why Choose E.N. Banks-Ware Law Firm, LLC?

Noreen has many professional accolades and is often sought after to share the wisdom behind her success and professionalism. For starters, she is a Master in the Weltner Family Law American Inn of Court - which is an honor only bestowed upon experienced family law attorneys recognized for their skills and expertise by their colleagues. She has been a member of the Inn since 2010.

attorneys.name: Christiane C. Bard
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Dalton, GA
attorneys.bio:
Christiane is primarily a transactional attorney with a decade of legal experience. She specializes in real estate transactions, estate planning, and probate and estate administration. Valuing integrity and service to her community and clients, Christiane is committed to providing a quality legal experience.

Christiane graduated magna cum laude from Mercer Law School in 2014. In addition to graduating with honors, Christiane received the Guerry R. Moore Insurance Award and was inducted into the National Order of Scribes and the Brainerd Currie Honor Society. While in law school, she was a member of the Mercer Law Review; Christiane competed on the John J. Gibbons National Criminal Procedure Moot Court Competition; and she wrote and co-organized Mercer’s Hugh Lawson Memorial 1L Moot Court Competition. Outside of school, Christiane clerked for the Honorable Jason E. Ashford of the State Court of Houston County.

Throughout her legal career, Christiane has handled numerous guardianship and conservatorship cases across the Northwest Georgia region. Her knowledge of Georgia’s probate process is vast, ranging from simple estate administration matters to more complex probate proceedings. More recently, Christiane’s practice has primarily focused on residential real estate, including title examinations, real estate closings, and homeowners’ association matters. Christiane is also knowledgeable in nonjudicial foreclosures, Georgia Open Records Act compliance, creditor rights and liabilities in bankruptcy cases, and contract negotiations.

Outside of work, Christiane enjoys a good Netflix binge, attending her local church, and traveling with her husband and two daughters.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Received the Guerry R. Moore Insurance Award for the best performance in insurance law and was inducted into the National Order of Scribes and the Brainerd Currie Honor Society.

attorneys.name: Laura McDonnell Barron Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Wills, Trusts & Estate Planning Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Laura M. Barron brings nearly two decades of legal experience to Georgia Legacy Law Group, LLC, where she helps individuals and families navigate some of life’s most important decisions. With a background in high-stakes personal injury litigation—having handled hundreds of civil matters across Georgia—Laura now focuses her practice on estate planning, probate and estate administration, and guardianships and conservatorships, empowering clients to protect what matters most.

Laura’s clients turn to her for clear guidance on Wills, Trusts, Powers of Attorney, and Medical Directives, as well as for support in probating estates and administering trusts following the death of a loved one. She is also a trusted resource for families facing guardianship and conservatorship decisions, including those with adult children with disabilities.

Along with the firm’s founding partner, Cleve Hill, Laura is a 1997 Sequoyah High School graduate. Laura earned her Bachelor of Science in Psychology with a concentration in Medical Humanities from Davidson College, then her law degree from Penn State University Dickinson School of Law. There, she distinguished herself as a leader, serving as Student Bar Association treasurer and honor code committee co-chair. Laura is admitted to practice before all Georgia courts, including the Supreme Court.

Beyond her legal work, Laura is deeply committed to giving back. She has served as a board member and volunteer leader for Hope2Africa, mentoring youth and strengthening communities abroad. Locally, she has guided high school students as a mentor for Teach One to Lead One®, and has provided pro bono estate planning for single parents and widows through First Baptist Church Woodstock’s LoveLoud program.

Laura’s approach is rooted in compassion, clarity, and a genuine desire to help clients find peace of mind for the future. Whether you’re planning your estate, resolving a dispute, or seeking guidance on guardianship, Laura is dedicated to helping you move forward with confidence.

attorneys.name: Charlie Barrow
attorneys.practice_type: DUI Lawyers in Watkinsville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Having extensive courtroom and trial experience, Charlie is a capable and respected litigator. In the criminal arena, he has handled hundreds of felony and misdemeanor cases, representing individuals accused of violating state and federal law. He has successfully tried cases before juries, obtaining not guilty verdicts in a range of criminal cases. His experience also includes the appellate process, where he represents those who have been convicted at trial. He has argued before the Georgia Supreme Court and written numerous appeals to both the Georgia Supreme Court and the Georgia Court of Appeals. He has lectured on appellate issues at GPDSC Appellate Division training seminars.

In addition to his criminal practice, Charlie currently serves as a Solicitor in both the Walton County Magistrate and Probate Courts where he prosecutes local ordinance and traffic violations.

As a civil litigator, Charlie has successfully represented multiple clients who have been injured and are in need of compensation. He has also helped many clients in a variety of civil matters, including probate, and business disputes. Charlie also serves as counsel for the City of Lexington, advising the City on a range of Municipal issues.

Charlie is admitted to practice law in all Georgia State and Superior Courts, the Georgia Court of Appeals, the Georgia Supreme Court, the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals, and the Federal District Court for the Middle District of Georgia. He is an active member of The Georgia Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

Charlie graduated cum laude from the University of Georgia with degrees in both History and English and a minor in French. He then attended Mercer University’s Walter F. George School of Law where he was awarded the Julius R. Lunsford academic scholarship in the study of law.

In the community, Charlie serves as the current Chair of the Oconee Rivers Greenway Commission and is Past President of the Board of Directors of the Altamaha Riverkeeper. He is also a graduate of LEAD Athens, a leadership program dedicated to building a vibrant community in Athens.

Awards and Honors

Honors

2014 State Bar of Georgia Best Law Day Activities Award

attorneys.name: Kenneth E. Barton
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate Law Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
People love telling bad lawyer jokes and enjoy watching unscrupulous lawyers in their favorite shows and movies. For those reasons, many of us forget that we seek the help of an attorney during the most important times of our lives.

Each day, Ken attempts to use the same approach to advocating for clients as a Macon attorney that he did while teaching his students in a low-income community in Atlanta. Regardless of whether a client comes seeking advice for their business or legal assistance for a matter of a more personal nature, Ken is often thinking about that client, their needs, and how to be the advocate they need. Ken strives to explain and ensure that all of his clients truly understand the often-complex details of the law, so we are part of one team that is working toward the same goals.

An attorney's personal investment in his clients is not enough; clients have a right to a competent lawyer. Ken has used his educational opportunities and other experiences to become the best young attorney that he can be. As a student at Georgetown University Law Center in Washington, D.C., he went beyond what was required in the classroom to improve his knowledge of the law, trial skills, and drafting legal writing.

Ken is proud to have served as an intern for the Honorable Amy Totenberg of the United States District Court for the Northern District of Georgia and as the law clerk for Chief Administrative Law Judge David Simmons of the District of Columbia Commission on Human Rights. Ken also spent time as a student attorney where he fought passionately for low-income tenants in housing disputes in the D.C. Superior Court. These and his other experiences in business, corporate law, appellate litigation, employment, and discrimination law have helped Ken develop a strong foundation as a trial attorney and legal writer.

Ken believes that his life purpose is based on the proverb that man's obligation is to improve the lives of other men and that this obligation applies equally to society at large as well as his clients' needs. As a native Georgian, Ken has and will continue to work hard to strengthen our communities with his work as a teacher, Eagle Scout, and volunteer in the Boy Scouts of America and Order of the Arrow.

Each day, Ken looks forward to teaming up with his clients, both old and new, to help solve their legal and business needs and being the legal support they need in some of the most important times of their lives.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Eagle Scout, Boy Scouts of America

Founders Award, Order of the Arrow

For 16 years, Leslie has provided efficient, creative, energized, and personalized employment and ERISA representation to clients on all sides of employment and benefit matters. She has represented sponsors and fiduciaries of employee benefit plans in complex employee benefit and ERISA litigation matters in federal and state courts throughout the country, including litigation involving breach of fiduciary duty and employer stock held in 401(k) plans. Leslie also counsels clients in connection with governmental investigations and other regulatory matters involving benefits issues and executive compensation agreements.

Leslie has helped countless clients navigate employment transitions with ease, providing empathetic, efficient employment strategies and solutions to executives, individuals, boards of directors, and human resources professionals. Leslie has a unique ability to evaluate a matter from a holistic perspective and to create and negotiate a solution for all involved. Perhaps equally importantly, she has counseled and resolved numerous disputes in early stages, preserving the goals of cost-effectiveness, efficiency, and discretion for her clients.

Leslie "balances" her legal with her active single parenting of her two sons and three puppies. She can often be found transporting her tween boys to baseball fields, walking puppies in the park, or cheerfully feeding and hydrating her sons and their twenty closest friends.

Leslie has maintained her commitment to giving back to the community by, among other things, representing children in the juvenile justice process and advocating for victims of child trafficking.

attorneys.name: Katie Bates
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Hinesville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Katie R. Bates was admitted to the Georgia Bar in 2009 and practices in the areas of family law, criminal law, personal injury, corporate law, and general civil litigation. She has extensive experience representing clients in cases involving divorce, custody, child support, motor vehicle accidents, slip and falls, and corporate contract disputes.

Prior to attending law school Mrs. Bates worked as a social worker for the Department of Family and Children Services as well as an investigator and for Safeco Insurance Company as a claims adjuster. Both positions served to provide her with a unique insight into the workings of the civil and criminal court systems. Her tenure as an insurance adjuster especially provided her with firsthand experience in understanding how insurance companies operate including the means by which many companies push inequitable settlements on unrepresented people.

Her father, now a retired full bird Colonel in United States Air Force, was a fighter pilot stationed aboard when she was born. At only six weeks old she made her first trans-Atlantic flight and she’s loved traveling the world ever since. Her personal experience navigating the complexities of military life gives her a deeper understanding of the many legal issues that impact military families.

Mrs. Bates has written and lectured on family law topics relating to adoption and juvenile law. She taught as an adjunct professor of Juvenile Law at the former Savannah Law School- Savannah, Georgia, and during law school published an article for the John Marshall Law Journal: Adoption- How Protecting Privacy Protects the Best Interest of Children, 2009. She earned her J.D. in 2009, graduating Cum Laude from John Marshall Law School- Atlanta, Georgia, where she was Salutatorian, named the Outstanding Graduate by the faculty, and was appointed as a Dean’s Fellow. She earned a B.A. with a double major for Anthropology and Sociology from Georgia State University graduating Summa Cum Laude, in 2004. While at Georgia State University she was named to the National Dean’s List, named Faculty Scholar, as well as receiving several other academic honors.

Mrs. Bates is married to Lt. James “Corey” Bates, with the Ft. Stewart-Hunter Army Airfield Fire Department. They, along with their children reside in McIntosh County, Georgia.

attorneys.name: Michael Bauer
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accident Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Michael Bauer grew up in South Bend, Indiana. He received his Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from the University of Georgia in Athens, Georgia in 2006. Michael then attended John Marshall Law School in Atlanta, Georgia, where he received his Juris Doctor in 2009. While in law school, he was highly involved with the Moot Court program and also served as a Research Assistant in the area of Constitutional Law.

After being sworn in to practice law in Georgia, Michael spent some time as a Special Prosecutor at the DeKalb County District Attorney's Office. He later started a law practice focusing on estate planning and probate administration. During that time, Michael also worked extensively with a prominent consumer defense firm and served for several years as an Adjunct Professor of Advocacy at John Marshall Law School. Michael now concentrates primarily on practicing in the areas of estate planning, probate administration, and civil litigation.

Michael is a member of the State Bar of Georgia, the American Bar Association, and the Estate Planning and Probate Section of the Atlanta Bar Association. Michael is also admitted to practice before the United States District Court Northern District of Georgia.

Outside of work, Michael enjoys fishing, golfing, playing tennis, and spending time with his family.

attorneys.name: Laura Barfield Baxter Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Laura Barfield Baxter’s focus includes estate planning, probate matters (including guardianships and conservatorship) and corporate work. Laura practiced law in Macon, Georgia for over nine years before moving to the Atlanta area. While in Macon, Laura had exposure to a wide variety of corporate transactional work, probate issues, and business. Laura is licensed to practice in both Georgia and Tennessee.

Laura obtained her undergraduate degree from the University of Georgia in 1998, with a B.A. in English and Political Science. Following graduation, she decided to pursue a law degree while working at a non-profit organization in Charlotte, North Carolina, realizing that a law degree would be a useful tool in serving others. Laura attended Mercer University’s Walter F. George School of Law in Macon, Georgia, graduating in 2004. She was a member of Mercer’s Moot Court Board and served as a student coach.

Laura has helped numerous rural clients receive pro bono estate planning services through the Georgia Appleseed program. She also volunteers with the Dekalb County Probate Clinic, the Georgia Justice Project, and Bible Study Fellowship.

Laura is a native of Perry, Georgia. She and her husband, Jamie, have one daughter, Kate, and two miniature Australian Shepherds, Nickels and Oliver.

attorneys.name: David Beaudry
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Johns Creek, GA
attorneys.bio:
Having practiced solely in family law during his entire legal career, David has over ten years of experiencing litigating these difficult and very personal issues. Originally from Florida, David attended law school at Seton Hall University in Newark, New Jersey and clerked for The Honorable Edward Torack in New Jersey who sat on the Superior Court Bench hearing exclusively Family and Divorce cases. This experience gave David first-hand experience as to how Family Law judges view cases, the factors that are important, and the arguments that are most effective on a variety of issues. David continued his family law practice when he moved here to Georgia where he worked for Stern & Edlin, P.C. prior to joining Meriwether and Tharp, LLC.

David is both well-known and well-respected within the family law field and the legal community at large. David has been an active contributor and leader in the family law field and has lectured in many speaking engagements. In many of his speaking engagements, David provides Continued Legal Educational training to other practicing attorneys and is a great resource for other attorneys practicing family law.

Understanding that the dissolution of a marriage is a difficult time for clients, David is attentive to the individual needs and goals of his clients. While always encouraging reconciliation if possible and settlement if the parties are able to negotiate and agree, David understands that there are some cases that require trial. David has extensive experience in trial practice. Utilizing his experience and knowledge gained both as a judicial law clerk and in practice, David has a keen understanding of the law and relevant factors that a Judge may evaluate on an issue. David is a persuasive speaker, zealous advocate, and a powerful presence in the courtroom.

On a personal level, David has an interest in drama and theater and has served on the Board of Directors of the Roswell Community Theater for the last six years. In addition to theater and drama, David is an avid runner and has completed a marathon and multiple half-marathons.

attorneys.name: Ellen K. Begley
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
During an era when law practice specialization is the trend, Ellen Begley bucks legal industry norms by serving as the Sutton Law Group’s legal generalist. Ellen works across the firm’s practice areas, leveraging her unique combination of business acumen and legal knowledge and skill to help clients solve the legal issues they face.

A native of Peachtree Corners, Georgia, Ellen is a “Double Bear,” having received her Bachelor of Arts (2013) and Juris Doctor (2016) degrees from Mercer University. Though admitted to the State Bar of Georgia shortly after law school, Ellen began her career choosing business over law practice, working in business development for several technology start-up firms.

Since joining Sutton Law Group, she has represented individuals, business, insurers, self-insured companies, and servicing agents throughout Georgia for general civil liability litigation and insurance coverage counsel and litigation. This, in addition to using her background in business to provide external general counsel services to the firm’s clients.

Ellen is licensed to practice in all Georgia State and Superior Courts, the Court of Appeals of Georgia, and the Georgia Supreme Court.

Outside of work, Ellen enjoys hiking, camping, and kayaking with her dog, Quinn, learning new craft skills, baking, and fly fishing.

Phillip Beggs joined Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele, LLP in 1986 and is a Partner in the firm’s Real Estate Department. He has handled a wide variety of transactional and litigation matters involving real estate issues over the last 25 years. In the Real Estate Department, he heads the firm’s commercial leasing practice representing clients in lease negotiations and litigation. Phillip also handles closings and sales contract negotiations for property owners, developers, builders and lenders and coordinates service delivery with the firm’s land use practice group for numerous clients.

attorneys.practice_type: Truck Accidents Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Ben O. Bengtson is an associate in the firm Slappey & Sadd, LLC. Ben attended Augusta State University where he graduated Magna Cum Laude in 1999 with a BA in Political Science with a concentration in International Studies. In 2005 he graduated Cum Laude with a Juris Doctorate from Georgia State. While in law school Ben was active in Jessup International Moot Court Competition and was the President of the International Law Society. Ben has been a member of the State Bar of Georgia since passing the bar examination in 2005.

Prior to college and law school, Ben spent 4 years in the United States Army where he studied Arabic at the Defense Language Institute in Monterey, California. After 2 years of study at the Defense Language Institute, Ben served as an Arabic Linguist in Army Intelligence at Fort Gordon Army Base.

After receiving his undergraduate degree, Ben worked as a disability advocate representing Social Security applicants in hearings before federal judges until he graduated from law school. Ben’s six years of concentrating on medical issues enables him to give his clients a better understanding of the issues surrounding their injuries and how the injuries will affect their ability to work.

Upon graduating from Georgia State law school, Ben worked for an insurance defense firm where he represented insurers and employers in workers' compensation and liability cases. This provided valuable insight to the strategies used by employers and insurance companies, which he now uses to help his clients with workers' compensation controversies.

In August 2008, Ben joined Slappey & Sadd, LLC where he now represents workers' compensation claimants and Social Security disability applicants.

attorneys.practice_type: Environmental Lawyers in Newnan, GA
attorneys.bio:
Even in childhood Laura was a self-motivated, driven, passionate individual who wanted to make a difference in her community. She graduated from Harrison High School in Kennesaw GA before attending Furman University and receiving a Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science and a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science in four years. She then received an academic scholarship to attend Case Western Reserve University School of Law where she received her J.D. in 2003 before returning home to Georgia.

Laura represents local governments, public utilities, developers, and private individuals on state and federal environmental planning, permitting, regulatory compliance and natural resource management. Her business practice is based on integrity, honesty and a strong worth ethic, which she believes has been key to her success and building of long-term trusting relationships. Her knowledge of the Clean Water Act, National Environmental Policy Act, National HIstoric Preservation Act and Endangered Species Act have resulted in a client confidence of her abilities to obtain the desired client objectives which are exemplified by obtaining five of the last five new reservoir permits issued in the State of Georgia in the last ten years.

Laura performs pro bono legal services in her community for minor criminal and civil matters and also is involved in the Georgia Legal Military Assistance Program.

Laura lives in Sharpsburg, GA with her husband, Arthur, their three children and two dogs. She enjoys spending time with her family, playing sports, and cooking. She aspires to read for pleasure but recognizes the likelihood of that happening is moot until after baseball/soccer season. Laura is an active member of her faith community at Holy Trinity Catholic Church in Peachtree City, GA.

attorneys.name: Phill Bettis Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Phill Bettis has practiced law in Forsyth County, Georgia – near his hometown of Cumming – since he was admitted to the State Bar of Georgia in 1980. In May of 2001, Phill left the firm of Boling, Rice, Bettis and Martin to establish his own practice specializing in real estate, corporate, and probate law and mediation and dispute resolution. He now serves as senior Of Counsel with Georgia Legacy Law Group, LLC, in addition to managing his own firm. In December of 2013, Phill was appointed as an associate judge on the Magistrate Court of Forsyth County.

A native of Forsyth County, Phill enjoys taking an active role in the community. He is currently the Chairperson and a Trustee of the Benjamin Brady Foundation, which supports many local charities. Phill has served as a Vice Chairman of the Georgia Baptist Health Care Ministry Foundation, and is an ordained Deacon. He is a former Executive Committee Member of the Georgia Baptist Convention. Phill was the 2005 Chairman of the State Bar of Georgia Committee on Professionalism and a former Trustee of the Forsyth County Library Board and Lanier Technical College as well as a member of the Board of Visitors at Shorter University. Phill was honored to be named the 2004 Volunteer of the Year by the Metro Atlanta YMCA, and was also named as an Atlanta Magazine Georgia Super Lawyer for 2005, 2009, 2010, again in 2018. Phill was selected for inclusion in Georgia Trend Magazine’s Legal Elite in 2012 in the area of Real Estate law.

Aside from his law practice, service as judge, and community activities, Phill has authored a book titled “The Little Book of Annoying Questions,” which was published in summer 2012. Phill is working on his second book now. He also enjoys spending time with his friends and family, including his wife and three children.

attorneys.name: Donald Lee Biola
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of D. Lee Biola
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation- Injured Workers Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Lee Biola represents workers who have been injured on the job before the State Board of Workers’ Compensation. Lee is a former insurance company attorney who now declines offers to represent insurance companies. After graduation from law school, Lee worked for the law firm of Lowendick, Speed, and Cuzdey where he primarily represented insurance companies in workers’ compensation cases. Upon opening his own law practice in 2001, Lee changed his focus from representing insurance companies to representing injured workers.

Before becoming a lawyer, Lee worked as an associate producer for CNN in Atlanta. He worked on all of CNN’s major news programs at one time or another, including the legal affairs program “Burden of Proof.”

Lee is a graduate of the Georgia State University College of Law where he served as Co-editor of the legislative history section of the Georgia State University Law Review. Lee competed as a member of the Jessup International Moot Court Team and completed externships with Fulton County Superior Court Judge Wendy Shoob and the office of Georgia Attorney General Thurbert Baker.

Lee personally handles all of his workers’ compensation cases. Clients do not deal with paralegals or legal secretaries, but receive individualized attention directly from an attorney.

attorneys.practice_type: U.S. Immigration Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Rachel Binstock handles cases in all areas of U.S. immigration law, especially humanitarian relief, family-based immigration, and naturalization. She specializes in VAWA, SIJS, U/T, Parole in Place, and other humanitarian cases. She also prepares writs of mandamus to the Federal District Court seeking adjudication of long-pending delayed applications.

After finishing law school at Hofstra University School of Law, Rachel Binstock and her husband moved to Australia for 15 months where she studied, traveled, and began working at an Australian Immigration firm. This is where her interest in immigration started. Upon returning, she began working in U.S. immigration and has been hooked ever since. Born and raised in Atlanta, GA, Rachel Binstocki s happy to be back in Atlanta permanently, doing the work she loves.

attorneys.name: Damon S. Bivek
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Damon is a founding partner of Bivek Brubaker & Prescott LLC. Together with his partners, they have built a firm dedicated to excellence, client service, professionalism, and forward-thinking representation. "My partners and I recognize that the foundation of an effective attorney-client relationship lies in communication and trust." When dealing with your family law issues, it is important to recognize that emotions can cloud judgment. Selecting the right advocate to represent your interests and help you design a strategic roadmap to guide you is one of the most critical decisions an individual going through a family law dispute can make."

"We believe that everyone should have the opportunity to consult with first-rate attorneys who are knowledgeable, and can offer a specialized expertise in the area of family law." Bivek Brubaker and Prescott LLC focuses its practice exclusively in the area of family law, and Damon handles cases in the Superior Courts of Cobb, Fulton, Paulding, Dekalb, Henry, Forsyth, Cherokee, Canton, Gwinnett and the Court of Appeals.

Damon has clerked for the Supreme Court of Georgia, and is trained as a Guardian Ad Litem. He recently served, from 2010- 2011, as the President of the Family Law Section of the Cobb County Bar Association, and has also served on the Cobb County Bar Association's Board of Trustees. He has organized several Continuing Legal Education events for Family Law practitioners in Georgia, and recently served as the Chair of a Family Law Symposium that covered hot topics and trends in family law including E-Discovery and social media, utilizing private investigators, dividing closely-held family businesses, dividing complex stock options, 401(K)s and retirement assets, and working effectively with a Guardian Ad Litem in contested custody cases. Damon regularly leads a Family Law Workshop at the Cobb County Superior Court for pro se litigants who need help resolving their family law disputes.

When Damon is not in the courtroom or serving the legal community, he enjoys spending time with his Wife and Son, golfing, traveling, and playing with his Labrador Retriever, Cocoa. Don't let his calm assertive demeanor deceive you, as one client puts it: "He is definitely a lawyer I would want on my side, not against me in a tough battle."
