attorneys.name: Ashley A. Cooper
attorneys.practice_type: Juvenile Criminal Defense Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Ashley is a graduate of the Appalachian School of Law in Grundy, Virginia, where she focused her studies on trial advocacy and criminal law. During law school, she interned with the Honorable John S. McLellan, III, of the Second Judicial District in Sullivan County, Tennessee.

Ashley primarily concentrates her practice in the areas of criminal law, juvenile criminal defense, juvenile dependency proceedings, and appellate law. She has extensive trial experience, both in the Juvenile Courts of Georgia and the Superior Courts of Georgia.

Prior to entering private practice, this Macon lawyer was an Assistant District Attorney in the District Attorney's Office for the Macon Judicial Circuit where she worked for several years. During that time, she screened all juvenile cases that went through the DA's Office, deciding what to prosecute, what plea bargains to accept, and which cases would need to be tried before the Juvenile Court, which is a non-jury proceeding.

After handling thousands of cases in the DA's Office, Ashley decided that she would spend the rest of her career committed to defending teenagers, not locking them up. In 2013, Ashley started her own law firm, where she built her practice focusing on civil litigation, domestic relations, criminal defense, juvenile defense, juvenile dependency proceedings, and criminal appeals.

Ashley grew up in Kingsport, Tennessee, where her father is a second-generation veterinarian. Despite her love of animals, she realized that she wanted to be a trial attorney while she was studying at East Tennessee State University, where she earned a Bachelor of Arts in Honors English and in Political Science. Based on experiences of friends and classmates in college, Ashley realized that she especially wanted to help young people, like college students, to stand up for themselves and their rights in court.

attorneys.name: Cathy Cooper
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Cathy brings over three decades of exceptional legal expertise and entrepreneurial leadership to her practice, combining knowledge of family law, corporate law, and business innovation to guide clients through complex personal and financial transitions. Since earning her J.D. from Tulane Law School in 1992, Ms. Cooper has established herself as a strategic attorney, accomplished business leader, and compassionate advocate who delivers tailored solutions with precision and empathy.

Ms. Cooper handles all aspects of family law, including divorce, child custody, spousal support, property division, and the preparation of prenuptial and postnuptial agreements. Her keen negotiation abilities and proven courtroom skills ensure clients receive strategic, results-driven representation. Ms. Cooper is known for making complex legal matters understandable, empowering clients to move forward through difficult family transitions with clarity and confidence.

Her entrepreneurial background and corporate law experience provide a distinct advantage, particularly in high-asset divorces and cases involving business interests. As founder and Chief Legal Counsel of WaistLite™ since 2021, Ms. Cooper developed and launched an innovative dietary supplement addressing alcohol-related weight management, with the company earning recognition as “the most innovative brand of 2024.” She managed every dimension of the business—intellectual property protection, FDA compliance, trademark strategy, direct-to-consumer sales, and cross-functional team leadership. This real-world experience in business operations and financial structures enables her to navigate complex asset valuations and business ownership disputes with exceptional skill.

Between 2009 and 2020, Ms. Cooper founded and led an e-commerce platform in the beauty industry, negotiating global distribution agreements and hundreds of professional contracts as Master Broker for a premier hair color brand in Australasia. Since 2024, she has advised C-suite executives on contract negotiations, regulatory compliance, intellectual property, technology licensing, and corporate governance across multiple for-profit and nonprofit organizations. This corporate acumen strengthens her ability to serve family law clients with professional practices or sophisticated financial portfolios.

Earlier in her career (1992–2008), Ms. Cooper represented clients across diverse practice areas including complex business litigation, employment law, criminal defense, and medical malpractice in Atlanta and New Orleans. She edited a comprehensive 700-page Sourcebook on labor and employment law and directed business development for the intellectual property division of an AmLaw 100 firm. Her published work has appeared in Business to Business, Atlanta Business Chronicle, Atlanta Magazine, and other publications.

Ms. Cooper earned her J.D. from Tulane Law School in 1992, where she served as Managing Editor of the Tulane Maritime Law Review and externed for Judge Steven R. Plotkin. She is admitted to practice in Georgia and Louisiana. She holds a B.A. with honors from the University of Pennsylvania, where she edited for The Pennsylvania Review, produced for The Pennsylvania Players theatrical group, and competed on the equestrian team. A former officer of the Federal Bar Association in Atlanta, she remains active in the Georgia Bar Association’s Family Law Section.

Beyond her legal practice, Ms. Cooper has demonstrated a strong commitment to community service, chairing high-profile fundraisers including the Atlanta Opera Ball, serving as PR Chair for the Atlanta Junior League, and contributing as a board member for literacy and media organizations.

Ms. Cooper is married with three adult children. She is an avid dressage rider and German shepherd enthusiast.

attorneys.name: M. Devlin Cooper
attorneys.practice_type: Eminent Domain Proceedings & Condemnation Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Devlin is a graduate of the George Mason University School of Law in Arlington, Virginia, where he completed the Regulatory Law Specialty Track of study. After law school, Devlin clerked for the Honorable Lamar W. Sizemore, Jr. and the Honorable Tilman E. Self, III, of the Superior Courts of Georgia, Macon Judicial Circuit.

Our Macon attorney primarily concentrates his practice in the areas of eminent domain law, business litigation, probate litigation, and other corporate law. He has extensive jury trial experience, having tried more than fifteen cases to verdict before juries throughout the State of Georgia.

Devlin is a native of Milledgeville, Georgia, and graduated summa cum laude with a Bachelor of Science in Economics from Georgia College in 2002. During his final semester at Georgia College, Devlin interned for Attorney General Edwin Meese, III in the Center for Legal and Judicial Studies at The Heritage Foundation in Washington, D.C.

Georgia Attorney General Samuel S. Olens appointed Devlin to serve as a Special Assistant Attorney General in 2013, and in that capacity, Devlin represents the Georgia Department of Transportation in real estate matters and eminent domain/condemnation law proceedings. Devlin was also elected Secretary/Treasurer of the Eminent Domain Section of the State Bar of Georgia for 2017.

Ultimately, a trial attorney is judged by the results that they achieve and how many cases they try. Devlin has the experience and reputation to allow him to resolve many cases without needing a trial. Devlin is both an efficient and aggressive litigator, which allows him to place his clients in a favorable position to resolve their matters via settlement or trial.?

attorneys.bio:
Hector Cora was admitted to the State Bar of Georgia in 1993, receiving his undergraduate degree (B.B.B Accounting 1990) and law degree (Juris Doctor, 1993) from Georgia State University. Hector’s practice focuses on Immigration Law, Personal Injury, including victims of violent offenses, and Workers’ Compensation.

Representing numerous clients before the Executive Office of Immigration Review, Hector has obtained favorable results including Lawful Permanent Residency and dismissal of cases seeking removal.

Hector has obtained favorable results for clients who were victims of violent crimes, including U-Visas, Lawful Permanent Residency and money damages. He also represents injured persons in personal injury and workers’ compensation cases in various courts throughout the Southeastern U.S.

Being fluent in Spanish, Hector has spoken at various conferences on various areas of Immigration Law, including how victims of violent crimes can obtain permanent residency in the United States and pursue claims against those that can be held responsible for injuries from violent offenses.

Our law office was founded by attorney Carlos L. Corless, a native of Venezuela and longtime Atlanta-area resident. Since 1992, he has guided clients to positive outcomes in workers' compensation and personal injury cases. He is bilingual and intimately familiar with the needs of the Latino communities in Georgia and the Southeast United States.

The Law Office of Carlos L. Corless — A History of Success

We bring steadfast and bold representation to jury trials, bench trials and other legal proceedings. Our willingness to take the necessary steps to overcome all challenges and get results has allowed us to obtain more than $20 million in verdicts and settlements in personal injury and workers' compensation cases. While less easy to quantify, we have established an impressive record of guiding clients to outcomes they are happy with, outcomes that take into account both short-term and long-term needs.

A Welcoming and Family-Friendly Environment

We understand that our clients are going through some of the most stressful situations they have ever encountered. Their lives are shaken by serious injuries or the loss of a loved one, or their family structures are being redefined because of a divorce. When you come to us, you will find that we are understanding and welcoming. We will make it clear that we are here to help you through your stressful situation as soon as possible.

attorneys.name: Alex Cornejo
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Law Lawyers in Woodstock, GA
attorneys.bio:
Alexandros H. Cornejo has a strong presence in the United States, with offices in New York, Dalton, and Woodstock, GA. Adept in immigration law, he handles cases related to the adjustment of status, citizenship, deportation defense, and family reunification.

Having recently expanded his firm to Lima, Peru – his birthplace in La Planicie – Mr. Cornejo has gained significant media attention. He provides skilled commentary on televised immigration cases and is mentioned in publications such as Viver Magazine, Revista COSAS Perú, and Business Empresarial.

As a distinguished Peruvian-American attorney, Mr. Cornejo is renowned for effectively representing a varied client base. He is authorized to practice across all 50 states and U.S. territories. Notably, in 2021, he achieved the release of more than 120 Latino immigrants from federal detention.

Mr. Cornejo’s academic journey began at the Pontificia Universidad Católica del Perú in Lima, a premier law school in the region. He furthered his education in the United States, receiving his Bachelor of Science in criminal justice from the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, in 2016. He then received his Juris Doctor from Atlanta’s John Marshall Law School in 2018, graduating with honors and receiving the “Distinguished Alumni Award 2023.” He was admitted to the New York State Bar Association in 2019.

Beyond his professional prowess, Mr. Cornejo is recognized for his philanthropic commitment to underrepresented communities, providing legal representation to those who might otherwise be neglected. His personal immigration experience allows him to empathize deeply with his clients, advocating for their rights with fervor and precision. He is trilingual, speaking English, Spanish, and Portuguese fluently.

His personal immigration experience allows him to empathize deeply with his clients, advocating for their rights with fervor and precision. He is trilingual, speaking English, Spanish, and Portuguese fluently.

Voted Georgia Super Lawyer 2016 – 2026!

Arturo Corso created The Corso Law Center from his servant’s heart. attorneys.name: Robert Adam Cowan
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Dalton, GA
attorneys.bio:
Rob began his legal career representing insurance companies but realized it was people, not insurance companies, he most wanted to help. After practicing and becoming a partner at Kinney, Kemp, Sponcler, Joiner & Tharpe until 2001, he established Cowan, Plumley, and Bucci, LLC, and maintained two offices in North Georgia until 2003. Rob then established The Cowan Law Firm in early 2003 in Dalton, GA, where he focuses on personal injury and wrongful death claims, business and contract disputes, and mediation and arbitration.

Personal attention and accessibility set Rob Cowan apart from other attorneys. When you enter The Cowan Law Firm, the first door you’ll see is the one for Rob’s own office, and on any given day, you’ll find it open. He doesn’t hide from his clients. Instead, he invites them in. A number of attorneys barely explain or communicate with their clients, leaving the client barely aware of the legal issues in the case and what they can expect moving forward. Rob makes sure that each client knows and understands the complexities of their case, their role as a litigant, and the need to be well prepared so the client’s expectations can be achieved.

Rob understands that you are not just a case or claim. He learns about each of his clients, their lives, and businesses. It’s in these other details that he finds important factors and pieces of the puzzle that may also be affected by the main problem being presented. Whether helping clients in a wrongful death case, personal injury or family law matter, or business dispute, Rob enjoys helping people find relief from the problem they’re facing.

Other attorneys look to Rob to help them with their clients and cases. So much so that they have come to him to help solve disputes through mediation. Rob regularly conducts over 150 mediations a year, most to a successful settlement.

Rob lives in Dalton with his family and practices primarily in north Georgia – from the Alabama line east to Union County. He values his community and was the recipient of the Justice Robert Benham Award for Community Service. An avid runner, having completed several marathons, he shares his love for running by volunteering at a local elementary school where the running club he started has grown from 20 to 80 students in just a few years. He has served as chairman of the Whitfield County Hospital Authority, The Northwest Georgia Regional Library Board, The Creative Arts Guild, and many more organizations.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Justice Robert Benham Award for Community Service, 2006

Cynthia Craig is a native of Pennsylvania. She received an Honors Bachelor’s degree in Psychology with High Distinction from Pennsylvania State University – The Behrend College. She also received a master’s degree in clinical psychology from Edinboro University. She earned her Juris Doctorate degree from New England Law Boston, where she served as an editor of the New England Law Review. While still in law school, Cynthia was a judicial intern at the Massachusetts Court of Appeals. After graduating, she was hired as a law clerk for the Justices of the Massachusetts Superior Court.

Prior to joining the firm, Cynthia represented utility companies in litigation stemming from catastrophic natural gas and electric-related fires, explosions, and accidents. She has also represented corporations in complex commercial litigation matters involving allegations of negligence, fraud, breach of contract, breach of warranty, and in SEC investigations. She now utilizes that experienced to inform her representation of people that are injured by the negligence of others.

Cynthia brought her fanatical support for the Boston Red Sox with her when she moved to Atlanta. She also supports the Atlanta Braves by attending as many games as she can. She also enjoys gardening, cooking, hiking with her dogs (Bobby John and Fenway) and playing league bocce.

attorneys.name: Jason L. Crawford
attorneys.practice_type: Class Action and Consumer Litigation Lawyers in Columbus, GA
attorneys.bio:
Jason has been practicing law since May of 1993, when he graduated third in his class from the University of Georgia, School of Law. Since he graduated from law school, Jason has successfully represented hundreds of clients, including victims of automobile design defects, consumer, lender, and insurance fraud, trucking negligence and impaired commercial and private drivers, roadway design and construction defects, faulty playground equipment, defectively designed industrial and agricultural equipment, and he has also represented small business owners in venture capital and other business disputes.

Mr. Crawford has been appointed lead counsel in a multi-state class action lawsuit that was certified as a class adversarially in the Georgia state court system. Mr. Crawford was also one of the primary lawyers involved in the successful, nationwide class action settlement reached in federal district court in the case of McBride v. Life of Virginia d/b/a GE Life. The McBride case involved universal life insurance policies. The company claimed the right to increase the premium payments of its policyholders, many times even after the policyholder had paid on the policy for many years. The settlement made over $150 million in relief available to the policyholders.

Mr. Crawford has successfully prosecuted cases against GM, Ford, Chrysler, Toyota, Honda, Mitsubishi, Asplundh, Altech, and the DOT. Some of the types of defects involved were fuel system design (gas tank location, fuel lines), door latch strength, instability and unreasonably high rollover likelihood, roof strength, seatback strength, and cable strength in aerial lifts.

All of the partners at DC&B began their trial practice and litigation careers at a nationally recognized law firm. Jason worked at that firm for almost 13 years. He made partner there in 2000 and became a name-partner in 2004. Mr. Crawford owes much of his success and training to his time at his previous firm.

Along with Pete Daughtery and Dustin Brown, Mr. Crawford founded DC&B in March of 2006. The partners enjoyed practicing with each other and wanted the increased flexibility that comes with a smaller law firm. DC&B still represent the same types of clients in the same types of cases as when they were at their original firm.

Mr. Crawford has held many leadership positions in the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association. He has authored or co-authored more than a dozen law review articles. He is a member of the Board of Directors at the Gardens at Calvary, a retirement community in Columbus, and for more than a decade, he coached the Columbus High School Mock Trial team.

attorneys.name: Nicole Crites
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Nicole began her legal career in high school when she participated in Volusia County, Florida’s Teen Court Program, which is designed as a diversionary program for juvenile defendants facing minor criminal charges. She volunteered as a teen prosecutor and went on to win Prosecutor of the Year in her county.

Nicole’s commitment to service continued into adulthood, when she became a volunteer Guardian ad Litem for Florida’s Eighth Judicial Circuit, in Alachua County. Even before starting law school Nicole had plenty of experience making court appearances, speaking to judges, and confronting uncomfortable truths in pursuit of the best interests of the children she served. It was through these experiences that Nicole solidified her desire to help families going through tough times, and more specifically, to help the children of these families.

Nicole received her undergraduate degree from the University of Florida in 2011 and went on to receive her Juris Doctorate from the University of Florida, Levin College of Law. While in law school, Nicole participated in the prosecution clinic and worked in the Domestic Violence Unit of the State Attorney’s Office in the Eighth Judicial Circuit, seeking justice and, most importantly, safety for the victims of domestic violence. It was through this clinic, as well as working for a private firm, that it became clear that the years Nicole spent inside of a courtroom before attending law school had given her an advantage, as Nicole’s ease and comfort addressing the court and advocating was well advanced for her years. Unlike other recent law school graduates, who stumbled through objections, Nicole was calm, determined, never wavering, and a force to be reckoned.

After being admitted to the Florida bar and working in domestic relations in Florida, Nicole decided to move closer to her family in Atlanta. Nicole continued to work in domestic relations law after her move and has frequently litigated complex matters involving trusts, closely held business entities, complicated child custody matters, litigants with narcissistic personality disorder, and equitable division of assets whose value is difficult to ascertain.

Nicole fervently believes that it is best for children if their parents can resolve issues through a collaborative and non-adversarial approach. However, she recognizes that this approach is not always feasible for certain litigants and has developed an assertive and confident style in the courtroom.

Nicole understands that there is wisdom in the Art of War and that a long-term strategy, not short-term tactics, leads to the best results for clients. Nicole doesn’t engage in foolishness that only serves to drive up costs and instead focuses her calm demeanor and patience on formulating a strategy designed to get her clients to the end of their litigation with favorable results.

Nicole worked as a professional chef while in undergraduate school and law school, and has brought those skills home. When she is not being a lawyer, she enjoys cooking five-star meals and being home with her children and dogs.

attorneys.name: Lori D. Crosby
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Lawrenceville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Lori graduated from Mississippi College School of Law in 1998. While in law school, she was an Associate Justice on the school's Honor Court and a member of the Moot Court team. Lori is a member of the State Bar of Georgia. She is admitted to practice in all Georgia state trial courts, the Georgia Supreme Court, Court of Appeals, and the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia.

Since graduation, she has worked tirelessly as a lawyer and mother. She started her legal career as the Staff Attorney for the Honorable Linda Warren Hunter in DeKalb County Superior Court. As the Superior Court is the highest trial court in Georgia, she assisted Judge Hunter on cases ranging from domestic relations to felonies. In 2001, she joined the Decatur firm of Wilson, Morton & Downs, LLC as an associate. During her tenure there she focused on complex civil and domestic litigation. In addition to her experience in the areas of domestic and civil litigation, Lori has now turned her focus to assisting those charged with crimes.

In 2006, when Lori and Matt welcomed their second child, she became an inactive member of the Georgia Bar choosing to turn her focus to supporting her family at home and helping Matt grow his criminal defense law practice. As the Office Manager for Matthew D. Crosby, PC, Lori oversaw the day to day operations of the firm. To keep current on the law while she was inactive, Lori researched and wrote legal briefs with Matt. She also directed and assisted in the renovation of the building which now houses Crosby Law.

Both kids attend the Gwinnett County Public Schools and Lori still volunteers regularly. She also enjoys playing tennis, traveling and spending time with her family.

attorneys.name: Matt Crosby
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Lawrenceville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Crosby grew up in the metro-Atlanta area and honed his trial skills serving as an Assistant District Attorney in the Gwinnett County District Attorney’s Office prosecuting felonies. As a prosecutor, Mr. Crosby successfully tried and convicted individuals charged with murder, rape, kidnapping, child molestation, armed robbery, drug, vehicular homicide, aggravated assault, forgery, theft among other charges. Before prosecuting Matt worked with his father, Attorney David Crosby in Atlanta where he not only defended those charged with crimes, he also handled complex civil litigation issues for corporate, as well as individual clients.

During his career, Mr. Crosby has had extensive litigation experience, appearing as lead counsel in well over two thousand felony criminal cases. He has tried over 150 jury and bench trials. Mr. Crosby has a significant amount of appellate experience as well, handling and successfully arguing cases in front of both the Georgia Court of Appeals and the Georgia Supreme Court. Mr. Crosby also served as an Assistant City Solicitor in the City of Suwanee, GA prosecuting misdemeanors such as DUI’s.

Mr. Crosby is married to his law partner with two children. He and his family live in Snellville, GA. In his free time, he enjoys spending time with his family, traveling, watching college football, and exercising.

attorneys.name: Michael D. Cross Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate Law Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
As a Partner at Briskin, Cross & Sanford, LLC, Michael Cross brings more than two decades of experience advising privately held companies, entrepreneurs, and nonprofit organizations in all aspects of business law. His practice spans corporate transactions, mergers and acquisitions, partnership and LLC law, franchise law, employment law, and commercial real estate. Known for his pragmatic and creative problem-solving, Michael helps clients structure, protect, and grow their businesses while navigating complex legal and regulatory landscapes.

Michael’s work encompasses everything from negotiating executive employment agreements and commercial leases to structuring multimillion-dollar mergers and acquisitions. He has also developed a strong niche advising nonprofit and charitable organizations on formation, governance, and tax-exempt compliance. Clients value his ability to combine deep technical knowledge with practical business insight—an approach that consistently helps them achieve efficient, results-driven outcomes.

Beyond his legal practice, Michael is a frequent lecturer and author on topics of business law, employment law, and leadership. Over his career, he has taught more than 30 continuing legal education seminars and served for eleven years as an adjunct professor, teaching courses in business law and leadership. His professional recognition includes repeated listings in Super Lawyers, Rising Stars and Georgia Trend’s Legal Elite.

An active leader in the Alpharetta community, Michael serves on the Board of Directors of the Greater North Fulton Chamber of Commerce and as Trustee and Citizen Representative for the Alpharetta Public Pension Plan. He previously served as Chairman of the Alpharetta Development Authority and as an elected member of the Alpharetta City Council. Outside the firm, he is deeply involved in youth sports and local ministry, having coached over 2,000 youth games and participated in church music and outreach for decades.

Michael earned his J.D. from Emory University School of Law in 2000 and his LL.M. in Taxation from the University of Alabama School of Law in 2007. He received his B.A. in Political Science from Anderson University in 1997. He is admitted to practice in Georgia and Indiana and is a Certified Retirement Plan Fiduciary.

Guided by the philosophy, “Work hard, treat people well, add an element of faith, and good things will happen,” Michael approaches every client relationship with integrity, empathy, and a commitment to delivering practical, long-term solutions.

attorneys.name: Richard J. Crowson
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Sandy Springs, GA
attorneys.bio:
Rick Crowson is a trial lawyer dedicated to helping his clients collect money owed and resolve business disputes. He specializes in helping contractors and other vendors collect unpaid bills from commercial property owners.

At Isenberg & Hewitt, P.C., Rick had the privilege of working with and learning under the late Harriet Isenberg – one of the preeminent creditor’s rights attorneys in the state. Rick and his team work every day to honor her legacy and represent clients with the same vigor and skill that sets the firm apart from others. As a client, you can expect Rick to value your time and money and give honest and direct advice, based on years of hard-won experience. His willingness to take cases to trial is a key advantage in resolving disputes without one.

In addition to commercial collections and business litigation, Rick is a passionate advocate for injured victims of crime. Rick and the firm have recovered millions of dollars for victims of shootings, sexual assaults, nursing home abuse, wrongful death, child abuse and sex trafficking.

Isenberg & Hewitt has the knowledge, skill, and resources to fight the biggest corporate opponents and insurance companies to obtain justice for its clients. As experienced representatives of victims of crime and survivors, Rick and the rest of the team understand how trauma can affect the legal process and work with our clients to build trust during a process that can be difficult. Rick also selectively represents people seriously injured in car wrecks and slip-and-falls, based on the individual merits of each case.

Rick attended Tulane Law School where he had the pleasure of interning for the Honorable Fredericka Homberg Wicker of the Louisiana Fifth Circuit Court of Appeal and the late Honorable Gary Andrews of the Georgia Court of Appeals. He is a proud member of Georgia Trial Lawyers Association, National Crime Victim Bar Association, Lawyers Club of Atlanta, and the Commercial Law League of America. He is admitted to all state and federal courts in Georgia. sections.content:

At Isenberg & Hewitt, P.C., Rick had the privilege of working with and learning under the late Harriet Isenberg – one of the preeminent creditor’s rights attorneys in the state. Rick and his team work every day to honor her legacy and represent clients with the same vigor and skill that sets the firm apart from others. As a client, you can expect Rick to value your time and money and give honest and direct advice, based on years of hard-won experience. His willingness to take cases to trial is a key advantage in resolving disputes without one.

In addition to commercial collections and business litigation, Rick is a passionate advocate for injured victims of crime. Rick and the firm have recovered millions of dollars for victims of shootings, sexual assaults, nursing home abuse, wrongful death, child abuse and sex trafficking.

Isenberg & Hewitt has the knowledge, skill, and resources to fight the biggest corporate opponents and insurance companies to obtain justice for its clients. As experienced representatives of victims of crime and survivors, Rick and the rest of the team understand how trauma can affect the legal process and work with our clients to build trust during a process that can be difficult. Rick also selectively represents people seriously injured in car wrecks and slip-and-falls, based on the individual merits of each case.

attorneys.bio:
Derric Crowther

Derric Crowther attended Atlanta Public Schools prior to attending prep school at the Northfield Mount Hermon School in Northfield, MA. As a young boy, Coach Ronald Brown and Ken Johnson drilled in Derric that he "could do all things through Christ." In 1986, Derric entered the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a mentee of the late Judge A. Leon Higginbotham; student of the legendary Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC) Leader, Julian Bond; as well as, member of an Ivy League Championship football team. Derric graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 1990.

After graduating from Penn, Derric worked in several positions prior to going to law school, but none was as rewarding as his time spent on active duty during Desert Shield/Desert Storm. In 1996, he earned his law degree from the University of Dayton Law School where he was a Dean Scholarship recipient, member of the National Mock Trial Team, member of Moot Court Team, and president of the Black Law Student's Association. He also completed an externship for United States District Court Judge, The Honorable Walter Herbert Rice. In 2003, Derric was a student at the Trial Lawyer's College and immediately thereafter invited to be a part of the staff where he served for years. In 2007, Derric began teaching as an adjunct law professor at John Marshall Law School. Since 2008, Derric and the firm have been sponsor and host in the Justice Bentham project. Derric's prior affiliations include: Henry Spiegel & Milling, Evert & Weathersby and KPMG.

Mr. Crowther was featured in Georgia's Super Lawyers 2007 Rising Stars Edition.

attorneys.name: Norman H. Cuadra Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lawrenceville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Cuadra has been married for 24 years and has three daughters. Mr. Cuadra is fluent in Spanish, speaks a little French and knows some sign language. He loves to coach and play soccer, volleyball, baseball, basketball and football.

Mr. Cuadra has been practicing law since 1995 and is presently the Chief Judge of the Municipal Court of Suwanee. Norman is the managing member of Cuadra & Patel, LLC, where the firm practices criminal law, family law, personal injury law and issues related to criminal/immigration matters.

Mr. Cuadra received his bachelors degree in Rehabilitative Services from the University of Florida in 1989. In 1991, Mr. Cuadra obtained his Florida

Department of Law Enforcement certificate and worked with the Florida Department of Corrections as a Felony Probation Officer supervising a specially designated Gang-affiliated caseload. In 1995, Mr. Cuadra graduated with his Juris Doctorate from Nova Southeastern University.

Mr. Cuadra is a member of the Georgia Bar, Gwinnett Criminal Defense Bar, Forsyth County Criminal Defense Bar, Criminal and Family Law Sections of the Georgia Bar, Georgia Court of Appeals, Supreme Court of Georgia, and US Federal Northern District of Georgia. Mr. Cuadra has litigated at all of the different levels of court in the State of Georgia, including presenting oral argument before the Georgia Court of Appeals and the Georgia Supreme Court.

Mr. Cuadra is an active member in his community. He was past President of the Gwinnett Criminal Bar Section. He has served as a 4th District Representative for the Municipal Court Judge's Council. He was a member of the Commission on Interpreters, serving on the Rules Committee and Ethics Hearing Committee, as a Municipal Court Judge member. Mr. Cuadra has been a guest lecturer for the Georgia Bar and Municipal Court Judge's Continuing Legal Education Seminars. He has also been a guest on CNN Español and PBS television show "Leyes Cotidianas."

Mr. Cuadra has served on the Riverside Elementary School Council, instructed the North Gwinnett High School Mock Trial Team and has been a guest speaker for Suwanee Youth Leaders.

Mr. Cuadra is presently a Deacon for Sugar Hill Church. He and his family have been attending church at Sugar Hill Church for the last 15 years. Mr. Cuadra has served on the Personnel Committee and is presently a representative board member for the North Gwinnett Cooperative.

attorneys.name: Nicola Cummings
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in McDonough, GA
attorneys.bio:
When you’re facing a personal injury battle, you need more than just an attorney — you need a relentless fighter who knows how to build a case from the ground up. Attorney Nicola Cummings brings a rare combination of legal firepower and forensic expertise to every case she handles. A former prosecutor and seasoned crime scene investigator, she knows how to dismantle the opposition’s case and construct a rock-solid strategy for her clients.

Attorney Cummings earned her Juris Doctor from Mercer University School of Law, where she also received a Certificate in Advanced Legal Writing, Research, and Drafting. She holds a Master of Law in Forensic Justice from Virginia University School of Law, further deepening her understanding of the intersection between law and science. She began her academic journey with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from John Jay College of Criminal Justice — a natural choice for someone drawn to justice from day one.

Before stepping into the courtroom, Attorney Cummings spent over 20 years in the trenches of crime scenes as a forensic scientist and crime scene investigator. For nearly a decade, she worked with a metro Atlanta police agency, processing everything from burglaries and arsons to homicides. She didn’t just collect evidence — she analyzed it, interpreted it, and used it to uncover the truth. That same sharp eye for detail and analytical mindset now powers her legal strategies.

Attorney Cummings also served as a prosecutor, where she built and tried cases with the same intensity and precision she brings to personal injury law today. She knows exactly how the other side thinks — and how to beat them.

Whether you’re up against an insurance company that’s trying to deny your claim or need someone who won’t back down from a tough fight, Attorney Cummings is ready. She’s not just aggressive — she’s strategic, experienced, and fully committed to getting you the justice you deserve.

attorneys.name: Brian K. Cunha
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Brian Cunha is an associate concentrating in Workers' Compensation. He joined Slappey & Sadd in 2011 after graduating, cum laude, from Georgia State University College of Law. While attending Georgia State, Brian served on the executive committee of the Moot Court Team. Prior to attending law school, Brian obtained a degree in political science with a focus in legal studies from Kennesaw State University, graduating magna cum laude.

After working as a clerk for an insurance defense firm that primarily defended workers' compensation claims, Brian began to focus on gaining experience while helping individuals in need. He worked with Georgia State's HeLP Clinic, a partnership with Children's Hospital of Atlanta, where he helped families with children being treated with various legal issues. In the summer of 2010, Brian earned a grant through Emory University to work for the Georgia Advocacy Office, a group charged with advocating on behalf of individuals with mental and developmental disabilities. Brian also interned for the Georgia Hospital Association, where he researched various healthcare issues and how they impacted Georgia hospitals.

Since earning his law degree and joining the State Bar of Georgia, Brian has exclusively represented injured workers against their employers and insurers. Brian is a member of the American Bar Association, the Atlanta Bar Association, and the Workers' Compensation Claimant Lawyers section of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: William J. D'Elia
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
William J. D'Elia is a personal injury attorney with the Stein-Caron Law Group. Mr. D'Elia's practice centers around the firm's active litigation caseload, where he is responsible for researching complex legal issues, drafting and responding to pleadings and discovery, attending depositions, mediations and preparing cases for trial.

Mr. D'Elia is a graduate of the Emory University School of Law in Atlanta, Georgia. While earning his Juris Doctorate degree, Mr. D'Elia was an active member of Emory's Mock Trial Society and competed in several Mock Trial competitions across the United States. As a result of his contributions, he was honored with the Emory Mock Trial Society "Achievement in Trial Advocacy" Award. Mr. D'Elia also participated in Emory's nationally recognized Trial Techniques program. To further improve his advocacy abilities outside of the courtroom, Mr. D'Elia became active in the Emory Law Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Society, which focused on advocacy skills in the fields of negotiation, mediation, and arbitration. Mr. D'Elia competed in several ADR competitions throughout the South and also served on the ADR Society's executive board. Upon graduation from Emory, Mr. D'Elia was inducted into the Order of Emory Advocates, an award granted for students who exhibited excellence and attained high honor through the art of advocacy and persuasion.

During law school, Mr. D'Elia interned at Northeast New Jersey Legal Services, where he assisted in the representation of victims of fraud and illegal debt collection practices. Mr. D'Elia previously served as an intern to the Honorable Thomas P. Brown presiding in the Allegany County Supreme Court in New York State.

Mr. D'Elia is a member of the American Bar Association and the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association, and is admitted to practice in the Georgia Supreme Court, Georgia Court of Appeals, all Georgia State and Superior Courts, as well as the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia.

attorneys.practice_type: Birth Injuries Lawyers in Savannah, GA
attorneys.bio:
J.C. Daniel was born in Dawson, Georgia and was raised to love, respect, and appreciate people from all walks of life. J.C. has joined the Savannah office of Morgan and Morgan to fight for justice for clients who have been harmed by medical errors and mistakes by medical professionals and licensed health care facilities such as physicians, nurses, hospitals, nursing homes, and rehab/therapy centers. He is an accomplished litigator with thirty years' experience and sixty plus trials including fifteen years of experience in handling the defense of cases against physicians, nurses, hospitals, and nursing homes. J.C. also recently served for three years as General Counsel for a hospital where he gained valuable insight regarding patient rights, patient safety events, and quality assurance functions.

J.C. takes tremendous pride in being an officer of the court. He is rated AV preeminent by Martindale Hubbell and has twice been named a Georgia Trend Legal Elite.

Over the years, J.C. has coached several youth sports teams, and he also coached a high school team for four years in the Georgia Mock Trial Competition. In his spare time, he enjoys golf and tennis. He and his wife Kathy are empty nesters but have two cats and two golden retrievers.

attorneys.bio:
At Daniels & Rothman, P.C., we pride ourselves on the ability to provide personal service and experience while we aggressively fight for each client's rights. We represent people in a broad range of legal matters including criminal law, drunk driving defense (DUI), divorce, custody and child support matters, and personal injury. We represent businesses and individuals throughout the State of Georgia and try cases in State, Magistrate, Municipal, and Superior Courts.

Many of our clients come to us for representation when they have been arrested for DUI, or drunk driving. We take on more DUI cases than any other Athens firm and we offer free telephone consultations with an attorney and online evaluations. Because we have handled so many DUIs, we know the process inside and out and take the best steps for each client.

Our clients come from all walks of life. While many contact us for DUI defense, criminal matters, or family law representation, they often return for advice on unrelated matters. Because we focus on personal service and years of experience, our clients know they can trust our character and judgment. We offer advice and counsel in many practice areas. As a result, we understand our clients' overall situations and can more adequately help them meet their goals. They know their attorney will personally handle their legal matters and will answer inquiries promptly. Experience has taught us that working closely with clients is a sure method for success.

Our clients' legal triumphs come from communication and an aggressive approach. A strong conviction for the rights of each client and willingness to fight to protect those rights gets the right results. We recognize that people come to us to exercise their day in court and we are always ready to litigate. Sometimes, however, our clients decide that settlement is the answer. Whether we are in court or at the negotiating table, no adversary intimidates us. Our clients are the ultimate authority on the choice to litigate or settle and we are ready to take either road to its logical conclusion. We always explain the pros and cons of each possibility and stand with our clients through their decisions.

At Daniels & Rothman, P.C., we offer dedication to our clients, an aggressive approach, and experience. Whether you need help with a drunk driving or other criminal charge, family law matter, personal injury claim, or another legal matter, we will provide the best representation possible. We encourage you to take advantage of a free phone consultation with an attorney, send us an email. While many of our initial consultations are free, we accept all major credit cards, should you decide to retain us. If you have a legal matter that needs resolution, don't wait to consult a quality attorney. We look forward to hearing from you.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Savannah, GA
attorneys.bio:
When you need to be sure that you are getting the very best legal representation, count on us protect your rights, fight aggressively on your behalf, and get results.

If you are being charged with a crime, you need an attorney with the experience and competence to take every measure to protect your rights, in the courtroom and out. Attorney Richard Darden handles criminal law cases including, drug cases; sex crimes; murder; death penalty cases; white collar crimes; thefts; assaults; health care fraud; federal and state appeals; admitted to federal courts; 5th and 11th circuit court of appeals; admitted to Supreme and Appeals court of Georgia-over 50 appeals handled in State appeals.

In addition to having a stellar record as criminal defense attorney, Richard Darden has 31 years of law experience, giving him the intricate understanding of legal procedures necessary to develop a winning strategy for your case. He was a Public Defender for 2 years, and practiced law in Germany and Italy for 10 years, representing military members worldwide in criminal cases. Attorney Richard Darden has handled 14 state court death penalty cases-successfully defended all against imposition of death penalty, and tried over 30 murder cases.

So when you have been charged with a crime, choose an attorney that not only knows your rights, but will do everything in his power to protect them. Choose the Law Office of Richard Darden.

attorneys.name: Sheldon Dartt
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Sheldon is a Georgia native who grew up in Cobb County. He attended the University of Georgia where he received a Bachelor's Degree in Finance in 2008. In 2011, Sheldon received his Juris Doctor from the Georgia State University College of Law.

While in law school Sheldon had the opportunity to work for Judge Debra Bernes of the Georgia Court of Appeals. After finishing law school, Sheldon worked as in-house staff counsel for GEICO. In this position, Sheldon learned how insurance companies evaluate and judge their claims for personal injuries and property damage. He now uses the insights he gained to help all of his clients achieve the best possible results.

When he is not working, you can find him spending time with his friends and family, out on the golf course, or in a movie theater.

attorneys.name: Alexa Dato
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Johns Creek, GA
attorneys.bio:
Alexa Dato is an associate attorney with Meriwether & Tharp, LLC. She graduated summa cum laude from the University of Alabama in 2018 with a bachelor's degree in Spanish and Political Science as well as a master's degree in Public Administration. At Alabama, Alexa gave tours of the university as a member of Capstone Men & Women, and she served as Personnel Chair of Chi Omega sorority. Following her family's move from Memphis, TN to Alpharetta, GA, Alexa attended law school at the University of Georgia.

Alexa became interested in working with families after spending three semesters with UGA Law's Family Justice Clinic, which provides legal aid to victims of domestic violence. Alexa continued her advocacy work as a member of the Moot Court team, placing as a Finalist in the National Online Moot Court Competition and participating in the Intrastate Moot Court Competition. During her time as a "Law Dawg," Alexa helped students and administrators navigate challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic as Vice President of her 2L and 3L classes. In her final year of law school, Alexa completed training to be a Neutral Mediator with the Georgia Office of Dispute Resolution and she clerked for the Honorable Chief Judge Eric Norris at the Superior Court of Athens-Clarke County.

Outside of the office, Alexa enjoys spending time with family at Lake Lanier and hanging out with her pug, A.J., and her cat Dolly, named for beloved humanitarian Dolly Parton.

attorneys.name: Kristy Davies
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Gainesville, GA
attorneys.bio:
A 2010 graduate of Florida State University of Law and 2006 magna cum laude graduate of The University of Georgia, Kristy began her career representing victims of crime as an Assistant State Attorney in the First Judicial Circuit of Florida. In just 18 months, Kristy honed her trial skills as lead prosecutor in over 20 jury trials.

A Georgia native with considerable trial experience, Kristy was soon recruited by a prominent personal injury firm that specialized in catastrophic injury and wrongful death cases. For 7 years, Kristy obtained many multi-million dollar settlements and jury verdicts against auto manufacturers, trucking companies, and other giants whose negligent acts resulted in catastrophic harm. Kristy knows the devastation experienced by victims and their family members when someone suffers paralysis, dismemberment, a traumatic brain injury, or death as the result of someone else’s negligent acts. She also knows the extent to which insurance companies, trucking companies, and auto manufacturers will deny responsibility and compensation for these injuries, and the dedication required to successfully litigate these claims.

Kristy has consistently been named as a Super Lawyers’ Rising Star, which recognizes the top 2.5% of attorneys under 40 in Georgia. She is an active member of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association and was selected to participate in the 2016-2017 LEAD program, which recognizes outstanding lawyers with potential for leadership in the legal and political communities. Kristy is a co-author of two editions of “Commercial Transportation,” a survey published by Mercer Law Review, and has served as a speaker for continuing education.

Kristy lives with her husband, Dustin Davies, and their three children in Gainesville, Georgia where she is an active member of her community. Kristy believes the practice of law at Davies Hothem connects her faith and career as she serves others in need. In Micah 6:8, the Lord commands his followers to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with God. For his Glory, Kristy’s passion is to take hardship, suffering, loss, and all the things the enemy intends for evil, and turn it into something good – justice for her clients that paves a path to physical, emotional, and mental recovery. It is through this passion and faith that assistance funds such as the Davies Hothem Domestic Violence Legal Fund was founded. Kristy is actively involved in her church, Gainesville First United Methodist Church, the Path Project at Baker Glover, the Telford Child Advocacy Center, Gateway Domestic Violence Center, and Marketplace benefiting Safe Kids Hall County.

attorneys.bio:
A native Georgian, Dustin graduated cum laude from the University of Georgia and graduated from the Walter F. George School of Law at Mercer University. Dustin is a graduate of the State Bar of Georgia’s Leadership Academy, GTLA LEAD Program, and Leadership Hall County.

Every year since 2014, Dustin has been selected by his peers as a Super Lawyer Rising Star. Only 2.5% of attorneys in Georgia are selected for this honor. He has also been recognized as a “Legal Elite” by Georgia Trend Magazine. Every year since 2015, Dustin has been selected by The National Trial Lawyers as a Top 40 Under 40 trial lawyer. In 2015, he was named to the Fulton County Daily Report’s “On the Rise 40 Under 40.”

Dustin’s experience of trying cases to juries will help maximize the value of your case. Insurance companies know the attorneys who have success in the courtroom and that is what motivates them to resolve your case for its full value. Many of Dustin’s jury verdicts have far exceeded the best offers from the insurance companies. Dustin has successfully tried cases throughout Georgia and Tennessee and Alabama. He has also handled cases in Florida, South Carolina, and Mississippi.

Mr. Davies was so friendly and professional and took care of everything! He was amazingly thorough, patient, and ultimately very successful.

Dustin Davies is a great lawyer and very good in the courtroom. He loves what he does and it shows.

Dustin may be one of the most understanding and caring individuals to work with.

Dustin did exactly what he said he was going to do.Dustin helped change my life!

Dustin and his wife, Kristy, have three children. They are members of Gainesville First United Methodist Church. Dustin coaches football for his son’s football team with North Hall Junior Trojans.

attorneys.name: J. Anderson Davis
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Rome, GA
attorneys.bio:
J. Anderson (Andy) Davis is a founding partner of Davis Lucas Carter, LLP, specializing in complex business litigation, personal injury, governmental official liability, and class actions. He serves as City Attorney for the City of Rome, lead attorney for the Rome-Floyd County Development Authority, and outside General Counsel for Shorter University.

​In 2016, Andy was named a Fellow of the American College of Trial Lawyers, one of the premier legal associations in the U.S. Since 2006, he has been named a Georgia Super Lawyer by Law & Politics Magazine and Atlanta Magazine. He serves as an active member of Federation of Defense and Corporate Counsel, and member of the International Municipal Lawyers Association.

​Andy has been co-counsel or lead counsel in over 350 cases in the federal courts. He has tried numerous cases in federal and superior courts. Currently, Andy is handling several high stakes cases:

​He represents the City of Rome in a water pollutant case, seeking compensation for Rome to install a new water treatment facility because of PFAS and related contaminants; (City of Rome vs 3M, Dupont, et al, Floyd Superior Court.

He and a group of attorneys represent numerous Georgia, North Carolina, Virginia and Kentucky cities and counties to recover for the Opioid crisis facing communities.

Andy and his Co-Counsel represent City of Summerville in a water pollutant case, also seeking compensation to upgrade a water treatment facility because of PFAS and related contaminants.

Three of his previous notable cases include:

Andy served as Counsel for Cities and Counties in Georgia in the class action litigation against the Online Travel Companies for excise taxes. Andy served as Class Administrator for the Settlement paying out proceeds collected to over 183 cities and counties. (City of Rome, et al. vs. Hotels.com, et al., U.S.D.C., N.D.Ga., Civ. Action No. 4:05-cv-249-HLM).

Andy and Sam Lucas tried a wrongful death case in the United States District Court and won a $30 million verdict. That case was featured on the Investigative Discovery channel’s “Behind Mansion Walls” TV show.

Andy served as lead and liaison counsel for 56 funeral homes in the class action multi-district litigation involving the Tri-State Crematory, Noble, Ga. (In Re Tri-State Crematory Litigation, 215 F.R.D. 660 (N.D. Ga 2003).

Active in the community throughout his time in Rome, Andy has received many community and civic awards for his leadership. He was one of the first recipients of the Georgia Supreme Court Chief Justice Benham Awards for Community Service. Currently he is President of the University of Georgia Law School Alumni Association and a member of the Board of Governors of the State Bar of Georgia.

Andy, an Eagle Scout, received the Silver Beaver Award from the Northwest Georgia Council of Boy Scouts of America. He was honored with a Heart of the Community Award, presented by the Heart of the Community Foundation and Redmond Regional Medical Center to unsung heroes. He has served as chairman of the board for Leadership Georgia, an affiliate of the Georgia Chamber of Commerce.

He graduated from the University of Georgia with a Bachelor of Arts in political science and a Juris Doctorate from the University of Georgia School of Law. He is married to the former Janice Jetton who graduated from the University of Alabama; she is a CPA with Whittington, Jones, & Rudert CPA firm in Rome. They have two adult children. Claire Davis McWhorter who is a finance major graduate from the University of Georgia and Hunter Davis, who is a “Triple Dawg” graduate with a Bachelors and Masters in Accounting, along with a Juris Doctor from the University of Georgia.

attorneys.name: Madalyn S. Davis Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
With over 9 years of experience in estate planning, probate, guardianships, and conservatorships, Madalyn Davis is a seasoned attorney who is passionate about her work and has devoted herself exclusively to these areas of law. In 2023 Madalyn was recognized as an upcoming attorney in the southeast who is committed to advancing estate planning and probate with her nomination, and subsequent graduation, into the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel (ACTEC) Southeast Fellows program. As a Fellow, Madalyn has demonstrated exceptional expertise in managing simple to complex planning strategies and takes a holistic approach to planning.

Madalyn has provided tailored legal counsel to individuals and families from all stages of life for planning and is compassionate, but efficient, in navigating the intricate probate process. She believes in taking a collaborative approach to matters with other professionals and balancing legalism with practicality.

Madalyn offers comprehensive legal services, from drafting estate plans to managing probate and uncontested guardianship matters, ensuring clients receive clear guidance through each stage. Her practice focuses on empowering clients to make informed choices about wealth transfer, care arrangements, and protecting the interests of loved ones.

In addition to her professional life, Madalyn is a wife and is a mom to three young children. In her spare time, Madalyn attends North Gwinnett Church and studies apologetics. Her personal life helps guide her approach to serving families during difficult times, providing legal expertise with compassion

attorneys.name: Regina Wilson Davis
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Law Lawyers in Rome, GA
attorneys.bio:
Regina Wilson Davis was born in Florence, Alabama, and is a lifelong fan of the Crimson Tide. Therefore, it was only natural that she attend the University of Alabama at Tuscaloosa, first to earn her Bachelor's in Psychology and then her Master's in American History. Due to her love of history, she initially considered becoming a teacher, but instead decided to devote her life to helping those that needed it most. So she moved to Georgia, where she became a social worker in inner-city Atlanta, dedicating herself to defending the rights of children.

As part of this work, Ms. Davis often appeared in court representing the interests of the children in her protection. Realizing that she could be a better advocate for their needs as an attorney, she resolved to put herself through law school. During the day, she continued to work full-time as a social worker, while at night she attended the Woodrow Wilson College of Law in Atlanta. They were challenging years, but she was successful, and in 1979, she obtained her Juries Doctor and became a member of the Georgia Bar.

Since earning her law degree, Ms. Davis has practiced disability law exclusively, working on both sides of the bench. For years, she worked with the Social Security Administration as a staff writer for the Office of Hearings and Appeals, writing hundreds of disability decisions for Social Security Judges, becoming well acquainted with the inner workings of the system, the ins and outs of the disability regulations, and the preferences of one judge after another. This knowledge was invaluable when she entered private practice in 1990, and began her work on the other side of the bench - helping disability claimants secure their hard earned Disability Insurance Benefits and much needed Supplementary Security Income.

Ms. Davis has successfully handled thousands of disability cases, at both the administrative and appellate levels, all over North Georgia and Alabama. She is a member of the National Organization of Social Security Claimants Representatives (NOSSCR), and is admitted to practice in the Superior Courts of Georgia, the Georgia Court of Appeals, the Supreme Court of Georgia, the United States District Courts for the Northern District of Georgia, and the Middle District of Alabama, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit.

Honors

attorneys.name: Robert Davis
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Rome, GA
attorneys.bio:
Born in Kentucky, and raised in Georgia, Mr. Davis left the South at the age of 17 when he enlisted in the U.S. Marines. After serving four years in the infantry, he attended college on the GI bill, graduating Magna Cum Laude from the University of Massachusetts at Boston in 1981, with the unlikely degree in Classical Studies and Russian. For the next couple of years, he worked in construction until he gained admission to Mercer University School of Law, in Macon, Georgia. After obtaining his Juris Doctor, Mr. Davis began his legal career by signing on with the Georgia Legal Services Migrant Project, to pursue issues arising under the Fair Labor Standards Act and the Agricultural Protection Act. While his representation of farm workers was receiving national attention, Mr. Davis began learning about disability law. He handled claims at the hearing and appellate levels, and was fortunate enough to assist in prosecuting an important case in the Eleventh Circuit which is still quoted today. After that he worked as an associate with the firm of Nathan Deal and Tom Jarrard in Gainesville, Georgia, dealing with a variety of types of cases, in various Courts, but still developing his experience with disability issues. In a few years he was practicing disability law exclusively, representing claimants all over Georgia, and eventually South Carolina, North Carolina, Florida, Alabama and Tennessee, as well.

In 2003, Mr. Davis married Ms. Regina Wilson, and together they represent claimants all over North Georgia and beyond.

Mr. Davis has successfully represented literally thousands of disability claimants, at all administrative levels, and before the United States District Court and in the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals. He is a member of the National Organization of Social Security Claimants Representatives (NOSSCR), and is admitted to practice before the Middle, Southern and Northern Districts of the United States District Court, the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals, the Superior Courts of Georgia, the Court of Appeals for the State of Georgia, the Georgia Supreme Court, and the United States Court of Veterans Appeals.

William C. Davison was raised in Athens, Georgia and graduated from the University of Georgia Law School in 1989. attorneys.name: David J. Deganian
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
David Deganian is an experienced attorney with expertise in Social Security law. After graduating from the University of the Georgia andGeorgia State University College of Law, Mr. Deganian began his legal career representing indigent criminal defendants at the Office of Public Defender, Atlanta Judicial Circuit.

After leaving the Office of the Public Defender, he was awarded the University of Georgia School of

Law's Public Interest Fellowship, fully funding a legal services program he crafted to provide legal services to minority and low-income clients.

As a fellow, he drafted legislation for the City of Atlanta, represented community organizations in federal litigation, and worked with experts to map areas of environmental inequality in Atlanta. He also served as a visiting professor of law at Barry University School of Law, where he led a team of law students in the provision of legal services to non-profit organizations.

For the past several years, Mr. Deganian has been zealously representing clients in the area of Social Security law. He has successfully represented hundreds of clients in disability hearings before administrative law judges. He has a passion for representing disabled clients who have been unable to secure the benefits they are entitled to under the law.

attorneys.name: William J. Degenhart
attorneys.practice_type: Dog Bite & Animal Attacks Lawyers in Savannah, GA
attorneys.bio:
William J. ""Jay"" Degenhart focuses his practice on premises liability actions, such as slip and fall and negligent security. Licensed to practice in both Georgia and Florida, Mr. Degenhart is an experienced and effective trial attorney who joined the firm after three years with a highly regarded Plaintiff's firm in his hometown of Savannah, Georgia. While with his former firm, Mr. Degenhart assisted in trying numerous significant and high profile cases, including a wrongful death/medical malpractice case that culminated in a $4.475 million dollar verdict. Mr. Degenhart has represented numerous clients in a diverse array of cases, with jury verdicts and settlements for millions of dollars.

Mr. Degenhart enjoys fighting for his clients, and he represents each and every client with an eye focused towards trial to maximize the value of his client's case.

Mr. Degenhart graduated cum laude from the University of Florida Levin College of Law in 2015, where he was a member of the Honor Committee, after a career in the Southern California commercial real estate industry. Mr. Degenhart chose to attend law school after a personal experience convinced him to pursue a legal education and fight for the rights of those who had been wronged by others.

Mr. Degenhart graduated from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2003, where he was a student-athlete on the Tar Heel golf team. Still an avid golfer, Mr. Degenhart competed in the 2011 U.S. Amateur and 2013 U.S. Mid-Amateur. Mr. Degenhart is also an avid traveler, having visited over 71 countries in his lifetime, which gives him a unique cultural perspective to more effectively represent a diverse client base.

attorneys.bio:
Jay V. Dell, Jr. is the founding partner of the Dell Law Firm and has been practicing law for over 25 years. Jay received his J.D., cum laude, Walter F. George School of Law, Mercer University in 1994 and B.S. from Georgia Institute of Technology in 1990. While at Mercer he was on the Mercer Law Review. Jay provides experience, knowledge, and reliability in his practice and service to clients. His practice covers many different areas of the law, but he concentrates on Real Estate, Corporate and other Business matters. Jay also enjoys giving back to the community and has proudly served as the President of the Ocmulgee Judicial Circuit Bar Association, President of the Greene County Chamber of Commerce, and on the Executive Committee of the Real Property Law Section of the State Bar of Georgia, where he was the Chairman of the Residential Closings sub-committee. He is a member of the Rotary Club of Greene/Putnam County, assistant scout master for the local boy scout troop, and has coached baseball, softball, and soccer for the local youth recreational sporting leagues. Jay has also served on numerous boards for local charities and continues to assist them with his time, talent, and donations.

When not working, Jay enjoys spending time with family and friends. Jay and his wife have 3 children and they enjoy outdoor activities, such as golf, boating, hiking, soccer, baseball, and softball. Jay also enjoys woodworking and other projects around the house. Jay's wife, Angela also works at the firm as the marketing director and bookkeeper.

Jay has redefined the Gold Standard in legal services by guiding his clients with clarity and purpose through life's biggest moments. His core values of Trust, Purpose, Loyalty, Value and Ethics have created the best law firm in the Georgia Lake Country.

attorneys.name: Stephen D. Delk
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Valdosta, GA
attorneys.bio:
For years, Stephen built a respected career defending hospitals, national trucking carriers, insurers, and businesses across Georgia in complex liability cases—from medical malpractice and transportation claims to premises and governmental liability. But today, Stephen has turned the page. Drawing on his deep experience and insider knowledge of defense strategy, he now proudly represents individuals and families who’ve suffered serious injuries due to negligence. Stephen lives in Adel, Georgia, and serves clients throughout South Georgia and beyond. His practice is rooted in compassion, strategy, and a commitment to helping people rebuild their lives after injury.

A native of Tifton, Stephen earned his undergraduate degree magna cum laude from Valdosta State University, where he was a student-athlete on the football team. He went on to receive his Juris Doctor from Mercer University’s Walter F. George School of Law. He is admitted to practice in all Georgia state and superior courts, the Georgia Court of Appeals, the Supreme Court of Georgia, and the United States District Courts for the Middle and Southern Districts of Georgia.

Stephen has been selected as a Rising Star, a recognition achieved by only 2.5% of attorneys statewide. He has long been AV Rated by Martindale Hubbard, the highest rating level for legal ability and ethics. Stephen has served as both President and Vice-President of the Tifton Judicial Circuit Bar Association. Outside of work, he enjoys cycling, running, tennis, and spending time with his wife and daughters.

If you or someone you care about has been injured in an auto or trucking accident, harmed due to unsafe conditions on someone’s property, or suffered from medical negligence, Stephen is ready to help. Call today to schedule a consultation.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
JaNelle L. Dennard graduated from Spelman College in 2000 receiving a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science. She graduated from Howard University School of Law upon completion of a Juris Doctorate Degree in 2003. After graduation, Ja Nelle practiced personal injury litigation in Arizona and was also an adjunct professor teaching Business Law at Mesa Community College.

JaNelle is admitted to practice law in the states of Arizona and Georgia. She is also licensed to practice before the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia, U.S. District Court for the District of Arizona, and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit.

JaNelle has practiced all aspects of personal injury litigation including premise liability, medical malpractice, auto accidents, product liability, and wrongful death. JaNelle takes pride in treating all her clients as if they are family members. She works closely with clients to develop case strategies and obtain successful results. She has a sincere passion to help others, not just as part of her job, but outside of work as well. She enjoys volunteering with such organizations as the Junior League of Atlanta and the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association. JaNelle was also a contestant on "Wheel of Fortune".

attorneys.name: David H. Dickerson
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury - Plaintiff Lawyers in Cornelia, GA
attorneys.bio:
David believes practicing law is about helping people navigate real-life challenges. It’s an honor and privilege to step in and help clients when they need you most.

David has been practicing law in Northeast Georgia for over 15 years. He is the son of an accomplished trial lawyer, and he knew from an early age the value of hard work and the responsibility of pursuing justice. David began his legal career in Gainesville and became a partner at one of the oldest and most well-respected law firms in Georgia, Whelchel, Dunlap, Jarrard & Walker, where he had the privilege of working alongside some of the finest trial lawyers in the State. In 2015, David served as President of the local Bar Association, a group of over 200 lawyers and judges from the area.

Over the course of his career, David has gained a tremendous amount of experience and skill in handling many types of trial work. He has a unique perspective and advantage for understanding the real strengths of his cases. David was thrilled to join Cathey & Strain, LLC in 2023. He knew it was an opportunity to join forces with a group of great men who also happen to be incredible trial lawyers. Today, David’s practice is 100% devoted to representing Plaintiffs in serious personal injury and wrongful death cases.

attorneys.name: Loraine M. DiSalvo Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Loraine DiSalvo has been practicing law in Georgia since 1997. Loraine is a partner with Morgan & DiSalvo, P.C., the Alpharetta law firm dedicated to helping individuals and families plan and prepare for the many changes that life brings.

Loraine's areas of concentration include Estate Planning, Probate, Estate Administration, Trust Administration, Tax Planning, Business Succession Planning, Estate and Trust Dispute Resolution, Charitable Gift Planning, and Charitable Organizations. She specializes in addressing the unique needs of blended and non-traditional families as well as same-sex couples.

Loraine is a member of the North Fulton Bar Association, the Stonewall Bar Association, the Georgia Bar Association, the American Bar Association, the Atlanta Bar Association, and the Georgia Association for Women Lawyers. She is a past Chair and past member of the Board of Directors of the Atlanta Bar Association's Estate Planning and Probate Section, and a current member of the CLE Board of Trustees for the Atlanta Bar Association. She also serves as the Editor-in-Chief of The Mortmain, which is published by the Estate Planning and Probate Section for its members. Loraine spent two consecutive years as President of the Professional Women's Information Network (ProWIN), an organization which provides networking, educational, and charitable opportunities for entrepreneurial and professional women in the metropolitan Atlanta area. Prior to becoming President of ProWIN, Loraine spent three years as Treasurer and one year as President-Elect. After her two years as President, followed by a year as Immediate Past President and another year as a Member-at-Large on the ProWIN board of directors, Loraine left the board of directors and joined ProWIN's Advisory Board.

An Atlanta native, Loraine graduated cum laude from Georgia State University and earned her J.D. degree, with distinction, from Emory University. Loraine has one adopted daughter and two grandchildren. She lives in Sandy Springs with her husband, Anthony, and enjoys riding motorcycles and using her expertise as a trained auto mechanic to work on their multiple cars and bikes.

Working at a boutique Atlanta family law firm for many years, Sean has extensive trial experience in matters of divorce, child support, custody, legitimation, paternity, contempt, modification and adoption. On top of his practice, Sean is extremely active in leadership positions in various local and state bar organizations, volunteers extensively and serves as a Guardian Ad Litem in both Superior and Probate court matters.

Formerly a Board Certified Civil Trial Specialist for thirty (30) years and formerly a Board Certified Criminal Trial Specialist for 20 years, trial attorney Roger Dodd has represented clients in legal matters since 1976. Mr. Dodd has been a lecturer, expert witness, and teacher in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, Russia, St. Thomas, Puerto Rico, Canada, Mexico, and various Caribbean locations.

Mr. Dodd is a frequent guest and commentator on television programs, including Court TV, Good Morning America, Geraldo at Large, and is co-author of Cross-Examination: Science and Techniques. He is one of a select group of attorneys to receive the distinguished Super Lawyer rating in multiple states. In addition to teaching throughout the U.S. and other countries, Mr. Dodd provides specialized individual training (www.doddlawclinic.com) and trial lawyer coaching (www.rogerdoddtriallawyercoaching.com).

Mr. Dodd is also a partner in the Jacksonville, Florida plaintiff law firm Spohrer & Dodd P.A. (www.sdlitigation.com) and the firm of Dodd & Kuendig, Park City, Utah (https://www.doddandkuendig.com/).
