attorneys.name: Dustin W. Hamilton
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Savannah, GA
attorneys.bio:
Dustin Hamilton is a founding partner of Hamilton & Padgett, LLC and leads the firm’s Savannah office. He focuses his practice on catastrophic injury, wrongful death, and serious personal injury cases, with extensive experience handling claims involving commercial vehicle collisions, car accidents, premises liability, and nursing home negligence.

Born and raised in Georgia, Dustin earned his bachelor’s degree in political science from the University of Georgia and his Juris Doctor from Mercer University’s Walter F. George School of Law. His legal work is rooted in a strong commitment to justice and a relentless drive to secure fair outcomes for the clients he serves. His dedication to his law practice has earned him recognition as a Super Lawyers’ Rising Star from 2023 to 2025, an honor bestowed upon only the top 2.5% of attorneys under 40 in Georgia.

Dustin is a graduate of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association LEAD program, which selects attorneys with strong potential to lead in both the courtroom and the community. He holds memberships in the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association, the Savannah Bar Association, the Savannah Trial Lawyers Association, and the Academy of Truck Accident Attorneys.

Outside the office, Dustin enjoys spending time with his wife and their two children.

attorneys.name: Michael Hammond
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Michael Hammond is originally from Statham, Georgia and now resides in the Atlanta area. He studied Social Science Education at the University of Georgia prior to attending law school. After graduating from the University of Georgia he worked as a high school teacher and basketball coach. Michael also worked in marketing for a private university. He decided to begin a legal career as an attorney because he wanted to help injured people in need of legal assistance and graduated from Emory Law School. Since graduating, he has focused on workers' compensation. He strives to help his clients navigate the legal system and achieve the maximum recovery.

Michael previously handled workers' compensation cases for a defense firm and understands how to deal with difficult insurance companies. He has also worked as a mediator helping injured workers resolve their disputes.

Outside of work, Michael is an avid sports fan. He is a huge fan of the Georgia Bulldogs and Atlanta Braves. Most of all, Michael enjoys being with his wife and children during his time away from the job.

attorneys.name: Robert M. Hammers Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: Hammers Car Accident & Personal Injury Lawyers
attorneys.practice_type: Automobile Accidents Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Rob is the cofounding partner of Hammers Car Accident & Personal Injury Lawyers. He began his legal career representing insurance companies and large corporations in auto, trucking and industrial accidents cases involving wrongful death and catastrophic injuries. Rob earned his Bachelor of Arts in History from the University of Georgia and his Juris Doctorate from Florida State University College of Law. After college and before studying law, Rob worked in legal presentation services where he developed his love for the law and learned the important role that trial lawyers play in protecting our right to a trial by jury.

Rob is proud to call himself a trial lawyer, and he is dedicated to getting fair and just results for victims of negligence. He began his legal career representing the insurance companies for big corporations involved in motor vehicle accidents, trucking accidents and industrial accidents causing death and catastrophic injuries. During this time, he gained valuable experience which his firm now uses in prosecuting these cases on behalf of those injured by the negligence of others. Rob and his firm only represent personal injury victims. Rob is committed to providing each client with the personal attention that their case deserves and works diligently to obtain the most fair and substantial recovery as possible under the circumstances of each case. He and Jason Schneider have tried dozens of cases to verdict together and have settled thousands of cases, netting millions of dollars for injured persons and their loved ones. These successes have earned Hammers Car Accident & Personal Injury Lawyers the respect of its adversaries and the gratitude of the firm's many satisfied clients.

Rob has been recognized as a National Trial Lawyers Top 100 Trial Lawyers and has been named a Super Lawyers Rising Star for 2012, 2013 and 2015. He has also been selected to the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association LEAD program, which is a very competitive leadership program focused on developing and preparing future leaders to protect each and every citizen of Georgia's 7 th Amendment right to a trial by jury.

Rob's primary areas of expertise are auto and trucking accident cases, premises liability cases, and cases involving defective drugs and medical devices. Rob is admitted to practice law in the State of Georgia, Georgia Court of Appeals, Supreme Court of Georgia, and the United States District Courts for Northern and Middle Districts of Georgia.

attorneys.name: Mary Beth Hand
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Mary Beth Hand joined Adams Law Firm in March 2018, bringing nearly 15 years of legal experience to the firm. As one of Georgia’s great legal minds, Mary Beth applies her experience in the representation of seriously injured individuals in all areas of litigation. Prior to joining Adams Law Firm, Mary Beth was fortunate to practice at two premier law firms in Macon, James-Bates-Brannan-Groover-LLP and Sell & Melton, LLP, both of which allowed her to hone her skills as an attorney in a wide range of matters, including insurance litigation, employment law, business litigation, and appellate litigation.

Mary Beth was also honored to serve as a federal law clerk for the Honorable Hugh Lawson at the United States District Court for the Middle District of Georgia. During that time, Mary Beth gained extensive experience in all areas of federal law and practice and procedure and gained unique knowledge and experience by being at the right hand of Judge Lawson for five years.

Growing up in McRae, GA, Mary Beth graduated as valedictorian of the TCHS class of 1996 and learned about being a team player on the softball field. She continued her education at Georgia Southern University, earning her degree summa cum laude in 2000, all while working a full-time job at a local law firm. That experience taught Mary Beth the importance and value of hard work and stoked her interest in the law. She went on to the University of Georgia School of Law, where she continued to shine academically, serving as managing editor of the Georgia Journal of Intellectual Property Law, graduating magna cum laude in 2003, and being inducted into the Order of the Coif in recognition of her high academic standing.

Being an effective attorney and advocate takes a village, and Mary Beth could not provide the services she does without the support of her husband Adam, a reformed attorney who is now a teacher, and their daughter, Allison. The Hand family loves to travel near and far and spends most Saturdays at the soccer field. Mary Beth is a competitive tennis player and loves to read and listen to the latest hot podcast.

attorneys.name: James W. Hardee
attorneys.firm_name: Fain, Major, Brennan, Sanford & Hardee, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Litigation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Jim Hardee was raised in Marietta, Georgia and is a 1983 graduate of Walton High School in Marietta. Jim then received a Bachelor of Science degree from Auburn University in 1987 where he was president of the School of Public Administration. He then attended the Cumberland School of Law at Samford University in Birmingham, Alabama where he was named outstanding trial advocacy board member and was an honor court justice. Jim and his wife, Stephanie currently reside in Marietta with their twin sons.

Upon graduation from law school, Jim accepted a job as a prosecutor from 1990 until 1997. Jim was given the outstanding service award to his community in 1997. In his time as a prosecutor, Jim tried over 100 first chair jury trials, including 8 capital murder cases. During his last 4 years, Jim was felony division chief and assigned to the major crimes unit prosecuting homicide cases.

Since then, Jim has been lead counsel in roughly 80 civil jury trials in both federal and state court, the vast majority of which have resulted in defense verdicts. All but two trials have resulted in a verdict less than the last settlement offer. Jim concentrates on the defense of wrongful death, products liability, premises liability, vehicular, and trucking accidents. Jim also handles the defense of consumer related claims, particularly as it pertains to the automobile industry.

Jim is a member of the National Institute of Trial Advocacy, Defense Research Institute, Atlanta Claims Association, Atlanta Bar Association, and recently served an appointment a the Education Coordinator for the Atlanta Claims Association.

As a father of special needs children, Jim devotes pro bono time representing the particular needs of these children and various entities serving this amazing and precious group of kids.

Jim is an “AV” Peer Review Rated Attorney by Martindale-Hubbell, reflecting a combination of achieving the highest level of professional achievement and excellence in ethical standards and legal ability.

Awards and Honors

Top Rated Lawyer by The Atlanta Journal and Constitution in Insurance Defense field from 2010 to present

Georgia Legal Leader as recognized by Defense Research Institute

attorneys.name: Travis Hargrove
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accident Lawyer & Auto Injury Attorneys Lawyers in Columbus, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Hargrove graduated Magna Cum Laude from Auburn University with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Economics in 2001. He graduated from the Walter F. George School of Law at Mercer University (where he attended on a full scholarship) Magna Cum Laude in 2004, finishing 4th in his Law School Class. While at Mercer, Mr. Hargrove was a member of the Mercer Law Review, Moot Court Board, and the Brainerd Curie Honor Society. Mr. Hargrove also obtained a Certificate in Advanced Legal Writing.

Mr. Hargrove is licensed in the State and Superior Courts of Georgia, the Northern and Middle Districts of Georgia, all Alabama State and Federal Courts and the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals. Mr. Hargrove has been honored as a Georgia Super Lawyers "Rising Star” in his younger years and more recently as a Georgia Super Lawyer voted by his peers as one of Georgia’s best Civil Litigation Lawyers.

Mr. Hargrove began his legal career in private practice in Atlanta with the firm of King & Spalding, LLP. Mr. Hargrove then made the decision to return to his hometown of Columbus, Georgia. He joined the firm of Page, Scrantom, Sprouse, Tucker & Ford, P.C. where he practiced for ten years (six as a Partner) before joining the Finley Firm where he was a Partner for nearly eight years. During his time in private practice, Mr. Hargrove has handled cases throughout the state and federal courts in Georgia and Alabama, representing both plaintiffs and defendants in Personal Injury cases, Business Disputes, Contractual Disputes, Landlord/Tenant Disputes and Evictions, Construction Litigation, Copyright and Trademark Litigation, Banking Litigation, Workouts and Foreclosures. Mr. Hargrove has successfully tried numerous cases to verdict in Jury Trials, Bench Trials and Arbitrations acting as lead counsel and has obtained Summary Adjudication in his clients’ favor in a multitude of cases. Mr. Hargrove's recent Trial successes include a jury verdict in the amount of $1,825,000 in the United States District Court for the Middle District of Alabama and a jury verdict in the amount of $525,000 in the State Court of Muscogee County, Georgia.

After having success representing small and large businesses in complex business disputes, Mr. Hargrove made the decision to devote his talents exclusively to assisting those who have been injured through the negligence of others.

In 2022, Mr. Hargrove was appointed by the Judges of the Chattahoochee Judicial Circuit as an Assistant Magistrate Judge for Muscogee County, Georgia, a part-time position which he continues to hold in addition to his full-time law practice.

Mr. Hargrove is an Elder at Church on the Trail in Columbus, Georgia, and is the Chairman of the Board of Auburn Christian Fellowship, a Campus Ministry at Auburn University. He and his wife Trisha have three daughters. In his spare time, Mr. Hargrove enjoys coaching women's basketball and soccer. In Soccer, he holds a National USSF "D" License and is the head coach and age group lead of the 2014 Girls team at Concorde Fire South, having previously coached in multiple other age groups. In Basketball, his team will seek its fourth consecutive YMCA Championship in the winter of 2024. When not working or coaching, you can likely find Mr. Hargrove freshwater and saltwater fishing.

attorneys.name: David Harris
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Watkinsville, GA
attorneys.bio:
David was born in Denver, Colorado, and raised in Augusta, Georgia. He graduated magna cum laude from the University of Georgia with a degree in Business Administration and earned his J.D. cum laude from the University of Georgia School of Law.

In law school, David was a member of the Moot Court team, where he drafted and argued appellate issues. He also participated in the Criminal Law Society and the Criminal Defense Practicum, working with the Western Circuit Public Defender’s Office in Clarke and Oconee County Superior Courts for three semesters.

David gained additional experience during his summers as a judicial intern with the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Georgia and as a law clerk with Wiggins Casto Barrow, PC. In these roles, he conducted legal research, drafted opinions, prepared trial materials, and assisted in courtroom proceedings. Before law school, David worked with Kimbrough Law in Athens, Georgia, where he drafted wills, powers of attorney, advance directives, and other estate planning documents.

Beyond his legal work, David has served his community through the Athens YMCA as a basketball coach and after-school counselor. He is married to his wife, Andrea, and they are active members of Athens Church.

attorneys.name: James K. Hasson Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Tax Matters for Tax Exempt Orgs. Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Federal tax law is a major regulatory mechanism for hospitals, universities, foundations, medical research institutes, trade associations and other tax-exempt organizations and the individuals and businesses that support them. Jim Hasson advises clients and defends them in matters addressed by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and other governmental agencies such as the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services and state attorneys general.

Jim guides clients in designing the optimal structure for a new or reorganized organization, planning for the organization's financial support and programmatic operations, and negotiating contracts, licenses and financing arrangements for their projects. With more than four decades of experience, Jim has deep knowledge of the legislative process and he works to craft legislative or regulatory provisions for the benefit of tax-exempt organizations. Jim also counsels clients in the operation and financing of closely-held businesses, especially those owned by supporters of charitable organizations, and in the estate planning alternatives for philanthropists.

A recognized authority in tax and non-profit law, Jim frequently speaks at conferences around the country and has published numerous articles. From 1987 to 1990, he served as a member of the Exempt Organization Advisory Group to the Commissioner of the IRS, and he served nearly 20 years as an adjunct professor of law in the graduate tax program at Emory University School of Law.

attorneys.name: Stephen R. Hasner
attorneys.firm_name: Hasner Law Injury & Workers’ Compensation Attorneys
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Stephen Hasner’s life is built on two pillars: family and faith. These core values drive his personal life and his law practice, shaping every aspect of his journey.

Since earning his J.D. in 1997, he has dedicated his legal career to workers’ compensation and personal injury cases. Initially focused on the defense side, he quickly recognized the importance of advocating for the rights of those facing life’s challenges through personal and workplace injuries. Hasner sought to provide legal representation for these individuals, giving them a voice to be heard and securing victories to ensure they receive both financial and medical assistance.

What truly sets Hasner apart is his holistic approach to client care. The invaluable insights gleaned from his early experience defending insurance companies now empower Hasner to navigate his clients’ cases with strategic precision. The firm operates in comprehensive systems and processes that assist clients from their very first phone call to the successful resolution of their cases. With a dedicated team of top-notch personal injury attorneys, paralegals, and intake specialists, Hasner ensures that each client receives personalized attention and unwavering support.

Stephen Hasner not only leads his staff to care for every person coming to Hasner Law Injury & Workers’ Compensation Attorneys for legal help, but he models it in his personal life as an active leader outside the courtroom in local and global non-profit organizations. He is a co-founder of a ministry in Nicaragua (rayodesol.org) that educates, feeds, and supports the children and their families in need. Closer to home, he actively leads in professional organizations that advocates for the rights of injured workers. He volunteers with his family in local ministry work and community programs.

In every endeavor, whether in the courtroom or the community, Stephen Hasner remains steadfast in his commitment to serving others with integrity, compassion, and unwavering dedication. His is a legacy defined not merely by legal victories but by the lives he touches and the hope he inspires.

Associations and Committees

He is also active in various professional organizations. He co-founded the Georgia Injured Workers’ Advocates (GIWA) and is a current member of the executive committee and serves as treasurer of that group. He is the board chairman of the Workplace Injury Network Political Action Committee (WIN-PAC) and has served as a member of the board of directors of the Workers’ Compensation Claimant Lawyers, a division of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association. He also served as co-chair of the Workers’ Compensation Law Institute, which is a yearly seminar for lawyers and judges throughout Georgia.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Andrea Dyer Hastings is the Founding and Managing Partner of Hastings Shadmehry Family Law, having formed the firm in 2023. Previously, she was a Managing Partner of Waggoner Hastings, which she co-founded in 2009. Andee began her Family Law career in 2004 at Warner Mayoue Bates and Nolan, where she became a partner of noted family lawyer John Mayoue.

Andee was born in Richmond, VA. She is the daughter of a U.S Navy Captain and a teacher, and her family lived in Virginia Beach, VA, Herndon, VA, and eventually the Marietta, GA area, where Andee graduated from North Cobb High School. Andee earned her B.A. in Russian at The University of North Carolina Chapel Hill, where she graduated With Highest Distinction and was named Phi Beta Kappa; and she earned her Juris Doctorate at The University of Georgia School of Law, where she graduated at the top of her class in 1997.

After law school, Andee became an Assistant District Attorney in Rockdale County, GA, where she became a Family Violence Prosecutor. After this, she moved into Civil Litigation, and then to Family Law. Andee has successfully argued in front of the Georgia Supreme Court, and the Georgia Court of Appeals, where she made case law in the state in her first year as an attorney.

Andee is a fierce advocate for her clients, with whom she is empathetic, warm, and steady. She manages their cases with cunning, sophistication, and precision. She is also extremely proud of the firm she has co-founded and takes pride in helping to develop lawyers and paralegals into first rate legal professionals.

Andee is married and is a loving "mom" to seven rescue dogs. When not working she enjoys home life and taking refuge in the North Georgia mountains.

attorneys.name: Thomas E. Hatfield
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury & Automobile Wrecks Lawyers in Waycross, GA
attorneys.bio:
The Honorable Thomas E. "Tommy" Hatfield is a native of Waycross and Ware County. After graduating from Waycross High School in 1990, he attended the University of Georgia in Athens as an undergraduate, initially on scholarship to the UGA School of Music, where he spent two years as a music education major, before changing direction and earning a Bachelor of Science in Biology from UGA's Franklin College of Arts and Sciences in 1994. While at UGA, Tommy was inducted as a member of Alpha Epsilon Delta (Georgia Alpha Chapter - Premedical Honor Society), and he served a term as President of the UGA Tau Delta Chapter of Beta Beta Beta Biological Honor Society. Tommy was also a proud member of the University of Georgia Redcoat Marching and Symphonic Bands (alto saxophone) during his tenure in Athens, and it was through his participation in the Redcoat Band that Tommy was introduced to his college sweetheart and eventual wife, Deanna (Black) Hatfield of Gainesville, Georgia.

Tommy's education and career goals took another significant shift after his college graduation when he decided to attend law school at The University of Tulsa School of Law in Tulsa, Oklahoma. While in Tulsa, Tommy became interested in becoming a trial attorney and earned a spot as a 1L student on TU's Association of Trial Lawyers of America (ATLA) Mock Trial Team. He was also inducted as a member of Phi Delta Phi Legal Fraternity, Rogers Inn. He earned his Juris Doctor from Tulsa in 1997 before returning home to become a member of the State Bar of Georgia and enter the practice of law with his brother, Mark.

During the first twenty-three years of his legal practice, Tommy concentrated in the areas of Plaintiff's personal injury, criminal defense, and divorce and domestic relations law. He has been a tenacious litigator and proven himself willing to fight the long, hard fights which are often necessary to prevail in the trial arena. He is licensed to practice in all trial courts in Georgia, the Georgia Court of Appeals, and the Georgia Supreme Court. He is also experienced in the handling of civil and criminal matters in federal court, and he is a member of the Bars of the United States District Courts for the Southern and Northern Districts of Georgia.

In 2020, Tommy offered himself as a candidate to become Judge of the State Court of Ware County. With much gratitude to the voters of his native Ware County, Tommy won a convincing election, and on December 30, 2020, Tommy was sworn in as the first newly elected State Court Judge in Ware County in 25 years. His first term of office began on January 1, 2021. The State Court of Ware County has general trial jurisdiction over civil matters (except for those specifically reserved by law to the Superior Court) and misdemeanor criminal cases. However, because the Ware County State Court Judge's position is a part-time judgeship, Tommy is happy to be able to continue his private practice of law and his representation of clients with Hatfield & Hatfield, P.C. Tommy and Deanna have two daughters, Kate and Charlotte. The family are members of First Presbyterian Church of Waycross, where Tommy serves as an Elder. Tommy remains an avid musician and enjoys finding musical projects in Waycross in his spare time. He also enjoys golf and RV camping.

He is licensed to practice in all trial courts in Georgia, the Georgia Court of Appeals, and the Georgia Supreme Court. He is also experienced in the handling of civil and criminal matters in federal court, and he is a member of the Bars of the United States District Courts for the Southern and Northern Districts of Georgia.

In 2020, Tommy offered himself as a candidate to become Judge of the State Court of Ware County. With much gratitude to the voters of his native Ware County, Tommy won a convincing election, and on December 30, 2020, Tommy was sworn in as the first newly elected State Court Judge in Ware County in 25 years. His first term of office began on January 1, 2021. The State Court of Ware County has general trial jurisdiction over civil matters (except for those specifically reserved by law to the Superior Court) and misdemeanor criminal cases. However, because the Ware County State Court Judge's position is a part-time judgeship, Tommy is happy to be able to continue his private practice of law and his representation of clients with Hatfield & Hatfield, P.C. Tommy and Deanna have two daughters, Kate and Charlotte. The family are members of First Presbyterian Church of Waycross, where Tommy serves as an Elder. Tommy remains an avid musician and enjoys finding musical projects in Waycross in his spare time. He also enjoys golf and RV camping.

attorneys.name: J. Mark Hatfield
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury & Automobile Wrecks Lawyers in Waycross, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mark Hatfield was born and raised in Waycross, Georgia. He was educated in the Waycross City Schools and graduated from Waycross High School as Valedictorian of the Class of 1987. Mark graduated from the University of Georgia in 1990 as a First Honor Graduate with an A.B. degree in Political Science, Summa Cum Laude, with Highest Honors. He subsequently earned his Juris Doctor, Cum Laude, from the University of Georgia School of Law in 1993.

During Mark's undergraduate career at UGA, he was elected to Phi Beta Kappa; was a member of the UGA Honors Program; served as President of the UGA Zodiac Honor Society; and was a recipient of the UGA President's Award in 1990. In law school at Georgia, Mark was a member of the Joseph Henry Lumpkin American Inn of Court; won the 1992 Intraschool Third Year Mock Trial Competition; won the 1992 Verner F. Chaffin Award for Excellence in Fiduciary Law; and served as a Graduate Senator to the UGA Student Government Association from 1990-1992.

A former Georgia All-State alto saxophonist in 1987, Mark was also a member of the University of Georgia Redcoat Marching, Concert, and Symphonic Bands during his years at UGA. Mark was admitted to the State Bar of Georgia in 1993, and he prosecuted criminal cases as an Assistant District Attorney for the Western Judicial Circuit based in Athens, Georgia from 1993- 1994. He then returned home to Waycross and joined the private law practice of distinguished trial attorney Leon A. Wilson II, with whom he later formed a partnership known as The Wilson Law Firm.

Mark and his brother, Tommy, began practicing law together in Waycross in 1997, focusing on serious personal injury and wrongful death claims; workers’ compensation claims; criminal defense; divorce, custody, and related domestic relations cases; Wills and administration of estates; and general litigation matters.

In 2005, Mark was elected to the Georgia House of Representatives as State Representative for House District 177, representing Ware and Charlton Counties. He served four (4) terms in the House, until 2013, during which period he served at various times as Vice-Chairman of the Judiciary (Civil) Committee; Vice-Chairman of the Judiciary (Non-Civil) Committee; Secretary of the Governmental Affairs Committee; a member of the Transportation Committee; a member of the Higher Education Committee; and a member of the Appropriations Committee, on which he served on the Higher Education Subcommittee. Mark also served as Chairman of the General Oversight Committee for the Georgia Public Defender Standards Council.

A former President of the Waycross Bar Association and a former Chairman of the Ware County Republican Party, Mark has also been actively involved in the community, serving his neighbors in several different capacities. He is a former member of the Waycross Jaycees; a former member of the Board of Directors of the Southeast Georgia Chapter of the American Red Cross; a former member and officer of the Waycross Elks Lodge # 369; and the former Vice-President of the Ware County Band Boosters Club, Inc. He currently plays saxophone with the "Big Sound of the Okefenoke" community jazz band in Waycross.

Mark and his wife, Lee, married in 1995. They have two children, John Mark II, who is a law student at the University of Georgia School of Law, and Annabeth, an undergraduate at the University of Georgia. The family are members of the First United Methodist Church, Waycross, where Mark and Lee have served on the church’s Administrative Council and in various other positions of church leadership over the years.

University of Georgia President's Award, 1990

attorneys.name: David V. Hayes
attorneys.firm_name: Owen Gleaton Egan Jones & Sweeney, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Business Counseling & Litigation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
David V. Hayes is an associate practicing in the firm's medical malpractice, products liability, governmental liability and corporate law practice groups. David also maintains a governmental relations practice at the state and local levels. From Birmingham, Alabama, David received his B.A. in Political Science from Samford University. Upon graduation David worked in the Washington D.C. offices of Congressmen Spencer Bachus and Mike Rogers before accepting a position in the Legislative Affairs Division of the National Rifle Association. David returned to Birmingham and attended the Cumberland School of Law where he was an Associate Editor on the American Journal of Trial Advocacy, a member of the Cumberland Trial Advocacy Board and a member of the Cumberland National Negotiation Team. His student note, "Browning v. U.S.: Is A Court's Refusal To Give A Jury Instruction Regarding Pretext In An Employment Discrimination Case Reversible Error?" was published in the Spring 2009 issue of the American Journal of Trial Advocacy.

After graduating law school, David accepted the Sir Edward Coke Scholarship to study for an LL.M. in International Business and Commercial Law at the University of East Anglia in Norwich, England. After spending a year in England and receiving his LL.M., David and his wife moved to his wife's hometown of Atlanta.

David is admitted to practice law in Georgia and Alabama and is involved in the American Bar Association, the Georgia Bar Association and the Atlanta Bar Association. In 2013, he was elected to serve as Member-at-Large on the Executive Council of the Young Lawyer's Division of the Georgia Bar Association. Additionally, David was appointed by the American Bar Association to serve as an Associate Judge on the Awards and Subgrants Team of the Young Lawyer's Division.

David spends his free time cheering for the Alabama Crimson Tide, being involved in the Atlanta Alumni Chapter of Sigma Chi, spending time outdoors and traveling. He and his wife, Elizabeth, reside in Buckhead.

attorneys.name: Jordan J. Hendrick Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Jordan J. Hendrick devotes 100 percent of his practice to family law and is committed to working with his clients to find sensible, efficient and favorable solutions to personal and often complex domestic cases.

Jordan is a proficient litigator who has successfully tried divorce and child custody cases before numerous judges across metropolitan Atlanta and argued before the Supreme Court of Georgia. Through this experience Jordan has earned the respect of his clients and peers, and has been recognized repeatedly as a Rising Star and a Super Lawyer by Super Lawyers Magazine and named to Georgia Trend's Legal Elite in 2014 and 2018. Jordan also holds a 10 out of 10 rating on avvo.com.

Jordan grew up in east Cobb County and became a partner in a multi-practice firm in Atlanta in 2011. He left that Atlanta firm amicably in 2019 to help create the family law firm of Abernathy Ditzel Hendrick Bryce near the historic Marietta Square. However, Jordan still maintains an active presence in Fulton County and is a member of the Family Law Section of the Atlanta Bar and the Lawyers Club of Atlanta. Further, Jordan finds time to provide community service by volunteering with the Cobb Justice Foundation, providing free representation to victims of domestic violence.

Jordan lives in East Cobb with his wife Cynthia, daughter Ashley and son Evan.

You can email Jordan directly at jordan@adhfamilymatters.com

attorneys.name: Robert L. Hendrix III
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Columbus, GA
attorneys.bio:
Robert L. Hendrix, III (Rob), is an accomplished trial lawyer that has recovered over $35,000,000.00 in benefits for his clients in over sixteen years of practice. His practice focuses exclusively on representing injured individuals in Georgia workers' compensation claims. He has tried over one hundred cases in every corner of the State in front of nearly every Administrative Law Judge.

In addition to Mr. Hendix's trial accomplishments, he is also an experienced appellate advocate. Mr. Hendrix has handled numerous matters through the appellate process, including the Georgia Court of Appeals and Georgia Supreme Court. Notably, he received a favorable decision in Dekalb County Board of Education v. Singleon, 294 Ga. App. 96; 668 S.E. 2d 767 (2008), which was landmark in that the decision allowed for an injured employee to receive income benefits for a psychic only injury after the physical injury resolved.

Mr. Hendrix has been recognized frequently for his skill as an attorney. He holds an AV rating from Martindale reflecting the highest level of professional skill and ethical standards. For four straight years (2010 - 2013) he was named a Georgia Rising Star SuperLawyer, which is published by Atlanta Magazine in conjunction with Law & Politics Magazine. This is an honor recognizing the top 2.5% of attorneys in their practice area under the age of forty. In 2014, Mr. Hendrix was named a Georgia SuperLawyer recognizing the top 5% of all attorneys in their practice area, making him the youngest to receive this honor. He has continued to receive this honor from 2015-2020. Additionally, Mr. Hendrix was named a Top 100 by The National Trial Lawyers. Further, he has also been named a Top 40 Under 40 by the American Society of Legal Advocates for 2013 & 2014. Mr. Hendrix has also been named one of the Best Attorneys in America by Rue Ratings, recognizing less than 1% of attorneys nationwide. He has been honored as a Premier 100 by the American Academy of Trial Lawyers, and a Top Lawyer by the Global Directory of Who's Who.

Mr. Hendrix takes his obligations to leadership seriously and is active in the legal community at the National, State and local levels. He served as Chair of the Workplace Injury Section of the American Association for Justice. Additionally, Mr. Hendrix serves on the Executive Board as President Elect of the Workers' Compensation Claimant's Lawyers (WCCL) arm of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association. Previously, he served on the Amicus Curiae Committee of the Georgia Legal Foundation aimed at addressing appellate issues in workers' compensation. Finally, he is a Member of the American Bar Association, Workers' Injury Law Group (WILG), State Bar of Georgia and Columbus Bar Association.

Mr. Hendrix has served as a frequent lecturer on workers' compensation issues at the National, State and local levels. He has given presentations at nearly every major legal conference involving workers' compensation law; including: The American Bar Association, American Association for Justice, State Bar of Georgia, The annual ICLE seminar at St. Simon's Island, GTLA Annual Convention, State Board of Worker's Compensation Annual Convention, WCCL Annual Seminar. Atlanta Bar Association, Gwinnett Chamber of Commerce and Travelers Employer School. He has spoken across the country in San Francisco, New Orleans, Chicago, Miami, Phoenix, Denver and in Nashville. Mr. Hendrix has lectured on such topics turning around the tough case, affirmative defenses, taking depositions, civil discovery, common mistakes made by employers, independent medical examinations, developing medical evidence, preexisting conditions, psychological injuries, federalization of workers' compensation, case intake, light duty job offers, the interplay between workers' compensation and Federal employment law and the use of medical marijuana in workers' compensation claims. Moreover, he has authored journal articles for State Bar of Georgia and American Association for Justice.

Mr. Hendrix also lectures on legal issues outside of bar related events. More specifically, he was featured on the radio as an invited speaker on Atlanta Legal Experts. Further, he has been an invited guest lecturer to the legal studies and paralegal programs at Clayton State University and Georgia State University.

Personally, Mr. Hendrix enjoys spending time with his his three children (Sammy, Harrison & Max). This keeps him busy, especially coaching soccer, football and basketball when not shuttling the kids to tennis, reading bowl, robotics competitions, guitar and drum lessons, plays and running competitions. When not busy with the kids, he is passionate about following his beloved Georgia Bulldogs and traveling (especially to Las Vegas).

attorneys.name: Paul Henefeld
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Paul Henefeld graduated from Emory University School of Law in 2001 and joined the Firm in 2002. Paul has handled and tried hundreds of personal injury cases for a variety of insurance companies, other entities, and individuals. attorneys.bio:
Brittany Hepner practices in the litigation section of The Minor Firm. Her practice areas include medical malpractice defense, insurance defense, general civil litigation, and business litigation. Her clients include physicians, advanced practice providers, medical practices, hospitals and long-term care facilities, commercial vehicle insurers, and a national casualty insurance carrier. Ms. Hepner’s health care law experience includes litigation, risk management, medical staff matters, and representation of providers in matters involving the Georgia Composite Medical Board and Georgia Board of Nursing. Her insurance defense experience includes cases with allegations of general negligence, premises liability, dog-bite, and nuisance.

Ms. Hepner is a native of Northwest Georgia. She attended Mercer University where she graduated summa cum laude from Mercer’s College of Liberal Arts in 2012. Ms. Hepner attended Mercer University’s Walter F. After graduation, Ms. Hepner retuned to the Northwest Georgia area where she clerked for the Honorable M. Cindy Morris of the Conasauga Judicial Circuit. Ms. Hepner joined The Minor Firm in 2016. She is a 2017 graduate of Emerging Leaders Institute and is a 2018 graduate of Leadership Dalton. She is a member of the State Bar of Georgia and the Conasauga Bar Association. Ms. Hepner enjoys spending her free time with her husband and three children.

attorneys.name: Thomas W. Herman
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Herman has over 27 years of experience representing the injured and disabled, with an emphasis on handling workers' compensation claims. He is recognized around the state as a leader in advocating for injured workers' to insure that their rights are protected and that they receive all the benefits that the law provides. He has developed an expertise in high value catastrophic injury claims under the Georgia Workers' Compensation Act.

Mr. Herman has extensive experience at all levels of litigation, both in personal injury cases and workers' compensation claims, having tried a significant number of cases around the State, and made numerous appearances before both the Georgia Court of Appeals and the Georgia Supreme Court. He has obtained a number of significant appellate decisions in the field of workers' compensation favorable to injured workers including: Davis v. Carter Mechanical, Inc; Rite-Aid Corp. v. Davis; Keystone Automotive v. Hall and Imerys Kaolin v. Blackshear. Other significant appellate decisions he has obtained in other fields include Warehouse Home Furnishings v. Davenport; Progressive Cas. Ins. Co. v. Bryant; and, Ngyuen v. State.

In 2014 Mr. Herman was selected as a Fellow in The College of Worker's Compensation Lawyers. Mr. Herman is the only attorney in the Middle Georgia area and only the 18th statewide to have been selected for induction in the College. He has been selected as one of Georgia's "Super Lawyers" for the years 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013 and 2015. Mr. Herman is active in the Macon Bar Association, having served on the Executive Committee from 2002 – 2009, including serving as President in 2005-2006. He is also active at the State Bar level, serving as a District Representative of the Younger Lawyer Section of the State Bar from 1992 – 1996 and as a Director of that Section in 1995 – 1996. He has served as a member of the State Bar’s Board of Governors since June, 2004. He previously served on the Executive Committee of the Workers' Compensation Section of the State Bar from 1999 – 2004, including a year as Chair from 2002 - 2003. He is a member of GTLA and has served on the Executive Committee of the Workers' Compensation Claimant's Lawyers Section since 1999. He has been a member of the Georgia Legal Foundation since 2007.

attorneys.practice_type: Private Adoption Lawyers in Lawrenceville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Sherriann H. Hicks focuses her legal career on adoption, assisted reproduction and surrogacy. Since 1995, she has been working to place children in loving adoptive families. She views adoption as a gift for all parties involved: giving children an opportunity to grow in a healthy environment, adoptive parents a chance to raise children and birth mothers peace of mind. Locally and nationally known for her experience in adoption and surrogacy related matters, she can help you. Sherriann is a member of the Academy of Adoption Attorneys. She is a member of the Gwinnett County Bar Association and is a former President of the Gwinnett County Bar Association. She is also former President of the Georgia Council of Adoption Lawyers.Sherriann received her Juris Doctor in 1995 from the University of Memphis School of Law. While at the University of Memphis Sherriann was a member of the Moot Court Board and Student Government Association. Before law school, she attended Greater Atlanta Christian School in Norcross, Georgia and received her Bachelor of Arts in Speech and Political Science in 1992 from David Lipscomb University in Nashville. Sherriann was admitted to the practice of law in the state of Georgia in 1995, and is licensed to practice before the Georgia Supreme Court, the Georgia Court of Appeals and the United States District Court for the Northern District of Georgia. She is also a member of the Academy of Adoption Attorneys and the Family Law Section of the State Bar of Georgia.

Sherriann has served as an attorney coach to the Greater Atlanta Christian School Mock Trial Team and as an evaluator for the Mock Trial Competition. Sherriann lives with her family in Suwanee.

attorneys.name: John Cleveland Hill Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Wills, Trusts & Charitable Planning Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Inspired by Family. Dedicated to Yours.

For John Cleveland (“Cleve”) Hill, estate planning is more than a profession—it’s a calling shaped by personal experience. When Cleve was a small child, his paternal grandfather, a successful inventor and entrepreneur, passed away unexpectedly—thankfully, leaving behind a solid estate plan. In the years that followed, Cleve watched his father carefully administer his grandfather’s estate and trust as it provided for his beloved grandmother for the final 31 years of her life. The impact of his grandfather’s thorough planning was evident, providing stability and support following a sudden loss.

That early experience left a lasting impression. Cleve was fascinated by the process and saw firsthand how good planning could protect loved ones and create peace of mind for a family. It was this inspiration that set him on the path to becoming one of Georgia’s most trusted estate planning and probate attorneys.

Today, Cleve brings that same sense of care and dedication to every client he serves. Recognized by peers as a leader in his field, Cleve is honored to help families secure their legacies and provide for the people they love most.

Cleve is frequently invited to share his knowledge at seminars throughout metro Atlanta, making complex topics like wills, trusts, and asset protection accessible and understandable.

Cleve’s excellence has been celebrated by his legal peers and the community:

Georgia Trend Magazine’s “Legal Elite” in Wills/Estates/Taxes

Super Lawyers “Rising Star” (2017, 2018) and Super Lawyers honoree (2023)—an honor reserved for the top 5% of attorneys statewide

Cherokee County Chamber of Commerce “10 in 10 Young Professionals to Watch” (2013)

Cleve’s journey began at one of Atlanta’s most prestigious law firms, Powell Goldstein Frazer & Murphy (now international law firm Bryan Cave) where he honed his skills in financial restructuring. But it was his desire to make a meaningful difference in people’s lives that led him to join attorney Phill Bettis in 2007 to focus exclusively on estate planning, probate, guardianships, wealth preservation, asset protection, and special needs planning. Today, as a founding partner of Georgia Legacy Law Group, LLC (previously Bettis, Hill & Vann, LLC and Hill & Watchko, LLC), Cleve leads a boutique practice devoted to helping clients secure their legacies and provide for their loved ones.

A sixth-generation Cherokee County native, Cleve’s roots run deep in the community he serves. He is a 1997 graduate of Sequoyah High School (along with his law firm colleague, attorney Laura Barron). He graduated magna cum laude from Atlanta’s Oglethorpe University in 2001, having served two terms as student body president, and where he was awarded the university’s highest student honor, the James Edward Oglethorpe Award, presented annually to the top two seniors in the graduating class, was the inaugural recipient of the President’s Community Service Award, and earned the Charles Longstreet Weltner Award presented by the Stormy Petrel Bar Association.

Cleve earned his law degree cum laude from Mercer University’s Walter F. George School of law in 2004, ranking in the top 10% of his class, and served on the Editorial Board of the Mercer Law Review.

Cleve’s dedication extends far beyond the office. He has served for over a decade on the Oglethorpe University Board of Trustees, led major campus initiatives, and presided over the Alumni Association as its president for two years. He served for over 9 years on the Forsyth County Tripartite Committee, overseeing the County’s indigent legal defense services. For almost 20 years, Cleve has served on the board of Act Together Ministries serving foster children in metropolitan Atlanta. In 2025, Cleve joined the Board of Directors of Plan of Georgia, Inc., a non-profit assisting families with loved ones who are 18 years of age and older with severe and persistent mental illness, those with intellectual disabilities, and the at-risk elderly.

Cleve is especially proud of his pro bono work, providing estate plans for first responders and rural families who need it most. He and his family are active members of their Cherokee County church, and he is always looking for ways to give back to the community that shaped him.

But it was his desire to make a meaningful difference in people’s lives that led him to join attorney Phill Bettis in 2007 to focus exclusively on estate planning, probate, guardianships, wealth preservation, asset protection, and special needs planning. Today, as a founding partner of Georgia Legacy Law Group, LLC (previously Bettis, Hill & Vann, LLC and Hill & Watchko, LLC), Cleve leads a boutique practice devoted to helping clients secure their legacies and provide for their loved ones.

A sixth-generation Cherokee County native, Cleve’s roots run deep in the community he serves. He is a 1997 graduate of Sequoyah High School (along with his law firm colleague, attorney Laura Barron). He graduated magna cum laude from Atlanta’s Oglethorpe University in 2001, having served two terms as student body president, and where he was awarded the university’s highest student honor, the James Edward Oglethorpe Award, presented annually to the top two seniors in the graduating class, was the inaugural recipient of the President’s Community Service Award, and earned the Charles Longstreet Weltner Award presented by the Stormy Petrel Bar Association.

Cleve earned his law degree cum laude from Mercer University’s Walter F. George School of law in 2004, ranking in the top 10% of his class, and served on the Editorial Board of the Mercer Law Review.

Cleve’s dedication extends far beyond the office. He has served for over a decade on the Oglethorpe University Board of Trustees, led major campus initiatives, and presided over the Alumni Association as its president for two years. He served for over 9 years on the Forsyth County Tripartite Committee, overseeing the County’s indigent legal defense services. For almost 20 years, Cleve has served on the board of Act Together Ministries serving foster children in metropolitan Atlanta. In 2025, Cleve joined the Board of Directors of Plan of Georgia, Inc., a non-profit assisting families with loved ones who are 18 years of age and older with severe and persistent mental illness, those with intellectual disabilities, and the at-risk elderly.

Cleve is especially proud of his pro bono work, providing estate plans for first responders and rural families who need it most. He and his family are active members of their Cherokee County church, and he is always looking for ways to give back to the community that shaped him.

Mr. Hill is first and foremost a trial attorney that limits his practice to divorce and other domestic relations cases. Mr. Hill holds a peer review rating of AV-Preeminent from Martindale-Hubbell and an AVVO rating of 10/10 – Superb. While Mr. Hill plans a strategy for each case individually, his basic approach is to prepare for war and use the power that provides to settle the case wherever possible. If settlement becomes impossible, Mr. Hill has ample experience in both bench trials and jury trials. He also has experience in appealing divorce cases to the Supreme Court.

Mr. Hill brings a strong background in business, accounting and cost analysis (both educational and practical experience) to the practice of domestic relations law. His business skills combine effectively to allow him to achieve excellent results in cases involving high asset and complex marital estates especially those that include on-going businesses.

Mr. Hill has published papers in technical trial techniques and areas of applicability to the family law practitioner. He is a Guardian Ad Litem for the Superior Court of Cobb County and he is a Registered Neutral with the Georgia Office of Dispute Resolution.

Mr. Hill is a member of the State Bar of Georgia; the Family Law Section of the State Bar of Georgia; the Cobb County Bar Association; the Family Law Section of the Cobb County Bar Association; and Phi Delta Phi. Mr. Hill is also a member of First United Methodist Church of Marietta, the Marietta Kiwanis, and the Kennesaw Business Association.

Georgia Court Grapples with Generative A.I.

Shahid v. Esaam

In June 2025, the Georgia Court of Appeals published its opinion in the Shahid v. Esaam case – one of the appellate cases where I represented the appellant. This case turned out to be an important case in Georgia jurisprudence as well as garnering national attention. It addressed the dangers of generative artificial intelligence (A.I.) in legal practice.

My client was the wife in a divorce action who did not get proper service of the petition for divorce against her. Her husband claimed ignorance of her whereabouts and convinced the trial court to allow him to serve her by publication. For those unfamiliar with this process, service by publication involves running a legal ad in the newspaper for four consecutive weeks advising a party that there is a case pending against them. After that four weeks, everyone proceeds as if the party had actually be served and had actual notice of the case pending between them.

Because the case proceeded to trial without my client’s knowledge, the result she received was very poor. She was not there to represent herself.

When she Shahid learned that she was divorced, she hired an attorney and brought a motion to set aside the decree of divorce because her constitutional right to notice had been denied. The trial court denied her motion and, in support of that denial, cited two cases of purported Georgia law. The problem was that neither of those cases existed. The trial court relied upon nonexistent law in making its judgment.

I represented Ms. Shahid in appealing the trial court’s decision to deny her motion to set aside the decree. I filed our brief in support of her appeal, and the same attorney who represented her husband in the trial court filed an opposing brief in the Georgia Court of Appeals. That brief was also filled with citations to fictitious law.

Ms. Shahid prevailed in her appeal and the Georgia Court of Appeals sent the matter back to the trial court. I did not ask the Court to impose frivolous appeal sanctions against the Appellee or his attorney, but the Court imposed sanctions on its own motion. The Court made it clear in its opinion that reliance upon generative A.I., while a convenience for attorneys, imposes upon an attorney the duty to ensure that the materials created by A.I. are legitimate and what they profess to be.

Ron has been lead counsel in trials and appeared in the Georgia Supreme Court, Georgia Court of Appeals, United States Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit, United States District Courts for both the Northern and Middle Districts of Georgia.

attorneys.name: Sadarie Hines
attorneys.practice_type: Federal Employment Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
An Associate at Southworth PC, where her practice focuses on Federal Employment Law, a field in which she represents clients before pivotal institutions such as the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the Merit Systems Protection Board, and Federal Court. Her international background, hailing from the United Kingdom with a vibrant legal career that spans across both the UK and the United States, equips her with a distinct perspective and creative approach to law. Sadarie is a New York licensed attorney, renowned for her eloquence, strategic thinking, and drive to help ensure professional legal outcomes for her clients.

Sadarie embarked on her legal journey inspired by a childhood vision, nurtured by her late father through a simple yet impactful gift—a book portraying a young girl as a lawyer. This image resonated with her, guiding her towards a fulfilling career in law, where she has been able to leverage her voice for those who cannot. Graduating with honors in Law with Social Sciences, and further enriching her knowledge with a postgraduate research diploma in Women and the Law from the London Metropolitan University School of Law, Sadarie has always been driven by a passion for public law and service.

Before joining Southworth PC, Sadarie's career was marked by significant roles, including serving as an In-house locum lawyer for UK Local Authorities and working under a Georgia Special Assistant Attorney General. She has also dedicated herself to pro bono work, notably assisting underserved communities with housing and landlord issues through the Atlanta Volunteer Lawyers Foundation.

Sadarie values the "one team" ethic at Southworth PC, crediting it with her professional growth, especially through opportunities to draft briefs for complex cases requiring innovative solutions.

attorneys.name: Thomas H. Hinson
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Thomas H. Hinson is recognized for his ability to promptly and successfully resolve serious injury and death claims for his clients. Mr. Hinson devotes 100% of his practice to the litigation and/or settlement of catastrophic injury and wrongful death cases. He began his career as a felony prosecutor but for the last 30 years he has used that trial experience to achieve legal victories in civil damage suits for victims of medical malpractice, defective products, and serious auto/truck accidents. Hinson has spent the vast majority of his professional life helping individuals and families who have suffered human losses caused by the negligence of others. With years of experience, he has helped families deal with the myriad of problems associated with serious injuries or the sudden loss of the family bread-winner.

He has been the senior attorney in charge of the trial practice section of his firm for the last 25 years and has a staff which includes a full time physician, a case manager, and several experienced legal assistants. Clients are given immediate and courteous responses to all inquiries.

Mr. Hinson has been called upon on many occasions to speak at legal seminars and to instruct in classes for attorneys who want to become proficient in jury trial techniques. He believes that aggressive and professional representation is the key to a successful law practice. Some of his recent cases have resulted in multi-million dollar recoveries. See "Cases" shown on the tab at our Home page.

Over the last 25 years Mr. Hinson has represented hundreds of individuals and families who have been severely injured or killed through the negligent act of others. His many years of experience in the courtroom, use of the best possible experts, and thorough preparation have given his clients the ability to obtain substantial recoveries in complex malpractice cases and in cases involving catastrophic injuries and death.

Mr. Hinson has been selected as one of Georgia's Super Lawyers by Atlanta magazine in 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2017.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Matt Hirsch has been practicing law in Georgia for about 25 years. He understands what a frightening place the courts can be for those who have never experienced them, and even for those who unfortunately have.

Matt Graduated from the University of Georgia with a BA in Criminal Justice. From there he received his law degree from John Marshall Law School. He was born and raised in Columbus, Georgia, and even practiced law there before moving back to Atlanta in 2006.

Matt has dedicated his career to guiding and defending adults and children accused of criminal offenses through the criminal justice process. He has represented hundreds of people on a wide array of felony, misdemeanor, and traffic related crimes in Superior Court, State Court, Juvenile Court, and Municipal Traffic Courts all over the Metro-Atlanta area and the State of Georgia.

Matt is most proud of the friendships and relationships he's cultivated with prosecutors, law enforcement agents, and other lawyers practicing in a wide variety of other practice areas.

attorneys.bio:
Ms. Hise takes pride in being your “Bulldog in the Courtroom,” displaying the work ethic and drive necessary in obtaining million dollar verdicts for her clients. attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning & Legacy Protection Lawyers in Cumming, GA
attorneys.bio:
Advising on Asset Protection, Estate Planning, and Complex Disputes for 30+ Years.

Russell Hodges has devoted more than three decades to advising individuals, families, and businesses on how to protect what matters most: their assets, their families, and their long-term interests.

His practice combines estate planning, asset protection, and extensive litigation experience, allowing him to advise clients not only on how to structure and preserve wealth, but also how to respond when those interests are challenged.

Mr. Hodges has successfully represented clients in a wide range of disputes, including:

will and trust litigation

fiduciary disputes and breach of trust claims

inheritance interference and asset recovery matters

personal injury and high-value civil litigation

He has recovered significant funds for clients and has been recognized among the top verdicts in Georgia, reflecting his ability to act decisively in complex, high-stakes situations.

In addition to litigation, Mr. Hodges advises clients on proactive strategies to:

protect assets from creditors and liability exposure

structure wealth in anticipation of life transitions, including divorce or business risk

minimize tax exposure and preserve generational wealth

plan for long-term care through Medicare and Medicaid strategies

His work frequently involves situations where legal, financial, and personal considerations intersect — including matters where disputes, public exposure, or reputational concerns may be present.

Mr. Hodges approaches these matters with a focus on clarity, discretion, and control, helping clients navigate both planning and conflict with a structured legal strategy.

As an honors graduate of Vanderbilt University, Vanderbilt University Law School, and a recipient of the AV Preeminent® rating, he is recognized by peers for the highest standards of legal ability and ethics.

Approach to Client Representation

Estate planning and asset protection require more than documents — they require sound legal judgment and careful execution.

Mr. Hodges works closely with clients to:

understand their financial and personal circumstances

identify risks and areas of exposure

develop structured legal strategies aligned with their goals

His approach is focused on helping clients make informed decisions that provide long-term stability, protection, and clarity.

attorneys.name: Andrew Wayne Holliday
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Andy Holliday graduated law school in 2002. During his career, Andy clerked for a federal United States Magistrate Judge, practiced law for and became a partner at a primarily insurance defense law firm, practiced as staff counsel for an insurance company, and has now opened his own law firm. During this time, Andy has worked in fields such as personal injury, medical malpractice, employment discrimination, corporate litigation, and several other areas of law. During that time, Andy practiced almost exclusively for defendants who were being defended by their insurance company.

Now Andy has opened his own practice and is representing those hurt in all types of personal injury cases. This includes automobile accidents, slip and falls, medical malpractice, etc. After more than a decade defending those who are claimed to have caused injury to another person, Andy is taking the opportunity to switch gears and represent individuals who have been hurt.

With his experience working for a judge, a law firm, and an insurance company, Andy is uniquely qualified to represent plaintiffs. Andy understands the judicial system and how defense lawyers and insurance companies do business. When you hire our firm, you get the personal attention of a lawyer.

Andy takes each case as an individual case, devotes the time and resources it deserves, and does not treat his cases as a "number." He would be honored to assist you through the litigation process and achieve the best results possible for you and your family.

attorneys.name: Larry Neal Hollington
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Law Lawyers in Augusta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Larry N. Hollington received his undergraduate degree at Troy State University and attended law school at Walter F. Georgia School of Law at Mercer University, where he graduated cum laude in 1982. He was admitted to the State Bar of Georgia, Court of Appeals of Georgia and Supreme Court of Georgia in 1982.

Larry began practicing law with Swift, Currie, McGhee & Hiers in Atlanta, Georgia, in 1982 as an associate, where he practiced until June, 1985. During his time with Swift, Currie, McGhee & Hiers, the majority of his practice was workers compensation defense work. In June, 1985, Larry left Swift, Currie, McGhee & Hiers and relocated to Augusta, Georgia, where he founded the law firm of Larry N. Hollington, P.C. Since that time, Larry has been focusing his practice in the workers compensation arena, representing injured workers. Since 1995, Larry has been honored by his peers by being nominated among the Best Lawyers in America, as well as the Top Super Lawyers in Georgia.

Larry has been an active member of the Workers Compensation Section of the State Bar of Georgia since 1982. From 1998 to 1999, he served as Chairman of the Workers Compensation Section of the State Bar of Georgia.

Larry is a member of the American Bar Association, American Trial Lawyers Association, State Bar of Georgia, Georgia Trial Lawyers Association and the Augusta Bar Association. He served as First Lieutenant in the United States Marine Corps from 1973 to 1977. Larry and his wife, Judy, have a daughter, Lauren, and a son, Neal. Larry is an active member of the First Baptist Church of Augusta, Georgia.

attorneys.name: Jennifer Hothem
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Gainesville, GA
attorneys.bio:
While studying History at the University of Georgia, Jennifer began her legal career at 18 as a paralegal where Jennifer’s passion for advocacy was born. During her second year of law school, Jennifer welcomed a baby boy, all the while juggling the demands of law school and two prestigious clerking positions. Jennifer served two terms for the Superior Court of Hall County, once before the Honorable Jason Deal and again before the Honorable David Burroughs. After graduating from John Marshall Law School in 2016, Jennifer started her own firm specializing in family and child advocacy. In just 4 years, Jennifer has spent thousands of hours advocating in the courtroom and has litigated hundreds of civil cases as lead counsel. In addition to this litigation, Jennifer has served as a court-appointed Guardian ad Litem for children throughout North Georgia, many of whom were victims of neglect and abuse. Through her role as a Guardian ad Litem, and a court-appointed juvenile advocate, Jennifer gives innocent children a voice and opportunity to be heard. Jennifer knows her way around a courtroom.

Outside of the courtroom, Jennifer serves on the board of We Care, a non-profit organization that aids children and their families that may not qualify for conventional public assistance. A native of Northern California, Jennifer’s family moved to Flowery Branch in 1996. She now resides in Gainesville, Georgia with her husband, also an attorney, and their three children. In her free time, Jennifer enjoys family activities on Lake Lanier and is an avid kickboxer.

It was through her role in child and family advocacy that Jennifer honed a deep passion for those who have suffered injury or wrongful death. Sharing this passion, Jennifer and Kristy partnered together in 2021 to form Davies Hothem Injury Law. Jennifer and Kristy have the skills, experience, and, most importantly, fierce passion to get you or your loved one justice after suffering an injury. If you or a loved one has suffered injury or wrongful death, call Jennifer or Kristy at Davies Hothem Injury Law today.

attorneys.name: Matthew J. Howard
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Matthew joined Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele in 1989 and currently serves as senior partner in the firm's Corporate, Tax and Estate Planning Department. Matthew specializes in Estate Planning and has served as an active member of the Estate and Gift Tax Committee of the American Bar Association Tax Section since 1996. In addition, he heads up the firm's Tax Litigation Department, handling disputes for individuals and corporations before the Internal Revenue Service, as well as litigating against the Commissioner of Internal Revenue Service in the United States Tax Court and the Department of Justice in United States District Court. Matthew stays involved in the firm's larger merger and acquisition transactions, providing valuable tax advice to either the purchaser or seller.

Beginning in 2006, Matthew formed the firm's Captive Insurance Company practice. As of 2012, MIJS Captive Management, LLC manages 56 small captive insurance companies domiciled in Kentucky, Delaware and Hawaii for privately held businesses throughout the United States.

Born in Columbus, Ohio, September 28, 1960, Matthew was admitted to the State Bar of Georgia in 1989 after receiving his Economics degree from Vanderbilt University in 1984, and his J.D. from Capital University Law School in Columbus, Ohio. Matthew transferred to Emory University Law School to complete his third year of law school and to obtain his Master's Degree (LL.M.) in Taxation in addition to his law degree.

Matthew and his wife, Suzanne, are members of Peachtree Presbyterian Church and involved with The Westminster Schools and Whitefield Academy, where their children attend. Matthew also serves as a Director of Atlanta Community Ministries (ACM) and is also a Board member of Feeding the Homeless Project, Inc. Mr. Howard was named one of Georgia's Top Rated Lawyers in 2012 by LexisNexis® Martindale-Hubbell®. Their lives are filled with the activities of their five children: Taylor, Patrick, Charlotte, Noah, and Jordan.

attorneys.bio:
A. A. “Beau” Howell is a native of Valdosta, Georgia, and graduated from Valdosta High School in 2001. He graduated from Auburn University in 2005 with a Bachelor of Science in Finance summa cum laude. Thereafter, he obtained his Juris Doctor (JD) degree cum laude from the University of Georgia School of Law and was admitted to the State Bar of Georgia in 2008. From 2008 until 2023, Mr. Howell primarily devoted his practice to the defense of personal injury claims, most of which involved defending medical providers and institutions against medical malpractice claims. During that time, Mr. Howell successfully litigated numerous dispositive motions on behalf of his clients and was involved in obtaining multiple settlements and jury verdicts in his client’s favor.

In the fall of 2023, Beau changed his focus to representing victims of negligence and medical malpractice. At the Law Office of A.A. Howell, IV, LLC, Beau now primarily represents plaintiffs in all aspects of personal injury and business litigation.

Beau and his family currently reside in Valdosta and are members of the Valdosta First United Methodist Church.

attorneys.name: Robert D. Howell
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Thomasville32, GA
attorneys.bio:
Robert D. "Robb" Howell is one of the founding partners of Howell Law Firm, P.C.. He handles catastrophic and high-stakes injury cases, medical malpractice, pharmaceutical lawsuits and business litigation. From his offices in Moultrie, Thomasville, and Albany, Georgia, he represents clients throughout the state and the southeast. He also maintains an Atlanta office and as serves as Of-Counsel to the firm of Conley Griggs Partin, LLP.

Due to his dedicated representation and trial skills, Mr. Howell has obtained many seven-figure and eight-figure recoveries on behalf of his clients. Since opening in February, 2006, Howell Law Firm has recovered well over $100,000,000 for clients who were injured or harmed by the negligence of others. Robb has been particularly successful in securing large recoveries for his clients in small, rural and traditionally-conservative venues. For example, in May, 2014, Mr. Howell was lead counsel in a medical malpractice trial in Lowndes County Superior Court which resulted in a record-setting verdict of $1,811,377.09 for his client. This was the highest personal injury jury verdict in the history of Lowndes County, Georgia at the time. Mr. Howell's verdict in this trial was featured as one of the top verdicts in Georgia in 2014 by the Daily Report on July 31, 2015.

In January, 2017, Mr. Howell was lead counsel in another record-setting trial verdict in Lowndes County, Georgia. In that case, Mr. Howell secured a $10 million dollar verdict on behalf of his client who suffered a brain injury from a fall at South Georgia Medical Center. This verdict was reported as the largest ever for a plaintiff in this venue and far surpassed the previous record verdict (also Mr. Howell's) from 2014.

His successes have earned him an AV rating,* and he has been selected by his peers as a Super Lawyer/Rising Star in 2009, 2010, 2011 and 2012 and as a Super Lawyer ever year from 2016 to 2023. Mr. Howell was also honored as a Top 100 Trial Lawyer by the American Trial Lawyers Association for the years 2010-2012 and received recognition by that organization as one of the Top 40 Trial Lawyers in the State of Georgia under the age of 40. Mr. Howell was recognized on August 31, 2012 as The Best Attorney In Moultrie Georgia by the Moultrie Observer.

As an active member of his legal community, Mr. Howell serves on the Executive Committee of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association and is a member of GTLA's Political Action Committee Board. Mr. Howell presently serves as a member of the University of Georgia Law School Council.

Mr. Howell graduated magna cum laude from Valdosta State University in 1994. Four years later, he received his law degree from the University of Georgia School of Law, graduating cum laude. While in law school, he was the chairman of the Moot Court Board and an active participant in the law school's prestigious moot court program, winning several titles and awards for his work.

attorneys.name: Michael L. Hubbard
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Douglasville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Hubbard is a life-long Douglas County, Georgia resident and graduated from Lithia Springs High School in 1985. He was a member of the U.S. Army and Georgia National Guard from 1988 to 1994 and received an honorable discharge. He received an Associate's Degree Equivalent in the field of Journalism and Public Relations from the Defense Information School at Fort Benjamin Harrison in Indianapolis, Indiana. He attended Georgia State University in Atlanta and later transferred to Mercer University in Atlanta where he graduated in 1999 with a B.S. in Business Administration. This degree was earned while Mr. Hubbard worked full-time as a district manager for a mall based specialty retail company for a period of ten years.

In 2002 Mr. Hubbard graduated from The Walter F. George School of Law at Mercer University in Macon, Georgia. Mr. Hubbard was a member of the Mercer Law School Moot Court team and competed in successful regional and national competitions. While finishing his law school education Mr. Hubbard served under O.C.G.A. 15-18-22 as an assistant district attorney in the Tallapoosa Circuit serving both Haralson and Paulding Counties where he prosecuted both felony and misdemeanor cases.

In late 2002 Mr. Hubbard formed Michael L. Hubbard, PC and began practicing as a sole practitioner in Fulton County, Georgia. Mr. Hubbard relocated to his home town of Douglasville Georgia in 2003 and has served as a full-time trial lawyer since that time in his Douglas County office. A resident of the city of Villa Rica, Georgia, Mr. Hubbard currently serves as the city solicitor for his home town and prosecutes all cases in the Municipal Court of Villa Rica. Mr. Hubbard also serves as General Counsel for the S.H.A.R.E. House and has successfully tried both criminal and civil cases inside and outside of Douglas County. He is a member of the American Bar Association, the Georgia Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the Douglas County Bar Association, and the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: Parks F. Huff
attorneys.practice_type: Eminent Domain - Condemnation Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Upon graduating from Emory University in 1988 with an Anthropology degree, I took a year off from school and worked as a Congressional Aide to George "Buddy" Darden. After talking to Congressman Darden and my Uncles Sam and Mike Huff about their experiences as lawyers, I decided to go to the University of Georgia School of Law. Law was a family profession and tradition, with my Grandmother, Helen Huff, being the first female lawyer in Cobb County and with two of her four sons being long-time Marietta lawyers.

After graduating from the University of Georgia cum laude, I had the privilege of accepting a Staff Attorney position with then Cobb Superior Court Chief Judge Watson L. White. The experience was invaluable. Judge White embodies the term "judicial temperament" and his seasoned staff knew more about the legal system than most lawyers.

In 1994, I accepted a position in the Cobb County Attorney's office. In my three-year tenure as an Assistant County Attorney, I had the opportunity to represent the Planning and Zoning Department, Code Enforcement Division, Tax Board of Equalization, Tax Commissioner, Business License Division, Department of Transportation and the Board of Commissioners in state and federal litigation.

In 1997, Garvis Sams and Joel Larkin asked me to join their firm. They were frequent adversaries when I worked for the County and I knew it would be enjoyable working for them. After practicing with the firm for five years, I was invited to become a Partner in 2002. My practice allows me to tackle a wide range of problems for clients. I continue to use the experience from my Cobb County employment to represent individuals and businesses that have disputes with either county or municipal governments, be it property tax disputes, eminent domain issues for road projects, development disputes or acquiring alcohol licenses for restaurants and other businesses. Experience in development has also provided relevant experience for all forms or real estate litigation, from disputes over construction contracts, trespasses, erosion and boundary line disputes.
