attorneys.name: Danielle C. Humphrey
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Danielle C. Humphrey is an elder law attorney at the Hurley Elder Care Law, which has multiple offices located in Georgia – Atlanta, Peachtree City, Duluth, and Woodstock. She works out of her office in Atlanta, assisting elderly clients with legal matters involving:

Guardianships

Probate and estate planning

Life care planning

Wills and trusts

Conservatorships

Ms. Humphrey holds the distinction as one of the fourteen elder lawyers in Georgia who have been elected to be Certified Elder Law Attorneys by the National Elder Law Foundation. She assists her clients and their families in obtaining guardianships and conservatorships to protect the elderly population from predators, scammers and other such vulnerabilities. Known among her clients as a compassionate and knowledgeable attorney, she strives to offer efficient solutions with their best interests in mind.

Graduating magna cum laude with a bachelor’s from the University of New Orleans in 1987, Ms. Humphrey went on to pursue her law degree at Tulane Law School. Earning her Doctor of Jurisprudence cum laude in 1990, she was admitted to the Louisiana State Bar Association the same year and later, gained her license to practice in Georgia (2010). She holds an “Excellent” rating on Avvo.

Maintaining an active presence in the legal community, Ms. Humphrey is a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys, the State Bar of Georgia and the Atlanta Bar Association’s CLE Committee. As part of her volunteer service, she plays an active role in the One Good Deed program by the Jewish Family & Career Services of Atlanta. She also presents at various conferences and seminars on legal topics related to elder law.

attorneys.name: David J. Hungeling
attorneys.practice_type: RICO Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
David Hungeling has over 25 years’ experience as a trial lawyer with a focus on complex litigation in state and federal court, including bankruptcy adversary proceedings. Mr. Hungeling began his legal career as an associate in the Securities Litigation Group at Alston & Bird, LLP in Atlanta. In 2003, he left big law to found his own firm, specializing in trial and appellate work. Mr. Hungeling received his J.D., magna cum laude, in 2000 from Georgia State University College of Law, where he was Managing Editor of the Georgia State University Law Review during the 1999-2000 school year. He received his B.A. in 1995 from the University of Notre Dame, where he served as student body president, and then went on to receive his M.A. in 1997 from the University of Portland. During law school, Mr. Hungeling was a law clerk for Justice Hugh Thompson of the Georgia Supreme Court and Stephen H. DeBaun, Special Administrative Law Judge. Before attending law school, he was a volunteer for two years in the Alliance for Catholic Education, which is part of the Americorp Program. As an ACE volunteer Mr. Hungeling served as a high school social studies teacher in Jackson, Mississippi. In addition to practicing law, Mr. Hungeling has been an adjunct faculty member at Georgia State University College of Law since 2016, where he teaches trial advocacy. He has served as a standard-of-care expert witness in legal malpractice cases and an expert witness in attorney’s fee disputes. He also serves on numerous civic and charitable boards and is a volunteer for area schools and the Catholic Shrine of the Immaculate Conception in downtown Atlanta.

attorneys.name: Donald Hunt
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Gainesville, GA
attorneys.bio:
After graduating from the University of Georgia Lumpkin School of Law in 1981 (having graduated from Emory University in December, 1977), Donald Hunt has practiced law for more than 40 years in Northeast Georgia. Donnie came to Gainesville, Georgia in 1983 as an assistant district attorney for the Northeastern Judicial Circuit. At the time he left the district attorney's office in 1985 to join the local law firm of Smith, Gilliam & Williams, he was serving as the chief assistant district attorney. Donnie's early private practice of law focused on litigation (insurance defense) and municipal law (City of Gainesville). After he left to form his own firm, Donnie has practiced in the areas of litigation, probate and estates and has served as a Special Assistant Attorney General and as the city attorney for the City of Oakwood, Georgia for 32 years and as county attorney for Habersham County for ten years. He brings to the practice of law years of experience of handling and negotiating politically sensitive issues efficiently and effectively - especially land use and zoning matters.

Donnie is also very involved in our local community having been a member of various service clubs and coaching youth sports such as recreational boys' and girls' soccer and basketball as well as an Athena girls traveling soccer team. He served in many roles with the sports and band programs at North Hall High School and is an active member of Lakewood Baptist Church where he has taught an adult Sunday School class and served as a deacon for over 38 years. He is a huge Georgia Bulldog fan - having grown up in Washington, Georgia - near Athens. His wife, Kathy, is a retired professor of mathematics (and chair of the math department) at the University of North Georgia and they have two grown children (Jared who resides in Texas and Rebekah who resides in Western/Central Asia after a lengthy stay in Southeast Asia.) Pictures of all four grandchildren are available upon request.

attorneys.name: Wade Hunter
attorneys.practice_type: Premises Liability Lawyers in Savannah, GA
attorneys.bio:
Wade Hunter was born and raised in Jacksonville, Florida. He received his undergraduate degree from Boyce College in Louisville, Kentucky before moving to Savannah, Georgia to attend law school at the Savannah Law School. While in law school Wade served on the board for the Savannah Law Review as Notes Editor and also worked part-time for a small firm in town focused on representing Plaintiffs that had been injured through the negligence of others. It was in the early stages of his legal career when Wade realized his passion for representing people that were being pushed around by the big insurance companies.

After graduating law school, Wade began working for another firm in Savannah that was focused on representing Plaintiffs injured in motor vehicle collisions. Over the course of his first 5 years in practice, Wade successfully represented over 1,000 clients recovering millions of dollars in the process.

In October 2021 Wade joined the Morgan & Morgan team in order to focus on premise liability actions. In addition to the wealth of experience he brings to the table, Wade also has a stellar reputation among his peers in the legal community. Even more importantly, Wade has great report with his clients and always makes sure they fully understand their rights, and options, before making any final decisions with their case.

attorneys.name: Miles P. Hurley
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Miles P. Hurley is the founder and owner of Hurley Elder Care Law, which has law offices in Atlanta, Peachtree City, Duluth, and Woodstock, Georgia. Serving clients throughout the state, Mr. Hurley provides unmatched counsel and support in all areas of elder law, and he holds his certification as an elder law attorney from the National Elder Law Foundation.

Over the course of his legal career, Mr. Hurley has achieved remarkable success advocating on behalf of the elderly population in his region, helping them to maintain independence and financial security in the face of life's inevitable challenges. A leader in his field, he has served as president of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys' Georgia Chapter, and he helped establish and served as vice president of the Life Care Planning Law Firms Association.

In addition, Mr. Hurley has served on the Practice Development/Practice Management committee of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys, and he has served as chair of the State Bar of Georgia's Elder Law Section. He has also served as vice president of the Lewy Body Dementia Association's board of directors, and he is a contributor to the Senior Services North Fulton Quarterly Newsletter as well as the Alzheimer’s Association's Georgia Chapter.

Furthermore, Mr. Hurley has been invited to present for many local and national organizations such as the Alzheimer's Association, AARP, ALS Association, and the American Parkinson's Disease Association.

In recognition of his impeccable professionalism and outstanding client service, Mr. Hurley has earned an AV Preeminent peer review rating* from Martindale-Hubbell along with many other top rankings and endorsements from his peers. He has also received Superb, 10 out of 10 client ratings on Avvo as well as numerous testimonials and referrals from those he has served.

Mr. Hurley began his legal career in 1992 after obtaining his Juris Doctor from Georgia State University College of Law and his license to practice from the State Bar of Georgia.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Rating™ fall into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.

attorneys.bio:
Matt Hurst is an experienced trial and appellate attorney representing individuals and families who have suffered due to serious personal injury, medical / nursing home negligence, and wrongful death. He has represented clients at the trial and appellate levels in both state and federal courts.

Matt's practice is based on a desire to help good people through difficult times. This sense of compassion drives Matt's thorough and diligent approach to handling his clients' cases. He has repeatedly obtained favorable results for his clients due to his keen attention to the factual and legal details of their cases.

Matt graduated with honors from the Georgia State University College of Law. While in law school, Matt served as the Vice-President of the Moot Court Honor Society and as a pupil on the Logan E. As a result of his demonstrated interest and skills in trial advocacy, Matt received the Georgia Civil Justice Foundation's Trial Advocacy Scholarship.

Matt is a member of the Georgia Trial Lawyer's Association. He is admitted to practice in all Georgia trial and appellate courts, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia, and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit.

attorneys.name: Harriet C. Isenberg
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Sandy Springs, GA
attorneys.bio:
Harriet Isenberg, founding principal of Isenberg & Hewitt, passed away on January 3, 2024. As a native Atlantan, she grew up in Buckhead. In 1985, she was admitted to the Georgia Bar after attending Atlanta Law School at night while working full-time.

Over the course of her adult life, Harriet worked in various fields including teaching, banking, real estate and law. She served as General Counsel for Globe Security and later co-founded Isenberg & Hewitt where she practiced with her then husband, Melvin L. Hewitt, Jr. and later her son Ryan Isenberg. She was a dedicated member of the Commercial Law League of America and played a pivotal role in shaping creditor's rights legislation in Georgia.

Harriet’s dedication, expertise and leadership were instrumental in shaping our firm. We remain committed to providing exceptional legal services and we will work tirelessly to honor Harriet’s legacy.

attorneys.name: Ryan L. Isenberg

attorneys.bio:
Admitted to the State Bar of Georgia in 2001, Ryan Isenberg has been litigating and trying cases in state and federal courts for more than 20 years. His practice primarily focuses on complex litigation involving trademarks, copyrights, partnership and corporate governance disputes, and creditor’s rights.

In addition to representing businesses and investors in complex business disputes, Ryan has represented international recording artists, record labels, fashion houses and movie distributors in their intellectual property disputes and he has successfully represented banks and other creditors in pursuing hidden or transferred assets. He also supports the firm’s other lawyers and practice areas whenever needed as he has litigated dozens, if not hundreds, of personal injury cases.

He’s a member of the American Bar Association Sections of Business Law and Litigation and the Business Law and Creditor's Rights sections of the State Bar of Georgia.

Notable recent results:

Obtained dismissal of copyright claims against Sony Music, UMG Recordings and Capital Music Group.

Obtained dismissal of copyright claims on behalf of Rae Sremmurd.

Obtained declaratory judgment relief on behalf of movie distributor, Maverick Entertainment

Obtained summary judgment and an award of attorney’s fees on behalf of search engine 4Internet.

Additional seminars:

2018 Advanced Debt Collection

Has moderated, chaired, and/or spoken at numerous American Bar Association Conferences.

sections.content:
Admitted to the State Bar of Georgia in 2001, Ryan Isenberg has been litigating and trying cases in state and federal courts for more than 20 years. His practice primarily focuses on complex litigation involving trademarks, copyrights, partnership and corporate governance disputes, and creditor’s rights.

In addition to representing businesses and investors in complex business disputes, Ryan has represented international recording artists, record labels, fashion houses and movie distributors in their intellectual property disputes and he has successfully represented banks and other creditors in pursuing hidden or transferred assets. He also supports the firm’s other lawyers and practice areas whenever needed as he has litigated dozens, if not hundreds, of personal injury cases.

He’s a member of the American Bar Association Sections of Business Law and Litigation and the Business Law and Creditor's Rights sections of the State Bar of Georgia.

Notable recent results:

Obtained dismissal of copyright claims against Sony Music, UMG Recordings and Capital Music Group.

Obtained dismissal of copyright claims on behalf of Rae Sremmurd.

Obtained declaratory judgment relief on behalf of movie distributor, Maverick Entertainment

Obtained summary judgment and an award of attorney’s fees on behalf of search engine 4Internet.

Additional seminars:

2018 Advanced Debt Collection

Has moderated, chaired, and/or spoken at numerous American Bar Association Conferences.

Personal:

Ryan and his wife, Jennifer, live on a farm outside of Atlanta where they have rescued and care for retired racehorses, chickens, dogs and a turkey.

attorneys.name: N. Nickolas Jackson
attorneys.practice_type: Class Action & Mass Torts Lawyers in Columbus, GA
attorneys.bio:
Nick Jackson grew up in Phenix City, Alabama, and earned his undergraduate degree from Auburn University before attending Samford University’s Cumberland School of Law. He graduated as one of the youngest members of his class, receiving his Juris Doctor cum laude and ranking in the top 7%.

Nick represents plaintiffs and defendants across industries in complex, high stakes trial and appellate litigation. Nick regularly serves as lead counsel in wrongful death actions, particularly those involving negligent security and construction defect allegations.

Nick also practices in the areas of multidistrict litigation, class action litigation, mass torts, and personal injury. Nick has played a key role in significant data breach class actions in Georgia history and successfully argued on behalf of over 497,000 class members in a landmark data breach case that is frequently cited for its foreseeability analysis.

Nick is currently leading one of the largest mass litigation campaigns in Georgia history alongside consumer advocate, Erin Brockovich, where he represents hundreds of individuals, businesses, municipalities, and counties across the State in claims involving environmental contamination stemming from carpet manufacturing.

Nick prides his practice on being results driven and uses a “business” approach in all of his cases. Nick attributes his business acumen to his grandmother who grew a small staffing agency in Columbus, Georgia into one of the nation’s largest female-owned employment agencies.

Nick is a lifetime member of the Auburn Alumni Association. When he is not working, Nick enjoys spending time with his family, watching Auburn football and basketball, duck hunting, and fishing at his family’s farm in rural Southwest Georgia. Nick also loves Alabama history and is the creator of a former exhibit at the National World War II Museum in New Orleans, Louisiana. Nick’s exhibit highlighted the roles of women and African Americans in Alabama’s contributions to the war effort.

Successes

Wrongful Death:

$5,000,000 wrongful death bench verdict in a negligent security case in Muscogee County, Georgia, settled for policy limits

$4,000,000+ settlement involving wrongful death claim

$2,000,000 settlement involving negligent security wrongful death claim

$2,000,000 settlement involving wrongful death claim

$1,000,000 settlement involving negligent security wrongful death claim at a hotel

$1,000,000 settlement involving negligent security wrongful death claim at a strip mall

Trucking Accident:

$499,000 trucking accident settlement

Premises Liability

$250,000 slip and fall accident settlement

Defense Results:

Obtained a defense verdict as lead trial counsel in a multi-day jury trial for a disputed liability car accident where Plaintiff alleged permanent and life altering injuries

Regularly serves as lead counsel for large governmental entity in large multi-party wrongful death actions

Regularly serves as lead counsel for large governmental entity in large multi-party construction defect wrongful death actions

Negotiated confidential settlement for large insurance company in a high-risk personal injury action that was in permanent default in Georgia state court

Regularly serves as lead counsel for various large financial institutions in various litigated matters throughout the Georgia state and federal court system

attorneys.name: Miracle C. Jackson
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Miracle C. Jackson received her Bachelor of Arts from Florida A&M University, where she graduated Summa Cum Laude. She then went on to attend the Florida A&M University-College of Law in Orlando, Florida. During Law School, she participated in various organizations such as the Women's Law Caucus, Black Law Students Association, and she served as the Parliamentarian for the Association of Trial Lawyers of America. Ms. Jackson was also a participant of the Frederick Douglass Moot Court Team. She later went on to judge the competition.

Prior to founding Jackson Steed, LLC, Ms. Jackson practiced Criminal Law as a Court Appointed attorney. While practicing criminal Law, Ms. Jackson represented thousands of individuals charged with offenses in State Court giving her extensive experience in handling DUIs and traffic offenses. She has also handled various other criminal cases such as assault, batteries, domestic violence cases, and drug offenses. Ms. Jackson then went on to work at a small Family Law Firm where she practiced both criminal and family law. There she focused on divorces, alimony, custody and visitation, child support modifications, legitimations, adoptions, and domestic violence cases.

During her years of practice, Ms. Jackson has received extensive litigation experience and has participated in numerous jury trials. She is also skilled at negotiating with state prosecutors to obtain favorable results for her clients.

Ms. Jackson is also a very active member of the legal community and is a member of the Georgia Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the Atlanta Bar Association, the Cobb County Bar Association, the Gate City Bar Association and is admitted to the Georgia Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court of Georgia. She also serves as the Vice President of the Family Law Section of the Cobb County Bar.

attorneys.name: Terry Jackson
attorneys.practice_type: Catastrophic Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Terry D. Jackson is an accomplished Georgia trial lawyer who has devoted his career to helping seriously injured victims and families secure justice. With more than 20 years of legal experience, Terry has handled a wide range of cases involving catastrophic injuries and wrongful death, including those resulting from serious truck and auto collisions.

Terry is a passionate advocate for the injured and the wronged, and he has accumulated the tools and resources to protect victims’ interests against powerful corporations and insurance providers. He has helped numerous clients put their lives back together following tragedies – and his record of success includes over 100 trials in state and federal court, more than $100 million in compensation recovered on behalf of clients, and some of the largest verdicts in the state.

After earning his undergraduate degree and a master's in accounting and taxation from the University of Tennessee-Knoxville, Terry went on to earn his law degree at the University of Georgia School of Law. He was admitted to the Georgia Bar in 1993, and opened Terry D. Jackson, P.C. in 1996.

Terry remains as committed and compassionate to clients as he did the day he opened the firm. His goals are to help provide clients with a bold voice in our civil justice system, and to secure the compensation they rightfully deserve.

attorneys.name: Rebekah James
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Johns Creek, GA
attorneys.bio:
Rebekah A. James currently serves as a Law Clerk with Meriwether & Tharp, LLC. She graduated magna cum laude with a bachelor's degree in Psychology from the University of West Georgia and earned her Juris Doctorate at the University of Georgia School of Law.

During her undergraduate career, Rebekah maintained the HOPE Scholarship, was a member of both the University of West Georgia Honors College and the Kappa Tau Chapter of Sigma Kappa sorority, and volunteered as a Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA).

In law school, Rebekah worked as a Student Practitioner at the Wilbanks Child Endangerment & Sexual Exploitation (CEASE) Clinic for two semesters and one semester at the Family Violence Clinic. In January 2018, Rebekah had the opportunity to participate in the Wilbanks CEASE Clinic's Child Welfare Mock Trial, which was centered on child sexual abuse and child welfare.

Rebekah has served on the Editorial Board and Managerial Board of the Journal of Intellectual Property Law. She is also a Registered Neutral through the Georgia Office of Dispute Resolution and served as a mediator for civil cases in the Magistrate Court of Athens-Clarke County. While in law school, Rebekah was a member of the Family Law Society, Student Bar Association, Alternative Dispute Resolution Society, Women Law Students Association, and Law Republicans. During her final year of law school, Rebekah served as Vice President of Programming for the Family Law Society and Publicity Officer for the Women Law Students Association.

Growing up as a child of divorced parents, Rebekah understands firsthand the challenges associated with divorce. Rebekah's interest in the legal field was inspired by a Guardian ad Litem who represented her as a child. Following law school, she entered the field of family law focusing on child welfare and child custody.

On a personal level, Rebekah is active in church, enjoys hiking, painting, spending time with family and friends, and cheering on the Georgia Bulldogs.

attorneys.name: Kyle Jarzmik
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
I was born in suburban Chicago, grew up in Charlotte, North Carolina, and attended Wake Forest University. After working for a large law firm while in college and graduating with a bachelor’s degree in economics, I attended Georgia State University College of Law in Atlanta.

During law school, I interned with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia. There, I was involved in the prosecution of federal drug, fraud, and white-collar crime cases. I was also given the rare opportunity as an intern to make arguments and question witnesses in a mail fraud jury trial in which the defendant was convicted.

After graduating from law school in 2008 and working for a year in a private civil firm, I joined the Office of the Fulton County Solicitor General in early 2010. For more than 5 years, I prosecuted thousands of criminal cases involving a wide range of charges. Among these charges were DUI, battery, theft, stalking, hit and runs, driving with a suspended license, vehicular homicide, reckless driving, speeding, and other traffic offenses.

Insight Gained from The Other Side

During my time as a prosecutor, I negotiated pleas, argued motions to suppress, and represented the State as lead counsel in numerous bench and jury trials. I also received training from police officers in how they conduct DUI investigations. These experiences gave me a unique insight into criminal law, which to this day benefits the clients I defend in criminal cases.

You see, having worked alongside other prosecutors and police officers, I understand how they think and what makes them tick. This gives me a distinct advantage when preparing a defense on behalf of my client. As I thoroughly investigate the facts and evidence, I consider all possible avenues in order to find the one that will give my client their best chance at a successful outcome.

Applying My Approach to Other Areas of The Law

Once I became established as a criminal defense attorney, I decided to expand my practice to include personal injury. I chose to make this change because, the way I see it, people who have been wrongfully injured need a strong advocate on their side — and who better to represent them than someone whose focus has always been on justice?

attorneys.name: Patrick D Jaugstetter
attorneys.practice_type: Eminent Domain Lawyers in McDonough, GA
attorneys.bio:
Patrick D. Jaugstetter is a partner in the law firm of Power ▪ Jaugstetter. Patrick joined the firm in 2008 after serving as County Attorney in Henry County, Georgia for five years (2003-2008). Prior to serving as County Attorney, Patrick was General Counsel at Killearn, Inc., a regional resort development company (1999-2003) and a partner in the law firm of Smith, Welch and Brittain (1993-1999).

Patrick has been practicing law since 1993 and is licensed to practice law in the Georgia Supreme Court, the Georgia Court of Appeals, all State and Superior Courts in Georgia, the United States District Court for the Northern District of Georgia and the United States Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit.

Patrick's practice focuses primarily on commercial and business litigation and eminent domain litigation. In recent years, Patrick has represented a number of governmental entities, businesses and individuals in a wide variety of disputed matters. Most recently, Patrick has successfully defended business owners against fraud claims, defended against a class action suit alleging violations of the Telephone Consumer Protection Act of 1991, represented property owners in property tax appeals and represented individuals and businesses in various contract claims.

In addition to his litigation practice, Patrick has represented buyers, sellers and lenders in hundreds of complex real estate transactions, drafted Restrictive Covenants, assisted in the creation of condominiums under the Georgia Condominium Act, served as Qualified Intermediary in 1031 Exchanges.

Patrick is also a Registered Mediator and is frequently called upon by courts, litigants and their counsel to mediate claims and assist parties in resolving their disputes.

Patrick is a graduate of the University of Georgia (Bachelor of Arts in Economics, 1988) and the Georgia State University College of Law (Juris Doctor, 1993).

Recent Results:

Power ▪ Jaugstetter gets Franchisee released from Non-Compete Covenant contained in Franchise Agreement.

After 8 months of litigation in DeKalb and Henry Counties, partner Patrick Jaugstetter was able to gain a Franchisee's release from the Non-Compete Covenants in the Franchise Agreement. After meeting with their client, Patrick filed suit against the Franchisor asking the Court to declare void a non-compete clause in the Franchise Agreement. After eight months of litigation, the Franchisor relented and released the Franchisee from the covenant. The non-compete covenant, if enforced, would have prevented the franchisee from doing business.

Power ▪ Jaugstetter obtains favorable settlement in Telephone Consumer Protection Act class action.

Patrick Jaugstetter recently obtained a favorable settlement on behalf of a client subjected to a class action claim for violation of the Telephone Consumer Protection Act. The claim against the client alleged that the client sent Ajunk faxes in violation of the TCPA. The Client faced statutory damages in excess $2,500,000; after defending the allegations, the claim was settled in a manner that resulted in a cash payment by the firm's client of less than $250,000

Power ▪ Jaugstetter obtains defense verdict in claim for fraud in Federal Court.

In June, 2010, Patrick Jaugstetter, with the assistance of associate Lauren Thompson, obtained a defense verdict in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Georgia in favor of client sued for fraud arising from breach of a Factoring Agreement. The claim alleged that the client, a business owner, engaged in fraudulent conduct in the execution and performance of the Agreement; the Plaintiff sought damages in excess of $1,500,000. The case was tried before a Federal Judge who found in favor of Mr. Jaugstetter's client on all claims alleging fraud.

Power ▪ Jaugstetter obtains directed verdict in favor of client facing claims for fraud.

After three days of trial before a jury in the Superior Court of Henry County, Georgia, Patrick Jaugstetter obtained a directed verdict in favor of a shareholder in a business that was sued for fraud by a vendor. The Plaintiff sought damages in excess of $150,000 from the business owner. At the conclusion of the Plaintiff's case, Mr. Jaugstetter asked the Court to grant a verdict in favor of his client; the Court agreed with Mr. Jaugstetter and entered judgment releasing the business owner from any liability. Mr. Jaugstetter is currently pursuing a claim against the Plaintiff and the Plaintiff's attorney for the recovery of the attorney fees expended by his client in defense of the claims.

Power ▪ Jaugstetter defends against multiple foreclosure confirmation petitions.

During the first half of 2010, Patrick Jaugstetter has successfully represented multiple property owners against lenders seeking to confirm foreclosure sales. The successful defense of these actions has relieved Patrick's clients of facing lawsuits seeking millions of dollars in judgments.

Power ▪ Jaugstetter successfully defends suit seeking title to clients property.

In early 2010, Warren Power and Patrick Jaugstetter represented a client in trial before a jury in Henry County, Georgia. At trial, the Plaintiff claimed title to property owned by the firm's client. The trial lasted 4 days; after 3 hours of deliberations, the jury returned a verdict in favor of the firm's clients on all claims asserted by the Plaintiff and awarded the firm’s clients over $15,000 in attorney fees.

attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Hinesville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Andrew S. Johnson is an associate attorney at Arnold & Stafford, Attorneys at Law, in Hinesville, Georgia. Mr. Johnson practices in a variety of areas, including consumer real estate, family law, government relations and personal injury, serving clients throughout Hinesville.

Mr. Johnson has been a licensed attorney since 2006 and has more than 14 years of experience. He is admitted to practice in all Georgia state courts and before the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Georgia and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit.

Over the course of his career, Mr. Johnson has been involved in several high-profile cases and had many successful verdicts and settlements. He represents a diverse group of clients, including The Heritage Bank and the School Boards of Liberty and Long Counties. He provides personalized service to each client and works hard to help them achieve the best possible outcome, offering free consultations, fixed hourly rates and fixed feeds to best meet each client’s needs.

Mr. Johnson earned a bachelor’s degree in management from Clemson University. He received his law degree from the University of Georgia School of Law located in Athens, Georgia. He is a member of the Delta Tau Delta fraternity.

In addition to his practice, Mr. Johnson enjoys giving back to his community by being involved in pro bono activities. He served as the public defender from the Hinesville Municipal Court from 2008 to the present. He is a past chairman of the Bryan County Board of Elections and currently sits on the executive board of the Bryan County Chamber of Commerce.

Mr. Johnson is also actively involved in his legal community. He is a member of the Atlantic Judicial Circuit Bar Association and the State Bar of Georgia.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Daniele Johnson, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
I was called to serve and advocated for others at a very young age. I first answered that call while in my 3rd year of law school when I became court certified to represent victims of domestic violence. Upon graduating from law school, I was hired by the Dauphin County District Attorney’s Office. There, I was assigned to the Special Victims Unit, assisting in the prosecution of felony crimes committed against children.

In 1999, I relocated to West Cobb to pursue my true passion, the practice family law. Since then, I have been handling such matters as divorce, custody, child support, legitimation, and adoptions. In 2006, I became court-certified to serve as a Guardian Ad Litem in Cobb County, meaning, I am trained to determine and represent the best interest of children.

My basic philosophy in handling my cases is to get my clients from point A to point B as painlessly, expeditiously, and efficiently as possible while helping realize their hopes, dreams, and aspirations. I represent my clients with the appropriate level of aggressiveness while we remain in frequent communication. I then work very closely with my clients as we work together to reach their identified goal.

I would love to learn more about you and your family's law needs. Please contact me at the office to schedule an appointment to discuss your case in more detail.

Thank you and I look forward to working with you soon.

attorneys.name: Darwin F. Johnson
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Darwin Johnson, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Darwin F. Johnson, the premier Georgia workers' comp lawyer, graduated magna cum laude from the University of Florida in 1999 with a dual Bachelor of Arts in History and Sociology. He received his Juris Doctorate law degree from Florida State University in 2003.

After graduating from law school, Johnson went to work as a Senior Staff Attorney to the Honorable Michael P. Baird in Clayton County, Georgia. As an attorney working within the Georgia court system, he witnessed first-hand the lengths to which insurance companies would go to avoid paying injured workers and those injured due to the negligence of others.

Mr. Johnson found this behavior to be disturbing, and because he wanted to use his education in law to actually help people, he decided fighting for the rights of injured individuals was a noble and worthwhile pursuit. In order to combat the unjust strategies of insurance companies, Johnson focused his practice on workers' compensation in Atlanta.

In 2004 he joined forces with workers' comp attorney Louis B. Lusk. Together they spent five years battling insurance companies on behalf of people just like you. He's handled over 2,500 cases to date, and has won or settled over $25 million in workers' compensation and personal injury claims.

Today, Darwin Johnson has become one of Atlanta's premier workers' compensation attorneys, and continues to specialize in the representation of injured workers in cases before the Georgia State Board of Workers' Compensation.

He also represents individuals who have been injured due to the negligence or willful misconduct of others in personal injury cases. Mr. Johnson is a licensed workers' compensation lawyer in all State and Superior Courts throughout Georgia, and he is eager to help you!

Experience personalized attention, service, and results from a dedicated workers' comp attorney in Atlanta. Call Darwin F. Johnson today at (404) 692-6482!

"Your situation and case are unique. You deserve an attorney who not only takes the time to learn the details of your case, but also gets to know you as a person and that is exactly what you'll get when you work with me."

"With bigger firms, you are just a number, but when you call my office, you get ME, not an operator, not a paralegal who simply screens calls. You will speak with me personally and if I'm in court, I'll call you as soon as I am excused by the Judge. I'll get right to work on your case, becoming familiar with all the relevant details. Sure, there are bigger firms in town, but none can give you the personalized attention I will." - Darwin Johnson

attorneys.name: Gregory K. Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Columbus, GA
attorneys.bio:
Greg Johnson graduated Cum Laude from Georgia Southern University with a Bachelor of Arts degree in History in 2009 as well as a minor in Political Science. In 2013, Mr. Johnson went on to graduate from Mercer Law School in Macon. While at Mercer, Mr. Johnson was part of the National Trial Competition Mock Trial Team as well as the ABA Labor and Employment Mock Trial Team. Additionally, he competed in the 2012 Charleston School of Law Moot Court Competition.

While in school, Mr. Johnson interned for the District Attorney's Office in Rome, Georgia and in Macon, Georgia. After law school, he accepted a position as an Assistant District Attorney in the Cordele Judicial Circuit. Following his time in Cordele, Mr. Johnson moved to Columbus to join the Public Defender's Office for the Chattahoochee Judicial Circuit. During this time, he had numerous jury trials, ranging from simple misdemeanors to complex felony and murder cases.

In 2017, Mr. Johnson transitioned to civil practice, where he worked in a wide range of areas of the law, including but not limited to business litigation, landlord/tenant issues, wills and estates, and other issues involved in general litigation. Since 2018, Mr. Johnson has worked almost exclusively in the area of personal injury law. Given that Mr. Johnson has work in many different legal fields, which encompass both civil and criminal matters, he brings a unique perspective to our Firm.

Also, while in Columbus, he has been an active participant in the Columbus Inn of Court and was named as a 2016 Legal Elite by Georgia Trend Magazine. When not at work, you can usually find Mr. Johnson with his wife, Julie Johnson, their twins, Aiden and Elizabeth, and their golden retriever, Webster.

attorneys.name: Jarvis G. Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Domestic Relation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
The first meeting between an attorney and a man going through divorce will set the tone for the attorney-client relationship. It's at that meeting that Jarvis G. Johnson wants to listen to his client's side of the story and convey a general direction of what the options are.

"I want to understand their goals and explain how we can use the law to find the fairest solutions to difficult domestic situations," Mr. Johnson said.

Few family law issues are as impactful and personal as child custody, according to Mr. Johnson.

"In custody cases you get to know the individual more in-depth, you get to know their parenting style and the things they do each day to sustain their family. You want to keep that dynamic in place as much as possible," he said. "So in the end, if all parties feel as though a new chapter is beginning, the chances of sustaining a relationship that nurtures children and future objectives in life is greater."

attorneys.name: Kyle Johnston
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Kyle D. Johnston, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Workers Compensation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Originally from Chicago, Kyle has been practicing law in the State of Georgia for 15 years. He obtained his undergraduate degree in Philosophy and Portuguese at Brigham Young University and his law degree from University of Miami, graduating in 2007. At age 19, Kyle lived in Brazil for 2 years where he became fluent in Portuguese. During his time in Brazil, Kyle fell in love with the culture and people of Brazil. Because of this, he would like to extend his practice to better serve the Brazilian (and other Portuguese) speaking communities in Atlanta, and State wide. Kyle is proficient in Spanish and together with his native Spanish speaking Paralegal, Pirosa Merritt, is eager to serve our Spanish speaking clients and broaden our influence in Georgia's Hispanic Community.

Kyle dedicates his practice to representing injured workers in the State of Georgia as well as clients who have been injured due to the negligence of others. Kyle’s intention from the outset of his career was to represent and fight for individuals who had been injured on the job or as the result of negligence by another party. In anticipation of this, Kyle made the strategic decision to spend the first five years of his practice representing the employers and insurance companies in work accident claims. Through that process, he gained valuable insight and understanding as to how the employers and the insurance company evaluate and defend claims. With that knowledge, Kyle can more effectively represent injured Georgians.

In his free time, Kyle enjoys mountain biking, fishing and photography, cheering on the Chicago Blackhawks and Cubs, and spending time with his wife and four children.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Douglasville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Bethaney Embry Jones graduated from Spelman College with a Bachelor’s Degree in Chemistry. In 2008, Bethaney received her Juris Doctor, Magna Cum Laude, from North Carolina Central University School of Law. Bethaney Embry is a hardworking, experienced, and passionate attorney who began her legal career working as a Staff Attorney in the DeKalb County Superior Court. As a Staff Attorney, she worked on a high number of Personal Injury and Adoption matters and gained invaluable experience and insight into the manner in which cases are litigated.

Bethaney has handled nearly every type of serious automobile injury trials. She has single handedly settled and collected large settlements on behalf of her injured victim clients. This unique experience has afforded Bethaney a comprehensive knowledge of the practices and procedures of insurance companies and their tactics. Simply put, she knows the insurance companies’ cheap tactics and uses the same knowledge against the insurance companies to make certain that her injured client’s rights are protected and maximum favorable results are achieved.

Bethaney’s previous work experience also includes clerking at the Court of Appeals of North Carolina and working at a General Civil Litigation firm. Bethaney is actively involved in the legal community. Bethaney is also actively involved in the Douglasville and Atlanta community. Mrs. Embry Jones enjoys giving back to the community by volunteering for numerous nonprofit organizations. She is also an active member of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. In her free time, she enjoys traveling with her husband, working out and reading books.

With Bethaney’s experience you can rest assure that her first-hand knowledge will help you achieve the best possible outcome for you and your family. Bethaney’s dedication to your satisfaction is second to none. It is the goal of The Embry Law Firm to provide our clients with the services they need to get the results they want. When you choose the Embry Law Firm, you choose to have your interest protected with sincerity and integrity.

attorneys.name: Ford Jones IV
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Greensboro, GA
attorneys.bio:
As part of his day-to-day work, Ford regularly assists clients through the real estate closing process, planning for the future through estate planning (Last Will and Testaments, Powers of Attorneys, Healthcare Directives, and Trusts), and navigating the difficulties of the loss of a loved one (Probate and Estate Administration). From drafting complex Trust agreements for high-net-worth individuals, to helping clients through the probate process for an estate, Ford's thorough and detailed approach is part of what sets him and J.V. Dell P.C. apart.

Ford earned his law degree from Georgetown University Law Center (J.D., 2016), where he was a member of the Georgetown Journal of Law & Public Policy. Ford has been published in the Georgetown Journal of Law & Public Policy and has received Dean's List Honors and a Cali Award for highest marks in Contracts. During his time in Washington D.C., Ford was active in numerous Pro Bono opportunities, becoming an Exceptional Pro Bono Pledge Honoree at Georgetown Law, the highest public service honor bestowed on its graduates. Prior to attending law school, Mr. Jones attended the University of Georgia where he received his Bachelor's Degree in 2013.

Prior to joining Dell Law Firm PC, Ford held numerous positions at the highest levels of federal and state government. During his first year of law school, Ford worked in the Office of Legal Counsel for the Governor of Wisconsin and presidential candidate, Scott Walker. Ford also worked on complex policy, rulemaking, and procurement issues during his time with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Transportation Security Administration.

attorneys.name: W. Seaborn Jones
attorneys.firm_name: Owen Gleaton Egan Jones & Sweeney, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Government Law and Liability Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Seaborn Jones' practice includes litigation in the product liability, general personal injury, life and health insurance, and commercial fields. He is also active in alternative dispute resolution and has served as a mediator and court-appointed special master in cases of significance. Originally from Waynesboro, Georgia, Mr. Jones is a graduate of Davidson College (A.B., 1964) and of the University of Georgia School of Law (J.D., 1967), where he was a member of its National Moot Court Team and president of his class. Following law school, Mr. Jones served in the United States Army in Vietnam, rising to the rank of Captain. Mr. Jones then returned to Atlanta where he practiced for more than twenty years with the firm of Hurt, Richardson, Garner, Todd & Cadenhead.

Mr. Jones enjoys a well-deserved reputation as a "lawyers' lawyer." He has served as President of the Atlanta Bar Association (1984-85), President of the Metropolitan Bar Caucus (1993) and President of the National Conference of Bar Presidents (2000). He is also well-known in Georgia and nationally as a bar leader at the forefront of the professional reform movement. He was instrumental in forming the Professional Reform Initiative, a project of the National Conference of Bar Presidents which he continues to co-chair. He is the recipient of two of the Atlanta Bar Association's highest awards, the Charles Watkins Award for Distinguished Service (1993) and its Professionalism Award (2000).

Atlanta Bar Association’s Award: Professionalism Award, 2000

attorneys.bio:
Austin Joseph is an associate attorney at Meriwether & Tharp. He is originally from Waycross, Georgia. In 2018, Austin graduated magna cum laude from the University of Georgia with a degree in Entertainment and Media Studies. Austin's passion for family law began during his tenure as a student member of the Jane W. Wilson Family Justice Clinic, which provided legal assistance to domestic abuse survivors. Prior to rejoining Meriwether and Tharp in its Athens office, Austin practiced business litigation at a prominent Athens law firm.

On a personal note, Austin enjoys exploring the Classic City's many culinary options with his family, playing with Archie (the family's cocker spaniel), and reading a new find.

attorneys.name: Maria Justus
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Savannah, GA
attorneys.bio:
Maria Justus is an attorney with The Manely Firm, P.C. in Savannah, Georgia. Prior to working with The Manely Firm, Maria worked for many years with Former United States Attorney for the Southern District of Georgia Donnie Dixon. In that role, Maria assisted with and personally oversaw a variety of cases with a primary focus in federal criminal defense. She served as a Criminal Justice Act Panel Attorney providing legal counsel to indigent defendants accused of crimes in the Southern District of Georgia. Maria also worked as a volunteer attorney for the Georgia Justice Project Freedom Expungement Project. Through her practice, Maria quickly realized that her true passion in practicing law was helping people navigate through some of the most difficult chapters in their life. Her experience has taught her that for clients, these life circumstances can feel very isolating and confusing, but as a lawyer, you are tasked with the truly unique and humbling experience of helping guide people through and out of those overwhelming situations.

Maria grew up in Miami, Florida in a Greek-American family being the youngest of four children. She is the first attorney in her family. Maria attended college at Florida International University earning her B.S. in Criminal Justice. While in school she was proudly the recipient of the Florida Bright Futures Scholarship, also enjoying active membership to the sorority Alpha Omicron Pi. Following college, Maria attended Savannah Law School where she was a John E. Ryan Merit scholarship recipient. During her time as law student, Maria clerked for the Honorable Penny Haas Freesemann of the Chatham County Superior Court. She worked on a caseload consisting of various divisions including Major Crimes, Mental Health Court, and Veterans Court. She continued to intern in private criminal practice where she assisted in felony appellate brief writing for submission to the Supreme Court of Georgia.

Also, while at Savannah Law School, Maria was a member of the Trial Advocacy Team where she competed in national Mock Trial competitions. She was a member of the Phi Alpha Delta Law Fraternity, the Street Law Community Program where she spoke at local high schools about the law and its effect on teens, and participated in the Tiny House Project to house local veterans through the Veterans Law Society.

Maria is married to local attorney Daniel Justus and they have two daughters together. In her free time, she enjoys spending time with her family, watching movies and documentaries, traveling, and doing outdoor activities.

attorneys.bio:
Kaplan Legal Services is based in Atlanta, GA and lead by Attorney Bryan Kaplan. Bryan knows what it takes to protect his clients in business disputes in Georgia and Alabama.

Bryan’s legal experience is developed from a broad array of clients in such industries as advertising, agriculture, commercial banking, construction, distribution and wholesale, freight & transportation, commercial real estate (leasing/enforcement), professional services (accounting, legal, engineers & architects), foreclosures on personal and real property, insurance premium & audit, technology, trade secrets (non-compete, non-solicit, non-recruit, and trade secret agreements), registration/domestication of foreign judgments, staffing services, and shareholder and partnership agreements. Not only does Bryan handle commercial and creditor’s rights litigation, but he routinely enforces judgments through garnishment, post-judgment discovery and motion practice. Aside from breach of contract/open account claims and business torts, Bryan frequently called assists clients in the resolution of bankruptcy disputes including fraudulent transfers, preferences, 341 hearings, proofs of claim, rejection damage claims, and administrative claims.

If your business or you face a legal dispute, please reach out to Kaplan Legal Services for a free initial consultation. We look forward to assisting your business and you with a legal strategy for the desired outcome. While Bryan possesses big firm experience, he offers competitive hourly rates, contingency fee and hybrid fee arrangements, and flat fees.

attorneys.practice_type: Property Insurance Coverage/Measurement Disputes Lawyers in Sandy Springs, GA
attorneys.bio:
Brent Kaplan, an Atlanta native, has been a member of the Georgia Bar since 1983. He is a Summa Cum Laude graduate of Vanderbilt University, where he was elected to Phi Beta Kappa, and a cum laude graduate of the University of Georgia School of Law, where he served as a member of the Georgia Law Review.

Mr. Kaplan is a trial lawyer and has extensive experience in a wide range of practice areas, including property insurance coverage, measurement and subrogation cases, bad-faith claims, and also disputes under comprehensive general liability policies. Mr. Kaplan has extensive experience in personal injury cases, including wrongful death, product liability and medical negligence. In addition, Mr. Kaplan has litigated numerous commercial cases including class and collective actions and has significant experience litigating restrictive covenants in employment contracts. He has served as both lead trial and appellate counsel in cases throughout the country. He is also a certified mediator.

Mr. Kaplan comes to Isenberg & Hewitt from Robins, Kaplan, Miller, and Ciresi, where he served as managing partner of the firm's Atlanta office.

Mr. Kaplan is a member of the Atlanta Bar Association, State Bar of Georgia, the Lawyers Club of Atlanta and Gridiron Secret Society. He is co-author of the chapter "Procedural Points" in the Trial Practice Manual published by the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: Jason W. Karasik
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Johns Creek, GA
attorneys.bio:
Jason Karasik is a Partner with Meriwether & Tharp, LLC. Jason has also been managing Meriwether & Tharp's marketing department since 2014. Jason obtained his undergraduate degree from the University of Georgia in 2008. After graduating from the University of Georgia, he began work as a policy fellow for Georgia Governor Sonny Perdue. Jason worked with the House Education Committee and the Senate Education and Youth Committee while doing education policy research. Additionally, he worked closely with the Governor's Policy Director in providing solutions for Georgia's education issues.

Jason obtained his law degree from the University of Michigan Law School. While in law school, he received the Dean's Scholarship and was an Executive Editor of the Michigan Journal of Race & Law. After his first year of law school, Jason worked for three different Federal Judges in the United States District Court, Middle District of Florida. Jason's experience in Federal Court afforded him an insider's look at what it takes to succeed in trial proceedings. After his second year of law school, he worked for a large firm doing mostly commercial litigation work. During law school, Jason quickly developed a significant interest in family law while working in the University of Michigan's Child Advocacy Law Clinic (CALC). Here, he provided legal assistance to people going through difficult times in their lives and truly enjoyed helping his clients achieve a positive outcome. In CALC, Jason represented abused and abandoned children as a Lawyer Guardian Ad Litem. His job was to determine what was in the best interests of the child and advocate for their interests in court. Jason also represented parents in custody disputes, and he acted as of counsel for the prosecutor in child welfare cases.

On a personal level, Jason enjoys spending time with his wife while fly fishing on the Chattahoochee River and in the North Georgia Mountains. He also enjoys cooking, golf, college football and automotive repair and restoration.

attorneys.name: Rachel B. Keller Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Rachel Keller’s practice centers around estate planning, probate matters, guardianships, and conservatorships. Rachel also assists several local law firms as they navigate probate court for their clients: opening probate estates and obtaining approval of settlements for minors and incapacitated adults. Rachel enjoys working with clients and their advisors to collaboratively work towards a plan that will best meet that individual client’s needs.

Rachel has been practicing law since 2009. She joined Georgia Legacy Law Group, LLC after spending seven years practicing insurance defense and personal injury litigation at a boutique Atlanta law firm, where she handled hundreds of litigation matters. While this litigation background may seem unrelated to her current practice, it provides a unique perspective as Rachel works with clients to try and avoid litigation themselves – whether it is in the estate planning context or the probate context.

Rachel is a member of the Atlanta Bar Association’s Estate Planning and Probate Section and the Alpharetta Chamber.

Rachel was born in Athens, Georgia. She earned her Bachelor’s degree in Family and Consumer Sciences from the University of Georgia. She went on to earn her law degree from Cumberland School of Law in Birmingham. Rachel met her husband, Adam—who is also an attorney—at Cumberland School of Law. The couple currently resides in Alpharetta with their daughter, Millie, and rescue dog, Doc. In their free time, they enjoy hiking in the mountains, traveling, and spending time with friends and family.

attorneys.name: Othel Doyle "Trey" Kelley, III
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Cedartown, GA
attorneys.bio:
Trey Kelley grew up in Cedartown and was raised by Doyle and Laura Kelley, both educators in the Polk County School District. A 2008 honor graduate of Shorter University, Trey graduated with his Juris Doctorate degree from Georgia State University College of Law in May 2014.

A member of the Parker and Lundy team since 2013 Trey’s practice focuses on civil litigation, workers’ compensation, and wills, trusts, and estate probate matters.

Trey is also proud to serve the citizens of our community in the Georgia House of Representatives. First elected to the Georgia House in 2012, Trey serves as a member of the Judiciary, Banks & Banking, Code Revision, Energy, telecommunications, and utilities, Health and Human Services, and Ways and Means Committees, while also serving in a leadership position on the Higher Education Committee.

Staying active in the community, Trey has held multiple leadership roles such as President of the Cedartown Exchange Club, Board Member for the Murphy-Harpst Children’s Centers, member of the Rockmart Rotary, Polk County Chairman of Governor Deal’s 2010 & 2014 gubernatorial campaigns, and Chairman of the Polk County Republican Party.

Trey is married to the former Amy Marvin of Powder Springs. The couple are proud members of the First Baptist Church in Cedartown where they reside.

Trey is married to the former Amy Marvin of Powder Springs. The couple are proud members of the First Baptist Church in Cedartown where they reside.

attorneys.name: Robert M. Kent
attorneys.practice_type: Consumer Bankruptcy Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio: My main goal in practicing bankruptcy law is to not only help people file bankruptcies, but to change the way people think about themselves and to build their confidence and belief in themselves. Bad things happen to good people, which is why the bankruptcy laws were created to help people have a fresh start. Bankruptcy laws are in the Constitution and are a fundamental right of the people. The media and the popular belief is that if you declare bankruptcy, then you have failed in life. This is completely untrue. Declaring bankruptcy is essentially a financial decision and does not deem someone as a failure. Only people who give up are failures and declaring bankruptcy is a way to not give up but to start over. I want to help people because I am genuinely passionate about people’s lives and not only their finances but also their confidence and belief in themselves.

attorneys.name: Robert "Bob" P. Killian
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Brunswick, GA
attorneys.bio:
Robert P. Killian is a shareholder of the firm Killian Law Firm LLC, in Brunswick, Georgia. With almost four decades of experience, he focuses his practice on matters of civil litigation, primarily personal injury and wrongful death. Since he co-founded the firm in 1997, Mr. Killian and his partner have recovered more than $166 million in compensation for clients. He handles cases primarily in Glynn, Camden, Liberty, Brantley, McIntosh and Wayne counties. In addition to his principle area of personal injury and wrongful death, he has successfully represented clients in business litigation cases, condemnation cases, civil rights cases and estate disputes. He has tried well over 200 civil cases to verdict and has handled over forty appeals to the Georgia Court of Appeals and Supreme Court and the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals.

Mr. Killian obtained his Juris Doctor from the University of Georgia School of Law, and he was admitted to practice in Georgia in 1976. Currently a Regional Vice President of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association, he is also a member of the Brunswick-Glynn County Bar Association, the American Association for Justice, the American Bar Association, and the National Trial Lawyer's Top One Hundred in Georgia.

Dedicated to putting his extensive trial experience to work for his clients, Mr. Killian has garnered recognition among his peers. For twenty nine years, he has had Martindale-Hubbell's highest peer-reviewed rating of AV-Preeminent*, and he is a published author as well. One of his articles, “Stop Abusive Litigation in Clear Negligence Cases with a Kiss and Make-up Letter,” appears in the 1990 winter issue of Verdict, the quarterly journal of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association. He also wrote "Use of Experts to Show How Darkness Affects Driver Vision in Tractor Trailer Wrecks" for the journal's 1997 winter issue. Mr. Killian additionally co-authored "Examination of the Police Officer in an Automobile Collision Case," published in Calendar Call, a publication of the trial section of the State Bar of Georgia. He speaks at Georgia Trial Lawyer seminars.

*AV-Preeminent and BV-Distinguished are certification marks of Reed Elsevier Properties Inc., used in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the confidential opinions of members of the Bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell ratings fall into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.

Author: "Stop Abusive Litigation in Clear Negligence Cases with a Kiss and Make Up Letter," Verdict Journal of Georgia Trial Lawyers Association, November/December 1990 Issue; Article, "Use of Experts to Show How Darkness Affects Driver Vision in Tractor Trailer Wrecks," Verdict Journal of Georgia Trial Lawyers Association, Winter, 1997. Co-Author: "Examination of the Police Officer in an Automobile Collision Case," Calendar Call, official publication of the General Practice and Trial Section of the State Bar of Georgia.

attorneys.bio:
Andrew King is a wrongful death and catastrophic injury trial attorney. He represents people who have been seriously injured and the families of loved ones who have been needlessly killed in nursing homes, automobile, trucking, medical malpractice, and premises liability cases.

Before representing plaintiffs, Andrew spent many years defending companies, physicians, hospitals, nurses, nursing homes, dentists, psychotherapists, and other medical providers in medical malpractice cases in complex matters. He left his partnership with an AmLaw 200 law firm to pursue his passion representing injured persons and the families of those that have been injured.

Andrew was honored to be placed on multiple moot court teams traveling around the nation representing his school. He was also made the Treasurer and Secretary of the UGA Moot Court Team. He served as the Notes Editor for UGA’s Journal of Intellectual Property. He was also selected to clerk for and draft opinions in both the District Court for the Middle District of Georgia and the Superior Court of Athens-Clarke County during law school.

He left his partnership with an AmLaw 200 law firm to pursue his passion representing injured persons and the families of those that have been injured.

Andrew was honored to be placed on multiple moot court teams traveling around the nation representing his school. He was also made the Treasurer and Secretary of the UGA Moot Court Team. He was also selected to clerk for and draft opinions in both the District Court for the Middle District of Georgia and the Superior Court of Athens-Clarke County during law school.

attorneys.name: Jessica A. King
attorneys.practice_type: Workers Comp Lawyers in Cartersville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Jessica King focuses her practice on residential and commercial real estate and workers’ compensation matters.

In her real estate practice, Jessica handles residential and commercial closings, title curative matters, zoning, contract matters, lease negotiations, and other transactional issues. She advises agents, lenders, builders, buyers, sellers, and investors on complex transactions, guiding them from the signing of contracts through closing. Jessica prioritizes clear communication and a smooth, informative, and engaging experience for all parties involved.

In workers’ compensation matters, Jessica fights to ensure her clients receive the benefits they are entitled to. She pursues all possible avenues of financial recovery, from negotiation and mediation to depositions and trial, holding liable parties accountable while securing maximum compensation.

Jessica began her legal career representing insurance companies in liability matters, gaining experience with fact and expert discovery, motions, mediations, and trial practice. After transitioning to plaintiff-side work, she broadened her practice to include transactional matters, combining strategic problem-solving with practical advocacy.

Jessica earned her B.S. in Management from Georgia Institute of Technology and her J.D. and M.B.A. from Cumberland School of Law at Samford University. She is actively involved in the community, serving on the board of the Good Neighbor Homeless Shelter. She is a member of the State Bar of Georgia and lives in Marietta with her husband, two sons, and dog.

attorneys.bio:
Gregory H. Kinnamon was born in Dalton, Whitfield County, Georgia in 1958 and has lived in the Dalton area all of his life. Mr. Kinnamon graduated high school from Northwest Whitfield High School as part of the School's first graduating class in 1976.

He graduated from the University of Georgia with an A.B. degree in Political Science in 1980 and received his Juris Doctor degree from Mercer University, Walter F. George School of Law cum laude in 1984. While at Mercer Law School Mr. Kinnamon received American Jurisprudence Awards in the areas of Criminal Law, Commercial Paper and Business Associations. Mr. Kinnamon was admitted to practice law in Georgia in 1984.

He is a member of the State Bar of Georgia and a member of the Conasauga Circuit Bar Association. Mr. Kinnamon has practiced before various Probate, Magistrate, Superior and State Courts as well as Federal Court, Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals, State of Georgia Court of Appeals, Georgia Supreme Court and the United States Supreme Court.

Mr. Kinnamon served two terms in the Georgia House of Representatives from 1992-1997 where he served as Secretary of Governmental Affairs, Chairman of the Elections subcommittee, Industrial Relations, Chairman of the Worker's Compensation subcommittee, and on the prestigious Judiciary Committee.

Mr. Kinnamon served as counsel for the Carpet Capital Association of Realtors from 1992-2012. Mr. Kinnamon has served as Murray County's attorney since 2000. Mr. Kinnamon has served as former Director/Organizer of Premier National Bank of Dalton, former Director of Dalton-Whitfield Bank, former Board member of Whitfield Education Foundation, former Board Trustee of Dalton College Foundation, former Advisory Board member of First National Community Bank, formerly known as the First National Bank of Chatsworth, former Executive Committee member of Dalton-Whitfield Chamber of Commerce, Past President of Cherokee Area Estate Planning, Past President of the local chapter of the Georgia Bulldog Club, Past President of Dalton Golf and Country Club. Mr. Kinnamon previously served on the Board of the Humane Society of Northwest Georgia. He also previously served as Trustee of the Whitfield Healthcare Foundation.

He practices in the areas of Civil Litigation, County Government Law, personal injury, automobile and truck accidents, wrongful death, probate law, wills, estates and trusts, business law, formation of corporations, partnerships and limited liability companies, and all types of real estate transactions.

Mr. Kinnamon has a client rating of 5.0 of 5.0 from Martindale Hubbell/Lawyers.com and an AV (preeminent) peer review rating from Martindale Hubbell/Lawyers.com, the highest rating available.

Gregory H. Kinnamon and Gregory H. Kinnamon, P.C. is a recognized member of the Worldwide Registry, an exclusive prestigious network of top professionals in the United States.

Gregory H. Kinnamon has also been selected for participation in the Elite American Lawyers program! This honor is reserved for members who have exhibited dedication, leadership and longevity in their career fields.

Voted Best Attorney in Northwest Georgia by the readers of the Dalton Daily-Citizen News, Reader's Choice Award for 8 years in a row from 2017-2024. He also won the award in 1997 and 2010.

Gregory H. Kinnamon, P.C. [ The Kinnamon Law Firm] was nominated by his peers statewide in the Georgia Business Journal, Best of Georgia in 2020 - 2024, and has won in the category of Probate Law Firms five years in a row. Likewise, The Kinnamon Law Firm won Best of Georgia in 2024 (Regional) in the category of Estate Planning Law Firms. The Kinnamon Law Firm, under the leadership of Mr. Kranzlein was nominated by his peers statewide in the Georgia Business Journal, Best of Georgia in 2024 in the category of Real Estate Law Firms.

attorneys.name: Kim Kirby
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Hiram, GA
attorneys.bio:
Kim wants all people to have quality representation during every stage of the criminal justice system. She knows that being charged with a crime is a terrifying prospect that can have lasting effects on the lives of those around you. Whether you or someone you love has been charged with a misdemeanor, felony, or juvenile delinquency offense, Kim wants to help you understand your options and guide you to the best available for your unique case.

Kim has extensive experience working with and around prosecutors. She began working full-time in the Cobb District Attorney's Office in an administrative capacity, while she attended school at night and on weekends to earn her undergraduate and law degrees. Since leaving the Cobb District Attorney's Office, Kim has worked as a prosecutor for the Douglas County Solicitor's Office. At the Douglas County Solicitor's Office, she prosecuted countless misdemeanor cases including traffic offenses, DUIs, and domestic violence cases before she ultimately became the head of the Domestic Violence Unit. After leaving Douglas County, Kim joined the Paulding County District Attorney's Office handling criminal prosecution focused on Juvenile delinquency cases.

She is particularly passionate about helping juveniles charged with criminal actions. It may surprise you to learn that the juvenile justice system is different in many ways from the adult justice system. If your child has been charged with a crime, Kim will fight to clear their name and protect their record.

attorneys.name: George Koenig
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Koenig founded Koenig Law Group, P.C. in 2009 after returning home to Atlanta from Washington, DC.

During his time in Washington, DC, George was Senior Counsel for Kemp Partners and Vice President & General Counsel for Land Bridge Equity LLC. Kemp Partners, founded by former Congressman, Cabinet Secretary and Vice-Presidential candidate Jack Kemp. George specialized in defense and homeland security matters providing his clients with legal and strategic counsel, relationship development and marketing advice to enable them to accomplish business and policy objectives. He was also Vice President and General Counsel for Land Bridge Equity LLC, a real estate investment company in which Secretary Kemp was a principal investor and advisor.

Before joining Kemp Partners, George was Counsel with Alston & Bird LLP, an AmLaw 100 firm, where he practiced in the areas of mergers and acquisitions, securities, trial practice and litigation, government investigations and public policy.

Previously, George served as the Counsel to the General Counsel for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), where he advised the General Counsel and senior leadership at the Department. He served under both Secretary Tom Ridge and Secretary Michael Chertoff. Immediately following Hurricane Katrina, George was deployed to Louisiana and Mississippi in support of the Department's response and recovery efforts where he served as legal advisor to the principal federal official, Vice Admiral Thad Allen.

George received his J.D. from Catholic University's Columbus School of Law and his undergraduate degree from Vanderbilt University. He is a veteran of the Unites States Marine Corps where he served as infantry and logistics officer.

George serves as vice-chair of the Homeland Security Division of the American Bar Association's (ABA) Admin Law Section and is Vice-Chairman of the ABA's Annual Homeland Security Law Institute.

George has authored or co-authored a number of homeland security related articles for the ABA and other publications. In the Fall of 2006 and 2008, he has been a Professorial Lecturer in Law at George Washington University Law School teaching a course entitled Homeland Security Law and Policy. In the spring of 2005, he was an adjunct professor at American University's Washington College of Law, where he has taught a course by the same name.

George is married and the father of five. He is active with his Church and is Chairman Emeritus of the Marine Corps Association of Georgia Lawyers.

attorneys.name: Karisa Kopaczewski Klee Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Karisa Kopaczewski Klee’s legal career has exclusively been dedicated to the field of workers’ compensation. She began her career with a large insurance defense firm and was subsequently named Partner while working for a full-service regional law firm. After a decade of representing employers and insurance companies, Ms. Klee now represents injured workers throughout the state of Georgia. She uses her prior experience to obtain compensation for her clients and helps them navigate Georgia’s complex workers’ compensation system. She has successfully litigated numerous workers’ compensation cases and has represented clients from the trial level through the appeals process. Ms. Klee regularly speaks on workers’ compensation topics at conferences and seminars.

Ms. Klee was born and raised in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. She graduated magna cum laude with a B.S. in Business Finance from Carroll University in Wisconsin. She moved to Atlanta to work for a large insurance company prior to attending law school at Georgia State University. While in law school, Ms. Klee was President of the Business and Law Society and a member of Georgia State University's mock trial team. She was also chosen as a Graduate Research Assistant for the law school’s Low-Income Taxpayer Clinic, a Pupil in the Bleckley Inn of Court and interned with the Georgia Innocence Project.

Ms. Klee enjoys freelance writing in her free time and has been featured by the New York Times and Forbes.
