Book Award (Highest Grade) Employment Law Class, 1996 - Present

Using this unique background and experience, Kimberly founded Martin & Martin with the sole goal of vindicating the rights of employees. She has successfully litigated cases on behalf of workers in all areas of employment law. Kimberly represents employees in Family Medical Leave Act and disability cases as well as discrimination cases including race, sex and pregnancy discrimination. The New York Times reported on one of Kimberly's age discrimination lawsuits that was filed against a major U.S. company on behalf of a class of individuals who had been terminated in a reduction of force.

Kimberly also focuses a significant amount of her time handling overtime wage and hour cases. She takes particular pride in obtaining unpaid wages for workers who have not been paid properly. Kimberly specializes in cases involving unpaid overtime, unpaid wait and travel time, the misclassification of employees as exempt instead of nonexempt, the misclassification of independent contractors, failing to pay workers for all hours worked, and failing to pay nonexempt salaried employees overtime. Martin & Martin also handles wage cases on behalf of classes of employees in class actions. In 2009, Kimberly and her partner, Thomas Martin, represented a class of over 600 workers in a lawsuit alleging unpaid wait and travel time.

Kimberly also regularly handles tip pool violation cases involving servers, bussers, bartenders, and hosts/hostesses against restaurants that require employees to participate in illegal tip pools.

Martin & Martin is known for aggressively litigating their employment and wage cases to obtain the absolute highest amount of recovery they can for their clients. Kimberly prides herself on not running a "litigation mill" handling hundreds of cases and asking her clients to settle for pennies on the dollar. Instead, Kimberly gives each of her cases highly specialized and individual attention as she fights for all of the damages her clients deserve.

attorneys.bio:
KlinTisha Martin is a Georgia native raised in Powder Springs. A proud alumna of McEachern High School, she is a two-time women's basketball state champion. She continued her academic and athletic journey at the Illustrious Shaw University in Raleigh, North Carolina, where she excelled both in the classroom and in motherhood. KlinTisha graduated summa cum laude with a bachelor's degree in political science before earning her Juris Doctor from Ohio Northern University, where she co-founded the law school's civil rights journal, further reaffirming her commitment to excellence, advocacy, and public service.

After re-locating to Georgia in 2022, KlinTisha fulfilled her childhood dream of becoming an attorney. She passed the bar exam in July 2022 and was sworn in as a member of the Georgia Bar that December. Since then, KlinTisha has served as a federal judicial law clerk for the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Ohio. After transitioning out of her clerkship, KlinTisha worked as a family law associate with a small private firm before joining the Meriwether & Tharp team.

Outside of the office, KlinTisha Martin is a proud mother of two boys. She is a varsity women's high school basketball coach, member of motion running club, and enjoys traveling and spending time with friends and family.

attorneys.bio:
uke Martin is an experienced trial attorney and partner at Bratcher Martin, LLP. After graduating from the University of Alabama School of Law, Luke returned home to northwest Georgia and began serving as a prosecutor. In his career as a prosecutor, Luke tried and prosecuted a wide range of cases from DUI to capital murder and racketeering (RICO).

At Bratcher Martin, LLP, Luke has continued his thriving appellate practice. In his career, Luke has won dozens of appeals at the Georgia Court of Appeals and Supreme Court of Georgia and successfully argued several landmark cases that changed the legal landscape for attorneys throughout Georgia.

Luke is a native of Floyd County, Georgia and graduated from Armuchee High School. He is active in his community and lives in Rome with his wife, Sarah, and two children. Luke continues to serve as a Judge Advocate in the U.S. Army Reserve and has served as special victims’ counsel, trial counsel, military justice advisor, and brigade judge advocate for one of the largest brigades in the Army Reserve.

attorneys.name: Thomas F. Martin
attorneys.practice_type: Health Care Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
A graduate of the U.S. Naval Academy at Annapolis, Maryland, Tom F. Martin is a Vietnam war veteran, having served for a year on river patrol boats (PBRs) on the rivers and canals of the Mekong Delta. After active duty, Tom began a very successful health care career that lasted for 28 years and provided him with a wealth of experience in a wide variety of management and senior administrative and executive roles.

Tom has operated in both the proprietary as well as the not-for-profit segments of the health care industry, and has had many very successful experiences with: start-ups, takeovers, and turnarounds. He has served as multi-facility manager for Hospital Corporation of America with operational responsibility for 8 psychiatric hospitals, including Annawakee (now Inner Harbour). This latter facility, with over 500 wilderness treatment beds and its headquarters in Douglasville, Georgia, and satellite facilities in Rockmart, Georgia and Carabelle, Florida, was in serious jeopardy of losing its state licenses to operate, its JCAHO accreditation, and was on the verge of bankruptcy when Tom negotiated a contract with its not-for-profit facility's Board to manage the operations. Tom also served as a Board member, at the request of the licensing and accrediting entities, to help ensure against fraud and abuse and other potentially illegal activities.

Tom served as the Administrator and/or CEO of some of the best and largest private psychiatric hospitals in the nation including: Riveredge Hospital in Chicago, Illinois; Las Encinas in Pasadena, California; Belle Park in Houston, Texas; Tidewater Psychiatric in Tidewater, Virginia; and Brawner in Smyrna, Georgia. He also has experience leading substance abuse treatment facilities and a community mental health center.

He served as Vice President of Operations of a 500 plus bed medical surgical hospital and had responsibility for all physician and other professional contracting; development of an ambulatory surgery center organized as an LLC with physician owners; development of an open heart surgery program; and operation of a home health care agency.

A graduate of Case Western Reserve School of Law in Cleveland, Ohio, Tom uses his many years of practical hands-on health care leadership experience, combined with his legal education and training, to meet the needs of his clients.

attorneys.name: Whitney D. Mauk
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
When facing legal issues related to family law, the residents of Metro Atlanta, Georgia, rely on the law office of Whitney D. Mauk, P.C. With a deep understanding of a complex legal system and a passion for representing the rights of her clients, Ms. Mauk has worked for over 15 years to obtain the best results possible for those facing both complicated and simple family law issues.

Handling divorces involving complex assets, child custody, visitation, child support and alimony, relocation cases, contempt and legitimation issues, custody, child support and alimony modifications, collaborative divorce, paternity, and prenuptial/postnuptial agreements, she represents those in the Atlanta metropolitan area including Fulton, Cobb, and DeKalb counties. With a focus on creative solutions to settle disagreements through mediation, Ms. Mauk and her staff at the law office are nevertheless prepared to take any case to trial to get the appropriate results.

From high-asset divorces to contested custody battles and the drafting of prenuptial agreements, she is prepared to handle any legal matter with a qualified, knowledgeable approach gained through time and experience. At the law office of Whitney D. Mauk, P.C., the goal is to give clients personal and specific attention, as every family is unique and desires a different result.

As families change and needs adapt, many feel alone as they face the reality of family court, but Ms. Mauk is committed to presenting a united front that allows clients to do what they believe is best for their families. To lessen the stress of paying for an attorney, the office also accepts credit card payments for services.

Michael devotes his practice to helping individuals harmed by the negligence of others. He has handled cases against commercial trucking companies, financial institutions, insurance companies, and medical groups. Michael began his career as a criminal defense attorney to gain valuable experience in the courtroom. After obtaining considerable trial success, Michael transferred to civil practice with Martin Snow, LLP, one of the oldest large firms in Georgia. Michael represented insurance companies and their insureds in car wreck cases for years. While working for the insurance companies, Michael learned the systems and methods used by insurance companies and adjusters to lower the payouts to those injured by the negligence of others. Michael successfully tried numerous jury trials to a defense verdict before being named Partner at Martin Snow, LLP. Michael credits his mentors at Martin Snow, LLP for their invaluable training and example. Michael now uses his knowledge and experience to help individuals achieve the best result from the insurance companies. Michael has recovered millions of dollars on behalf of those harmed by others, including a single trial verdict and recovery over $1.6 Million. He has successfully defended his verdicts on appeal. Michael has represented the families of those killed by another's negligence and obtained large confidential settlements. He is experienced in mediation and arbitration, as well, and he routinely advises clients on the benefits and risks of litigation.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Michael devotes his practice to helping individuals harmed by the negligence of others. He has handled cases against commercial trucking companies, financial institutions, insurance companies, and medical groups. Michael began his career as a criminal defense attorney to gain valuable experience in the courtroom. After obtaining considerable trial success, Michael transferred to civil practice with Martin Snow, LLP, one of the oldest large firms in Georgia. Michael represented insurance companies and their insureds in car wreck cases for years. While working for the insurance companies, Michael learned the systems and methods used by insurance companies and adjusters to lower the payouts to those injured by the negligence of others. Michael successfully tried numerous jury trials to a defense verdict before being named Partner at Martin Snow, LLP. Michael credits his mentors at Martin Snow, LLP for their invaluable training and example. Michael now uses his knowledge and experience to help individuals achieve the best result from the insurance companies. Michael has recovered millions of dollars on behalf of those harmed by others, including a single trial verdict and recovery over $1.6 Million. He has successfully defended his verdicts on appeal. Michael has represented the families of those killed by another's negligence and obtained large confidential settlements. He is experienced in mediation and arbitration, as well, and he routinely advises clients on the benefits and risks of litigation.

attorneys.name: Charles H. McAleer
attorneys.practice_type: Plaintiffs and Injured Workers Lawyers in Decatur, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. McAleer founded The McAleer Law Firm, P.C., in 2003, to devote 100% of his practice to representing Plaintiffs in cases involving personal injury, workers' compensation, and contract litigation. He has never represented an insurance company. Each year, Mr. McAleer recovers millions of dollars for its clients and brings several cases to trial every year with outstanding results.

The type of cases Mr. McAleer brings to trial varies but includes cases that involve serious bodily injury and wrongful death but also smaller soft tissue cases. Unlike most firms, if an insurance company is unreasonable in its settlement negotiations, Mr. McAleer will bring all of his clients' cases to trial; not just the large cases but also the small cases.

After graduating from Emory in 1996, Mr. McAleer worked abroad for five years as General Counsel for an international manufacturing company. Mr. McAleer managed all litigation in which the company was involved. In addition, Mr. McAleer also negotiated and drafted numerous multi-million dollar (or Euro) transactions and managed key aspects of contract performance. Mr. McAleer also led a mergers and acquisition team through several purchases and mergers including post-transaction corporate integration.

Mr. McAleer has also been an adjunct professor of U.S. law at the University of Trier, Germany, which included legal research, torts, civil procedure, and contracts.

Mr. McAleer is an active member in good standing of the State Bar of Georgia, Georgia Trial Lawyers Association, The American Trial Lawyers Association, the Atlanta Bar Association, and the American Bar Association.

Mr. McAleer is fluent in German.

attorneys.name: Katherine L. McArthur
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury and Wrongful Death from Car and Truck Crashes Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Kathy McArthur is a personal injury attorney who has served the greater Macon, Georgia, community for more than three decades. During that time, Kathy has dedicated her legal practice to ensuring injury victims, no matter their backgrounds or ability to pay an attorney, have a voice in the courtroom. Kathy is board certified in civil trial advocacy by the National Board of Trial Advocacy and is also a member of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum. Kathy and her legal team have secured over $250 million in recoveries for her clients over the years. She focuses her practice on truck wrecks, automobile wrecks, and medical malpractice.

Personal injury lawyers in Georgia typically charge the same rate for attorneys fees across the board. Because of this, a new attorney with little to no experience in court will cost the same as Kathy. She encourages potential clients to review any lawyer's history of verdicts and settlements, as well as past client testimonials, before hiring an attorney. Kathy is a fighter who prides herself on fully investigating every case and preparing for trial in every situation. This preparation then lets the defendants know she's serious about proving the case in court if a full and fair settlement offer is not made. When the cases go to trial, her record-breaking verdicts are a testament to her litigation skills.

It costs potential clients nothing to contact one of the attorneys at the McArthur Law Firm and there is no obligation to hire. Call now for your free consultation and let Kathy fight for you!

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
DAVID H. McCAIN is a Macon native with an accounting degree from the University of Georgia. During each of his three years in law school, David was elected by his fellow students to serve as a justice on the law school's Honor Court, and he served as the Chief Justice in his final year. After graduating cum laude from the Mercer University Walter F. George School of Law, David focused his practice in the area of civil litigation.

David has experience representing seriously injured clients in catastrophic personal injury, wrongful death, workers' compensation and premises liability cases, and has successfully represented clients in bad faith actions against major insurance companies. David has assisted clients in a wide range of matters, including complex commercial litigation, breach of contract, liens, dispossessory, foreclosures, collections, and garnishments. David has practiced before trial courts across the State of Georgia, has assisted clients in appeals before the Georgia Court of Appeals, and has argued before the Supreme Court of Georgia.

David and his wife, Elizabeth, are members of Christ Episcopal Church. During their spare time, David and Elizabeth enjoy traveling, playing tennis, hiking, and visiting with family and friends.

attorneys.name: Thomas T. McClendon
attorneys.practice_type: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Tom focuses his practice on representing all parties in Chapter 11 reorganizations, other bankruptcy cases, and corporate workouts. Tom also represents clients in the buying and selling of businesses and business assets, commercial real estate transactions, and lease negotiations.

Tom represents small businesses and individuals in their Chapter 11 and Subchapter V reorganizations. He has obtained confirmed plans of reorganization on behalf of businesses in many different industries such as construction, trucking, retail, real estate and aviation, as well as for individuals with debt related to such businesses.

Tom also represents creditors in Chapter 7 and 11 bankruptcy cases, ranging from secured creditors, such as banks and other lenders, to trade creditors holding unsecured claims, to landlords and others needing relief from the automatic stay. He has represented creditors in the largest cases with thousands of creditors and millions in debt down to the smallest cases with a handful of creditors and limited debt. In each case, Tom advises his clients on their opportunities for recovery and risks, and navigates the case's progression in a cost-effective way while effectively advocating the client's interest.

Tom has no shortage of experience litigating interesting and complex issues under bankruptcy law and negotiating out-of-court workouts. Some of the successful results Tom has obtained for his clients are:

Tom represented the largest creditor in the case of In re BPI Sports, LLC, 23-17463-SMG (Bankr. S.D. Fla. 2023), a pre-negotiated Subchapter V case where his client agreed to serve as plan guarantor and execute a debt-for-equity swap; plan was confirmed in 32 days.

Tom represented the unsecured creditors' committee in In re Teri G. Galardi, 22-5035 (Bankr. M.D. Ga. 2022). After mediation with the committee, the debtor agreed to pay $10 million to a liquidating trust for the benefit of unsecured creditors. Tom currently is the liquidating trustee for the creditors' trust.

GMT Mgmt. Grp., LLC v. Belcher, 664 B.R. 879 (Bankr. N.D. Ga. 2024), where Tom obtained summary judgment on behalf of creditors against a debtor for nondischargeability of promissory notes totaling $15,489,178.59 based on the debtor’s fraud.

Gordon v. Webster, 629 B.R. 654 (Bankr. N.D. Ga. 2021), where the trustee asserted the ability to avoid transfers up to ten years old under the "golden creditor" rule and asserted claims of reverse veil piercing. After the debtor's motion to dismiss was partially granted, the trustee voluntarily dismissed the case with prejudice.

Tom advised a physicians' practice through an out-of-court workout for nearly two years, including negotiating consensual settlements in four substantial creditor or shareholder disputes.

In re Cristian Liquors, Case No. 20-40499-bem, first confirmed Subchapter V Plan of Reorganization in Georgia.

Prior to joining Jones & Walden, Tom clerked for the Hon. Robert G. Mayer of the Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Virginia. He also worked for a business boutique firm in Macon, Georgia and an AmLaw 100 firm in Atlanta.

Tom graduated magna cum laude from Washington and Lee School of Law. During law school, Tom was on the Washington and Lee Law Review, where he worked as lead articles editor, and received the American Bankruptcy Institute Medal of Excellence. Prior to law school, Tom attended Auburn University, where he graduated summa cum laude with a degree in history while attending (almost) every football game at JordanHare.

attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Defense Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Rodney joined Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele in 1996 and is currently a partner in the firm's Litigation Department. His legal fields of concentration are in workers' compensation defense, general insurance defense, insurance coverage disputes, and subrogation litigation.

Born in Bellefontaine, Ohio, June 6, 1967, Rodney received his B.A. and J.D. from the University of Georgia. He has worked for numerous insurance companies, third party administrators, and self-insured companies in both the Insurance Defense and Workers' Compensation area.

He is a member of the Cobb County Bar Association and a member of the Workers' Compensation Section of the State Bar of Georgia. Since 2005, he has been recognized with the Rising Star Award for Top Georgia Lawyers in the area of Workers Compensation. He has also served on the State Board of Workers' Compensation Rules Committee and is currently on the Chairman's Steering Committee for the Annual State Board of Workers' Compensation Education Conference. He frequently speaks on topics related to Workers' Compensation Laws in Georgia.

Rodney lives in Acworth, GA with his wife, Amy, and their three daughters, Maddie, Meagan and Meghan.

attorneys.name: Cameron M. McCord
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Since 2005, Cameron M. McCord has focused her practice on corporate and individual Chapter 11 bankruptcy, business law, commercial dispute resolution, and litigation with an emphasis on debtor-creditor disputes, problem loans, and business restructurings. She has served as lead counsel in over 75 corporate Chapter 11 bankruptcies and over 25 individual Chapter 11 bankruptcies, obtaining confirmed reorganization plans in the vast majority of those cases. In 2020, Cameron was appointed as a Sub Chapter V, Chapter 11 trustee in the Northern District of Georgia. Cameron has also represented clients in over 50 adversary proceedings, both as part of her client’s bankruptcy representation and as special counsel assisting other attorneys. Cameron also has experience in Chapter 15 Cross-Border insolvencies, filing 46 affiliated cases in the Northern District of Georgia in 2023 and 2024. Cameron fights for her clients’ interests and excels at finding practical solutions in even the toughest situations, including in complex litigation and cases involving fraud and fraudulent transfer claims.

After graduating from Georgia State University College of Law in 2005, Cameron joined Jones & Walden as an associate attorney. She became a Partner with the firm in 2013. Prior to law school, Cameron attended Humboldt State University and graduated with a Bachelor of Fine Arts in 2001. She also holds a Masters of Fine Arts degree from Georgia State University School of Art and Design with a concentration in photography and sculpture.

Cameron lives in the Buckhead area with her husband and two children and their dogs, Friday and Rocky.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Gloria grew up in Brooklyn, New York and received her B.A. from St. John’s University in Queens, NY. Prior to attending law school, she taught English in South Korea for three years.

Gloria graduated from Emory Law in 2025. During law school, developed an interest in business law and served as a Vice President for the Emory Corporate and Business Law Society. She was a Member of Emory Law Moot Court Society, where she advanced to Quarterfinals and co-wrote a Top-Ten Brief in the Tulane Sports Law Mardi Gras Invitational. attorneys.name: Parker McFarland Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Serious Personal Injury Lawyers in Cumming, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney R. “Parker” McFarland, Jr. is a fourth generation attorney whose mission is to restore lives shattered by wrongful death and serious accidents and injuries. Since 2019, Parker has been voted “BEST PERSONAL INJURY ATTORNEY” for 5 years by the Forsyth County News. Parker is a Christian advocate who prays for and with his clients, providing aggressive legal representation rooted in faith and genuine care and concern. Parker’s great-grandfather, John Alexander McFarland, started practicing in 1905 and quickly became a prolific trial lawyer who won 2/3 of his cases. His son, Parker’s grandfather, Joe Alexander McFarland, was president of his law school class at Ole Miss and was a county attorney and circuit judge in Jasper, Mississippi. Joe McFarland was so well respected that he was invited to be a judge at the Supreme Court of Mississippi.

Parker McFarland was raised in Cumming, graduated from South Forsyth High School in 1994, and obtained his B.A. degree in English at Covenant College. He earned his Juris Doctor degree from Mississippi College of Law in 2001, although he completed his final year of law school at the University of Georgia. Parker practiced law with his father, Robert “Bob” P. McFarland, Sr. at McFarland & McFarland, P.C. from 2001 until his father’s retirement in 2015.

Following a merger, Parker McFarland was brought to this firm as a partner in 2015. Since that time, the firm has been consistently been voted “Best of Forsyth.” Parker is a trial and appellate lawyer whose practice focuses on serious personal injury and wrongful death cases arising from auto accidents and others’ negligence. Through the firm’s core values of wisdom, integrity, prayer, excellence, and selflessness, Parker has secured many significant recoveries against auto insurance companies for serious injuries and wrongful death.

Parker is admitted to practice in all state, superior, federal, and appellate courts in Georgia as well as the United States Supreme Court.

Parker has served as attorney coach of the South Forsyth High School Mock Trial team since 2009. He is a past president of the Forsyth County Bar Association, member of the North Forsyth Rotary Club, and serves on the Board of Directors of Signature Awakening Ministries. Parker and his wife, Nicole, together with their three children, Mary Elizabeth McFarland, Robert Parker McFarland III, and Joshua VanMeter McFarland live in Cumming, Georgia and are active members of Restoration Church in Alpharetta.

Parker’s wife, Nicole, works in international missions, is an author, and highly sought after Bible teacher. Parker has coordinated the Forsyth County National Day of Prayer event since 2020 and also serves on the state team for Georgia National Day of Prayer.

attorneys.name: J. Michael McGarity Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Buford, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mike McGarity's practice focuses primarily in the areas of personal injury, wrongful death, civil litigation, family law, malpractice litigation, general business litigation and business law. He considers himself a problem solver/trial lawyer. He has represented individuals and their businesses in a wide variety of situations and complex areas. He believes in providing big firm quality with a small boutique firm service.

McGarity was named a "Georgia Super Lawyers" beginning in 2005, 2006 and again for 2008 by Atlanta Magazine and Law & Politics in the practice area of General Litigation and has received this award every year from 2008 forward. This is a peer review designation. Since 1987 he has been given an AV rating by the Martindale-Hubbell National Legal Directory, the highest such designation given for both lawyer competence and integrity.

McGarity graduated from Georgia Institute of Technology in 1976, receiving a Bachelor of Science degree in Industrial Management. Upon receiving his Juris Doctor from the University of Georgia School Of Law in 1979, McGarity joined the Gwinnett County District Attorney’s Office as an Assistant District Attorney.

In 1997, McGarity was appointed by Attorney General Thurbert Baker as Special Assistant Attorney General and for four years represented the Gwinnett County Child Support Enforcement Division. He was appointed by the Supreme Court of Georgia as Special Master in several disciplinary matters and has tried well over a hundred jury trials and hundreds of bench trials.

McGarity shifted into private practice, joining the Lawrenceville firm of Webb, Fowler, and Tanner as an associate. He became partner in that firm after trying many complex litigation cases, including wrongful death claims, medical malpractice, personal injury, multi-party claims, felony criminal trials and real estate litigation matters. McGarity was later named partner at Anderson, Tate, Mahaffey and McGarity, where he spent four and a half years before opening The McGarity Group in September of 2006.

McGarity is admitted to practice before the Supreme Court of Georgia, the Georgia Court of Appeals, The United States District Court for the Northern District of Georgia, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit.

McGarity is a member of the State Bar of Georgia, the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association, the Lawyers Club of Atlanta, the Old War Horse Lawyer's Club, and the Atlanta Bar Association and was a Past President of the Gwinnett County Bar Association. He is a current trustee of the Homer M. Stark Law Library Board of Trustees.

McGarity is an active community leader as well. He formerly served as president of the Northeast Georgia Council for the Boy Scouts (covering 26 Georgia counties) and was a trustee for Georgia Gwinnett College. He is a 1986 graduate of Leadership Gwinnett and a member of the Braselton Rotary Club, former member of the Gwinnett Chamber of Commerce Chairman's Club, former member of the Gwinnett County Board for the Department of Family and Children's Services and former member of the J.M. Tull YMCA Board of Directors (honored with Gwinnett's YMCA Volunteer of the Year Award). He and his wife, Caryn, live in the Braselton area of Gwinnett County with their gaggle of bird dogs.

attorneys.bio:
The Law Firm of Sean J. McIlhinney prides itself in fighting for justice and winning. The firm focuses on criminal defense with an emphasis on DUI and civil litigation. Sean authored an article titled "Brief Overview of Georgia's Law on DUI, Drug Crimes, License Suspensions & Parole" which can be accessed from his website.

Sean graduated cum laude from North Carolina State University in 1991 and completed law school at Georgia State University in 1995, where he again graduated with honors, cum laude, and was a member of the Law Review.

Upon graduation, Sean accepted a position at King & Spalding, the premier law firm in Atlanta and the Southeast, where he worked for approximately three years in the Products Liability Department as a litigator representing clients such as General Motors and Brown & Williamson, a tobacco manufacturer, in national high profile/high stakes cases.

In late 1998 Sean opened the firm and decided to fight for justice by representing individuals arrested and accused of DUI and crimes and people injured in accidents. With much hard work and great successes, the practice quickly expanded and now also represents many small businesses involved in civil litigation, contract disputes and collection of unpaid debts. Clients include IMEDEX USA, Inc., an international company with more than 50 employees, International Communications Inc., based in Knoxville, Tennessee, and numerous small to medium sized businesses located in the Atlanta metropolitan area such as InfoSoft Inc., Java Technologies, Inc., Statewide Siding and Quarry Truck Center, L.L.C.

Mary practices law with an unwavering commitment to her clients’ interests. She lives with her husband Doug and their three sons. Outside the office, she can usually be found hiking with her dog, Echo.

Direct Contact: 404-845-1954

Email: jmckinley@mfllaw.com

Mr. McKinley joined the firm as a partner in 2007. Mr. McKinley works in all areas of the firm’s defense litigation practice, including representation of self-insureds and insured companies in automobile and trucking cases, products liability, premises liability and other tort matters, as well as first-party representation of insurers in claims involving coverage, breach of contract and bad faith. He also represents insurers in suspicious or suspected fraudulent claims. He has presented seminars to claims professionals on a variety of insurance matters as an approved instructor with the Georgia Department of Insurance. He is a member of the Defense Research Institute.

Mr. McKinley also represents car dealers on various legal matters, including claims involving express and implied warranties, lemon law, the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act, fraud, bad faith, and other alleged breaches of contractual and tort obligations. He is a member of the National Association of Dealer Counsel.

Mr. McKinley previously served as an Assistant Attorney General for the State of Georgia, practicing in the Environmental and Civil Rights Litigation Sections of the Law Department and was also a partner at another Atlanta law firm.

Mr. McKinley received his undergraduate education at the University of Georgia and received his Juris Doctor degree from the University of Georgia School of Law, graduating cum laude in 1996. During law school, Mr. McKinley served on the Managing Board as an articles editor for the Georgia Journal of International and Comparative Law.

Mr. McKinley is a member of the American Bar Association and the Atlanta Bar Association. Mr. McKinley has been actively involved in the Georgia High School Mock Trial Program since 2002, including serving as an attorney coach.

In 2009, Super Lawyers magazine named Mr. McKinley as a Rising Star marking him as a top Georgia lawyer under age 40. No more than 2.5% of Georgia lawyers can be named a Rising Star.

Mr. McKinley was born in Falls Church, Virginia. He was admitted to the State Bar of Georgia in 1996 and has been admitted to practice in all trial courts in Georgia, the Georgia Supreme Court, the Georgia Court of Appeals, the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, and the United States District Courts for the Northern, Middle, and Southern Districts of Georgia.

attorneys.bio:
Andrew McMillen joined Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele, LLP in 2024 as an Associate Attorney in the firm's Litigation Department. His practice areas include Civil Litigation and Insurance / Liability Defense.

A native of Marietta, Andrew graduated from Louisiana State University in 2014 with degrees in Music Education and Music Performance and returned to Georgia in 2015 to serve as a high school band director in Fayetteville, Georgia. Andrew attended Georgia State University College of Law starting in 2021, where he served as a graduate assistant for the Academic Success Program and as Vice President of Academic Affairs for the Student Bar Association. While in law school, Andrew gained valuable experience working for the Honorable Eric Dunaway in Fulton County, the Office of the Attorney General of Georgia, the Cobb County District Attorney's Office, and as both a Summer Associate and later Law Clerk here at Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele, LLP.

Andrew returned to Marietta prior to law school and now lives there with his wife, Lisa, and their daughter, Annie. In his free time, Andrew loves cheering for the Braves, supporting all of LSU athletics, playing euphonium with the Cobb Wind Symphony, and working with local band programs.

attorneys.name: Paul Menair
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dahlonega, GA
attorneys.bio:
Paul Menair has practiced law for nearly two decades. He obtained his J.D. in 2002 and was admitted to the Georgia Bar in 2003.

After graduating from Georgia State University, Menair clerked for a United States District Court judge, handling dispositive motions at the trial level in federal court. After his clerkship, he went on to private practice, focusing primarily on civil litigation in both state and federal court, ranging from complex business, estate, and fiduciary disputes to tort and civil rights litigation.

Although Menair’s practice has mainly focused on litigation, he also has substantial transactional experience, including drafting and modification of trust and estate documents, contract drafting and review, and advising on fiduciary and corporate governance matters.

Menair is a certified mediator and is admitted to practice law in Georgia. He also holds a Ph.D. in history and has taught at the undergraduate level.

attorneys.name: Cecilia P. Mercer
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Athens, GA
attorneys.bio:
Cecilia P. Mercer, a longtime attorney known in the Athens community as Cici, focuses her practice in real estate, specifically residential and commercial property law. Her clientele will benefit from her assistance in matters of business and corporations, as well as wills.

A native of New York, Mercer graduated Magna Cum Laude from the University of South Carolina with a degree in business and accounting. In 1990, she earned her Juris Doctorate from the University of Georgia's School of Law. Following graduation, she became a faculty services reference librarian at the UGA Law Library, where she edited faculty treatises and articles. In addition, she worked with the Institute for Continuing Judicial Education and the Institute of Government. Cici was employed at both facilities throughout law school and gained valuable experience, all while running a household as a single parent of three children. Prior to working at Timmons, Warnes and Anderson, Cici was employed with another prominent real estate law firm in the area.

Mercer has taken every opportunity to be actively involved her community and in her field. She has training in mediation from the American Arbitration Association and in divorce mediation from Elizabeth Manley. Her knowledge of real estate and law is appreciated in all her affiliations. She is a member of several sections in the State Bar of Georgia, including real property, corporations and probate and trust. She is also a member of the Athens Area Board of Realtors, and a former member of the Board of Directors of Athens Area Habitat for Humanity.

attorneys.name: David M. Messer
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
David M. Messer is a Partner at Briskin, Cross & Sanford, LLC, bringing more than two decades of litigation and trial experience to the firm. Since joining the firm in 2007, David has built a reputation as a dynamic courtroom advocate and trusted advisor for companies, business owners, and executives across Georgia and Oklahoma.

David represents clients in a broad range of business and commercial disputes, with extensive experience in trials, appeals, mediation, and arbitration. His practice includes complex matters involving corporate and partnership disputes, high-value business litigation, oil and gas matters, homeowners’ association disputes, election challenges, and cases involving privately held and family-owned businesses. Clients value his strategic insight, steady demeanor, and ability to simplify complex issues to achieve efficient, favorable results.

Before relocating to Georgia, David practiced law in Oklahoma for six years, achieving both legally and socially significant courtroom victories and appellate results. In addition to his private practice, he served as Deputy General Counsel for Zynergy, Inc., where he advised on corporate and regulatory matters.

David is admitted to practice in Georgia and Oklahoma, as well as before the United States District Courts for the Northern, Middle, and Southern Districts of Georgia; the Northern and Eastern Districts of Oklahoma; and the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals in Denver.

A graduate of the University of Tulsa College of Law (J.D., highest honors, 2000), David also holds both Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees in Music. Since 2008, he has served as an Adjunct Professor at Reinhardt University, where he teaches business law and ethics. sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
David M. Messer is a Partner at Briskin, Cross & Sanford, LLC, bringing more than two decades of litigation and trial experience to the firm. Since joining the firm in 2007, David has built a reputation as a dynamic courtroom advocate and trusted advisor for companies, business owners, and executives across Georgia and Oklahoma.

David represents clients in a broad range of business and commercial disputes, with extensive experience in trials, appeals, mediation, and arbitration. His practice includes complex matters involving corporate and partnership disputes, high-value business litigation, oil and gas matters, homeowners’ association disputes, election challenges, and cases involving privately held and family-owned businesses. Clients value his strategic insight, steady demeanor, and ability to simplify complex issues to achieve efficient, favorable results.

Before relocating to Georgia, David practiced law in Oklahoma for six years, achieving both legally and socially significant courtroom victories and appellate results. In addition to his private practice, he served as Deputy General Counsel for Zynergy, Inc., where he advised on corporate and regulatory matters.

David is admitted to practice in Georgia and Oklahoma, as well as before the United States District Courts for the Northern, Middle, and Southern Districts of Georgia; the Northern and Eastern Districts of Oklahoma; and the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals in Denver.

A graduate of the University of Tulsa College of Law (J.D., highest honors, 2000), David also holds both Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees in Music. Since 2008, he has served as an Adjunct Professor at Reinhardt University, where he teaches business law and ethics. He is a frequent lecturer and advisor to churches and nonprofit organizations, combining his legal and leadership experience to support community initiatives.

Outside of his legal practice, David is an accomplished musician who enjoys playing piano and saxophone. He and his wife, Terri, reside in Johns Creek, Georgia.

attorneys.name: Brad Milkwick
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Savannah, GA
attorneys.bio:
Brad Milkwick is originally from Northwest Georgia and grew up in the Atlanta area. He entered law school after working many years in China, following graduation from college. Mr. Milkwick attended The Florida State University College of Law in Tallahassee, Florida where he had an impressive academic record, making the Dean's List regularly, earning merit-based awards, publishing in an International law journal, and graduating near the top of his class.

After law school, Mr. Milkwick practiced at a prestigious general trial practice firm in northwest Georgia before focusing his practice on workers compensation. Mr. Milkwick has practiced workers compensation law at the trial, appellate, superior court, and Court of Appeals level. He has tried some 70 cases in various courts throughout the state, achieving exceptional results for his clients.

Mr. Milkwick has given presentations at various seminars on workers compensation law and other legal subjects and has collaborated with Lexis-Nexis, a legal publishing company, to improve the way legal subjects are indexed in the book Georgia Workers' Compensation Laws, Rules and Regulations Annotated. Mr. Milkwick is proud to have received a number of awards for pro bono service on behalf of low-income families and the working community of Georgia.

Mr. Milkwick's hobbies include spending time with his family, playing piano and guitar, chess, coaching youth sports, reading, and being outdoors.

attorneys.name: Adian Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Rights Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Adian Miller is an attorney in the Labor & Employment department of Seyfarth Shaw LLP's Chicago office. Her practice focuses on ERISA claims.

Previously, Ms. Miller litigated cases before the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission on behalf of plaintiffs. She also has litigation experience with union trusteeship and anti-trust cases. She volunteered for four years, providing training to low-income workers and re-entry populations on their basic wage/hour and employment rights.

While attending law school in Washington, D.C., Ms. Miller clerked with the National Labor Relations Board, and was a Senior Policy Fellow with Polaris Project, drafting state legislation to combat trafficking. She has helped to pass tax legislation favoring limited-income cooperatives, and worked with non-profits providing comparative international legal analysis regarding personal status laws and women's rights.

attorneys.name: Jody A. Miller
attorneys.firm_name: Jody A. Miller, Esq. Attorney At Law
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law and Domestic Relations Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
At the Atlanta, Georgia, law office of Jody A. Miller, we have assisted clients with divorce, juvenile law and general family law issues for over 25 years.

Our philosophy is to provide outstanding and creative legal services in the area of general family law in an atmosphere in which client service and communication are our priorities. We never forget that while we deal with family law issues every day, this process is new to our clients, and each client deserves legal representation by an attorney who will take the time to listen, provide information and return phone calls.

Over the past 25 years, we have been called on to represent clients in a variety of disputes regarding alimony, child support, custody and visitation, paternity, legitimation, modification, enforcement and domestic violence. As a recognized leader in the area of family law, the Atlanta community has called on Ms. Miller to handle the most challenging cases.

In addition to her litigation experience, Ms. Miller is a certified mediator, collaborative law practitioner, guardian ad litem and parent coordinator.

Specialties: Family and Juvenile Law, Mediation, Collaborative Law, Guardian ad Litem, Parent Coordination, Divorce, Custody/Visitation, Child Support, Domestic Violence, Prenuptial Agreements, Legitimation, Paternity, Alimony, Adoption, Modification/Enforcement of all Domestic Relations Orders.

Justin Miller currently mentors and speaks to youths in and around the Atlanta area, and handles cases for families in Atlanta area juvenile courts. He handles a variety of personal injury cases, including those involving commercial trucks and other motor vehicles, pedestrian accidents, premises liability, and wrongful death.

attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of T. Andrew Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Workers Compensation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
T. Andrew Miller is a trusted and experienced workers’ compensation and personal injury attorney based in Atlanta, Georgia. For years, employers and insurance companies retained him to defend injury claims. Now he focuses his practice on serving the needs of injured workers and accident victims from all over the State of Georgia. Attorney Miller works only on a contingency fee basis, which means the client pays no attorney’s fees unless an award or settlement is obtained

Awards and Recognition

Named a “Rising Star” by Georgia Super Lawyers 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017

Highest Possible 10.0 Superb Rating on Avvo.com

AV-Preeminent Rated for Legal Ability, Professionalism and Ethics by Martindale-Hubbell

Perfect 5-Star Client Rating from Lawyers.com

Why Trust Your Case With The Law Offices of T. Andrew Miller?

Personal Attention: Other law firms with outlandish advertising budgets rely on having a high number of cases to make a profit. I choose to work with clients referred to me from other lawyers and medical professionals, and potential clients that contact me online. At my law firm, your case is one of a much smaller number, which results in more contact with you and more attention to your case.

Accessibility: As highlighted above, you want an attorney to handle your case, not support staff. With my law firm, you will almost always be contacted by me personally, especially when it comes to the crucial decisions in your case. I am typically available seven days a week and during non-business hours. Your injury claim is highly important to you, so I work to keep my clients informed when other law firms are either closed or too busy to have an attorney handle issues in your case. I am accessible to clients via telephone, text message and email.

No-Risk Legal Representation: Simply put, you owe nothing if you are not awarded a cash settlement in your case. No up-front fees, no billing invoices from my office, nothing! If we do not win, you do not pay any fees or expenses.

Skill, Experience and Knowledge of the Law: I spent years representing insurance companies in court and in settlement negotiations. I know the law and I know how to handle your case properly and efficiently. When it comes to settlements, I have the knowledge and experience to give you an honest and well-reasoned summary of what your case is worth and skill to negotiate a fair deal for you.

attorneys.name: Zachary J. Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lawrenceville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Zach Miller started college at the age of 16 while also attending High School via the “Fast Track” program at Wallace State Community College. Zach was able to receive his Associate’s degree before his high school diploma. Zach thereafter attended The University of Alabama at Birmingham with a Bachelors in Political Science and concentration in American Government and Philosophy. At UAB, Zach Miller was a proactive member of the UAB Pre-Law Society where he was nominated for President, was a member of Phi Theta Kappa Honor Society, UAB Golden Key International Honor Society, National Society of Leadership and Success, Presidential Honors List, and Cum Laude Honors.

Zach also attended Thomas Goode Jones School of Law with a Juris Doctorate. While at Thomas Goode Jones, Zach was a member of the Phi Alpha Delta Law Fraternity—Patterson Chapter, Black Law Student Association, and Women’s Legal Society. Additionally, among the handful of law articles that Zach wrote in law school, Zach received the CALI Award for Best Paper in Products Liability where he discussed the legal implications of vaping as well as the tax law implications on getting control over the regulations of such. Zach was also in the top third of his class. While in law school, Zach also worked on the highest levels of securities white collar crime with the Alabama Securities Commission, FINRA, and NASAA in efforts to protect investors.

After law school, Zach also attended Emory Law for an LLM in taxation. In Zach’s free time, he enjoys watching college football, going to the gym, spending time with family, and exploring the diverse restaurants that Atlanta has to offer.

attorneys.name: John T. Minor V
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Estate Planning Lawyers in Dalton, GA
attorneys.bio:
Having been a part of the Minor Firm family since he was three years old, John knows what it means to help clients find solutions. For nearly two decades, John has developed significant experience in complex estate planning and asset protection techniques, sophisticated tax planning, business law, elder care planning, health care law, regulatory issues, probate and estate administration, and guardianship law.

In helping individuals protect their assets, John focuses on trust strategies ranging from plans designed to protect the assets of high-net-worth individuals to strategies designed to protect the assets of families with seniors looking at potential long-term care options. John also has expertise in estate planning, wealth transfer planning, and complex tax planning. He brings unique perspectives to planning opportunities for blended families as well as for families with special needs. John stresses the importance of focusing not only on planning for death, but also on planning for issues that may arise during life, such as incapacity. Powers of attorney, health care directives, HIPAA authorizations, living wills, living trusts, and similar documents are necessities for everyone.

John also advises businesses and health care providers with business transactions, contracts, general practice matters, asset protection, employment matters, and similar matters. John has expertise in the complex regulatory issues surrounding the health care industry, such as the Stark and Anti-Kickback laws, HIPAA, Medicare and Medicaid, the False Claims Act, and many other areas.

In addition to assisting people plan during life, John assists people navigate the probate process, including tax strategies, postmortem planning opportunities, and estate disputes. John also handles guardianship matters, conservatorships, and other legal proceedings, bringing years of experience in the probate courts to his clients.

John values personal attention and communication as the foundation of effective problem-solving; he makes it his goal to truly know and care about his clients and the issues they face. From the simplest estate plan to the most complex, John focuses on detail.

He also values community involvement – he is active with nonprofit organizations in our communities, and he regularly speaks to the community on various legal matters. An Eagle Scout, John is twice a past president of the Cherokee Area Estate Planning Counsel. He has served for several years on the Executive Board of Directors of the Greater Dalton Chamber of Commerce, serving as Chair from 2024-2025. John serves on the Ethics Committee of Hamilton Medical Center and is a graduate of both the Leadership Catoosa and the Leadership Dalton-Whitfield programs. A past board member of Looper Speech and Hearing Center, John now serves on multiple nonprofit boards, including the Creative Arts Guild of Dalton, the Miracle League of Chattanooga (Founding Board Member), the Boys & Girls Clubs of Northwest Georgia, and previously on the United Way of Northwest Georgia’s campaign cabinet. He is also a member of the Rotary Club of Dalton and the Dalton Civitan Club.

John graduated Magna Cum Laude from Vanderbilt University in 2003, with majors in Music Composition and Theory and Cognitive Psychology. He received his Juris Doctorate from Mercer University, Walter F. George School of Law in 2006, and has been practicing with the Minor Firm ever since. A registered mediator, John is also a member of the Conasauga Bar Association and is a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys. John is admitted to practice law as a member of the state bars in both Georgia and in Tennessee.

attorneys.name: Glenda Mitchell
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Cartersville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Glenda Mitchell grew up in Greenville, South Carolina, where her strong sense of community and compassion for others took root early in life. After earning her bachelor’s degree from Anderson University, where she graduated summa cum laude, Glenda felt drawn to the legal field, specifically to advocating for those facing some of the most difficult times in their lives.

For more than 11 years, Glenda worked as a personal injury paralegal. This hands-on experience gave her not only an in-depth understanding of the law, but also a deep empathy for the clients she served. Driven by the desire to make an even greater impact, she pursued her Juris Doctor at Atlanta’s John Marshall Law School. There, she excelled academically, graduating magna cum laude and distinguishing herself as a dedicated student of the law.

Today, Glenda is the founder of Glenda Mitchell Law Firm, where she has built a practice devoted entirely to personal injury. Known for her relentless advocacy and genuine care for her clients, she has established a reputation as a trusted legal partner who stands by her clients every step of the way. Whether negotiating with insurance companies or standing up in court, Glenda is committed to securing justice and fair compensation for those injured through no fault of their own.

Beyond her legal work, Glenda is deeply involved in giving back to her community. She supports local causes, participates in outreach initiatives, and mentors young professionals who are pursuing careers in law.

attorneys.name: Nick C. Moraitakis
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Nick Moraitakis is an Atlanta trial lawyer with over 30 years of experience.

Early Legal Career

After graduating from Emory Law School in 1977, Nick immediately began practicing law with a defense litigation firm in downtown Atlanta, which eventually became known as Fain, Gorby, Reeves & Moraitakis. Nick went on to spend the first 14 years of his practice with this firm and its successor, representing insurance companies and self-insured corporations in the defense of tort actions in courts throughout the State of Georgia. As a defense lawyer Nick tried in excess of sixty cases to verdict involving automobile and truck accidents, product liability, negligent security claims, slip and fall accidents and insurance contracts among others.

Plaintiff's Practice

While with his defense litigation firm, Nick also began developing a plaintiff's practice. He successfully litigated product liability cases against Chrysler/Jeep/AMC, Nissan and Ford Motor Company involving product liability issues with heating and cooling systems, and fuel fed fires.

Nick also served as lead counsel in a highly publicized case against Atlanta Hospital. The case involved a doctor who was allegedly responsible for three deaths within a very short period of time. It was successfully resolved prior to trial based on negligent credentialing claims against Atlanta Hospital, which was investigated thereafter by the State Medical Review Board and eventually forced to close its doors.

In 1993, Nick and his partner Glenn Kushel began a plaintiff's practice dedicated exclusively to the representation of individuals injured or killed as a result of medical malpractice, nursing home abuse, trucking accidents, automobile accidents, product liability, premises liability and other negligent and intentional acts.

Notable Cases

Along with his partner, Nick successfully argued the case of Keenan v. Plouffe to the Georgia Supreme Court, which resulted in a landmark decision holding that a defendant physician, a faculty member of the Medical College of Georgia, was not immune from suit under the Georgia Tort Claims Act. Instead, the court held that the doctor could be individually liable and the case eventually settled for an amount exceeding seven and one half million dollars.

The firm also served as lead counsel in a significant case against the City of Atlanta, Marriott Hotels and a myriad of engineers and product liability manufacturers due to a sewer collapse under the parking lot of the Midtown Courtyard Hotel by Marriott in Atlanta. The case presented a complicated array of issues ranging from architectural and professional engineering responsibilities, professional standards to be exercised in the field of geotechnical engineering and municipal responsibility for negligent acts. After years of litigation, the case was resolved for a favorable settlement amount shortly before trial.

Nick, along with his partner Glenn Kushel, served as lead counsel in a negligent security case against the Metropolitan Atlanta Rapid Transit Authority (MARTA). The firm's client was stabbed at the Peachtree MARTA Station and having been offered nothing prior to trial, the case was tried successfully to a verdict of one million dollars. In addition, the firm recently settled another matter against MARTA involving a bus accident that rendered the plaintiff a quadriplegic.

attorneys.name: Nikki Jo Moreschi
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Johns Creek, GA
attorneys.bio:
Nikki Moreschi earned her undergraduate degree in Political Science from Edinboro State University of Pennsylvania and graduated magna cum laude in 1993. She attended The University of Dayton School of Law in Ohio and graduated with her Juris Doctor in 1996.

After admission to the Ohio State Bar, she worked for a large insurance defense law firm, handling complex civil litigation matters, including business litigation, medical malpractice, and wrongful death. Ms. Moreschi relocated to New York and was admitted to the New York State Bar in 2002. In New York, her practice focus centered on Family Law and Divorce, eventually leading her to open her own successful law practice in 2010. Ms. Moreschi served as an Attorney for Children for the State of New York ("Guardian ad Litem") for over a decade, advocating for the best interest of children in contested Family Law and Divorce proceedings.

Prior to relocating to Savannah, Georgia, the Hon. Nikki J. Moreschi served as a member of the New York State Judiciary in Glens Falls City Court. Mrs. Moreschi was admitted to the Georgia State Bar in 2021. With over 27 years of litigation and practice experience, Ms. Moreschi remains active in both the NYS Bar and the GA Bar.

attorneys.name: Richard M. Morgan Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Richard M. Morgan has been practicing law in Georgia since 1987. Richard founded the award-winning Alpharetta law firm of Morgan & DiSalvo, P.C. in 1995 to help individuals and families plan and prepare for the many changes that life brings. Morgan & DiSalvo was again named in U.S. News & World Report and Best Lawyers.com "Best Law Firms" ranking for 2015. Morgan & DiSalvo received the highest "Tier 1" rating in Trusts and Estates Law, a distinction held by only 10 law firms in the Metro Atlanta area.

Richard prides himself on bringing peace of mind to individuals and families by helping them prepare for significant life events. Richard specializes in finding creative solutions for clients in the areas of estate & tax planning, estate & trust dispute resolution, business succession planning, planning for special needs beneficiaries, charitable gift planning and tax controversies.

Richard's work is differentiated by his level of service and attention to detail. His technical and analytical capabilities and problem-solving approach are unique among attorneys. A leader in his field, Richard is past president of the Taxation Sections of both the Georgia and Atlanta Bar Associations, the Estate Planning & Probate Section of the Atlanta Bar Association, the North Georgia Estate Planning Council and the Georgia Planned Giving Council. Richard also serves on the Executive and Legislative committees of the Fiduciary law section of the Georgia Bar Association.

In 2014, Richard was elected as a Fellow in The American College of Trust and Estate Counsel (ACTEC). This is the most prestigious group of Trusts and Estates attorneys in the country, with only 50 Fellows in the State of Georgia. ACTEC membership is only offered to those who have provided substantial contributions to the field of trusts and estates law. Richard has used his charitable gift planning expertise over the years by serving as the chairman or member of professional advisory committees of several large Atlanta organizations including the Jewish Federation of Greater Atlanta, Jewish Family & Career Services, the Community Foundation of Greater Atlanta and YMCA of Metropolitan Atlanta.

Richard received is B.B.A. in Accounting, cum laude, and his J.D. degree, cum laude, from the University of Georgia. He received his LL.M. in Taxation from Emory University. Richard is a frequent speaker on estate and tax planning, charitable gift planning and other tax related topics.

Richard loves life and all that it has to offer, but his greatest accomplishments have all related to his wonderful and loving family, including his incredible wife and three children, and of course, now two Goldendoodles.

attorneys.name: Charles E. "Chuck" Morris Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury and Wrongful Death Lawyers in Cedartown, GA
attorneys.bio:
Charles E. Morris, Jr. (Chuck)

Chuck grew up Helena, Alabama, and graduated from Pelham High School in 1988. In 1992, Chuck received a B.A. in Theatre Arts and Speech at the University of the South in Sewanee, Tennessee.

In 1998, Chuck earned his Juris Doctor, magna cum laude, at Georgia State University’s College of Law. While in law school, Chuck was a member of the Student Trial Lawyers’ Association, and competed as a member of Georgia State’s trial team. Chuck served as an intern for Georgia Supreme Court Justice Carol Hunstein, and Fulton County Superior Court Judge Alford Dempsey. Chuck also completed an internship at the Georgia Indigent Defense Council’s Appellate Division, learning appellate law and practice under the mentorship of Appellate Division Director James C. Bonner, Jr.

Chuck joined the Law Firm of Parker and Lundy upon graduation from law school in 1998. Chuck has been admitted to practice before all levels of Georgia’s courts, including the United States District Court, the Georgia Court of Appeals and the Georgia Supreme Court. Since beginning his practice, Chuck has worked on his clients’ behalf to obtain substantial six-figure and seven-figure recoveries by litigating their cases to conclusion with jury trials, workers’ compensation trials, and settlement mediations. Chuck is a member of the Georgia Trial Lawyers’ Association, the State Bar of Georgia, the American Bar Association and the American Association of Justice.

In addition to his law practice, Chuck serves as an Associate Judge for the Juvenile Courts of Polk and Haralson Counties. As a part-time judge, Chuck hears cases involving allegations of delinquency and dependency on a weekly basis. Chuck’s work with the Juvenile Court provides opportunities to assist at-risk children and youth by obtaining vital services and support within the community.

Chuck has been active in the community since he began his law practice. Chuck has served as chair of the Tallapoosa Judicial Circuit Re-Entry Coalition, served on the Board of the Cedartown Walk of Fame Committee and Downtown Development Association, served as President of the Tallapoosa Bar Association, Campaign Chairman for the Cedartown United Fund, and President of the Cedartown Kiwanis Club.

Chuck has also re-kindled his interest in the Theatre, directing, producing and appearing in many productions in Cedartown and Rome. Chuck, his law partner Bill Lundy, and Bill’s wife Catharine founded the Cedartown Theatrical Performers’ Company which provided performing opportunities for Cedartown children and teenagers. In addition to his efforts with Cedartown Theatrical Performers’ Company, Chuck has served as President of the Board of Directors of Rome Little Theatre, Chairman of the Cedartown Civic Arts Commission Board of Directors, and Chairman of the Historic DeSoto Theatre Foundation.

Chuck has been active in the community since he began his law practice. Chuck has served as chair of the Tallapoosa Judicial Circuit Re-Entry Coalition, served on the Board of the Cedartown Walk of Fame Committee and Downtown Development Association, served as President of the Tallapoosa Bar Association, Campaign Chairman for the Cedartown United Fund, and President of the Cedartown Kiwanis Club.

Chuck has also re-kindled his interest in the Theatre, directing, producing and appearing in many productions in Cedartown and Rome. Chuck, his law partner Bill Lundy, and Bill’s wife Catharine founded the Cedartown Theatrical Performers’ Company which provided performing opportunities for Cedartown children and teenagers. In addition to his efforts with Cedartown Theatrical Performers’ Company, Chuck has served as President of the Board of Directors of Rome Little Theatre, Chairman of the Cedartown Civic Arts Commission Board of Directors, and Chairman of the Historic DeSoto Theatre Foundation.

attorneys.bio:

Morrison's practice focuses in the areas of family law, where he effectively represents clients in divorces, child custody disputes, modification of child support and alimony, and related domestic issues. He is able to utilize his background as a financial analyst to effectively work with accountants and other professionals in evaluating assets to ensure that clients are treated fairly and given an equitable share of their marital assets. He has successfully represented individuals and business entities in breach of contract claims and shareholder disputes involving closely held corporations.

Prior to attending law school, he worked for four years as a financial analyst for a fortune 500 company. Currently, Mr. Morrison resides in Marietta with his wife, Susan, and their four children, Alexandra, Joseph, Emma and Sophia.

attorneys.name: Brianna Moscowitz
attorneys.firm_name: The Siemon Law Firm Divorce and Family Law Attorneys, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Cumming, GA
attorneys.bio:
Brianna is an accomplished family and fertility law attorney known for her dedication, compassion, and unwavering advocacy for individuals and families navigating challenging personal and legal circumstances.

Brianna’s commitment to family law began during her undergraduate studies at the University of Miami, where she gained significant experience managing the nonprofit organization Silent Victims of Crime. In this role, she provided leadership and essential support to children with incarcerated parents, developing a deep understanding of the profound impact legal matters have on children and their families. This experience was foundational, strengthening Brianna’s resolve to advocate for vulnerable individuals within the legal system. She further expanded her expertise by serving as a Guardian ad Litem, advocating tirelessly on behalf of foster children and deepening her insight into the complexities inherent in family law proceedings.

After earning her undergraduate degree, Brianna pursued her Juris Doctor at Emory University School of Law in Atlanta. During her time at Emory, she actively sought opportunities to enhance her practical legal experience, completing multiple internships at the Atlanta Legal Aid Society. Through these internships, Brianna gained extensive knowledge and skills in divorce, custody, adoption, and guardianship matters, solidifying her passion and expertise in family law.

Brianna is committed to delivering personalized legal services, ensuring each client feels understood and supported while advocating diligently for their best interests.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Norcross, GA
attorneys.bio:
As a highly experienced personal injury attorney, John began fighting for the rights of victims who have suffered catastrophic injuries when he began practicing law in 1991. He focuses on railroad, trucking, and other types of injury cases.

John attended Furman University on an Army ROTC scholarship, and there he earned his undergraduate degree before being commissioned into the US Army upon graduation. He went on to complete his legal studies at Georgia State University and served as a JAG officer for 10 years in the Georgia Army National Guard.

Since 2008, John has given back to future litigators by teaching trial skills to 2nd year law students as an adjunct professor of advocacy

He has tried cases in six states resulting in numerous 7-figure verdicts and settlements for his clients. For more than 32 years John has worked tirelessly to help personal injury clients obtain the compensation they deserve. John and his wife Mimi live in Georgia, and in his free time he enjoys golfing and keeping active.

attorneys.name: John Moss
attorneys.practice_type: Rail Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
John A. Moss is a partner in Steel & Moss, LLP. For over twenty years he has practiced exclusively as a plaintiff's trial lawyer litigating in state and federal courts, primarily on behalf of injured railroad workers under the Federal Employers' Liability Act. He has litigated extensively on behalf of injured workers in all kinds of cases, including death, catastrophic injury, paraplegia, and amputation.

More recently, he has focused part of his time on whistleblower cases under 49 USC 20109 in which he represents rail workers against whom the railroad has retaliated following the report of a personal injury. These cases proceed in both the administrative context and in federal court. To see representative cases, please click the link below.

In addition to a full time trial practice, Mr. Moss has taught for the last seven years as an adjunct professor of advocacy to second year law students at the Georgia State College of Law in Atlanta. The class teaches essential litigation and trial skills to students who are closing in on graduation and the practice of law.

Mr. Moss is a native of Asheville, NC and has lived in Atlanta for most of his life. He graduated from Woodward Academy, Furman University, and the Georgia State College of Law. After completing college on an Army ROTC scholarship, he fulfilled his service obligation as a JAG officer in the Georgia Army National Guard for ten years.

attorneys.name: Doyle E. Mullis III
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Doyle is from Savannah and was raised in Hinesville, GA.

He attended the University of Tampa and was commissioned in the Infantry in the Army Reserve.

After law school at Mercer University, Doyle transferred to the JAG Corps and served as a military attorney until his military retirement. Doyle concurrently served with the Department of Defense (DoD) as a civilian special agent.

Doyle met his wife in Macon during the Flood of '94 when she was a water distribution volunteer, and he was in Macon on disaster relief duty. They returned to Macon after retiring from the DoD. They enjoy spending time with their church family.

As a DoD agent, Doyle was responsible for investigating complex criminal, civil, and administrative matters. Doyle investigated matters pertaining to contracts and vendors; healthcare false claims; employee misconduct; and bribery, kickbacks, and theft. Doyle's work frequently involved audits and external inquiries.

Doyle has expert knowledge conducting business and non-profit investigations and can help organizations and their attorneys when workplace allegations or government accusations are made against individuals or the organization. Doyle's work portfolio included compliance and due diligence matters. Prior to joining Anderson, Walker & Reichert, Doyle served as a consultant to the Department of Justice's Market Integrity and Major Frauds unit.

As a military attorney, Doyle counseled service members and their families on financial planning, and prepared wills, powers of attorney, and medical directives implementing estate plans. In addition, Doyle has extensive work experience with banking and other financial service areas.

Doyle helps individual clients plan the disposition and distribution of their assets to obtain long-term care and beneficiary goals. He assists clients with developing financial plans and strategies that include utilization of Social Security, Medicare, SSI, and Medicaid benefits. Doyle helps disabled family members with special needs via trusts and other strategies to maximize and protect assets.

Doyle assists businesses and other entities with workplace and government inquiries, to help protect stakeholder interests, while establishing facts and resolving issues arising from operations.

These internal investigations are necessary for clients to know what an outside entity will be evaluating and seeking.

Doyle also supports Anderson, Walker & Reichert's defense of military personnel, and military administrative matters.

attorneys.name: Albert Myers III
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
A native of Springfield, Illinois, Mr. Myers attended Yale University, majoring in History. He continued his education at the New York University Leonard N. Stern School of Business, where he pursued studies in business accounting and finance. He received his Juris Doctorate, magna cum laude, from New York Law School in 1994, where he was the John Ben Snow Scholar, the Executive Articles Editor of the New York Law School Law Review, a Teaching Fellow, and Moot Court coach.

Al Myers has been practicing complex litigation since 1995, including securities, professional liability, shareholder, commercial, and business tort matters. Mr. Myers began his legal career in the Business and Securities Litigation department of Weil, Gotshal & Manges, LLP under Dennis J. Block and other luminaries of the securities defense bar. He continued his career at other prominent law firms on both the plaintiff side and the defense side, where he litigated complex, multi-jurisdictional disputes on behalf of corporations and their boards of directors, including shareholder class actions and derivative lawsuits, fiduciary claims, SEC and regulatory investigations, and business and commercial disputes. For six of his now twenty-five-year career, Mr. Myers chaired the shareholder derivative practice at a prominent New Orleans-based firm, where he was the handling partner for that firm’s many successes on behalf of shareholders and other clients.

Mr. Myers excels in all aspects of litigation and dispute resolution, including jury trials and appellate representation. He handles trials and arbitrations as a first-chair litigator and, in doing so, takes pleasure in working with clients, witnesses, and experts from varied backgrounds.
