attorneys.name: Sadarie Hines
attorneys.practice_type: Federal Employment Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
An Associate at Southworth PC, where her practice focuses on Federal Employment Law, a field in which she represents clients before pivotal institutions such as the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the Merit Systems Protection Board, and Federal Court. Her international background, hailing from the United Kingdom with a vibrant legal career that spans across both the UK and the United States, equips her with a distinct perspective and creative approach to law. Sadarie is a New York licensed attorney, renowned for her eloquence, strategic thinking, and drive to help ensure professional legal outcomes for her clients.

Sadarie embarked on her legal journey inspired by a childhood vision, nurtured by her late father through a simple yet impactful gift—a book portraying a young girl as a lawyer. This image resonated with her, guiding her towards a fulfilling career in law, where she has been able to leverage her voice for those who cannot. Graduating with honors in Law with Social Sciences, and further enriching her knowledge with a postgraduate research diploma in Women and the Law from the London Metropolitan University School of Law, Sadarie has always been driven by a passion for public law and service.

Before joining Southworth PC, Sadarie's career was marked by significant roles, including serving as an In-house locum lawyer for UK Local Authorities and working under a Georgia Special Assistant Attorney General. She has also dedicated herself to pro bono work, notably assisting underserved communities with housing and landlord issues through the Atlanta Volunteer Lawyers Foundation.

Sadarie values the "one team" ethic at Southworth PC, crediting it with her professional growth, especially through opportunities to draft briefs for complex cases requiring innovative solutions.

attorneys.name: Brooks Neely
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Brooks Neely is the associate attorney at the Zagoria Law Firm. Originally from Birmingham, AL, Brooks attended Auburn University, where he earned his B.S. in Health Administration in 2000. Before becoming an attorney, Brooks worked in the medical field for ten years, seven of those as a medical equipment/device representative, and two of those as the co-owner of a boutique medical equipment company. During his time as a medical sales rep, Brooks worked tirelessly to help hundreds of clients to procure thousands of pieces of necessary medical equipment. Also during this time, Brooks learned to navigate the intricacies of Medicare and various insurance companies’ claims processes, and regularly advocated on his clients’ behalf in claims disputes. Brooks received his J.D. from Atlanta’s John Marshall Law School in 2013, where he worked as Dean Richardson Lynn’s Research Assistant his 3rd year. Brooks’s work history dovetails nicely with his career as a plaintiff’s attorney: he is passionate about plaintiff’s work and compassionate for his clients.

Brooks is an above-average home cook and a below-average golfer. He is married to his wife and traveling companion of 10 years, Dawn, and the two reside in Cobb County where they are members of St. Benedict’s Episcopal Church.

attorneys.bio:
Rich Neville is a Cumming, Georgia native and founder of Neville Law, LLC. Rich has practiced law in Cumming for over 30 years and founded Neville Law, LLC, in 2022, following the retirement of his law partner. Rich has practiced law in Cumming, Georgia and has successfully handled injury cases, including motor vehicle and trucking cases, product injury cases, slip/trip fall cases, will contests, fiduciary litigation cases, real property litigation, and business litigation cases. Rich has obtained winning verdicts, judgements, and appellate decisions and favorable settlements for his clients. Rich's primary motivation is to achieve a favorable outcome for his clients.

Rich resides in Cumming and is a father of three children. He is a member of Deer Creek Shores Presbyterian Church and has served as Clerk of the Session and Elder. He is a member and past president of the Forsyth County Bar Association and member and past president of the Forsyth County Rotary Club. He is a member of Georgia Trial Lawyers Association and Lawyers Club of Atlanta.

Rich serves part time as Chief Judge for the City of Cumming Municipal Court. Rich also serves as county administrator and county conservator by appointment of the Forsyth County Probate Court and also serves as Special Master and Receiver by appointment of the Forsyth County Superior Court.

attorneys.name: Katherine Hung Newsom
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Katherine Hung Newsom is a partner in the Morgan & Morgan Atlanta office. She is committed to defending the rights of all injured workers.

Ms. Newsom grew up in Columbus, Georgia. She received her undergraduate degree in Psychology from Boston College. She earned a Masters of Social Work and her law degree from the University of Georgia.

Her commitment to justice goes back to law school where she dedicated countless hours to the Equal Justice Foundation - a student run organization that raises money to provide summer stipends for law students who choose to work in unpaid, public interest positions. She was the President of EJF during her third year of law school. She also served as the Director of the 1st and 2nd Annual EJF 5K Runs.

After law school, Ms. Newsom worked as a law clerk for the Superior Courts of the Western Judicial Circuit in Athens, Georgia. She then clerked for a State Court Judge in Gwinnett County. Following her clerkships, she moved to Atlanta to work for an insurance defense firm.

After several years representing insurers and employers, she left insurance defense to represent injured workers. She has represented injured workers exclusively since 2005. Ms. Newsom's background in psychology and social work, combined with her past insurance defense work, inform her perspective and approach to representing injured workers in Georgia.

She lives in Atlanta with her husband, Sedgie, and their rescue dog, Max. She is proud to be a member of the Morgan & Morgan team.

attorneys.name: Keenan R.s. Nix
attorneys.practice_type: Business Tort Litigation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Keenan R.S. Nix is a partner of the trial law firm of Morgan & Morgan. He graduated from the Wharton School of Business and The University of Pennsylvania School of Law. By trade, Mr. Nix is a dynamic trial lawyer whose skill and passion in the courtroom are legendary. A true champion of justice, his impressive string of million dollar verdicts and settlements have earned him a reputation as one of Georgia's finest trial lawyers on the side of injured people. In 2016, Mr. Nix led the trial team that won an $11 million dollar verdict against Papa John's Pizza for brain damaging his client for life in a head-on collision, and then refusing to accept any responsibility for the wreck. That eight figure verdict against the national pizza chain was named one of the top 10 verdicts in the country for 2016.

His trial practice focuses on catastrophic injury, wrongful death, and business tort litigation. He annually is recognized by his peers as one of Atlanta's "SuperLawyers," and he was inducted into the Gate City Bar Association "Hall of Fame" in 2018. As a leader in the trial bar, Mr. Nix frequently teaches on the subject of trial advocacy, and bi-annually chairs a continuing legal education seminar on representing victims of traumatic brain injury, and coordinates the annual Excellence through Education seminar series for the Gate City Bar Association.

When he is away from the courtroom, Mr. Nix enjoys traveling, gardening, and college football. He is a published author, gifted motivational speaker and highly regarded radio talk show host. On the personal side, he has been married to Danielle Nix for 29 years, and they have three children, Rance (26), Glory (25), and Noah (21). He and his family are members of Ikon Community Church in Atlanta, Georgia.

attorneys.name: William H. Noland
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
William Noland, a highly experienced trial lawyer in Macon, has extensive experience presenting cases before juries and judges across state and federal courts throughout Georgia. With over two decades of experience, he has represented defendants in criminal and civil cases throughout Georgia in both state and federal courts.

Mr. Noland provides representation in matters concerning criminal defense, DUI defense, federal criminal defense, personal injury, and employee and whistleblower rights. He prides himself on representing those who have been falsely accused, injured by the negligence of others, or who are navigating an unfair and oppressive working environment.

Mr. Noland graduated from Auburn University in 1997 and earned his Doctor of Jurisprudence from Mercer University's Walter F. George School of Law in 2000. He received his license to practice law in Georgia in 2000 and has been admitted to practice in all Georgia state courts, the U.S. District Courts for the Middle and Northern Districts of Georgia, the Georgia Court of Appeals, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit and the Georgia Supreme Court.

Mr. Noland has tried dozens of cases to verdict and prides himself on his work and skill in the courtroom.

A prominent figure in his legal community, Mr. Noland has served as the past president of the Macon Bar Association, the William Augustus Bootle American Inn of Court and the Macon Bar Young Lawyers Division. He is also affiliated with the Georgia Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

In acknowledgment of his exemplary professionalism and service, Mr. Noland has received an AV-Preeminent* peer-review rating through Martindale-Hubbell, alongside other high rankings and endorsements from his peers. Moreover, the Macon Bar Association honored him with the 2016 William Augustus Bootle Professionalism Award.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer-review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Ratings™ fall into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Amir Nowroozzadeh is the founding attorney of Nowrooz Law Group LLC in Atlanta, Georgia. Since 2013, Amir has provided legal representation in a wide range of personal injury and litigation matters. When someone is injured by no fault of their own, he is there to help protect legal rights and pursue maximum compensation. He is committed to advocating for his clients with skill, dedication and personalized attention.

Graduating cum laude from the College of William and Mary in Virginia, Amir earned his Bachelors’ degree in Business Administration, double majoring in Process Management & Consulting and International Relations. Amir worked as an assistant at King & Spalding, Atlanta’s oldest and one of its most prestigious law firms, before pursuing his Juris Doctor at the University of South Carolina School of Law. His academic achievements reflect a strong foundation in analytical thinking, problem-solving, and strategic planning, skills he brings to every case.

Amir has extensive litigation experience, having worked for four years in insurance defense before joining a large plaintiff firm, where he leveraged his skills to advocate for clients injured in Atlanta, throughout Georgia, and throughout South Carolina. His professional background equips him with a comprehensive understanding of both sides of personal injury cases, providing a significant advantage for his clients.

A native of Atlanta, Amir grew up in an entrepreneurial family, fostering an outgoing and spirited personality that translates into passionate advocacy in the courtroom.

attorneys.name: Daniel J. O'Connor
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Vidalia, GA
attorneys.bio:
Daniel J. O’Connor focuses his legal practice on helping individuals, families, and business owners build strong legal foundations before problems arise. His work emphasizes thoughtful planning, clear communication, and durable solutions designed to protect what clients are working toward and help ensure it can be passed on to the next generation.

As a husband and father, Daniel understands that most people are not just managing assets. They are building lives, families, and legacies. Like many of his clients, he works hard to model a strong work ethic, provide stability and opportunity for his children, and preserve both financial security and shared values. Those priorities shape how he practices law and how he advises his clients.

Throughout his career, Daniel has seen how the absence of planning can undermine even the best intentions. Without the right structure in place, families can lose wealth, businesses can fracture, and relationships can suffer. His mission is to help clients avoid those outcomes by educating them, identifying risks early, and implementing practical plans that align with their goals. In short, he helps clients plan wisely, protect what they are building, and pass it on with confidence.

Daniel places a strong emphasis on education and long-term relationships rather than one-time transactions. He believes that good planning is not about documents alone, but about helping clients understand how the pieces fit together. That philosophy guides his work in estate planning, real estate transactions, and business formation and transfers, where careful planning can prevent disputes and preserve value over time.

Early in his career, Daniel practiced as a generalist, handling a wide range of matters both in and out of court. Over time, he recognized that strong outcomes require focus and depth. Buildings fail without proper design, and legal plans are no different. Rather than trying to do everything, he chose to concentrate his practice on areas where he could develop meaningful expertise and provide consistent, high-quality counsel. That decision was shaped by seeing the unnecessary cost, stress, and disruption clients often face when planning is delayed or handled without experienced guidance.

Daniel believes that investing in a solid legal foundation pays dividends in peace of mind, efficiency, and stability. With the right plan and trusted advisors, clients can spend less time reacting to problems and more time building businesses, supporting families, and enjoying life.

Daniel joined the firm in 2012 and partnered with Macky Bryant in 2017 to form Bryant & O’Connor Law Office. In 2021, he became the sole owner of the firm and sharpened its focus on helping families and small business owners plan for the future through estate planning, real estate, and business planning.

Born and raised in Montgomery County, Georgia, Daniel is proud to practice law in the Vidalia area. He has long believed that rural communities deserve the same level of professional service and leadership as larger markets. In addition to his private practice, he serves as City Attorney for the City of Vidalia and other local municipalities, and he represents multiple boards of education and a development authority. He views this work as part of a broader commitment to building strong communities, supporting responsible growth, and helping local institutions succeed.

Daniel earned his Juris Doctor from Mercer University School of Law in 2012, where he served on Law Review, and his Bachelor of Arts in English from the University of Georgia in 2009. He is licensed to practice law in all Georgia state courts and the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Georgia. He has been recognized as a Super Lawyers Rising Star in 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025 and is a graduate of Leadership Georgia’s 2020–2021 class, as well as the Leadership Toombs-Montgomery County program.

Outside the office, Daniel is a devoted husband to his wife, Rizza, and a proud father to Judson and Evie. He is an active member of Vidalia Cornerstone Church and has served as President of the Vidalia Kiwanis Club. He enjoys studying the Bible, reading history and personal development books, following college football, spending time outdoors with his family, and sharing good food and drink with family and friends.

attorneys.name: Lori C. Obenauf
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law -Divorce, Custody, Support, Visitation, Adoption, Deprivations Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Originally from Thomasville, Georgia, Lori C. Obenauf has lived in Macon since 1979 when she enrolled at Mercer University. She obtained her Bachelor of Arts in 1983 and went on to earn her Juris Doctorate from Mercer University's Walter F. George School of Law in 1986.

A member of the State Bar of Georgia since 1986, Ms. Obenauf has engaged in the practice of law, serving over seven years as an indigent defense panel attorney in the Superior Court of Bibb County. For four years, she served as a contract attorney in the Bibb County Juvenile Court handling delinquency and deprivation cases and acting as a guardian ad litem. Additionally, she served as a panel attorney representing indigents in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Georgia.

Lori Obenauf spent two years as the Director of Paralegal Studies at Middle Georgia College, where she also taught the Legal Environment of Business. For over fourteen years, Ms. Obenauf was engaged in the management of the Recovery and Bankruptcy departments in the financial services industry. She returned to the active practice of law in 2010 specifically to specialize in areas of Family Law (Divorces, Adoptions, and Custody) and in areas of Criminal Defense. Since that time, she has developed specialized knowledge in the areas of Military Divorce Law so that she is better able to assist her military clients.

In addition to her experience as a neutral mediator, she has gained valuable insight into the necessary negotiation skills needed to achieve outcomes that are in her clients' best interests.

Because she is well versed in a wide variety of business and legal matters, Lori Obenauf is well-qualified to handle your legal matters efficiently and expertly.

attorneys.name: Todd J. Obijeski
attorneys.practice_type: Chemical & Life Sciences Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
With fifteen years' experience and 6 U.S. Patents during a career in industry with major polymer film and plastics/packaging companies and a Fortune 50 chemical company, Todd truly understands the pressures and time constraints on inventors in the corporate world. He can put himself in his clients' shoes because he has been there, and he uses that insider's experience to produce top-quality legal work for his clients.

Todd is a registered patent attorney in the Atlanta office of Merchant & Gould. He is experienced in drafting and prosecuting U.S. patent applications, corresponding with foreign associates and prosecuting foreign applications, assisting in foreign opposition proceedings, drafting patent landscape reports, and drafting freedom to operate and invalidity opinions. Todd also has experience in inter partes reexaminations.

Todd handles patent matters in the material, pharmaceutical, chemical, superconductivity, thin film, coating/adhesive, polymer, catalyst, foam, packaging, wire & cable, flooring, medical device, semiconductor, instrumentation, and machinery/equipment industries.

Todd serves on the Georgia State University College of Law Intellectual Property Advisory Board, and co-chairs the CIP CUP (Charity IP) Golf Tournament, proceeds from which benefit the Georgia Lawyers for the Arts, GSU Public Interest Law Association, and GSU IP Scholarship Fund.

Todd is married with three children. He enjoys attending his kids' sports events and activities, and traveling to the beach in Destin, Florida, with his family.

attorneys.name: David W. (Dave) Orlowski
attorneys.practice_type: Banking and Corporate Law Lawyers in Albany, GA
attorneys.bio:
David W. (Dave) Orlowski was born in Mattituck, New York in 1964. He attended Wake Forest University as a Guy T. Carswell Scholar, graduating cum laude in 1987. He then attended The University of Georgia School of Law, receiving his J.D. in 1991. Mr. Orlowski was a partner of the firm of Hodges, Erwin, Hedrick & Coleman, LLP. Thereafter, he served as in-house counsel, as well as Vice-President of the legal department, for Heritage Bank of the South. Mr. Orlowski is a member of Lee Durham, LLC, which he joined in April 2004.

Early in his career, workers’ compensation and insurance defense were Mr. Orlowski’s primary concentration. His practice is now predominantly focused on the areas of banking and corporate law, creditor representation in bankruptcy matters, corporation formation and governance, business litigation, real estate, commercial transactions, and workers' compensation.

Mr. Orlowski is a member of the Dougherty Circuit Bar Association and State Bar of Georgia, including its Agriculture, Banking, Bankruptcy, and Workers' Compensation sections, as well as being an associate member of Georgia Bankers Association.

He is an active member of St. Paul's Episcopal Church, where he serves as Chancellor and Finance Chairman. Mr. Orlowski is on the Board of Directors of Easter Seals Southern Georgia, having served as President two separate terms and was honored as Easter Seals Volunteer of the Year in 2014. He has served as adjunct professor at Albany State University West Campus (formerly Darton College).

A soccer enthusiast, Mr. Orlowski is licensed by U.S. Soccer as a National D coach. Currently serving as President of the South Georgia United Soccer Academy, he also serves on the Risk Management Board for the State of Georgia’s United Futbol Academy and is on the coaching staff of United Futbol Academy’s travel soccer club. Locally, Mr. Orlowski is head coach of the junior varsity and assistant coach of the varsity soccer teams at Deerfield-Windsor School.

Donald W. Osborne comes to Meriwether and Tharp with a wide array of expertise. He began his career as a judicial law clerk after graduating from Emory School of Law. He was later appointed by those judges as the Public Defender of the Cordele Judicial Circuit, handling and trying felony cases. Following his tenure there, he returned to Atlanta where he practiced in the area of Insurance Defense and Medical Malpractice Defense.

Don began practicing in the area of Family Law in 2001 and has been guiding clients through the delicate process of Family law cases ever since.

Don has extensive trial experience having tried over 200 jury and bench trials in Georgia and other states. Don is active in his community serving the City of Norcross as a member of the Norcross Housing Authority. He is involved in Community Theater and started the first Farmer's Market in Monroe Georgia. He lives with his wife. Michelle, and dog, Felix, in downtown Norcross and has four adult children living in various parts of the state.

Don served for many years as an instructor in the Emory Law School's, National Institute for Trial Advocacy, (NITA), as a part of the curriculum

attorneys.name: Greyson Oswalt
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Cartersville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Partner Greyson Oswalt-Smith is a native of Rome, Georgia, and has made Cartersville his home shortly before joining the Firm. He graduated Magna Cum Laude from Kennesaw State, then moved on to receive his Juris Doctor Degree from Florida State University's College of Law. While in law school, Greyson exhibited his trial skills by victoriously taking FSU's trial team to National competitions. Further, Greyson's excellent legal research and writing skills were displayed as Staff Editor for the Florida State University's Law Review.

While pursuing his education, Greyson served as an Intelligence Analyst and Non-Commissioned Officer in the United States Army Reserves for six years. Accordingly, Greyson demonstrates a high level of strategy when preparing and handling client's cases. He has gained valuable trial experience from his internships and previous experience at firms in the area of criminal defense by working through all phases of client's cases and comes to Cansino Blanchette & Oswalt- Smith, LLC with an excellent reputation for achieving results.

Greyson enjoys staying physically active and spending as much time as he can outdoors. When not outdoors, he enjoys reading about history and spending time with family and friends.

Attorney Oswalt-Smith focuses his practice on DUI defense, drug charges, and serious felonies, but is well equipped to handle all criminal law related matters big and small.

attorneys.firm_name: Owen Gleaton Egan Jones & Sweeney, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Aviation Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Owen has represented insurance companies since he left the State Attorney General’s office over thirty years ago. This practice has included direct representation in regulatory and transactional disputes as well as defense of insureds. His practice today involves defense of health care professionals and institutions in medical malpractice cases as well as aviation products liability cases. Mr. Owen was educated at LaGrange College (B.A., 1962) and Emory University (J.D., with distinction, 1971) where he was named to the Bryan Society and Order of the Coif. He served as Managing Editor, Journal of Public Law (1970-71). Mr. Owen is a member of the American Bar Association; Defense Research Institute, Georgia Defense Lawyers Association (Board of Directors), and the Lawyer-Pilots Bar Association. He was a carrier based pilot in the United States Navy (1963-1968) and served as Senior Assistant Attorney General, State of Georgia (1971-1975), representing the Insurance Commissioner and other State agencies.

attorneys.name: Rizza Palmares O’Connor
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Vidalia, GA
attorneys.bio:
A dedicated and compassionate attorney, Rizza Palmares O'Connor loves helping people succeed in their lives. Real estate, estate planning and small business law are the main focuses of her practice. She is a community leader and volunteer, helping families and business owners protect their assets and developing plans and solutions to expand their interests. Ms. O'Connor guides her clients through financial matters such as real estate loan closings and purchasing a home. In addition to assisting customers with the acquisition or financing of residential and commercial properties, she works closely with them to maintain the legality of their residences, families and businesses.

For eight years, Ms. O'Connor presided as the Toombs County's Chief Magistrate Judge, during which time she saw the anguish and suffering of several people. As an attorney, her goal was to enable her clients to alleviate their disputes and financial loss and give them a peace of mind. Implementing the solutions that she offers allows her clients to live peacefully without worrying about themselves or their loved ones if they passed away or became incapacitated.

Ms. O'Connor claims that getting one's legal affairs in order might be scary for many people because they are often confused and unsure of what needs to be done. She advises her clients to plan ahead with a dedicated legal advisor to avoid future hardships for their families.

After ten years of public service, Ms. O'Connor has just recently joined the Bryant and O'Connor law firm. She spent more than two years as an assistant district attorney and held numerous leadership positions within the State Bar of Georgia, including serving as the president of their Young Lawyers Division. She has extensive experience working with attorneys throughout Georgia, enhancing the provision of legal services in various communities.

A Savannah native, Ms. O'Connor is a Filipino immigrant child, whose parents made many sacrifices so she could have the best possible education. After completing her high school studies at Calvary Day School, she enrolled in the Mercer University to obtain her bachelor's degree and then decided to pursue her legal studies at the Walter F. George School of Law. While there, she was the president of the Student Bar Association, and she continues to serve on Mercer Law School's Alumni Board. She spent a year studying abroad in Oxford, England, and it turned out to be one of her favourite experiences, which inspired her love of travel and adventure.

Since 2011, Ms. O'Connor has lived in Vidalia, where she currently resides with Daniel, her husband, and their two kids, Judson and Evie. She enjoys social gatherings like events and parties. Both Ms. O'Connor and her husband raise their kids to have a sense of history, be inquisitive about the world around them, and be proactive about making a difference. She also enjoys all things Disney, playing practical jokes on her friends and watching feel-good films and TV shows.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Best Under 40, National Asian Pacific American Bar Association, 2020

Inaugural Young Alumni Council Volunteer of the Year Award, Mercer University School of Law, 2020

On the Rise 14 Under 40, Georgia Legal Awards by the Daily Report of ALM Media, 2019

25 Most Influential Asian Americans in Georgia, Georgia Asian Times, 2018

The Thomas Sewell Plunkeet Young Alumna Award, The National Alumni Association of Mercer University, 2017

attorneys.name: Joseph Padgett
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Savannah, GA
attorneys.bio:
Joseph Padgett is a founding partner of Hamilton & Padgett, LLC and leads the firm’s Brunswick office. He focuses his practice on personal injury and wrongful death cases, with deep experience in motor vehicle negligence and trucking accident litigation across both Georgia and Florida.

A native of Coastal Georgia, Joseph previously owned and operated semi-trucks in the Savannah area, giving him firsthand knowledge of the transportation industry. He began his legal career defending trucking and insurance companies but quickly shifted to representing injury victims, using the insights he gained to advocate for those harmed by negligence. His dedication to his law practice has earned him recognition as a Super Lawyers’ Rising Star from 2023 to 2025, an honor bestowed upon only the top 2.5% of attorneys under 40 in Georgia.

Joseph is bilingual in Spanish and proudly represents Spanish-speaking clients throughout Southeast Georgia. He is also a member of the Academy of Truck Accident Attorneys and a graduate of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association LEAD program.

Outside of the courtroom, Joseph enjoys life in Brunswick with his wife Julia and their three children.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Cartersville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Sydney Painter is an associate attorney at Trotter Deems & King LLC, focusing on family law and general litigation matters.

Sydney focuses her practice on representing individuals and families in matters such as divorce, child custody and support, modification of existing orders, and other general litigation disputes. She is dedicated to helping her clients navigate the complexities of the legal system, ensuring they understand their options, and advocating for their rights every step of the way.

With a client-centered approach, Sydney strives to provide practical solutions while prioritizing clear communication and personalized guidance. She understands that family and litigation matters can be stressful and emotionally challenging, and she works diligently to provide support, insight, and effective legal strategies to achieve the best possible outcomes for her clients.

Sydney earned her J.D. from John Marshall Law School and her B.S. in Psychology from Florida State University, providing her with a strong foundation in both legal principles and human behavior.

Outside of the office, Sydney enjoys spending time with her boyfriend, Austin, and their dog, Milo.

attorneys.name: James L. Paisley
attorneys.practice_type: DUI Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
James L. Paisley is an Atlanta native. He grew up in Marietta, GA and did his undergraduate work at Georgia Tech and graduated with high honors. After completing law school at Florida State University near the top of his class, he began his legal carrer as a public defender. This perspective did wonders before he switched sides and became a state prosecutor for several years. As a prosecutor Mr. Paisley got the experience of knowing most judges, and the most experienced attorneys and litigating with all of them. As a prosecutor Mr. Paisley tried over fifty jury-trials against the most reputable attorneys.

James L. Paisley was not meant to be a prosecutor.He realized that really good people make honest mistakes and they need effective representation at affordable prices. He missed the client contact and being able to help people put their life back together. He started his defense work again and started focusing on only traffic related cases like DUI's and other traffic citations. After opening his own practice, the firm has grown because people recognize how important their situation is to The Paisley Law Group.

attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Blake A. Poole, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Gainesville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Josh Panter is an associate attorney at the Law Office of Blake A. Poole, LLC. Josh attended the University of Cincinnati College of Law where he graduated Magna Cum Laude. While attending the University of Cincinnati College of Law, Josh interned for the Honorable Jerome J. Metz Jr. at the Hamilton County Court of Common Pleas. Josh also regularly engaged in pro bono work for the Immigrant & Refugee Law Center by performing legal research and writing pertaining to asylum cases. After law school, Josh joined Gatlin Voelker, PLLC as an associate attorney. At Gatlin Voelker, Josh performed legal work pertaining to a variety of legal matters spanning from illegal searches and seizures in criminal defense cases to violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

Josh was born and raised in Gainesville, Georgia. He graduated from Gainesville High School, and he is a member of the Gainesville Jaycees. Josh is married to his wife Brittany. Josh and Brittany met while attending Marshall University where he graduated with a B.A. in Political Science. They have a daughter named Adalaide.

Josh’s practice focuses solely on criminal defense. Josh aggressively defends his clients and their rights with skill and a meticulous attention to the details of each case.

attorneys.name: Amy Carol Parker
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Amy C. Parker is a lawyer dedicated to helping secure justice for her honorable clients. Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Ms. Parker was a banking and finance attorney with Dentons Atlanta (formerly Long, Aldridge & Norman) and then spent a decade working as an educator in Atlanta teaching students and teachers how to use technology and how to do research effectively. She brings those technology and research skills to her law practice, finding information that corporations and insurance companies would rather remain hidden.

Ms. Parker graduated from Florida State University with a degree in Accounting, cum laude, and then attended Mercer Law School, working on the Law Review's Managing Editor's staff and graduating cum laude. After her children reached school age, she obtained a Masters Degree in Information Systems, graduating summa cum laude at the top of the graduating class of more than 6,000 students, and taught research and technology skills until her youngest child began college at Georgia Tech. Returning to the practice of law under the masterful tutelage of Mssrs. Keenan Nix and Christopher Graddock, Ms. Parker is thrilled to work with these talented men to help their worthy clients.

When not practicing law, Ms. Parker enjoys volunteering at the venerable Fox Theatre with her husband, seeing Broadway shows and standout performers like Prince, Aretha Franklin, and Paul Simon, spending time with their six young adult children (ages 22-27), and playing with their two pampered and energetic pups.

attorneys.name: R. Kyle Paske
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
R. Kyle Paske is an Associate Attorney at Briskin, Cross & Sanford, LLC, where he represents businesses, executives, and individuals in commercial litigation and related transactional matters. His practice focuses on business ownership and partnership disputes, restrictive covenant and noncompete claims, contract disputes, and corporate governance issues. Kyle also advises clients on entity formation, business structuring, and risk management strategies designed to help prevent disputes before they arise.

Before joining Briskin, Cross & Sanford, Kyle practiced in Atlanta representing businesses and their insurers in a wide variety of civil defense matters, including personal injury, premises liability, and employment-related claims, including significant experience with workers’ compensation claims and premium disputes. This experience provides him with a valuable understanding of both sides of a dispute and informs his balanced, results-driven approach to litigation.

Kyle earned his J.D., cum laude, from the University of Florida Levin College of Law, where he competed nationally on the Securities and Business Litigation Moot Court Team. He received his B.S. in Political Science from the University of Central Florida. Kyle is admitted to practice in Florida and Georgia and is an active member of the North Fulton Bar Association.

Known for his efficiency and clear communication, Kyle focuses on achieving favorable outcomes through practical, tailored strategies that align with each client’s business objectives. He lives in Dunwoody, Georgia with his wife and three children and enjoys cooking, fly fishing, and sports.

attorneys.name: Ann Patterson
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Rome, GA
attorneys.bio:
Ann Patterson has been helping the people of North Georgia collect the government benefits they deserve for decades.

Growing up in Cumming, Georgia, she learned the importance of public service at an early age. She was active in 4-H, eventually becoming a State Officer, and also served as a camp counselor at Rock Eagle and Wahsega 4-H Centers. She first became interested in the law as a teenager, while babysitting the children of the youngest Superior Court judge in the state of Georgia. After putting his children to bed, she would stay up and read the transcripts from his trials, dreaming of one day becoming an attorney.

In 1975, after graduating from Forsyth County High School, Ms. Patterson left Cumming to make her dream come true. In 1979, she graduated from the University of Georgia, with degrees in Political Science and Criminal Justice. A loyal fan of the Georgia Bulldawgs - she drives a red and black car to this day - she stayed in Athens to attend the UGA School of Law. Her legal studies also took her further afield. She spent two summers working in Washington, DC, first for Senator Sam Nunn, and then for the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. She also studied one semester at the University of Athens Law School, in Athens, Greece. In 1982, she graduated with her Juris Doctor, and became a proud member of the Georgia Bar.

Ms. Patterson then returned home to North Georgia, where she has had a distinguished legal career. She was the first female appointed Assistant District Attorney in the Lookout Mountain Judicial Circuit, which serves Catoosa, Chattooga, Dade, and Walker Counties. For ten years, she was also the Municipal Court Judge of Fort Oglethorpe, the first woman to hold such a position in Catoosa County.

As Assistant DA and later a Judge, Ms. Patterson witnessed the challenges faced by the people of North Georgia. Since the early 1980s, she has devoted herself to helping them collect the government benefits they deserve. In 1984, she formed a partnership with another attorney, which handled nothing but social security and disability claims. In 2009, she fell in love with the town of Rome, and joined the practice of Davis and Davis.

Ms. Patterson has represented claimants at all levels in the state of Georgia. She is licensed to practice in all the state's courts - including the Superior Court, the Georgia Court of Appeals, the Georgia Supreme Court, the United States District Court for the Northern District of Georgia, and the Sixth and Eleventh Circuits of the United States Courts of Appeals. Two of her winning cases in the U.S. Courts of Appeal have set legal precedent and been published decisions, one in the 6th Circuit, and one in the 11th Circuit. She is also a member of the National Organization of Social Security Claimants Representatives (NOSSCR).

attorneys.bio:
Jeremy Penland is a life-long North Georgia resident, having grown up in Walker and Catoosa counties. He graduated from Lakeview-Fort Oglethorpe High School and then enlisted in the United States Marine Corps. He spent four years on active duty and was honorably discharged.

Following his time in the Marine Corps, Jeremy attended college in Southern California and received a Bachelor’s Degree in Economics. After graduation, he worked for several years in the banking and finance industry. The economic downturn helped him decide that it was time to pursue his dream of becoming an attorney.

He earned a full scholarship to Liberty University School of Law and served on several committees while there, including the school’s law journal and ADR boards. He also co-opted in Washington D.C., which gave him several professional and educational opportunities – including the chance to personally meet with United States Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito.

But, the opportunity that impacted Jeremy the most was his internship with the Catoosa County District Attorney’s office. That experience led directly to his decision to return home to North Georgia and open his law office.

Jeremy wants to work on behalf of the people of his community to assist them with their legal needs. If you are in the North Georgia area and need a lawyer near you, call Penland, Romans & Rayburn Law Firm, GP, today. Jeremy and his team are ready to help you and your family handle your legal needs. Penland, Romans & Rayburn Law Firm, GP, is able to help you with your family law, personal injury, or criminal law needs. Whether you are going through a divorce or need representation for a DUI, call Jeremy Penland today.

attorneys.practice_type: Corporate and Business Law Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Michael A. Penn is an equity partner at Briskin, Cross & Sanford, LLC, and has been practicing law in the State of Georgia since 1993. Michael’s practice concentrates in the areas of (i) Corporate and business law, including mergers & acquisitions, partnership and LLC law, business contract drafting and review; (ii) Intellectual property law including trademarks, service marks, copyrights and trade secrets; (iii) Employment Law, including executive employment agreements, independent contractor agreements, and employment manuals; (iv) Franchise law, including representing franchisors and franchisees; and (v) Commercial litigation related to the above areas.

Michael has received the highest peer and client rating of “AV Preeminent Lawyer” by Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory, for business law, litigation, and general legal practice.

Michael is admitted to practice before all state and local courts throughout Georgia, including the Supreme Court of Georgia, the Georgia Court of Appeals, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit, and the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia. Michael received his J.D. from the Widener University School of Law in Wilmington, Delaware in 1993, and received his B.A. from the University of Maryland, College Park in 1990.

Michael currently serves as the Treasurer and President-Elect of North Fulton Bar Association. As part of Michael’s commitment to the community, he sat as one of the first appointed Municipal Court Judges in the City of Johns Creek upon the initial incorporation of that city in 2006.

Michael volunteers as an attorney coach with the Johns Creek High School Mock Trial team and is a graduate of Leadership North Fulton. Michael can also be found coaching youth baseball at Ocee Park and was Cubmaster of Cub Scout Pack 1818 in Alpharetta for several years.

Michael lives with his wife and four children in Alpharetta, Georgia.

attorneys.name: Anthony Perrotta
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Cartersville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Anthony Perrotta is the founder and senior partner of Perrotta, Lamb & Johnson, LLC. Born and raised in New York, Tony moved to Georgia in 1976 to attend Emory University. It was during this time that he made the decision to make Georgia his home. He has been practicing law in North Georgia since 1982.

Tony's dedication to law is matched only by his devotion to his clients and the community in which they live. Tony contributes time and money to numerous charitable organizations in the community including the League for Battered Women and the Bartow Aids Alliance.

Tony has both personal and professional ties with Mexico and takes great pride in his ability to provide effective legal services to the Spanish community. Perrotta, Lamb & Johnson, LLC employs several Spanish-speaking employees that are able to effectively assist our Spanish speaking clients.

Tony Perrotta received his Juris Doctorate from the University of Georgia School of Law in 1982. Prior to law school, Tony graduated with high honors from the Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University, where he earned a Bachelors in Biology and Chemistry. He then graduated from Emory University, where he completed studies for his Masters in Biology.

Tony is admitted to practice in all Georgia state courts, and in the Georgia Court of Appeals and Georgia Supreme Court. Tony Perrotta is a member of the State Bar of Georgia; the Cartersville-Bartow Bar Association; League for Battered Women (Board of Directors 1985-1998); Bartow Aids Alliance (Board of Directors 1990-2010); and the Stonewall Bar Association of Georgia. He has also published articles on family law and has served on the faculty of several State Bar sponsored continuing education programs.

Outside of the law, Tony enjoys traveling the world as he has visited 52 countries. He also enjoys spending time at his home in Mexico, where he spend his hours fishing and reading.

attorneys.name: Anna Perry
attorneys.practice_type: Family Lawyers in Villa Rica, GA
attorneys.bio:
Anna was born and raised in Villa Rica, Georgia. She is a proud 2003 graduate of Villa Rica High School. Anna moved to Waleska, Georgia to attend Reinhardt College where she received an athletic scholarship to play on the Women’s Soccer Team. After completing her freshman year, Anna was recruited to University of West Georgia where she received an athletic scholarship to play on the Inaugural Women’s Soccer Team and returned to Villa Rica. Anna graduated from the University of West Georgia with a Bachelor of Science in Criminology, and she then took two years off when she had her first child, Vance Smith. During her time off, she worked as a legal secretary for The Pilgrim Law Group, where she learned the invaluable lessons of hard work, dedication to your employees and dedication to your clients. In 2009, Anna was accepted to law school, attending John Marshall Law School in Atlanta. While there, she worked as a Dean’s Fellow for the Legal Writing Department and received the CALI Award for Trial Advocacy and Writing. Anna graduated in 2012 and was admitted to the State Bar of Georgia in May of 2013.

Anna has diligently worked as an attorney for the past 10 years in Villa Rica, Georgia, where she was a partner at a local firm for 8 of those years. Anna is an experienced family law attorney, probate attorney and real estate attorney. She has also represented clients in personal injury cases, where she thoroughly enjoys being able to help those who have been injured navigate their future and overcome that particular trial in their life. Anna loves her job and is always grateful for God who has provided her this platform to work with those who need her at times in their lives when they may feel like they have no one on their side.

Anna is married to her husband, Dan Perry, and they have three wonderful blessings in life, Vance Smith, Piper Perry and Harley Quinn Perry. She and her family reside in Bremen, Georgia. She also has two bonus blessings, Taylor Smith and Shelby Smith who reside in Temple, Georgia, along with two grandchildren, Rowan and Reed Smith.

Anna has been a member of First Baptist Church in Villa Rica for the past ten years. She and her husband have been blessed by being asked to teach in different areas in the Church, as it has always opened doors for new relationships to flourish. Anna puts her faith first and foremost and loves her family. Anna and her husband cultivate a home where her children are taught honesty, respect and work ethic, but most importantly a love for our Lord, Jesus Christ. In her free time, Anna loves to cook and enjoys reading. Her favorite time is spent playing Candy Land, Uno or Crazy Eights with the kids or just sitting around the dinner table with her family.

2 Peter 1:10

“Therefore, my brothers and sisters, make every effort to confirm your calling and election. For if you do these things, you will never stumble…”

attorneys.firm_name: The Siemon Law Firm Divorce and Family Law Attorneys, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Cumming, GA
attorneys.bio:
Christina, a senior lead attorney at The Siemon Law Firm Divorce and Family Law Attorneys, P.C. in Cumming, brings a unique background to her legal career. Born in Jacksonville, NC, she traversed various locations during her formative years, accompanying her family as her father served in the United States Marine Corps.

Her educational journey led her to The University of Georgia, where she earned a Bachelor’s degree in Business Management with a minor in African American Studies. Subsequently, Christina pursued her passion for law at Atlanta’s John Marshall Law School, attaining her Juris Doctorate in 2017. She officially became a member of the Georgia State Bar in 2022.

During her time at AJMLS, Christina honed her skills working for the LBJ Group, specializing in Family Law and Criminal Defense, and contributed to the Dekalb County Superior Court. As a Mediator with the Georgia Office of Dispute Resolution, she takes pride in her ongoing commitment to the Dekalb County Magistrate Court, showcasing her dedication to facilitating resolutions.

Inspired by her parents’ enduring 40-year marriage, Christina acknowledges that everyone’s journey is unique. She is fervently dedicated to helping families navigate the challenges of transitioning to a new normal. Beyond the legal realm, Christina finds joy in her love for travel, quality family time, and actively seeks opportunities to contribute meaningfully to her community.

attorneys.name: Jody Donald Peterman
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Valdosta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Jody Peterman is the owner of Jody D. Peterman, LLC and his practice focuses on representing individuals who have been injured, harmed, or suffered a loss through the wrongdoing or negligence of another.

Unlike many attorneys who handle a few cases each year in the area of personal injury or work for a television advertising mill, Jody is an experienced trial attorney who has practiced in the personal injury field in Georgia for nearly 30 years. He represents catastrophically injured victims and families who have lost a loved one, as well as individuals injured in motor vehicle collisions, tractor-trailer crashes, motorcycle accidents, medical malpractice, defective products, and other injury cases involving the wrongful death of a loved one. Jody only takes on serious accident cases with the intent of reaching the best possible outcome for his clients. Jody has tried over one hundred jury trials in his career, which makes him one of the most experienced trial lawyers in South Georgia.

Jody's practice also encompasses representing individuals charged with serious felony crimes, where the individual is innocent and wrongfully accused by the government.

In 1995, Jody graduated from Mercer University Law School. In law school, Jody received the highest grade in his Tort's II class (Americus Jurisprudence awarding for studying personal injury law) and also received the Milton Barwick Pleading and Practice award for being the best trial attorney in a trial practice class with Judge J. Taylor Phillips.

Jody is admitted to practice before the Supreme Court of the United States, the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, the Supreme Court of Georgia, the Court of Appeals for the State of Georgia, the United States District Court for the Northern District of Georgia, the United State District Court for the Southern District of Georgia, as well as the United States District Court for the Middle District of Georgia.

Jody is a member of the State Bar of Georgia, the Valdosta Bar Association, the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association, and the Georgia Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers. Jody is AV-rated by Martindale-Hubbell® (prestigious) and is a Top 100 Georgia Trial Lawyer as determined by the National Trial Lawyers Association. He also enjoys a 10/10 rating by Avvo.

Jody has lived in South Georgia his entire life. He has four children. His wife Mary teaches special ed in the Lowndes School System. Jody's hobbies include attending his children's sporting events, cooking, reading, and watching the Atlanta Braves and the New England Patriots.

Awards and Honors

AV-Rated By Martindale-Hubbell®

Top 100 Georgia Trial Lawyers, National Trial Lawyers Association

10/10 Avvo Rating

attorneys.name: Tom A. Peterson IV
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Firm of Tom A. Peterson IV, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Justice Lawyers in Vidalia, GA
attorneys.bio:
When facing federal or state crimes, people seek Tom’s diligent counsel and innovative representation. Tom handles all phases of the criminal justice process, from protecting folks who are initially targets of criminal investigations to representing them through trial, when trial is the only option. In these roles he successfully guides men and women through complicated pre-indictment and pre-trial negotiations, having secured the very rare, pre-trial diversion and non-prosecution agreements in federal and state courts, so people can live without the stigma of a conviction. Tom is also the veteran of hard-fought trials, where he presented juries with more than just the government’s version of the allegations, and as a result, juries unanimously awarded his clients with outright acquittals. From misdemeanors, like DUI, to complex and violent state and federal prosecutions, involving crimes such as armed robbery, child abuse, child exploitation, and conspiracy to distribute controlled substances and firearms, people turn to Tom’s ever-evolving knowledge of criminal law and procedure to guard their constitutional rights.

Regarding federal criminal cases, Tom understands the voluminous, harsh and fluctuating United States Sentencing Guidelines, which apply to almost every resolution, whether a client goes to trial or not, and require the consideration of many difficult concepts, such as relevant conduct and specific offense characteristics. Before and at sentencing, Tom’s knowledge of the Guidelines greatly assist his clients in appreciating their magnitude and the “how and why” of his or her guideline score.

Formerly, Tom served a felony prosecutor in the District Attorney’s Office in Augusta, Georgia, which covered one of the largest and most diverse judicial districts in Georgia, and where he gained extensive trial experience. Unlike many of his peers, Tom’s background gives him a better understanding of law enforcement investigations and prosecutorial strategy, which drives his ability to resourcefully investigate charges and effectively defend his clients.

As well, Tom’s practice focuses on workers’ compensation law, where he protects and obtains important income and medical benefits that belong to men and women who were injured on the job. In immigration law, he represents foreigners who face complicated issues such as status adjustment and removal. He litigates other civil matters involving real estate, where issues of foreclosure, confirmation and bankruptcy arise, and probate and estate law. And, he is active in municipal law, serving as City Attorney for the City of Lyons, Georgia, where he advises its governing body and administration on matters such as condemnation, employment and ordinance compliance.

Finally, Tom’s practice maintains an active real estate transactional component. He is a member of the American Land Title Association and a title insurance agent for First American Title Insurance Company. During his career, he has handled numerous residential, commercial, agricultural and timber closings, frequently represent buyers and sellers, as well as community, regional and national banks and credit unions.

In sum, Tom routinely achieves successful outcomes for his clients whatever the issues involved.

Awards and Honors

Honors

International Academy of Trial Lawyers Award, 2001

Advisory Committee for the United States District Court, Southern District of Georgia, Member from 2013-present

Circuit Public Defendant Advisory Panel, Middle Judicial Circuit, Member from 2012-present

National District Attorneys Association/National Advocacy Center, 2004 and 2005

attorneys.bio:
Kierston is a lifelong resident of Carroll County. During high school, Kierston attended the Advanced Academy of West Georgia, earning college credits while enrolled at Carrollton High School. After graduating high school in 2007, Kierston obtained her bachelor’s degree in accounting in 2008 and her Master’s in Public Administration in 2010, both from the University of West Georgia.

From there, Kierston went to law school at Atlanta’s John Marshall Law School and graduated in December 2012 with her Juris Doctor. Kierston was admitted to practice law in Georgia in 2013. Kierston is a licensed mediator in general civil mediation, family/domestic, juvenile delinquency and domestic violence. Kierston received all of her mediation training from the Justice Center of Atlanta. In 2016, Kierston was appointed as the county conservator for Carroll County. Most of Kierston’s litigation work is devoted to family law.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Kierston is a lifelong resident of Carroll County. During high school, Kierston attended the Advanced Academy of West Georgia, earning college credits while enrolled at Carrollton High School. After graduating high school in 2007, Kierston obtained her bachelor’s degree in accounting in 2008 and her Master’s in Public Administration in 2010, both from the University of West Georgia.

From there, Kierston went to law school at Atlanta’s John Marshall Law School and graduated in December 2012 with her Juris Doctor. Kierston was admitted to practice law in Georgia in 2013. Kierston is a licensed mediator in general civil mediation, family/domestic, juvenile delinquency and domestic violence. Kierston received all of her mediation training from the Justice Center of Atlanta. In 2016, Kierston was appointed as the county conservator for Carroll County. Most of Kierston’s litigation work is devoted to family law.

attorneys.name: Nigel Phiri
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Nigel Phiri grew up in Zambia and South Africa before relocating to the States where he graduated from Roswell High School. Nigel attended Georgia State University, graduating cum laude in three years as a Pre-Law major. While at Georgia State, Nigel was the founding president of a student-run organization that focused on helping students balance the academic, spiritual, and emotional rigors of pursuing a modern-day college education.

Nigel received Georgia State University's Phil Peters Scholarship as a junior and a senior. After graduating, Nigel attended Mercer University School of Law. While at Mercer Law, Nigel received several accolades, including the Advanced Legal Writing & Researching Certificate and being the Student Coach of the Wagner National Moot Court Team. He also served as the Executive Managing Editor of the Southern Journal of Policy & Justice, Volume IX, and he was a member of the Frederick Douglass Moot Court Team during his first year of law school. Nigel won Second Place for his article titled "Follow The Money: The Integrity of The Career Expert Witness" in The Expert Institute's 2015 Legal Blog Post Writing Contest.

Nigel has been admitted to the Georgia Bar since 2015. Before joining the firm, Nigel worked as a defense attorney representing the interest of insurers and small to medium-sized businesses across the Southeastern United States. Nigel has experience defending large insurance companies in employment, personal injury and premises liability litigation. Nigel's defense experience enables him to incorporate the knowledge he gained representing insurance companies to help his personal injury clients recover the maximum amounts possible.

Nigel is active in the community. His Community Law Day program aims to provide access to lawyers to members of the Atlanta community. He strives to empower his clients to have the confidence to pursue the justice and compensation they rightfully deserve.

Nigel is admitted to practice law in the State of Georgia, Supreme Court of Georgia and the United States District Courts for the Northern District of Georgia.

Outside of the practice of law, Nigel enjoys reading, running, playing basketball and soccer, and spending time with his friends and family. He currently lives in Lawrenceville, Georgia.

attorneys.name: Daniel Philyaw
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Dan Philyaw is an attorney at Butler Prather LLP. He works at the firm's Atlanta office and represents individuals and their families in a wide range of serious injury cases. Dan served as trial counsel in Hill v. Ford Motor Company, in which a Gwinnett County, Georgia jury handed down a historic $1.7 billion verdict-the largest verdict in Georgia history. Dan has also worked as part of a product liability trial team that secured a $151 million verdict for a man paralyzed after an SUV rollover and worked to achieve a $2.8 million verdict for a client who was injured in a motor vehicle accident. Dan was named to the Super Lawyers Rising Stars list in 2022.

Dan received his Juris Doctorate from the University of Georgia School of Law in 2018, graduating cum laude. While in law school, Dan was a standout advocate in both moot court and mock trial competitions. He won Best Oralist at the 2017 Georgia Intrastate Moot Court Competition and was also named Best Oral Advocate at the 2017 Billings, Exum & Frye National Moot Court Competition. Additionally, Dan won Georgia Law's J. Melvin England Mock Trial Tournament in 2016 and finished as runner-up in the J. Ralph Beaird Closing Argument Competition during the same calendar year. Due to these successes, Dan was inducted to the Order of Barristers upon graduation as one of the ten best advocates in his law school class. Outside of the courtroom, Dan worked as a research assistant to evidence scholar Ronald L. Carlson and studied as a pupil in the Joseph Henry Lumpkin American Inn of Court. Dan also gained practical experience by serving as a summer clerk for then Judge Charlie Bethel at the Court of Appeals of Georgia and representing survivors of family violence in the law school's Family Justice Clinic.

Prior to law school, Dan earned bachelor's degrees in finance and international studies from the University of Missouri, graduating magna cum laude and cum laude, respectively. While at Mizzou, Dan served as VP of Finance & Records for the Interfraternity Council and as a Student Ambassador for the Trulaske College of Business.

attorneys.name: Steven A. Pickens
attorneys.practice_type: Tort Litigation Lawyers in Lawrenceville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Steve Pickens is a founding partner of Mahaffey Pickens Tucker, LLP and leads the firm's litigation group. Mr. Pickens is a trial lawyer whose specialty is trying cases to a jury. He has tried cases all over Georgia and is often associated by other attorneys to help them try their cases. He has litigated over fifty civil jury trials to a verdict. During the course of his 25-year career, Mr. Pickens has applied his trial skills wherever his clients need them. He is just as comfortable litigating a medical negligence case as he is a case involving business fraud, contract law, or even eminent domain.

The wide application of Mr. Pickens’s skill set is demonstrated by the fact he is one of the most recognized attorneys in the state of Georgia in the niche area of property tax litigation. For over than 25 years, Mr. Pickens has used his trial skills to fight for property owners seeking relief from inflated property tax assessments. In 2016, Mr. Pickens won a tax value reduction of over $125,000,000 for one client and a reduction of over $60,000,000 for another client in a separate case. In that same year, Mr. Pickens also handled Superior Court appeals for nine different mall anchor stores in Atlanta. Mr. Pickens won the first of these anchor store appeals in a three-day trial by successfully arguing that the inflated value should be slashed from approximately $30,000,000 to $12,000,000, recovering 100% of the attorney’s fees paid by his client from the defendant county. After this appeal, the county capitulated on the other eight appeals Mr. Pickens was handling, resulting in a collective value reduction that exceeded $50,000,000. In addition to these large successes, Mr. Pickens achieved property tax reductions on many other properties, including apartment complexes, distribution centers, warehouses, retail centers, vacant land, and luxury homes.

In addition to continuing to litigate his property tax cases, Mr. Pickens devotes a large portion of his practice to representing families who have lost loved ones due to the carelessness of others. In this area of his practice, he has achieved multiple seven-figure results in cases involving medical negligence, wrongful death, and catastrophic injury. In fact, Mr. Pickens’s personal office contains more medical textbooks than lawbooks because understanding the medicine is an essential part of presenting these cases.

Mr. Pickens grew up in Savannah, Georgia and is a product of the Chatham County public school system. After graduating with honors from Mercer University, he earned his law degree, cum laude, from the University of Georgia School of Law. For over ten years, Mr. Pickens has maintained the coveted “AV Preeminent – 5.0 out of 5.0” rating on Martindale-Hubbell, the leading national lawyer rating agency.

attorneys.name: Tim Pierse
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance/Liability Defense Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Tim Pierse joined MIJS in September 2022 as an Associate Attorney in the firm’s Insurance/ Liability Defense department. He received his bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice from the University of Mississippi in 2008.

After graduation Tim went to work as a Felony Probation Officer for the GA department of corrections supervising violent offenders in Cobb and Cherokee County. Then in 2013, Tim enlisted in the United States Army as an interrogator and source handler focused on combatting ISIS and the Taliban. After the Army, Tim leveraged his military experience into a position in Washington D.C. working for the Central Intelligence Agency and Defense Intelligence Agency to continue countering terrorism as well as Russia/China aggression against U.S. equities. While working full time in the Intelligence Community, Tim went to law school at night at the George Washington University Law School, earning his J.D. in the spring of 2022, and was admitted to the State Bar of Georgia in November of 2022.

In his free time, Tim enjoys spending time with his son, Timmy, his wife Kristy, and rooting for the Ole Miss Rebels.

attorneys.name: Phil Pilgrim
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Cumming, GA
attorneys.bio:
Phil Pilgrim graduated from the University of Georgia with a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and a Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice. He attended Georgia State University College of Law where he earned his Juris Doctorate.

During law school, Phil clerked for Judge Steve C. Jones of the Western Judicial Circuit who is now a United States District Court Judge for the Northern District of Georgia. Phil also worked as a prosecutor under the 3rd Year Practice Act for the Forsyth County Solicitor General’s Office and the DeKalb County District Attorney’s Office. After Law School, Phil returned to Forsyth County in public service as a prosecutor. During his time working for the State, Phil spent 75% of his time in court. He obtained the position of Senior Assistant and was the acting Assistant Solicitor on the Forsyth County DUI Court, prosecuting hundreds of DUI cases.

During his time there, Phil was very active in the training of Law Enforcement on the subject of DUI Detection and Enforcement and courtroom demeanor and testimony. He was often an instructor at the Georgia Public Safety Training Center (GPSTC) in the City of Forsyth, which is where many officers receive their Mandate Training. Being a “teacher” taught Phil that a vast majority of issues in cases involving DUI are a byproduct of a lack of training and experience of the officers we have out on the road. Likewise, for those that are well trained, an officer’s inability to recognize the limitations of the tools they are equipped with to investigate individuals suspected of driving under the influence result in many improper arrests.

Phil left public service in 2007 and until 2013, Phil was a partner in a Forsyth County law firm where he managed all the firm’s criminal cases and often associated on other firm cases being prepped for litigation due to his extensive trial experience. In October of 2013, Phil and Amy Carter left that Forsyth County firm and opened Carter/Pilgrim in Suwanee, Georgia. For nine years, Amy and Phil operated a very successful firm serving clients in counties throughout North Georgia, including Gwinnett, Forsyth, Barrow, Hall, Jackson, Banks, White and Lumpkin. In 2021, Carter/Pilgrim merged with Banks, Stubbs & McFarland where Amy Carter and Phil Pilgrim joined as partners while retaining the Suwanee office to extend BSM’s reach into counties previously not served.

Since joining BSM, Phil has transitioned his practice to focus 100% of his efforts on cases involving Driving Under the Influence, Serious Injury by Vehicle and Vehicular Homicide. He has an extremely successful record with nearly 85% of his resolving with a non-DUI resolution, whether through negotiation or trial by jury. He prides himself in consistently exceeding the expectations of his clients with integrity and professionalism. Obtaining the client’s goals is always a source of pride for Phil. He is a very experienced trial lawyer (and yes, there is a difference between a LAWYER and a TRIAL LAWYER). He has tried a countless number of cases before judge and jury ranging from misdemeanor cases of DUI to felony cases of murder.

Phil comes from a working-class family and often worked in construction/labor positions to financially support himself through school. He is the first of his family to go to college and the only one to complete a post graduate degree. He credits his family and personal work history for the tremendous respect he has for hard working people simply trying to provide for their families. He takes great pride that he is in a privileged position to help people through this line of work and never takes for granted how much personal and financial trust his clients place in him.

He is a devoted husband and father. When not working, he spends his free time with his family and friends. He is a member of The Vine United Methodist Church. His Faith, Family, and Friendships are the most important things in his life. Phil is confident that fervor for those three components in his life furthers his abilities in representing his clients.

attorneys.name: Noah H. Pines
attorneys.practice_type: Drug Crimes Defense Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
As a criminal defense lawyer, Noah handles all types of criminal cases, including juvenile delinquencies, misdemeanors, felonies and asset forfeitures in State, Superior and Federal Courts throughout the State of Georgia. Noah's knowledge of the criminal justice system and the trial skills he gained as a prosecutor makes him an invaluable asset to the clients he represents in criminal matters. Noah is known as a fearless trial lawyer who vigorously fights for his clients. Noah is also a skilled appellate lawyer. Noah has handled over sixty appeals and he is known for his ability to argue his cases before both the Georgia Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court of Georgia. In recognition of his work ethic and trial skills, Noah was named a Georgia Super Lawyer by his colleagues.

As a personal injury lawyer, Noah represents clients from across the State of Georgia who have been injured as a result of motor vehicle accidents, trucking collisions, defective products, medical malpractice, premises liability and constitutional violations. Noah uses the investigative and trial skills he honed as a prosecutor to hold responsible both the people who have injured his clients and the insurance companies who refuse to pay full compensation for his clients' injuries. Through these skills, Noah has helped recover millions of dollars in damages on behalf of his clients and their families.

attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Leslie focuses her practice on Bankruptcy, Creditor Rights, Commercial Litigation, Business Transactions, Commercial Real Estate Transactions and Trademark Law.

Leslie is a partner at Jones & Walden and joined the firm as an associate in 2008. She represents clients in a variety of legal matters in state and federal courts and in business transactions. Leslie's clients include small businesses, financial institutions, and entrepreneurs.

Leslie represents debtors, creditors and equity holders in chapter 11, chapter 7, chapter 12 and chapter 13 bankruptcies and adversary proceedings throughout Georgia. attorneys.name: Kenneth B. Pollock
attorneys.practice_type: Public Finance Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Kenneth B. Pollock is a public finance attorney with over two decades of experience in public finance transactions. Mr. Pollock regularly serves as bond counsel, as disclosure counsel, and as counsel to underwriters, issuers, borrowers, trustees, banks, and credit enhancers in tax-exempt and taxable financings for governmental and private entities. Mr. Pollock has significant experience on virtually every financing structure used by state and local governments to finance governmental projects, including general obligation bonds and sales tax bonds for counties, municipalities, and school districts, revenue bonds for water, sewer, and storm water systems, airports, convention facilities, gas and electric utilities, and other governmental enterprises, guaranteed revenue bonds for the State of Georgia, tax anticipation notes, annual appropriation debt, and debt secured by intergovernmental contracts.

Mr. Pollock also has experience on numerous conduit financings benefiting integrated health care systems, hospitals, nursing homes, assisted living facilities, charter schools, private schools, higher education, manufacturing facilities, and multifamily housing developments, as well as on economic development projects such as tax increment and tax allocation district financings and property tax abatement transactions.

In connection with these transactions, Mr. Pollock has participated in a variety of financing structures involving fixed rate and variable rate structures, public offerings and private placements, insured and letter of credit-backed bonds, auction rate securities, remarketings, interest rate conversions, and various derivative products, including interest rate swaps.

Mr. Pollock has served as a speaker at the Institute for City and County Attorneys in Georgia and at annual conferences of the Georgia Charter Schools Association. During law school at the University of Georgia School of Law, Mr. Pollock served as Notes Editor of the Georgia Law Review.

Mr. Pollock has been recognized by Georgia Trend magazine as one of Georgia's Legal Elite in the specialty of Public Finance/Bonds.
