attorneys.name: Scott T. Poole
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Canton, GA
attorneys.bio:
Scott grew up in Conyers, Georgia, graduating from Rockdale County High School in 1990. From there, he moved to Rome, Georgia, and attended Berry College, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts majoring in Political Science. After graduating from Berry in 1994, he was accepted at the Georgia State University College of Law in Atlanta.

While attending GSU Law, he completed a Governor's Internship with Superior Court Judge Stanley Gault in Forsyth County and worked with Fulton Senior Superior Court Judge William Daniel. There, he helped edit Daniel's Criminal Trial Practice, a handbook utilized by lawyers and judges throughout the state of Georgia. Also, he was a member of the Student Trial Lawyers Association Mock Trial Team where he competed nationally against other student mock trial teams.

After graduation from law school, Scott took a position as an Assistant District Attorney in Cherokee County, Georgia, where he worked as a prosecutor from 1997 until 2008. During his tenure at the Cherokee County District Attorney's Office, he prosecuted everything from theft to murder cases. Scott successfully prosecuted Cherokee County's first racketeering case pursuant to the Georgia RICO statute and has successfully argued cases (including oral arguments) before both the Georgia Court of Appeals and the Georgia Supreme Court. From 2001-2004 he was the designated Drug Prosecutor for Cherokee County and handled all cases made by the Cherokee Multi-Agency Narcotics Squad (CMANS). Additionally, he was the lead Asset Forfeiture attorney from 2001 until 2008.

In 2008, he was recruited by the District Attorney for the Appalachian Judicial Circuit to come on-board as the Senior Assistant District Attorney in Pickens County, Georgia. There, he ran the day-to-day operations of the office supervising a staff of Assistant District Attorneys and Investigators. This position also allowed him to focus his efforts on the most serious cases, such as those involving violent offenses (Murder, Aggravated Assault , etc.), sexual offenses (Rape, Child Molestation, etc.) and Drug Trafficking (Methamphetamine, Cocaine, and Meth Labs). While working as a prosecutor, Scott developed a reputation in the legal community (among both prosecutors and defense attorneys) as both an effective litigator and a knowledgeable teacher. He served as an instructor for the Prosecuting Attorney's Council of Georgia's Drug Prosecutor Training from 2003-2012, teaching drug prosecutors from around the state the "ins and outs" of drug cases. Scott is also certified by the Georgia Peace Officer Standards and Training Council as a Guest Instructor in the areas of Search and Seizure, Courtroom Testimony, Asset Forfeitures and Report Writing.

In January of 2013, Scott made the leap from government employee to private practice when he joined noted attorney Ross D. Grisham to form Grisham & Poole, P.C. He now uses the experience he gained from 15 years as a state prosecutor to zealously defend clients who have been charged with violations of the law. As a prosecutor, he saw first-hand that not everyone arrested is guilty and after trying more than 90 jury trials as lead prosecutor, he knows what it takes to win both in and out of the courtroom.

On a personal note, Scott has been married to his wife Jennifer since 2005. He has a 12 year old step-son named Frankie and, in 2011, added a daughter named Mollie to the family. The Poole family lives in Ball Ground and attends Ball Ground United Methodist Church, where Scott is Chairman of the Church Counsel and plays guitar in the church band. The family enjoys traveling and outdoor adventures such as hiking, kayaking, and four-wheeling.

While working as a prosecutor, Scott developed a reputation in the legal community (among both prosecutors and defense attorneys) as both an effective litigator and a knowledgeable teacher. He served as an instructor for the Prosecuting Attorney's Council of Georgia's Drug Prosecutor Training from 2003-2012, teaching drug prosecutors from around the state the "ins and outs" of drug cases. Scott is also certified by the Georgia Peace Officer Standards and Training Council as a Guest Instructor in the areas of Search and Seizure, Courtroom Testimony, Asset Forfeitures and Report Writing.

In January of 2013, Scott made the leap from government employee to private practice when he joined noted attorney Ross D. Grisham to form Grisham & Poole, P.C. He now uses the experience he gained from 15 years as a state prosecutor to zealously defend clients who have been charged with violations of the law. As a prosecutor, he saw first-hand that not everyone arrested is guilty and after trying more than 90 jury trials as lead prosecutor, he knows what it takes to win both in and out of the courtroom.

On a personal note, Scott has been married to his wife Jennifer since 2005. He has a 12 year old step-son named Frankie and, in 2011, added a daughter named Mollie to the family. The Poole family lives in Ball Ground and attends Ball Ground United Methodist Church, where Scott is Chairman of the Church Counsel and plays guitar in the church band. The family enjoys traveling and outdoor adventures such as hiking, kayaking, and four-wheeling.

attorneys.name: Marshall Lee Portivent Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Carlos L. Corless
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Marshall was born to working class folks in a small town in South Georgia. At age 3, his family moved to Florida for work. Growing up, he worked after school, on weekends, and during school breaks in his family's small construction business. After graduating high school, Marshall moved back to Georgia for college.

While in college, Marshall worked as a butcher, cut lawns, and did construction work to pay his way through. After earning his Associates degree in Political Science with Honors, he got his Class A CDL, and became an over-the-road, long haul truck driver. He travelled through nearly all the 48 contiguous United States.

After a couple years on the road, Marshall returned to Georgia to finish college. While working several part time jobs, in just two years, Marshall graduated Cum Laude with a Bachelor's degree in Political Science and a Minor in History. Thereafter, Marshall began studying at Mercer University School of Law. As always, Marshall had to work his way through school. He continued to work as a finish carpenter, interned for a Superior Court Judge, and worked at a personal injury and workers' compensation law firm, where he discovered that he wanted to spend his career helping injured folks. In his 3rd year of law school, he was chosen to join the prestigious and very selective William A. Bootle Inn of Court, and competed on Mercer's behalf at the AAJ Mock Trial Competition.

After working for 3 ½ years in South Georgia at a reputable law firm where he practiced in the Litigation Department, Marshall and his wife moved to the Atlanta area, to be closer to her family. For the first two years in Atlanta, he worked at another reputable law firm in the Litigation Department, this time specializing in defending insurance companies. After working for corporations and insurance companies for several years, Marshall decided it was time to pursue his passion of representing injured folks. Prior to joining The Law Office of Carlos Corless, Marshall represented injured folks for years at another reputable personal injury law firm.

Having worked for big corporations, insurance companies, and now for injured folks, Marshall has a distinctive insight into how companies work and, more importantly, how they value injury cases. Additionally, having attended "formal" schools and universities, as well as "the school of hard knocks" in the real world, Marshall has a unique perspective on what it is like for real, hard-working folks to have their job compromised when they get hurt, through no fault of their own. Folks who are not used to and do not like asking others for help. This is not just a job to Marshall - this is his calling.

attorneys.practice_type: U.S. Immigration Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Laine handles cases in all areas of U.S. immigration law, including employment-based immigration (both immigrant and nonimmigrant applications), family immigration (both in the United States and consular processing at the U.S. Embassies), and naturalization applications. Laine represents clients both big and small before the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), the Department of Labor (DOL), the Department of State (DOS), and the Administrative Appeals Office (AAO). Laine was an assistant adjunct professor of immigration law at Emory University School of Law and is an active member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA), where she served on the USCIS liaison committee from 2010-2011. Laine is also an active member of the Anti-Defamation League (ADL), which combats hatred and discrimination in our society. Prior to joining Schwartz Posel Immigration Law Group, Laine worked as an attorney in the labor and employment section for the Washington, D.C., office of Morgan, Lewis & Bockius, LLP.

attorneys.name: Theodore E.G. Pound
attorneys.firm_name: Owen Gleaton Egan Jones & Sweeney, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Defense Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Ted Pound has been practicing law in Atlanta since 1982. His practice focuses on civil litigation and trial practice in state and federal court, including defense of healthcare providers in professional liability litigation and representation of plaintiffs and in a wide range of other personal injury cases. He has defended physicians and hospitals in hundreds of medical malpractice cases, including dozens of jury trials; he has represented businesses on either side of commercial disputes; he has handled numerous slip-and-fall, automotive liability and products actions; he has represented catastrophically injured plaintiffs in construction disasters; he has successfully resolved wrongful death actions for the families of individuals fatally injured as the result of others' negligence.

Ted began practicing law in 1982 with the Atlanta firm of Swift, Currie, McGhee & Hiers. Until 1988, he practiced with Drew Eckl & Farnham, one of the largest insurance defense firm in Georgia, representing individuals and insurance carriers in a range of personal injury litigation, including premises liability, automobile, products liability, and professional negligence cases. In the early years of his practice, he also was engaged in extensive pro bono representation of indigent clients and in 1986 received the S. Phillip Heiner Award of the Atlanta Volunteer Lawyers Foundation.

Ted has tried more than 50 cases to a jury verdict in state and federal courts in Georgia. For the past several years, he has managed a diverse practice representing both plaintiffs and defendants in significant personal injury litigation as a sole practitioner and now as a member of a small firm, including business disputes, premises liability and wrongful death actions arising in the construction setting. He is admitted to practice in the Superior Courts of Georgia, the Georgia Court of Appeals, the Supreme Court of Georgia, the United States District Courts for the Northern, Middle and Southern Districts of Georgia, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit.

Ted lives in northwest Atlanta with his wife, Susan, and their two young children. He has two grown daughters, one a registered nurse and the other a high school teacher, who live with their husbands in North Carolina. He has been an active member of St. Luke's Episcopal Church in Atlanta for almost 30 years. For more than ten years, he served on the board and was a recent past president of the Atlanta Enterprise Center, a job-training program for the homeless, now known as the Atlanta Center for Self Sufficiency.

Awards and Honors

Honors

S. Phillip Heiner Award, Atlanta Volunteer Lawyers Foundation, 1986

AV Preeminent rating, Martindale-Hubbell

attorneys.name: Warren R. Power
attorneys.practice_type: Condemnation Lawyers in McDonough, GA
attorneys.bio:
Warren Power is a founding member of the firm and has more than twenty-eight (28) years of professional legal experience.

Warren has an AV rating with Martindale-Hubbell's Bar Registry which is the highest attainable rating as to skill level and integrity. Warren earned his bachelor's degrees from Christopher Newport University in Virginia and his JD degree from Mercer University. Warren is admitted to practice before all State and Federal Courts in Georgia, the United States Eleventh Circuit and the United States Court of Federal Claims. Warren has also been admitted pro hac vice in Alabama and Tennessee and is a member of the Virginia Bar.

Warren has lectured extensively on the topics of land use and eminent domain to members of the Georgia Bar since 2003, and is a Past Chair of the Eminent Domain Section of the State Bar. Warren is a Super Lawyer, is also listed in the Best Lawyers of America and has a "superb" rating from AVVO Lawyers Rating, which is the highest attainable rating. Warren is a past fellow of the Litigation Counsel of America, an honorary trial lawyer's society, an honor received by less than one-half of one percent of American lawyers.

Warren has extensive experience representing clients in land use matters focusing primarily in the complex area of eminent domain. Warren has represented the Georgia Department of Transportation in almost all of its highway projects in Henry County since 1997. Additionally, Warren represented the Department in improvement of projects in Butts, Clayton, Douglas, Jasper, Newton, and Spalding Counties. Other governmental entities such as Butts, Clayton and Henry Counties, and the cities of Atlanta, and Fayetteville have retained Warren to represent them in their eminent domain projects.

Warren has represented the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and has served as a Special Assistant Attorney General for the Georgia Department of Natural Resources, the Georgia Regional Transit Authority, and the Technical College System of Georgia.

Warren has also represented property owners against the local and federal governments. Warren has represented property owners against all of the cities in Henry County; the City of Riverdale, the City of Sandy Springs, Henry, Clayton, DeKalb and Bibb counties; and the United States of America.

Experience

Appointed Special Assistant Attorney General under Attorneys General Michael Bowers, Thurbert Baker, Samuel S. Olens and Christopher Carr for eminent domain and other real estate acquisition purposes.

Acquired over 1000 parcels of property for the State of Georgia as a Special Assistant Attorney General.

Handled over 100 condemnation cases for the State of Georgia as a Special Assistant Attorney General.

Served as outside eminent domain counsel to the City of Atlanta by assisting in the acquisition of subsurface right of way for the City, DeKalb and Fulton Counties to construct. The Nancy Creek Sewer tunnel. This project extended more than 8.25 miles and affected approximately 300 property owners.

Has served as sole or lead counsel in over 50 jury trials.

Handled numerous condemnation cases on behalf of property owners against various local governments, county authorities, the United States of America and the U. S. Airforce.

Has taught numerous continuing Legal Education Courses on eminent domain and land use since 2003.

Ramsey represents individuals and businesses in a variety of practice areas, including False Claims Act litigation, business torts, and personal injury matters. attorneys.name: Mary A. Prebula
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mary Prebula is committed to strong assertive legal representation to assist in difficult and complex cases. Born in upstate New York, and raised in humble beginnings in the Pennsylvania mountains then eastern North Carolina, she was the first in her family to graduate college, and then attended Emory University Law School. When you need skilled litigation attorney with experience, she knows the law well and will represent you earnestly in Court. She has practiced law in firms from a single lawyer to 2400-member international firm. Her clients have included individuals to a President of the United States and sole proprietors to Fortune 50 companies. Her civil litigation includes discrimination and harassment claims, contract disputes, ERISA pension and health care coverage litigation, family law, probate and wills and trusts.

The State Bar has honored her with its Tradition of Excellence General Practice. She is the first woman in private practice to receive this award. Her peers have rated her AV Preeminent, in the national Martindale-Hubbell Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers©, the highest possible designation given for both Legal Ability and Ethical Standards for over 35 years years as well as in the national Bar Register of Preeminent Women Lawyers© (2011 Inaugural Ed.), and Super Lawyers, all the top 5% of lawyers in the country. She also is one of Georgia's Top Rated LawyersTM.

Mary is a past President of the Georgia Association for Women Lawyers where under her leadership the group established the Scholarship Fund to provide scholarships to women law students. Mary also served on the Steering Committee that founded Gwinnett Legal Aid, and continues to support pro bono causes and entities.

Mary will be up front and direct with you, and when representing you, she will do so with her full heart and skill set.

attorneys.name: Ryan G. Prescott
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Ryan G. Prescott was born and raised in Marietta, Georgia. Ryan attended the University of Georgia, where he graduated with a degree in Psychology, cum laude, in 2001, followed by his Juris Doctor degree in 2004.

While in law school, Ryan participated in the Advocacy program, winning the American Bar Association Regional Moot Court Competition's Best Advocate Award in 2003. He was later named to the Order of the Barristers for Excellence in Advocacy.

After graduating from law school, Ryan practiced for 7 years at a prominent defense firm handling all aspects of litigation from the administrative law judge level to the Georgia Court of Appeals level. In 2011, Ryan was named as a Rising Star in the area of workers' compensation by Super lawyers Magazine, which is an honor that is bestowed upon only 2.5% of the State's attorneys who are under the age of 40.

Ryan has also served as a presenting speaker at seminars and conferences for the Georgia State Board of Workers' Compensation, the Southern Association of Workers' Compensation Administrators (SAWCA), the Georgia Self-Insurers Association (GSIA), and various CLE and certification programs.

Most importantly to him, Ryan is married to his beautiful wife, Suzanne, and a father to his adorably-devious 1 year old son, Conner. Suzanne and Ryan enjoy traveling, sports and cooking. Conner enjoys laughing at his parents when they tell him "no." Ryan also enjoys writing screenplays as a hobby.

attorneys.name: Suzanne T. Prescott
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Suzanne T. Prescott is a founding partner of the family law firm Bivek Brubaker & Prescott LLC. In her words: “My partners and I share a belief that getting the best result for our clients does not always have to involve long, expensive, contentious Court battles. I view divorce as the new beginning in my clients’ lives, and I focus on obtaining the best starting point for them from all aspects – financially, emotionally, spiritually and structurally. I find purpose and joy in helping my clients and their families jump start their new possibilities from a position of strength.” In furtherance of her goals, Suzanne trained in Collaborative Law, which offers a structured, non-adversarial approach to divorce.

Following graduation from the University of Georgia School of Law, Suzanne has dedicated her entire career solely to practicing family law because “I don’t strive to be the best general attorney, I strive to be the best family law attorney so that my clients are assured that I provide exceptional representation, and that they can trust and count on me when I’m in their corner.” She is experienced in all aspects of family law, having represented all manners of clients – husband, wife, wealthy, underprivileged – in all manner of situations – contested divorce, uncontested divorce, custody, child support, agreement modification, adoption, negotiation of prenuptial agreements, and contempt actions.

Suzanne grew up in Connecticut, but headed south for college where she graduated cum laude from Emory University before conquering law school. When Suzanne is not advocating for her clients she is an avid runner with 2 marathons and countless half-marathons under her belt. She is a food and wine enthusiast who enjoys cooking, and she reserves her Fall Saturdays for Bulldog football and tailgating in Athens. Suzanne and her husband Ryan live in Smyrna, Georgia with their son, Conner, their daughter, Bronwyn, and their labradoodle, Penny.

attorneys.name: Sarah Price
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Sarah Price is a family law attorney with particular experience in cases involving custody and complex family dynamics. She approaches each matter with a child-focused perspective, recognizing that legal outcomes in family cases shape the long-term stability and well-being of the children involved.

Originally from North Carolina, Ms. Price now considers herself a Georgian at heart. She earned her Juris Doctorate from Georgia State University College of Law and holds an undergraduate degree from Auburn University.

Since beginning her legal career, Ms. Price has been driven by a genuine passion for advocating for families and helping clients find a path forward during some of the most challenging moments of their lives.

Ms. Price also brings a unique background in military-related family matters, including issues affecting active-duty service members and military families navigating custody, relocation, and deployment-related parenting challenges.

Ms. Price is committed to helping her clients move into a new chapter in their life in a way that protects both their personal interests and the well-being of their children.

attorneys.name: Nancy B. Pridgen Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: ERISA Litigation, Employee Benefits Disputes Lawyers in Roswell, GA
attorneys.bio:
Founding Member Nancy B. Pridgen, Esq. focuses her practice on employment litigation in the federal courts, and has handled, in some capacity, nearly every type of employment law matter that exists, including employment discrimination (age, race/nationality, gender, disability), retaliation, harassment, unemployment, FMLA, FLSA/wage and hour, ERISA/employee benefits, etc. Nancy also enjoys assisting businesses, business owners, executives and key employees navigate the waters of transitioning out of old and into new employment relationships, with all of their attendant issues (including, for instance, negotiating severance or other benefits, and drafting/negotiating new employment terms, etc.). Nancy counsels both employers and employees.

Nancy sub-specializes in ERISA litigation, and has litigated scores of ERISA benefits claims and fiduciary cases throughout the country. Nancy first developed this expertise in ERISA litigation while at Alston + Bird, where she litigated numerous class actions and other complex litigation involving employee pension cases and welfare benefit claims. She has continued her focus on ERISA since then, at some of Atlanta’s most well-respected boutique firms. Nancy writes and speaks often on ERISA/employment litigation topics; you can access the titles of her publications and speaking engagements below. She has also recently served as an officer in the Georgia State Bar Employee Benefits Section.

Nancy brings to clients a wealth of federal litigation experience. She has litigated a wide array of cases including complex commercial litigation, securities, insurance, tax, immigration, antitrust, constitutional and common-law torts, and civil appeals. In addition to her active trial practice, Nancy has maintained her commitment to giving back to the community by, among other things, handling several low-cost or pro bono adoptions.

Prior to moving home to Georgia, Nancy served as an Assistant U.S. Attorney for the U.S. Attorney's Office in Detroit and an Assistant Attorney General for Michigan's Attorney General's Office. Her time in government service provided Nancy with valuable insight on how government investigations and litigation are handled. Nancy was also privileged to serve as a judicial law clerk for two federal district court judges in the Eastern District of Michigan and the Northern District of Ohio.

Nancy is a proud graduate of Auburn University, where she graduated summa cum laude as the President’s Award winner for the College of Liberal Arts for her graduating class, with a double major and in the University Honors Program. Nancy received her law degree from Vanderbilt Law School, where she served as a Managing Editor of the Vanderbilt Law Review, and was named NAWL’s Outstanding Woman Law Graduate for her class, in addition to her Dean’s List honors.

The Really Important Stuff

Nancy is a proud wife and mother of four beautiful children. When not working on her clients’ legal matters, she is spending quality time with her family, or traveling. You are most likely to find her at her son’s baseball game or her daughter’s competitive cheerleading competition. In the fall, she and her family are obsessed with SEC football (WAR EAGLE!!).

attorneys.name: Nick Protentis
attorneys.practice_type: Fire and Explosion Cases Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Nick is the founder of Protentis Law LLC and has been practicing law for over 12 years. Before Nick was an attorney at a large in Atlanta where he gained valuable knowledge and experience handling fire, explosion, negligent construction and product liability cases. Before that, Nick was an attorney for a large insurance company. There, he gained significant trial experience having been the lead attorney in numerous cases tried to verdict.

A native of New England, Nick graduated from Stonehill College in Massachusetts. He went on to earn his law degree from Georgia State University College of Law, where he was a member of the Jessup International Law Moot Court team, an Honor’s Recipient in Litigation, and performed a year-long externship in the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia.

In the years leading up to law school, Nick was a Construction Supervisor for the Albany, Georgia Chapter of Habitat for Humanity. Prior to that, Nick was a Team Member in the AmeriCorps National Civilian Community Corps, based in Charleston, South Carolina. While in AmeriCorps, Nick participated in various volunteer projects throughout the Southeast, including projects with the National Park Service and the Red Cross.

Nick is a member of the Lawyers Club of Atlanta, the Atlanta Bar Association’s Small Firm Section, and the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association. He is also on the Board of the Sandy Springs Bar Association and is a member of the Board of Advisors for Shepherd Center, an internationally-renowned hospital for patients suffering from multiple sclerosis, spinal and brain injuries, and neuromuscular diseases.

attorneys.name: Alexis Putt
attorneys.firm_name: The Siemon Law Firm Divorce and Family Law Attorneys, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Cumming, GA
attorneys.bio:
Alexis Putt is a Senior Partner at The Siemon Law Firm Divorce and Family Law Attorneys, P.C., where she has been a dedicated member of the firm for over a decade. Practicing exclusively in the area of family law, Alexis is known for her direct, no-nonsense approach and her unwavering focus on results.

With a strong foundation in both civil and criminal litigation, Alexis brings strategic precision and disciplined case management to even the most complex domestic matters. Her background allows her to assess risk quickly, cut through distractions, and keep cases moving forward efficiently and effectively.

Alexis graduated magna cum laude from Georgia State University with a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science. She went on to earn her Juris Doctor from Georgia State University College of Law. Her analytical training enhances her ability to navigate financial issues, technical evidence, and the detailed problem-solving required in high-asset and contested family law cases.

Following law school, Alexis practiced as a litigation attorney in both civil and criminal courts, with a primary focus on family law. She also served as a Guardian Ad Litem in the Cherokee County Juvenile Court, representing the best interests of children in sensitive and high-conflict matters — an experience that continues to inform her thoughtful and practical approach.

Alexis is licensed to practice in all Georgia state courts, as well as the United States District Court and the United States Tax Court.

Outside of the office, Alexis enjoys spending time with her husband and their dogs, as well as reading and painting.

attorneys.name: Elena Quinde
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Suwanee, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Elena Quinde is a founding partner of Quinde & Associates, LLC. Attorney Quinde started her legal career at the very prestigious downtown law firm of King & Spalding. While she enjoyed assisting in the representation of large corporate clients in multi-district tort litigation, she knew that a key component to her job satisfaction was missing.

For that reason, she decided to leave the downtown Atlanta firm and focus on helping the members of her community. Attorney Elena Quinde and her family are long time residents of Lawrenceville, GA and Gwinnett County, and she knew that was there she wanted her home base to be.

She started practicing heavily and primarily in the fields of family law and criminal defense. She became well acquainted with other attorneys as well as the judges and their staff in Gwinnett County in the process. The "key component" that had been missing became clear: Attorney Quinde thrives on being the person that can tell a client, a person as opposed to company: "I have a solution for the legal problem you are experiencing." She truly enjoys helping people and improving their lives.

After practicing in the county for several years for smaller firms, Attorney Quinde recognized a need in the area for a boutique law firm which ultimately culminated in the birth of Quinde & Associates, LLC. As a partner, she is able to make decisions that serve the best interests of her clients without having to consult an owner or superior that knows little to nothing about her clients' cases.

In her time away from the office and courtroom, Attorney Quinde is the mother to two precocious little girls, a dog, a cat and a fish. Her husband, Ed, is a remarkable chef who delights in spoiling all members of the household. She is an avid reader of fantasy novels, a former competitive athlete, a self-proclaimed "foodie," and

a fan of all things Disney. In short, she is a parent, spouse and person just like you. She understands the challenges that you're facing because, chances are, she has faced them too. Contact Attorney Quinde for an initial consultation today to find out how she can help you.

attorneys.bio:
Bettis is an advocate. He is committed to representing individuals in personal injury and wrongful death cases. He handles matters at every stage in every court, state or federal, throughout South Carolina and Georgia.

His career began in Columbia, South Carolina by clerking for Senior United States District Judge Joseph F. Anderson, Jr. who instilled in him a dedication for the pursuit of the truth and a genuine love for trial. Bettis then worked for a large regional litigation firm based in Columbia where he defended large manufacturers and insurance companies.

In 2019, Bettis joined Ray and became a plaintiff’s attorney. His practice is 100% devoted to representing people in wrongful death and catastrophic personal injury cases. Bettis especially enjoys product liability cases and has had substantial success battling manufacturers who design and sell cheap and dangerous products.

Bettis has been recognized in South Carolina and Georgia as a “Rising Star” by Super Lawyers – an honor bestowed on only the top 2.5% of attorneys in each state.

He, his wife, Melissa, and their four children, Beau, Vann, Phin, and Anne Catherine, split their time between a farm in his native Edgefield and a house in Augusta. When not practicing law or chasing his children around, Bettis can most often be found hunting or otherwise spending time outdoors.

In 2019, Bettis joined Ray and became a plaintiff’s attorney. His practice is 100% devoted to representing people in wrongful death and catastrophic personal injury cases. Bettis especially enjoys product liability cases and has had substantial success battling manufacturers who design and sell cheap and dangerous products.

Bettis has been recognized in South Carolina and Georgia as a “Rising Star” by Super Lawyers – an honor bestowed on only the top 2.5% of attorneys in each state.

He, his wife, Melissa, and their four children, Beau, Vann, Phin, and Anne Catherine, split their time between a farm in his native Edgefield and a house in Augusta. When not practicing law or chasing his children around, Bettis can most often be found hunting or otherwise spending time outdoors.

attorneys.name: David N Rainwater
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial & General Litigation Lawyers in Cordele, GA
attorneys.bio:
From 1973 to 1989, David Rainwater practiced law throughout South Georgia, specializing as a trial lawyer. He was one of the first ten lawyers in the State of Georgia to become Board Certified as a civil trial lawyer by the National Board of Trial Advocacy and one of the few lawyers who became "A" rated and a member of the Bar Registry by Martindale-Hubbell in less than ten years of practice.

From 1990 to 1997, David Rainwater left private practice to serve as First Vice President and General Counsel of Central Bank and Trust in Cordele, Georgia, and later as Executive Vice President and General Counsel for American Network Services, Inc. of Norcross, Georgia. As a co-founder of American Network Services Rainwater was part of the management team that created "DEPONET®" the largest legal support network in the world.

After selling the company in 1997, Rainwater returned to private practice in Cordele in November of 1997. With both a banking and entrepreneurial background, coupled with extensive litigation experience, Rainwater is able to develop creative strategies for individuals and companies to navigate the legal waters of South Georgia. Rainwater has recovered over $50,000,000 in settlements, verdicts and recoveries since 1998 for the citizens of SouthWest Georgia.

David Rainwater

attorneys.name: Thomas O. Rainey IV
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Thomas "Torrey" Rainey is an experienced trial lawyer who handles a variety of personal injury cases. His trial skills provide the opportunity his clients deserve in order to recover full and complete compensation.

Before making the decision to work for the people, Torrey spent many years working for one of the premier, national insurance defense firms. There, he represented insurance companies, individuals and corporate defendants in a mixture of personal injury cases ranging from automobile and tractor-trailer collisions to premises liability and other catastrophic claims. This prior experience representing the insurance companies provides him a unique understanding into how the insurance companies attempt to defend injury cases. Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Torrey spent several years working for a boutique personal injury firm in Atlanta where he honed his trial skills and developed a deep understanding of the stress and worry that comes with suffering injuries from an unexpected accident. Torrey now brings that experience and knowledge to Morgan & Morgan for the benefit of his clients who have been injured through the negligence of others.

A native of Virginia, Torrey graduated from Hampden-Sydney College in 2006 with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science. In 2012, Torrey received his Juris Doctor from John Marshall Law School in Atlanta where he was honored with The Outstanding Graduate Award. During law school, Torrey served as the Executive Articles Editor of the John Marshall Law Journal and interned for the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Georgia. Torrey was also a National Finalist in the American Bar Association's National Negotiation Competition.

attorneys.name: Chris P. Ramsay
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Chris P. Ramsay is an Associate Attorney at Meriwether & Tharp, LLC. He transitioned to family law after spending over a decade practicing as an eDiscovery attorney handling multinational mass tort and environmental civil cases. Chris is an alumni of the University of Georgia where he majored in International Business with a minor in Spanish. He received an M.B.A. from Kennesaw State University while working in procurement and logistics for an international engineering firm prior to earning his Juris Doctorate at Atlanta's John Marshall Law School.

Chris is a native of Clemson, South Carolina, but has lived in Georgia for over 25 years. Chris lives in Marietta with his wife, 2 kids, and their dog and cat. When not practicing the law Chris enjoys spending time with family including serving as Cubmaster for his children's Cub Scout pack, playing soccer, international travel, and supporting the Atlanta Falcons, Atlanta United, and Georgia Bulldogs.

attorneys.name: ShaMiracle Rankin
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Sha Miracle Johnson Rankin is an attorney at Morgan and Morgan, where her practice focuses on catastrophic personal injury cases arising from trucking and automobile accidents, wrongful death, medical malpractice, nursing home neglect, and premises liability. She attributes her ability to prevail in even the most challenging cases to the relationship and trust that she builds with her clients. Miracle maintains open and honest communication with her clients, which allows her to fully understand and appreciate their injuries and pain and suffering. Her ability to parse through complex medical and legal issues, engage a jury, and build trust in her clients, has resulted in favorable verdicts and seven-figure settlements.

Miracle is a graduate of Spelman College and the University of Georgia School of Law. She enjoys spending time with her family, while also making an impact on her community through board service. She is the immediate Past President of the Georgia Association of Black Women Attorneys. She currently serves on the boards of the Atlanta Volunteer Lawyers Foundation Leadership Council, Judicial Council of Georgia Technology Committee, PINK Frog Foundation, and Stride Ahead Horse Therapy Foundation.

Miracle is a frequent instructor of Continuing Legal Education programs. Her CLE programs include:

• "Justice Day," Leadership DeKalb

• "Winning at Mediation," Trial Guides

• "Can Mediators Fill the Void Created by COVID-19 Immunity Laws," American Bar

Association

• "Law Day, Distinguished Alumni Panel," UGA School of Law

• "Making it Rain: Strategies for Success in Business Development," GABWA

• "Setting Precedent: From Legal Marketing to Case Closure," State Bar of Georgia

attorneys.name: Damany F. Ransom
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
For more than two decades, Damany has represented clients in high-stakes personal injury and business litigation cases. He started his legal career working as a law clerk for a federal judge in New Orleans. He then joined one of the country's largest law firms, where he spent years defending personal injury, product liability and commercial litigation cases for corporate defendants. He achieved great successes for his clients and rose through the ranks of the law firm to make partner.

In February 2017, Damany started The Ransom Firm to provide top-notch legal representation to accident victims and their families. He now takes on the big corporations and insurance companies. His experience as a law clerk and as a defense attorney sets him apart from many plaintiff's attorneys. Having worked as a defense lawyer, Damany is very familiar with the tactics and strategies they employ. He uses that knowledge to overcome those defense tactics and strategies, and to help his clients maximize their recovery.

Damany represents clients in a variety of personal injury matters, including motor vehicle collisions, wrongful death, premises liability claims, and product liability cases. Damany also represents victims of unfair business dealings in business litigation cases involving claims such as professional liability, breach of contract, fraud, breach of fiduciary duty, and other business torts.

In just a few short years since starting The Ransom Firm, Damany has developed a track record of success. He has recovered millions in compensation for clients in countless personal injury and business litigation cases.

attorneys.name: Philip F. Ransom
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Philip (Phil) has over 40 years of experience as a business lawyer and advisor, both in private practice and as general counsel. He counsels clients on intellectual property strategy, including securing and maintaining protection for intellectual property, litigation avoidance and licensing. A considerable amount of his practice consists of registering and enforcing copyrights, and negotiating and drafting agreements relating to the transfer and licensing of such assets. Phil also negotiates and prepares various business agreements and documents, including operating agreements, independent contractor agreements, confidentiality and nondisclosure agreements, and purchase and sale agreements.

Phil served over ten years as executive vice president and general counsel of So So Def Recordings, Inc., an Atlanta-based record company that produced several platinum and multi-platinum artists. In that capacity, Phil oversaw the business and legal affairs of So So Def, including the development of corporate strategies and policies, and the management of So So Def's business transactions, contracts and litigation. He also drafted and negotiated recording, licensing, marketing, publishing, financing and distribution agreements.

attorneys.name: Caleb H. Ratliff
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Rome, GA
attorneys.bio:
Caleb H. Ratliff practices in the areas of real estate transactions, trusts and estate administration, and landlord/tenant disputes. He currently serves as the County Administrator for Floyd County for Probate Court matters.

Mr. Ratliff received his Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Georgia, where he majored in Criminal Justice. He also obtained his law degree from the University of Georgia School of Law, where he received the William Seaborn Ashley, Jr. Scholarship for his academic achievement while at UGA in the area of trusts and estates law.

Prior to joining the firm, Mr. Ratliff practiced in Florida and was admitted to the Florida Bar in 2016. He became a member of the Georgia Bar in 2018. He is admitted to practice in all Georgia trial and appellate courts, the Supreme Court of Georgia, the United States District Court for the Northern District of Georgia, the United States District Court for the Northern District of Florida and the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida.

Mr. Ratliff is an active member of the Young Lawyers Division of the State Bar of Georgia. He was named as the recipient of the 2024 Joe Dent Hospitality Award within the YLD for his service to the YLD. In 2025, Mr. Ratliff was elected as the Secretary of the Young Lawyers Division and currently serves in that role for 2025-26.

Mr. Ratliff is also active throughout the Rome community. He is actively involved in his church and currently serves as President of the Rome area University of Georgia alumni chapter.

In his spare time Mr. Ray enjoys working with classic automobiles, playing guitar and watching his children compete as year round and collegiate swimmers.

attorneys.practice_type: Domestic relations Lawyers in Ringgold, GA
attorneys.bio:
Bryan L. Rayburn focuses his practice on personal injury and wrongful death litigation, and estate planning. Bryan is the Special Assistant Attorney General (SAAG) for Gordon County, Georgia.

Bryan is a 2014 magna cum laude graduate of John Marshall Law School, and a 2007 graduate of the University of Mississippi. During law school, Bryan held a two-year internship with the District Attorney’s Office in Dalton, where he gained extensive litigation experience. Also, during law school, Bryan received the CALI Award for Academic Excellence in Wills, Trusts, and Estates, which led to Bryan developing his Estate Planning practice. Bryan is a 2019 graduate of Leadership Dalton-Whitfield.

Bryan serves his clients aggressively to achieve results. Bryan has obtained millions of dollars for his clients in personal injury cases, including a multimillion-dollar settlement in a wrongful death action. Bryan takes pride in working hard, working smart, and recognizing priorities to achieve the best results. In addition to his private practice, Bryan serves as the Solicitor for the Cities of Tunnel Hill and Cohutta, prosecuting traffic and misdemeanor cases.

Bryan is an avid Atlanta Braves fan and golfer. Bryan and his family reside in Dalton.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Kathryn Reeder founded the Reeder Law Firm over 20 years ago after being admitted to the Georgia Bar in 1988. Over the course of her career, she has focused her practice primarily in the areas of divorce, child support, custody, wills/trusts, and probate. In addition, Kathryn is a certified mediator and a trained arbitrator.

Kathryn obtained her law degree from Georgia State University School of Law and her undergraduate degree in Psychology from George Mason University. After graduating from law school, she served as an Assistant District Attorney in both Forsyth and Cherokee counties, where her exclusive practice area was the prosecution of child support cases. In 1992 she received the "Child Support Attorney of the Year" award from the State of Georgia. In addition to representing clients in her private practice, Kathryn continues to serve as a Special Assistant Attorney General in child support related matters.

attorneys.name: Tera Reese
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Cumming, GA
attorneys.bio:
Tera is proud to live and work in Metro-Atlanta. A Wisconsin Native, Tera attended the University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh and earned a Bachelor of Science Degree with a major in Political Science and a minor in Public Administration. She was proud to be a four-year letter winner on the UW-O nationally ranked women’s basketball team. After graduation, Tera headed south to attend law school at Loyola University of New Orleans School of Law.

A strong believer in community service, Tera spent much of her time working in the New Orleans community. She was an active intern with the Fair Housing Action Center; she participated in a program to educate public school students; she helped community non-profits as an officer in the St. Thomas Aquinas Society; and she was an award-winning participant in the Loyola Law Clinic, representing Louisiana’s indigent while in her third-year of law school. Tera moved to the metro-Atlanta in 1998 after graduation and continued her active community involvement through the Georgia Legal Services Program, helping Georgia’s indigent with family law matters and other civil legal issues.

In 2003, Tera proudly opened her own family law practice in Cumming, Georgia. In her career, Tera has successfully represented clients in over thirty counties in Georgia. Tera is known as a tenacious advocate who enjoys the courtroom, but who also believes all family law matters should settle out of court when possible. Tera has been asked to speak to local groups on family law issues, and enjoys doing so. Tera also writes family law articles for groups when requested. Tera is a certified and registered mediator with the Georgia Office of Dispute Resolution. She can mediate civil and family law cases. She enjoys her mediation practice thoroughly and feels that all cases, no matter how contentious, can settle.

Tera has served on the board of and been active with local Forsyth County non-profit organizations. Currently, Tera is a member-at-large of the Executive Committee of the Family Law Section of the Georgia Bar Association, and a member of the Forsyth County Bar Association, and the North Fulton and Forsyth County Chambers of Commerce. Tera lives in Cumming, Georgia with her husband, Brad, and their three children.

attorneys.name: Michael G. Regas II
attorneys.firm_name: Stone Law Group Trial Lawyers, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mike grew up in Sandy Springs and continues to live on the north side of Atlanta with his wife Mary and their children, Joe and Isabelle. A 1987 graduate of the University of Georgia with a BBA degree in finance, Mike was on the Dean's List and was active in the Defender-Advocate society throughout college. He also was a member of the Lambda Chi Alpha Fraternity.

Mike graduated from Georgia State University College of Law in Atlanta, Georgia in 1991. While in law school, he clerked for Justice Richard Bell of the Georgia Supreme Court and later was employed part-time for a medical malpractice defense firm. While in law school, Mike also served on the Moot Court Board and was a member of the school's student judiciary.

During the first ten years of his practice, Mike handled a wide variety of general civil litigation matters including personal injury, business torts, and contract disputes. In 2001, he accepted an opportunity to work for prominent plaintiff's personal injury firm where he began focusing his legal career on representing individuals in state and federal courts in all categories of personal injury and wrongful death matters including automobile accidents, trucking accidents, medical malpractice, products liability and premises liability cases.

Mike enjoys an AV Peer Review Rating from LexisNexis Martindale-Hubbell and has been honored to be included as a member of Georgia SuperLawyers from 2009 to the present. He also is one of the first plaintiff personal injury lawyers in Georgia to be board certified as a medical malpractice attorney by the American Board of Professional Liability Attorneys. Mike is a member of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association (GTLA Champion Member), the Atlanta Bar Association, Lawyers Club of Atlanta, and the American Association for Justice.

In his free time, Mike enjoys working out, playing golf, snow skiing and spending time with his family. Mike also is an active member of the Buckhead Lion's Club where he has served as President and as the chairperson for their annual golf tournament to benefit Children's Healthcare of Atlanta and the SHARE Military Initiative at Shepherd Center Atlanta.

You may contact Mike for a free consultation at mike@stonelaw.com.

attorneys.name: Robert A. B. Reichert
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Robert A. B. Reichert is the son of Mr. and Mrs. Albert P. Reichert, Sr., and was born in Macon. After completing his studies at Stratford Academy in 1966, he spent roughly two years at the University of Georgia before serving in the United States Army.

He was a helicopter pilot for the 1st Air Cavalry Division in Vietnam in 1970–1971. He served in the military for 20 years, rising to the rank of Chief Warrant Officer while stationed at Fort Hood (Texas).

After serving his country, Mr. Reichert moved back to Macon and enrolled at the University of Georgia, from which he graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Agriculture in 1978. After that, he went on to law school at Mercer University's Walter F. George School of Law, where he interned in the Fall of his last year in Senator Sam Nunn's legislative section in Washington. In 1981, after finishing law school, Robert became an associate attorney with the law office of Anderson, Walker & Reichert. In 1985, he was made a partner and focused on civil litigation. He has been honored as a Fellow by both the American Bar Foundation and the Lawyers Foundation of Georgia, and he holds membership in both the Georgia and American Bar Associations.

In 1987, Mr. Reichert ran for and was elected to a seat on the Macon City Council. From 1992 to the end of the 2002 legislative session, he served as the representative for northwest Macon and Bibb County in the Georgia House of Representatives, District 126. Mr. Reichert was first elected Mayor of Macon in 2007, and then, after that city's government merged with that of neighboring Bibb County, he was elected Mayor of Macon-Bibb County. attorneys.name: Kirkland E. Reid
attorneys.practice_type: Alternative Dispute Resolution Lawyers in Columbus, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Kirk Reid maintains an active appellate practice, handling appeals before state appellate courts and the Eleventh Circuit. Kirk also has a niche practice representing departments of correction in Eighth Amendment claims brought individually and as class actions.

​Kirk is a native of Columbus. He received his Bachelor of Arts degree, with honors, in English from Columbus State University. Kirk received his Master’s Degree from the University of Georgia, and was a Teaching Assistant in the English Department while there. Kirk graduated from Samford University’s Cumberland School of Law in 1998. At Cumberland, Kirk was a member of the Cumberland Law Review, and in his third year was on the editorial board of the law review, serving as Research Editor.

​Before returning home and joining The Finley Firm, P.C., Kirk practiced in Mobile, Alabama, and focused his litigation practice on the representation of financial institutions, as well as municipalities, governmental agencies, title companies, and both publicly-traded and privately-held commercial entities. As part of his responsibilities as outside counsel to various financial institutions, Kirk at one point oversaw and directed all litigation for a large regional bank throughout its southeastern footprint.

​In September 2008, Kirk’s Mobile-based firm joined with Jones Walker LLP, a large Gulf Coast firm with its principal office in New Orleans. Kirk continued his practice as a partner with Jones Walker, representing national and local clients in both litigation and arbitration. Kirk was part of a small team of law firms that represented General Motors in numerous arbitration proceedings in the congressionally-created Automobile Industry Special Binding Arbitration Program, a nationwide arbitral process administered by the American Arbitration Association that was occasioned by the 2008 economic downturn and subsequent bankruptcy filings of Chrysler and GM.

​Kirk and his wife Jane Ivy (formerly of Waycross, GA) have two daughters. In his spare time, Kirk enjoys reading, traveling, hiking, and spending time on his family property in Seale, Alabama.

attorneys.name: Albert P. Reichert Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Wills Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Albert P. Reichert Jr. is a partner at Anderson, Walker & Reichert, LLP, in Macon, Georgia. While growing up in Macon, Georgia, he attended both Joseph Clisby Elementary and Lanier High School. His senior class elected him president. There, he excelled academically and was elected president of the Emory Glee Club and Phi Beta Kappa. He served as Vice President of the Harvard Journal on Legislation while earning his law degree from Harvard. After finishing law school in 1964, he proceeded to work at Anderson, Walker, and Reichert, LLP.

Mr. Reichert focuses his practice on taxation, corporate and business law, and estate planning and administration. He chaired the State Bar of Georgia's Commission on Continuing Lawyer Competency, as well as its Fiduciary Law and Tax Sections. He has participated in the revision of the code in the areas of trust law, probate, and guardianship. Over the course of several years, these committees met once each month, finally leading to the adoption of new trust, probate and guardianship codes by the Georgia General Assembly.

Mr. Reichert has been accepted as a Fellow of the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel, an organization of lawyers and law academics who are experts in the areas of wills and trusts, estate planning, probate procedure, and the administration of trusts and estates. He also has the distinction of being a Fellow in the American College of Tax Counsel. He has been included in the list of The Best Lawyers in America.

In addition to his career as an attorney, Mr. Reichert has also been involved in the Boy Scouts, holding the positions of Scoutmaster and President of the Central Georgia Council. He has also served as the church's chair of the finance committee and as a member of the choir. The Macon Rotary Club president and the District 6920 governor are just two of his many Rotary International positions. He was on the board of the Community Foundation of Central Georgia, Inc. from its inception. He is the Community Foundation's legal adviser.

attorneys.name: Steven M. Reising
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate, Partnership, and LLC Law Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Steven M. Reising is a Senior Associate Attorney at Briskin, Cross & Sanford, LLC, where he advises corporate clients and individuals on complex business transactions and litigation matters. With more than sixteen years of diverse legal experience, Steve combines practical insight, creative problem solving, and disciplined advocacy to deliver effective results for his clients.

Steve’s practice spans corporate, partnership, and LLC law, business and contract litigation, mergers and acquisitions, franchise law, restrictive covenants, and construction and real estate disputes. Before joining Briskin, Cross & Sanford, he served as a partner at a nationally recognized full-service law firm, where he defended Fortune 500 companies and other clients in a wide range of litigation, including contract disputes, negligent security, premises liability, and construction defect claims. Earlier in his career, he practiced with firms in Chicago, representing both plaintiffs and defendants in civil litigation, and earning a reputation as a “utility player” for his ability to manage complex, high-volume caseloads across multiple disciplines.

Steve has appeared before magistrate, trial, and appellate courts as well as administrative law tribunals, consistently achieving favorable outcomes in high-stakes matters. Known for his energetic and solution-oriented approach, he focuses on resolving disputes efficiently while protecting his clients’ business interests and reputations.

An active member of the legal community, Steve serves as President of the Forsyth County Bar Association (2025–2026 term) and has held leadership roles with the North Fulton Bar Association, the Marion T. Pope, Jr. American Inn of Court, the Law Library of Forsyth County, and local chambers of commerce. He is also a frequent presenter and keynote speaker on litigation, risk management, and insurance topics for professional and business audiences.

Outside the office, Steve enjoys attending sporting events and spending time with his wife, children, and dog.

attorneys.name: Donald Edward Reott III
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Donald Reott spent his childhood in Georgia while his father was stationed at Kings Bay Naval Base. He later moved to Florida and earned his undergraduate degree cum laude in Physics from the University of Florida with a minor in Philosophy.

Donald returned to Georgia to enroll in Georgia State University's College of Law. As he worked toward his Juris Doctor, Donald focused on developing his litigation skills by joining the Student Trail Lawyer Association and attending upper level litigation courses. Donald graduated from law school with honors in 2012 and was admitted to the Georgia Bar later that year.

Before joining Stottlemyer & Associates, Donald worked for a small plaintiffs' firm in Gwinnett County. There, he practiced Personal Injury, Workers' Compensation, and Social Security. From there, he joined a firm in Sandy Springs, where he was responsible for managing a large caseload of active litigation files, many of which he brought to jury trials.

Now at Stottlemyer & Associates, Donald works to help injury victims in Georgia. Whether one is injured due to the negligent or intentional conduct of another or gets hurt while fulfilling their job duties, Donald navigates the legal issues that these victims face and diligently fights for the highest compensation under the law.

Outside of the practice of law, Donald enjoys hiking, football, and food. He currently lives in Brookhaven, Georgia with his wife, and their two daughters, dog, and cat.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Augusta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Ashton is a trial lawyer in Augusta, GA who focuses his law practice on the representation of individuals who have suffered serious injuries or damages due to the negligent or reckless conduct of others, including automobile wrecks, job-related accidents, unsafe premises, or defective products. Before beginning his practice, Ashton obtained his J.D., at Emory University School of Law, where he gained valuable courtroom experience as an intern assisting the District Attorney for DeKalb County. After his time at Emory, Ashton received experience as a trial attorney at a respected personal injury firm in Atlanta before moving to Augusta. Over the course of his career, Ashton has assisted deserving clients in recovering millions of dollars in injury cases throughout Georgia.

Ashton has enjoyed a variety of experiences in the legal profession. He assisted and helped manage a successful judicial campaign, and he is a member of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association LEAD class where he has the opportunity to collaborate with other up-and-coming plaintiffs lawyers across the State. Ashton believes that good communication between a lawyer and client is essential to effective representation, and he makes every effort to be accessible and straightforward with his clients.

Ashton is a native of the Aiken—Augusta area and attended Augusta Preparatory Day School and the University of South Carolina. He enjoys spending time with his family, attending football games, and playing golf.

Attorney Jacob Rhein represents people who have been harmed by the negligence, dishonesty, or incompetence of lawyers and other fiduciaries. He also represents individuals who have suffered serious personal injuries, including in slip and fall and auto accident cases.

Rhein has a reputation among his peers for novel legal argument and fierce loyalty to his clients. These abilities are best demonstrated in his results as a “second lawyer.” Rhein frequently spots issues in the law that other lawyers have missed, and is able to craft these issues into effective advocacy. Rhein represents clients in metro Atlanta and throughout Georgia.

Rhein earned his law degree at the University of Minnesota Law School, consistently ranked by the U.S. News & World Report as one of the top law schools in the nation. He was appointed Lead Managing Editor of the Minnesota Law Review and received his J.D. with honors.

attorneys.name: Richard A. Rice Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Richard Rice is a former Assistant United States Attorney, former counsel in the U.S. Navy Judge Advocate General's Corps (JAG Corps) and a former trial attorney at two of the nation's largest law firms. Richard Rice has prosecuted and defended civil and criminal cases in federal and state courts across the nation.

Richard Rice received his law degree at the University of Notre Dame Law School, where he was the managing editor of the Journal of Law, Ethics and Public Policy. He received his undergraduate degree from the University of Georgia.

As an Assistant United States Attorney, Richard Rice was a federal prosecutor in the Organized Crime and Drug Enforcement Task Force (OCDETF) section where he investigated and prosecuted large scale drug trafficking and money laundering organizations operating nationally and internationally. Richard Rice conducted some of the most extensive Title III (wiretap) investigations in the United States, and coordinated multi-jurisdictional and interagency investigations. He investigated and prosecuted the full spectrum of federal crimes, including public corruption, fraud schemes, firearm offenses, bank robberies and internet crimes. He also prepared and argued numerous appeals before the Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit.

As a trial attorney with the Special Litigation Section of the U.S. Department of Justice, Richard Rice worked on the prosecution of Zacarias Moussaoui, the twelfth hijacker. He also investigated and litigated civil enforcement actions against state and local police departments alleged to have engaged in a pattern of civil rights abuses and state and local detention facilities alleged to have had unconstitutional conditions of confinement.

As an officer in the Navy JAG Corps, Richard Rice achieved an acquittal rate of over 80%. He tried more cases than any other defense counsel in the second largest military district, and served as appellate defense counsel for defendants in the Navy and Marine Corps located throughout the world.

As an attorney in the Washington, D.C. office of Kirkland & Ellis, Richard Rice specialized in commercial litigation and products liability litigation, representing Fortune 50 companies in complex and high-dollar civil matters. In one case, he served as the senior associate on the trial team defending an international company in a multi-billion dollar class action trial in federal court that resulted in a full defense verdict.

As an attorney in the Washington, D.C. office of Hunton & Williams, Richard Rice specialized in white collar criminal defense and commercial and environmental litigation. His work included successfully defeating a federal health care investigation prior to indictment and without any publicity and defending utility companies against E.P.A. enforcement actions.

attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Dalton, GA
attorneys.bio:
Tommy grew up in Dalton, Georgia, graduating from Dalton High School as valedictorian of his class in 2015. He earned a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science, cum laude, from Vanderbilt University in 2019 and went on to receive his J.D. from the University of Georgia School of Law in 2022.

During law school, Tommy gained valuable judicial experience through an internship with Georgia Supreme Court Justice Charles J. Bethel, developing a strong foundation in legal research and writing. In law school, Tommy also served as a legal intern in the State and Juvenile Courts of Athens-Clarke County, served as Vice President of Communications of the UGA Law Federalist Society, and was a member of the Christian Legal Society. Today, Tommy’s practice consists primarily of business law, probate litigation, real estate matters, and general civil litigation.

Outside of practice, Tommy is involved in his local church and serves on the Board of Directors of the Whitfield County Law Library. He is also married to Laura Kate Ridley, with whom he has two children. In his free time, Tommy enjoys reading, traveling, and spending time with family.

attorneys.name: John A. Roberts
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Gainesville, GA
attorneys.bio:
John Roberts is the owner and senior member of the firm and has a diverse business, educational and legal background which brings unique incites to the administration and daily delivery of legal representation to our clients. Graduating from Indiana State University in 1972, Mr. Roberts began his career in the area of Risk Management for hospitals which exceeded 800 beds. Having worked closely with medical staff, Board of Directors and hospital administration, Mr. Roberts gained unmatched experience in the management of medical and hospital liability and malpractice. During his tenure in hospital administration his attention was directed to the development of pre-hospital emergency care and he was instrumental in the development of the Department of Transportation Regulations adopted by the United States government for both ground and air ambulance. From this beginning he later acted as Public Safety Director for a large metropolitan government and supervised well over 600 employees in police, fire and emergency medical services and was honored by President Ronald Reagan for his achievements in this area. As a result of his willingness to commit resources to these areas and cutting edge innovations he has worked with officials in many areas of the world. To name a few; The Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia, Abu-Dubai and United Arab Emirates, 101st Airborne, The Air Ministry of Canada, the newly formed government of Poland, and the Israeli Army. He acted as a special assistant to Governor Rockefeller in the development of a statewide air ambulance program administered by the state police and has been published in many trade and medical journals.

After living what most would declare a full life, Mr. Roberts was drawn to the practice of law. Having graduated summa cum laude and President of his legal fraternity, Mr. Roberts received at graduation the honor of being most likely to succeed in the practice of law by his fellow classmates. Mr. Roberts clerked for a downtown firm and after graduation continued to work for the firm for a short time prior to establishing his own law firm, The Roberts Law Firm which was established in late 1991.

Mr. Roberts has represented well over 16,000 clients in his tenure as owner and senior member of the firm. The Firm has continued to grow and flourish under his tutelage and has far exceeded his expectations. He currently enjoys the opportunity to work in the court room and has represented many diverse interests in his career. He is now routinely called upon to assist in the area of Indian Affairs and Gaming and other Native Peoples interests. His representation extends to Public Traded companies and a variety of nation wide corporations in the manufacturing, health-care, and food service industry. He has most recently represented a state agency in the United States Supreme Court and has been a municipal court judge in the State of Georgia since 2004.

Graham and his wife, Kitty, live in Atlanta. In his spare time, he enjoys fly fishing, duck hunting, and spending time with family and friends.

attorneys.bio:
Sam grew up in North Carolina and earned his Bachelor of Arts degree in English from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. He went on to obtain his Juris Doctor from Georgia State University College of Law, where he served as Assistant Student Writing Editor of the Georgia State Law Review. He graduated Magna Cum Laude and was inducted into the Order of the Coif in recognition of his academic achievement.

Sam began his legal career as a Public Defender, where he developed into a skilled and fearless courtroom advocate. He later transitioned into private practice, focusing exclusively on family law. Sam represents clients in matters involving divorce, child custody, protective orders and other areas of family law, with a high level of professionalism, empathy, and determination. He is dedicated to delivering effective advocacy tailored to the unique circumstances of each case, with an unwavering commitment to protecting the best interests of his clients and their families.

Outside of his legal practice, Sam is a lifelong musician and occasional oil painter. He enjoys spending time with his dachshund, Cowboy.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Savannah, GA
attorneys.bio:
Scott has handled DUI and criminal cases for 15 years. He has handled thousands of DUI cases, drug cases, theft, and domestic violence cases - while communicating with clients and their families, keeping everyone well-informed every step of the way.

Scott possess specialized training in the areas of DUI - he is certified in SFST (roadside sobriety tests) and ARIDE (advanced DUI and Drug impairment). A former prosecutor, Scott handled misdemeanor and felony DUIs, Vehicular Homicides, Theft, Elder Exploitation, Aggravated Assault, Firearm charges, Child Abuse cases, and Murder.

As a former prosecutor, Scott saw first-hand how a good attorney can positively influence the outcome of cases. Now, Scott uses his experience, skills, and training to vigorously defend clients and their rights.

Scott graduated from Vanderbilt University and from Indiana University McKinney School of Law. He lives in Savannah, with his wife and two children. His family attends Blessed Sacrament Church.

attorneys.name: Tiffiny Robinson
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Tiffiny Robinson was born overseas while her mother served in our faithful military before her family ultimately settled in Georgia to reside. Mrs. Robinson received her Bachelor's degree in Political Science from Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia. After college, she relocated to San Diego, California on a full scholarship, attending Thomas Jefferson School of Law. While in California, Mrs. Robinson was a member of the Mock Trial team where her love for advocacy and the Courtroom was nurtured.

As a Pastor's daughter, Mrs. Robinson was raised to respect and honor herself and her community and to always fight for what is right. She has received numerous accolades and awards highlighting her commitment to serving her community and Mrs. Robinson has dedicated her practice to civil justice, meticulously providing intentional excellence beyond measure to her clients.

attorneys.bio:
Buck is a partner at Rogers Fite LLC. He is a P.O.S.T. (Peace Officer Standards and Training) Certified Guest Lecturer, Commercial Motor Vehicle Collisions and Law, and holds a Class "A" Commercial Driver's license. Buck is the 55th President of the State Bar of Georgia and was President of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association for 2013-14 and served on the Atlanta Bar Association's Continuing Education Committee.

He is primarily a civil attorney representing victims of catastrophic claims and in In 2006, Buck was selected as one of the "14 Under 40" by the Fulton County Daily Report. Since 2008 he has been named by Georgia Super Lawyers magazine as a Georgia Super Lawyer and was included in the list of Top 100 Georgia Super Lawyers since 2011. Buck was also recently named to the list of Best Lawyers in Georgia in 2015.

He has devoted himself to community service, including serving on the Board of Directors for Road Safe America (trucking safety advocacy group), Chair of the Board of Directors of the Civil Justice PAC, Inc., Regional Council of Mothers against Drunk Driving (MADD), and the Shepherd Spinal and Brain Injury Center, where he is a Trustee and serves on both the Auxiliary and Advisory Boards.

Buck is a member of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum and the American Trial Lawyers Association Top 100 Trial Lawyers. He is a sustaining member of the Interstate Trucking Litigation Group, and an associate member of the National Association of Professional Accident Reconstruction Specialists, Inc.

attorneys.name: Cale Rogers
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial & Residential Real Estate Closings Lawyers in Gainesville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Cale Rogers is a partner with Coleman, Chambers & Rogers, LLP. Cale assists clients in a variety of areas including general business and civil litigation. He is the supervising attorney in our commercial and residential real estate closing department. He also regularly represents clients in probate matters, real estate litigation, and estate planning.

Cale has earned a number of noteworthy distinctions. In 2013, he achieved an AV Preeminent rating from Martindale-Hubbell, the highest possible rating in Legal Ability and Ethical Standards issued by one of the oldest directories for attorneys. He was selected by the American Lawyer as a Top Rated Lawyer, has been named as one of Georgia's Legal Elite by Georgia Trend Magazine, and is a member of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum. Recently, Cale participated in a jury trial that resulted in a seven-figure verdict in favor of aggrieved property owners against a neighboring landowner for nuisance and trespass and orchestrated the appeal that resulted in the verdict being upheld by the Georgia appellate courts.

As the supervising real estate attorney for our firm, Cale ensures that our clients' needs are met when purchasing or selling residential or commercial property. With more than 16 years of experience as a closing attorney, you can be assured that your closing will be handled professionally and efficiently. Cale also brings his real estate experience to the courtroom, and has litigated real estate related disputes, including boundary line disputes, easement disputes, and quiet title actions.

Cale frequently practices in local probate courts. Whether you are filing a simple will for probate, involved in a contested estate, or want to challenge or caveat a will that has been filed, Cale can represent you in your probate matter in any county in North Georgia. Cale is well versed in Year's Support statute and its implementation in avoiding certain claims of creditors, and prepares wills, trusts and other asset protection and estate planning documents for our clients.

Cale is also the go-to corporate attorney for a significant portion the firm's Business, Corporate and Contract work . Helping our clients prepare, interpret, negotiate and enforce contracts, Cale is proficient in real estate, business, and all varieties of contracts. Cale also handles a large portion of the firm's appellate work, filing briefs with the Georgia Court of Appeals and Georgia Supreme Court for the firm.

Top Rated Lawyer by the American Lawyer in 2013

AV Preeminent rating from Martindale-Hubbell
