attorneys.name: S. Lester Tate III
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury - Plaintiff Lawyers in Cartersville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Lester Tate has tried hundreds of cases in federal and state courts throughout Georgia and is recognized as one of the state's top trial lawyers by numerous publications. Additionally, he serves as the elected Treasurer of the State Bar of Georgia, the governing authority of the legal profession in this state.

In 2006, Georgia Trend Magazine named Lester as one of Georgia's Legal Elite. Additionally, Atlanta Magazine and the Journal of Law and Politics have included him on their Super Lawyers lists and, since 1996, he has carried the highest peer review rating given by the national legal directory Martindale Hubble. In 2002, he served as Chairman of the State Bar's Trial Section.

With more than a hundred jury trials to his credit, Lester has won several million dollar personal injury verdicts and settlements. He has successfully defended individuals against murder charges and obtained acquittals for countless others facing felony charges. Lester has also handled a number of complex commercial disputes, and argued more than a dozen cases before Georgia's State and Federal appellate courts.

Lester's recent victories include a $1.3 million dollar verdict against the Georgia Department of Transportation for a man whose wife was killed because of a downed stop sign, and a $2 million dollar judgment for a man who suffered severe brain injury as a result of the inhalation of natural gas. He has also been engaged to represent the chairman of the board and directors of a large electric membership corporation in a multi-million dollar derivative suit. Lester has repeatedly been called upon by both bench and bar for tasks within the profession. These include:

Representing the lawyers of the Cherokee Judicial Circuit on the State Bar's Board of Governors for over 10 years;

Appointment by the Supreme Court of Georgia to the Disciplinary Board's Investigative Panel, where he later served as Chairman; and

Election by the Judges of the U.S. District Court of the Northern District of Georgia to serve on the Federal Defender Board where he also served as President.

Lester is, and has been for many years active in civic and political affairs. He was the 1995 Chair of the Bartow County United Way campaign and is a former Chair of the Bartow County Democratic Party and the State Democratic Committee. Prior to law school, Lester served on the staff of the U.S. Senator Sam Nunn and as press secretary to Congressman George (Buddy) Darden. For several years Lester wrote a weekly political column for the Cartersville Daily Tribune. He has also served as a legal and political commentator on various radio and television broadcasts.

Jim is a member of the Atlanta Claims Association, American Bar Association, Georgia Defense Lawyers Association, Southern Loss Association and State Bar of Georgia, where he is a member and prior chairman of the Tort and Insurance Practice Section and the Property Insurance Law Committee and St. Thomas More Society.

attorneys.name: Lydia Taylor
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Lydia Taylor is the co‑owner, Partner, and Federal Employment Attorney at Southworth PC, where she directs the firm’s day‑to‑day litigation strategy and shares leadership of a mission‑driven team devoted to protecting the rights and livelihoods of current and former federal employees. A forceful advocate before the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the Merit Systems Protection Board, and the Office of Federal Operations, she has resolved scores of discrimination, harassment, retaliation, and whistleblower matters—often securing favorable settlements long before hearing—while also defending federal careers when removal or clearance actions threaten decades of service.

Her path to partnership is rooted in both deep legal training and front‑line personnel experience. After earning her J.D. from the University of Baltimore School of Law and a B.A. in Psychology from Oakwood College, Lydia spent years inside large public‑sector organizations as a Human Resources Director, Strategic Alignment Specialist, and Employee Relations Partner. Those roles taught her how agencies think, how policies are built, and where cracks appear—knowledge she now turns against the government when its own systems fail its employees. A stint with the U.S. Department of Justice as a Litigation Support Specialist and her certification as a federal EEO Investigator further sharpened her command of complex discovery, data, and procedural nuance.

Clients value Lydia’s uncommon mix of legal acuity and emotional intelligence. In one representative case, she guided a thirty‑year federal employee through a wrongful‑termination dispute that collided with a family crisis. By centering his personal goals—dignity, closure, and economic security—she crafted a negotiation strategy that delivered a substantial settlement and a graceful exit, proving that justice can be both efficient and humane.

Today, Lydia channels Southworth PC’s core values—truth, results, client focus, compassion, and continuous improvement—into every brief she files and every counsel she gives. Her leadership ensures that federal employees confronting the most intimidating stages of their careers find both a formidable litigator and a mindful ally committed to turning legal challenges into meaningful victories.

attorneys.name: Michelle Taylor
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Johns Creek, GA
attorneys.bio:
Personally and professionally, Michelle has always strived to be a number of things, but top of that list has always been advocate. Having had many people advocate for her during her life Michelle understands exactly how important a voice for the voiceless can be. After graduating with her Bachelor of Art in Sociology from Purdue University, Michelle began her career in social work working with children and families in crisis dealing with various positions. Some requiring emergency intervention sometimes working with state providers and private providers. Michelle greatly enjoyed working with families but soon realized there were limitations to her impact as a social worker and began looking toward fighting as a legal advocate. Michelle attended Roosevelt University in Chicago's paralegal program and began to discover how she could help from within the legal system.

After re-locating to Georgia in 2009 Michelle was able to realize her dream of becoming an attorney by attending Atlanta's John Marshall Law School. Michelle graduated with her Juris Doctorate in 2014. Passed the bar exam in October of 2015 and was sworn in as a member of the bar in December of 2015. Since then, Michelle has worked hard with clients from all walks of life to ensure their voice is heard in the courtroom and beyond. Including becoming a Guardian ad litem in Gordon County Georgia in 2020. So far in her career, Michelle has enjoyed working with all kinds of people, families, and situations and looks forward to assisting many more going forward.

When she is done advocating in the court room, Michelle likes to take some time for herself by hiking, paddle boarding, and kayaking Georgia's wilderness and waterways with her dog. Michelle dedicates as much free time as possible to her extended family network and attempts to visit them all over the United States.

Ralph Taylor is an experienced lawyer known for excellence in the practice of law. He has been recognized as a Super Lawyers by Georgia Trend magazine, Top Lawyers in Georgia by Atlanta magazine, America's Top 100 High Stakes Litigators, America's Top Honored Lawyer by the American Registry, and has been given the preeminent AV rating by Martindale Hubbell. attorneys.practice_type: Individual, Property and Business Law Lawyers in Cumming, GA
attorneys.bio:
STUART TEAGUE - Georgia Individual, Property and Business Law

Stuart Teague is a GA business and property attorney, emphasising in advising clients concerning disputes related to land and business in Georgia. His experience dealing with zoning issues and land use disputes make him an excellent choice if you need representation in a land-related case.

Land use and zoning cases require a GA business and property attorney who understands the ordinances and laws that relate to them. Stuart Teague has worked on GA zoning cases and land use disputes across the whole state. He understands the need for attention to detail in these cases thanks to the wide variety of local, city and country ordinances that can affect each case differently based on the location of the problem.

If you're involved in a land use or zoning dispute, don't trust your case to a GA attorney that doesn't have vast knowledge of Georgia law and of the types of details and issues that can arise in the state's 159 counties and hundreds of municipalities.

A good Georgia business and property attorney can handle cases for those counties and municipalities, as well as trade associations, real estate agents and brokers, land developers, citizens' groups, homeowner associations, homeowners and builders on both the local and national level.

Stuart Teague has handled cases for all these different types of individuals and groups, and can help you in your case dealing with things like commercial, residential and industrial rezoning, annexations, subdivision development ordinances, all types of use permits, zoning permits, landfills and waste, parking traffic flow and any other issues related to zoning and land use.

Don't waste time and money on an attorney with less knowledge and experience handling these issues. Your land use issue needs to be resolved as quickly as possible with a favorable outcome. By choosing an experienced GA business and property attorney you're taking the right steps to help that happen. Contact Stuart Teague today.

attorneys.name: Robert B. Teilhet
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Rob Teilhet became an attorney in order to give a voice to Georgians who otherwise may never be heard. Since 2001, he has practiced primarily in the area of workers' compensation, representing workers who have been hurt on the job. These workers are often denied the medical and income benefits to which they are entitled, and need someone willing to fight for them and their families.

In addition, Mr. Teilhet represented Smyrna and Marietta in the Georgia House of Representatives for four terms following his election in 2002 at the age of 28. In the legislature, he earned the respect of Democrats, Republicans and independents for his hard work, honesty, and integrity and served as Chief Deputy Whip of the House Democratic Caucus.

In his 2010 statewide campaign to become Attorney General, he raised more than $600,000 and earned more than 116,000 votes at just 36 years of age. Following the campaign, he was appointed by Governor Sonny Perdue to be Executive Director of the Georgia Public Defender Standards Council, the state agency charged with ensuring the representation of indigent criminal defendants.

He has been named one of Georgia's Most Influential People by James Magazine, a "Star to Watch" by the National Journal's Hotline, one of Cobb County's "20 Risings Stars Under 40" and one of The University of Georgia Alumni Association's "40 under 40." He has received awards for his public work from, among others, Georgia Conservation Voters, the Georgia Water Coalition, the Cobb County Association of Educators, Georgia Family Council, Georgia Psychological Association, and the Georgia Municipal Association.

Mr. Teilhet has served as an adjunct Professor at the University of Georgia School of Law and as a member of the Marietta First United Methodist Church Council. He's a member of the Leadership Georgia Class of 2009.

attorneys.firm_name: Josh W. Thacker, Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Griffin, GA
attorneys.bio:
Defending Your Rights in Georgia Criminal and Traffic Cases

If you have been accused of a crime in Georgia, you need a lawyer who will dedicate himself to protecting your rights.

I am criminal defense attorney Josh W. Thacker, and I have both prosecuted and defended all kinds of cases. I spent 6 years as an Assistant District Attorney. I handled everything from speeding tickets to murder cases. I know how the prosecution puts cases together, and I know how to fight them.

I believe that my experience as a prosecutor allows me to defend my clients more effectively. It gives me a clear understanding of your realistic options and practical knowledge about what strategies could work for you.

To set up a free consultation about any Georgia traffic or criminal case, contact me today

Accused of a Crime in the Atlanta Metro Area or Central Georgia?

Whether you are a Georgia resident or a visitor, I can help you put together a powerful defense. I handle a wide variety of felony and misdemeanor offenses, including traffic violations and speeding tickets:

White collar crimes

Property and theft offenses

DUI and traffic offenses

Commercial driver's license (CDL) defense

Drug crimes

Juvenile crimes

Violent crimes

Murder and manslaughter

I understand how important your case is and when you have a question, you expect a prompt answer from your attorney. I return calls as soon as possible, and I have a knowledgeable staff to answer most questions if I am unavailable.

Contact me to set up a free initial consultation to discuss the criminal charges you are facing. Please bring any paperwork you have to this meeting. Even if you don't think it's important, every piece of information helps me put together a strong defense.

My office is located across from the courthouse on East Solomon Street in Griffin, Georgia

attorneys.name: Marina D. Thelen
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Litigation Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Marina D. Thelen is an actively licensed attorney in Texas and in Georgia. She is currently a trial attorney in the Litigation Department of Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele.

Marina graduated Southern Methodist University in less than four years with a double major in Political Science and International Relations with a minor in Russian Area Studies. She spent a summer on the London trading floor through a Boston University internship program before obtaining her Juris Doctor from Tulane University School of Law where she was a member of the Journal of International and Comparative Law.

In Texas, Marina was an Assistant County Attorney in Austin for five Justice of the Peace Precincts where she participated in bench and jury trials and represented the State in competency hearings. She then went on to work for several big Dallas law firms in intellectual property protection, oil and gas, and complex commercial litigation. She gained experience in topics related to intellectual property rights, software technology development, theft of trade secrets, misappropriation of business concepts, breach of non-compete and tortious interference for several high-tech industry leaders. Marina was admitted to practice law in Georgia in 2024 and joined MIJS as a member of the litigation department.

In her free time, Marina enjoys mid-century modern design and architecture, travelling, hot yoga and spending time with her family and dogs.

attorneys.name: LaShanda Thompson
attorneys.practice_type: Federal Employment Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
LaShanda Thompson is an experienced federal-employment attorney with more than a decade of experience advising on, investigating, and resolving complex workplace matters within the federal government. She brings deep insight into agency operations and a strong commitment to protecting employee rights.

Before joining Southworth PC, LaShanda served at the National Institutes of Health, where she handled high-profile EEO complaints, reasonable-accommodation matters, MSPB cases, and performance and disciplinary issues. Her work advising senior leaders and overseeing internal investigations gives her a clear understanding of how agencies assess, manage, and defend employment cases—knowledge she now uses to anticipate agency strategy and build strong, evidence-based cases for her clients.

With experience across multiple federal agencies, LaShanda is well-versed in Title VII, the ADA/ADAAA, FMLA, and the procedural frameworks governing federal employment law. She applies a disciplined and analytical approach to every matter, helping employees navigate complex systems with clarity and confidence. She excels at identifying procedural weaknesses, promoting accountability, and positioning clients for the strongest possible outcome.

At Southworth PC, LaShanda leverages her extensive government background to help federal employees protect their rights, defend their reputations, and receive fair treatment in the workplace.

Outside the office, LaShanda enjoys traveling and spending time with her family. She values opportunities to explore new places and perspectives and is driven by a commitment to continuous learning and excellence.

attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Lawyers in Valdosta, GA
attorneys.bio:
PERSONAL INFO

Lucy Tomberlin was born and raised in Valdosta, Georgia and graduated from Valdosta High School. She received a B.A. in History at Agnes Scott College in Decatur, Georgia before attending law school at the University of Georgia. She graduated from law school in 1993 and returned to Valdosta to practice law. She is admitted to practice in both Georgia and Florida. Her practice in Florida is currently limited to Social Security appeals.

CAREER

Ms. Tomberlin limits her practice mainly to the field of Social Security. She represents Social Security claimants at all stages from the initial application through the Appeals Council. Although the majority of her Social Security cases are disability claims, she also handles a variety of other Social Security issues including survivor's benefits, retirement claims, and overpayment cases. Ms. Tomberlin also handles estate planning and probate practice for simple estates.

PROFESSIONAL ORGANIZATIONS

Ms. Tomberlin is a life long member of Christ Episcopal Church where she is an Altar Guild team leader. She formerly served on the church Vestry, including a term as Vestry secretary in 2013. She is an active member of Quota International of Valdosta, an international service organization that supports local charities. She is a past club and district officer. She is also a member of the Lowndes County Historical Society and the Georgia Association of Women Lawyers.

attorneys.name: Nancee Tomlinson
attorneys.practice_type: Mediation Lawyers in Athens, GA
attorneys.bio:
Nancee Tomlinson specializes in trial practice in the Courts of Georgia. She appears in criminal, civil, probate, and juvenile courts around Georgia.

As a trial attorney, Nancee has tried hundreds of bench trials and jury trials in and around North Georgia. She has 16 years experience and is respected by her colleagues. Her practice includes Athens, Athens-Clarke, Watkinsville, Bishop, Lexington, Crawford, Elberton, Bowman, Hartwell, Lavonia, Carnesville, Royston, Franklin Springs, Comer, Colbert, Hull, Danielsville, Ila, Winterville, Covington, Porterdale, Oxford, Monroe, Social Circle, Jackson, Monticello, Madison, Gray, Jefferson, Winder, Braselton, Commerce, Homer, Macon, Eatonton, and beyond.

In criminal practice, Nancee served as an Assistant District for five years. During her time as a prosecutor, Nancee obtained certification for child forensic interviews with Finding Words: Georgia, focused on handling sex crimes, domestic violence, and crimes against children. Since establishing her own law practice, Nancee has obtained positive outcomes, including acquittals and hung juries, for clients in drug cases, sex crimes, and a host of other cases, including serious violent felonies. Her training and experience in trial courts serve her clients well in negotiation as well as trial.

Nancee’s civil practice focuses on helping families resolve issues in probate court, aiding fathers with legitimation and obtaining rights to their children in superior courts, and guiding families through juvenile court processes.

attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Alpharetta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mary Trachian-Bradley is a Senior Litigation Associate at Briskin, Cross & Sanford, LLC, where she brings extensive trial experience to a wide range of corporate and employment litigation matters. Her practice includes, among other areas: FLSA claims, contract disputes, shareholder derivative actions and breaches of fiduciary duty, employment discrimination suits, franchise law, copyright and trademark infringement litigation, and general disputes involving partnerships and corporations.

Prior to joining Briskin, Cross & Sanford, Mary was a partner at the nation’s largest minority- and women-owned law firm, where she managed a team of associates and served as lead counsel in complex civil litigation matters involving claims of up to $26 million. Her substantial trial experience, combined with a strong command of complex transactional issues, enables her to strategically guide clients through sophisticated business disputes.

In addition to her legal practice, Mary is deeply engaged in professional and civic leadership. She serves as the 2026 Chair of the Board of the Alpharetta Business Council and is an officer of the Marion T. Pope, Jr. American Inn of Court, reflecting her commitment to the advancement of the legal profession and the broader business community.

Mary earned her Juris Doctor from Florida International University College of Law in 2005, where she served as Vice President of Moot Court and a Law Review Editor. A strong believer in service and mentorship, she is a proud foster parent and has been a dedicated Big Sister with Big Brothers Big Sisters for over twelve years.

Outside of her professional and community commitments, Mary enjoys traveling with her husband and son.

attorneys.name: Carrie P. Trotter
attorneys.practice_type: Probate Lawyers in Cartersville, GA
attorneys.bio:
Carrie Trotter focuses her practice on estate planning, probate, IRC Section 1031 qualified exchanges, business organization, and general corporate matters.

As the firm’s managing partner, Carrie oversees daily operations, financial management, and professional development, while implementing innovative technologies and processes to enhance client service and streamline legal work. She is dedicated to providing clients with clear, professional, and supportive guidance.

In estate planning, Carrie helps clients develop comprehensive, customized plans. From drafting trusts to Last Wills and Testaments, she ensures every detail is addressed to protect clients’ families and assets while providing peace of mind.

In probate, Carrie guides clients through administering estates, whether probating a will, handling an intestate estate, or managing guardianship and conservatorship matters. She also serves as County Administrator and County Conservator for Bartow and Paulding Counties, assisting with cases assigned by Judges Blake Scoggins and Angela Jackson.

Carrie earned her B.A. in English from the University of Georgia and her J.D. from Georgia State University College of Law. She is actively involved in the community, serving on the boards of Advocates for Children and the Cartersville-Bartow Community Foundation of Northwest Georgia. Carrie grew up in Cartersville and has deep roots in the community. She now lives in Marietta with her two daughters and their cats.

attorneys.name: William A. Trotter III
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Augusta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Bill concentrates his practice in handling commercial litigation, with emphasis on real property law. He also has substantial experience in commercial transactions and banking law.

Active in his profession and community, Mr. Trotter is a member of the State Bar of Georgia, the Augusta Bar Association, the Bar of the United States District Court for the Southern District of Georgia and the Bar of the United States Courts of Appeal for the Eleventh Circuit.

Representative cases:

Johnson v. Fleet Finance, Inc., 4 F.3d 946 (11th Cir. 1993)

Johnson v. Fleet Finance, Inc., 785 F. Supp. 1003 (S.D. Ga. 1983)

Sims Crane Service, Inc. v. Ideal Steel Products, Inc., 800 F.2d 1553 (11th Cir. 1986)

In re Ferris, 764 F.2d 1475 (11th Cir. 1985)

Ga. Railroad Bank & Trust Co. v. FDIC, 758 F.2d 1548 (11th Cir. 1985)

FDIC v. Willis, 497 F. Supp. 272 (S.D. Ga. 1980)

Fleet Finance v. Jones, 263 Ga. 228; 430 S.E.2d 352 (Ga. 1993)

Pollman v. Swan, 305 Ga. App. 369 (2010).

Mr. Trotter served as general counsel and member of the Board of Directors of First Columbia Bank and FCS Financial Corporation, a single-bank holding company acquired by Georgia Bank & Trust Company through a merger; served as counsel and co-counsel to numerous financial institutions in the defense of consumer class action litigation in the Superior Courts of the Augusta Judicial Circuit and the United States District Court for the Southern District of Georgia; member of the Board of Directors of University Health Care Foundation, Inc.; appointed by former Governor Zell Miller as the consumer member of the Composite Board of Medical Examiners of the State of Georgia and a member and Chairman of the Board of Directors of St. Joseph Hospital Foundation.

Mr. Trotter received his B.S. from the University of Georgia in 1968 and his J.D., cum laude, from the Walter F. George School of Law, Mercer University in 1971. Bill was born and raised in Augusta, Georgia. He is married to Susan and has 3 children and 7 grandchildren.

attorneys.name: Renee Y. Tucker
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Peachtree City, GA
attorneys.bio:
Renee Y. Tucker is a trial attorney who has a diverse background of experience. For two decades, she has litigated cases throughout the State of Georgia, first as a defense attorney, and for the last nine years, as a plaintiffs' attorney. Renee specializes in personal injury litigation, particularly medical malpractice, commercial vehicle liability, premises liability, and general negligence cases involving wrongful death and catastrophic injury.

Renee is recognized as a skilled litigator and a passionate and zealous advocate. She believes that a successfully handled case is one that is tried or settled to its assessed value. This requires prompt and skilled investigation, which includes ensuring that primary witnesses are identified and interviewed early and documentary evidence obtained and analyzed. It also requires the identification of any hurdles to a successful resolution and formulating the most effective and persuasive strategy to overcome those hurdles. In 2010, Renee was selected as one of Georgia Rising Stars in Atlanta Magazine/Law and Politics, voted by her peers as one of Atlanta's best young lawyers.

Renee grew up in Atlanta. She obtained her undergraduate degree from DePauw University (Greencastle, Indiana) and her law degree from the University of Georgia School of Law (Athens, Georgia) where she served on the Journal of International and Comparative Law and several Moot Court Teams. At the University of Georgia, Renee was named to the Joseph Henry Lumpkin Inn of Court. She was admitted to the Georgia Bar in 2001.

Renee is admitted to: the Georgia Bar, Georgia Court of Appeals; Supreme Court of Georgia; U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia; U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Georgia; U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Georgia; the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals; and the Supreme Court of the United States. Renee is also a certified Mediator.

attorneys.name: Sharee L. Tumbling
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Defense Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Sharee Tumbling practices primarily in the area of workers’ compensation defense. Sharee is a native Atlantan, she received her Bachelor of Science in Respiratory Therapy from Georgia State University in 2006. She later received her Juris Doctor from John Marshall Law School in Atlanta, Georgia in 2013.

While in Law School, Sharee competed in Moot Court and Negotiation competitions. In 2012, she won the Best Respondent Brief award at the Frederick Douglass Moot Court Competition. She is also a previous GABWA scholar and Gate City Bar Scholar.

During Law School, Sharee clerked for the Honorable Judge Kimberly Esmond Adams in Fulton County, Grady Hospital and Forrest B. Johnson & Associates. She was admitted to the Georgia Bar in 2013 and began her legal career as a Plaintiff’s attorney practicing in the areas of medical malpractice, wrongful death and workers’ compensation. Sharee’s career has allowed her to gain litigation and jury trial experience. Prior to joining Moore, Ingram, Johnson & Steele, she worked for an Atlanta defense firm defending general liability and workers compensation claims.

She currently lives in Atlanta, Georgia and enjoys traveling, spending time with family and cheering on the Atlanta Falcons.

attorneys.name: Robert E. Turner
attorneys.practice_type: Probate of Estates Lawyers in Decatur, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Robert E. Turner practices law in Atlanta Metro area and throughout the state of Georgia where he primarily focuses his practice on:

Elder Law

Estate Planning

Wills, Trusts, and Probate law

Probate, Trust, and Estate Litigation

Business Planning

Tax Law and Tax Controversies

Attorney Turner began his legal career by clerking for Chief Justice "Bo" Torbert of the Alabama Supreme Court, where he wrote the opinions of the Chief Justice.

An MBA graduate of the University of Alabama, Birmingham, Turner decided after his one-year clerkship with the Alabama Supreme Court to continue his education at the University of Florida graduate tax program, where he received his Master of Laws in Taxation (LL.M.)

After graduating from the University of Florida College of Law graduate tax program, Attorney Turner worked with the international accounting firm Coopers and Lybrand (now Price Waterhouse Coopers) as a Tax Specialist working on estate planning and business tax matters. He was hired away from Coopers and Lybrand by AmSouth Bank (now Regions Bank) to work as Estate Planning Counsel and Trust Officer. At AmSouth he was working with the Bank's customer's attorneys drafting Wills, Trusts and other Estate Planning documents.

While Turner was the estate planning counsel at AmSouth Bank, Turner drafted and developed simple and complex estate plans, from simple wills to estate plans involving complex estate planning techniques for high net-worth clients.

Attorney Turner left AmSouth Bank to do more complex planning in the Atlanta. While in Atlanta and Decatur, Georgia area, he taught at John Marshal Law School as an adjunct professor in probate, trusts, and estates, and was a partner in the law firm of Chandler and Turner. Also, during this time, he successfully appealed the case of Chandler v. Miller from the U.S. 11th Circuit Court of Appeals to the U.S. Supreme Court, winning the case for his client on an eight-to-one vote by the U.S. Supreme Court justices.

Turner formed his own law firm, Turner Law, P.C. Turner Law handles estate planning, probate, probate and estate litigation, tax law, and tax controversies throughout the state of Georgia. Attorney Turner works with clients throughout the nation with probate issues in Georgia . Primarily, Attorney Robert Turner's cases are in Decatur, Atlanta, Buckhead, Sandy Springs, Alpharetta, Cumming, Marietta, Lawrenceville and the metro Atlanta Area including DeKalb County, Fulton County, Gwinnett County and Rockdale County. Attorney Turner represents clients involving disputes with the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and the Georgia Department of Revenue.

Case of note:

• Chandler v. Miller, 520 U.S. 305 (U.S. Supreme Court 1997)

attorneys.bio:
Ken Turnipseed offers legal services to commercial and health care organizations and individuals. Recently, he assisted on a variety of matters, including:

Helping hospitals, medical practices and physicians with health care legal and transactional matters, such as corporate compliance systems and negotiating and drafting physician recruitment and employment contracts

Offering services that represent businesses, including building, advising on operation, combining and acquiring

Facilitating commercial and residential real estate purchases, sales and financings

Offering assistance to customers with estate planning that encompasses uncomplicated and complicated matters, such as trusts, estates and wills

Before settling in South Georgia, Ken offered legal services in Birmingham, Alabama, at Balch & Bingham, LLP. He advised public and private businesses on finance and securities matters and gave technical health care regulatory guidance to medical professionals, hospitals and health care systems. He also aided different business and wellness clients with transaction matters like mergers and acquisitions.

Prior to pursuing law, Ken was a tax specialist at Ernst & Young, LLP, in Birmingham, Alabama, where he offered taxation guidance to both large and small organizations concerning everyday operations and business transactions.

Ken has two daughters who are heavily involved in their local community. His family is an active part of the First United Methodist Church in Moultrie, and they lend their time to a range of voluntary efforts.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Rome, GA
attorneys.bio:
Christopher P. Twyman is a native of Rome, Georgia. He currently serves as the Managing Partner and leads the litigation practice at Cox Byington Twyman LLP.

Mr. Twyman is a graduate of East Rome High School's class of 1992 and served as President of his class. He received his Bachelor of Arts degree from Georgetown University in 1996 and obtained his Juris Doctor degree from the University of Georgia School of Law in 1999, where was elected to the Order of Barristers. As a member of the University of Georgia School of Law's American Bar Association Moot Court Team, Mr. Twyman was a member of the 2018 Regional Championship Team and was awarded Best Brief.

Mr. Twyman was admitted to the State Bar of Georgia in 1999. He is admitted to practice in all Georgia trial and appellate courts, the United States District Court for the Northern District of Georgia, the United States District Court for the Middle District of Georgia, the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, and the United States Supreme Court. Mr. Twyman has also been admitted pro hac vice to represent clients in state and federal courts in Alabama, Tennessee, and South Carolina.

Mr. Twyman practices in the areas of commercial and general business litigation, real estate litigation, banking law, school and education law, and criminal defense. Mr. Twyman practices in state and federal courts. His practice includes representing clients in complex civil and criminal matters such as actions under the Racketeer Influenced Corrupt Organizations (RICO) statutes, partnership and shareholder disputes including corporate dissolution actions, and employment discrimination claims.

Mr. Twyman has tried civil and criminal jury trials in state and federal courts. He has represented clients throughout Georgia and in courts and legal proceedings all over the United States. Mr. Twyman also served as counsel in appeals before the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, the Georgia Supreme Court, and the Georgia Court of Appeals, having argued cases before Georgia's appellate courts.

Mr. Twyman has been recognized for his accomplishments in the field of law. He was named as a Georgia Super Lawyers honoree in 2021, 2022, and 2023 (less than 5% of Georgia lawyers are recognized as Super Lawyers) and was named a Georgia Super Lawyers Rising Star 2011, 2012, 2013, and 2014.

Mr. Twyman was elected to the State Bar of Georgia Board of Governors, which governs and sets policy for Georgia's 54,000 lawyers. He served as chair of the Professional Liability Insurance Study Committee (2019-2021) and vice-chair of the Committee on Insurance. Mr. Twyman was elected and served as Secretary of the State Bar of Georgia in 2022. He currently serves as the Treasurer of the State Bar of Georgia for the 2023-2024 Bar year.

Bar affiliations, memberships, and service include:

attorneys.name: J. Ethan Underwood
attorneys.practice_type: Land Use & Zoning Lawyers in Cumming, GA
attorneys.bio:
Ethan Underwood practices in the fields of land use, real estate, and property tax law, representing developers, as well as individual property owners. He has negotiated numerous zoning and development actions and advises clients regarding environmental regulations and municipal ordinances.

Ethan also represents clients before government authorities and courts regarding land use matters, title and boundary disputes, and property tax appeals. Ethan is member of the State Bar of Georgia and the State Bar of Tennessee. Ethan earned his J.D. with a concentration in business transactions from the University of Tennessee College of Law, and MBA with a concentration in finance from the University of Tennessee. He also earned a B.S. in marketing from the University of Tennessee-Chattanooga.

Ethan is active in the community, serving in local civic and charitable organizations. He currently serves as a member of the Board of Directors for multiple nonprofit corporations, including the Bald Ridge Lodge, Inc., which operates a home for boys who are in the custody of the Department of Family and Children Services , and Rewarding Minds, Inc., which provides to underprivileged youth computer hardware to facilitate their education. From 2009-2013, Ethan served as Chairman of the Forsyth County Republican Party, and from 2013-2015 served as 2nd Vice Chair of the 9th Congressional District Republican Party. He is also a member of Rotary, International.

attorneys.name: Robert P. Varner
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Columbus, GA
attorneys.bio:
Rob Varner is a personal injury attorney at the Columbus, Georgia office of Morgan & Morgan, P.A. Licensed in both Georgia and Alabama, Rob's practice is dedicated to representing those that have been seriously injured or killed as a result of the negligence of others.

Mr. Varner was born and raised in Columbus, Georgia. He is a graduate of Columbus High School and Presbyterian College in Clinton, South Carolina, which he attended on a golf scholarship. Mr. Varner then graduated from the Charleston School of Law, where he was a member of the Maritime Law Review, received the CALI Award for the highest grade in Legal Research and Writing, clerked for Judge Irvin Condon, and served as research assistant for Professor William M. Janssen.

Mr. Varner began his legal career in Atlanta, Georgia with a large national firm focusing on complex litigation. Realizing he wanted to represent individuals and not corporations, Mr. Varner returned home to Columbus in 2013 and since that time has exclusively represented victims of automobile and trucking wrecks, premises accidents, dog bites, and a variety of insurance coverage disputes.

Mr. Varner joined Morgan & Morgan in 2019. He is married and the proud father of three young children.

Before he began advocating for the injured and their families, Max spent years at an Atlanta medical malpractice defense firm defending hospitals, doctors, nursing homes, mental health facilities, and pharmacies from claims of negligence. There, he learned how insurance companies and their lawyers evaluate and defend cases, knowledge he now uses to benefit those harmed by the health care system. Max then worked at an AmLaw 100 firm representing some of the most well-known health care providers in the country in both payor disputes and qui-tam litigation. Now, he provides each of the firm’s clients with the same level of focus and care that he once provided to billion-dollar companies.

Max graduated with honors from the University of Georgia and the University of Georgia School of Law, where he was a member of the Journal of International and Comparative Law and participated in Moot Court. Max began his career clerking for United State Magistrate Judge Benjamin Cheesbro, where he saw first-hand how federal courts evaluated and resolved cases.

In his spare time, Max enjoys cheering on the Dawgs, watching the latest new releases at a local theater, and continuing to cross destinations off of his travel list.

attorneys.name: Gail M. Walton
attorneys.practice_type: Entertainment Law Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Gail M. Walton possesses more than twenty-five years of experience as a lawyer. A graduate of Dartmouth College and the George Washington University Law School, she has licenses to practice law in the states of New York and Georgia and is admitted to the Eastern and Southern United States District and Bankruptcy Courts of New York.

Ms. Walton has extensive legal experience in varied areas of the law. She served as a former Assistant District Attorney in King's County (Brooklyn) New York; and as an Assistant General Counsel for the New York City Department of Probation and the New York City Housing Authority. She developed her interest and knowledge of Immigration Law initially as a law school student volunteering at the school's Immigration Law Clinic assisting residents in Washington, D. C., and after her graduation at a law firm in Manhattan that specialized in Immigration Law. She spent several years as a law guardian in the Family Courts of New York City where she was involved in abuse and neglect hearings, custody, guardianship and other related issues and defended youths charged with acts of juvenile delinquency. She provided oversight to children in foster care as a result of proceedings in Juvenile Court in DeKalb County Georgia as a member of the County's Juvenile Court Citizen Review Panel.

Prior to establishing her law firm, Ms. Walton worked with a not-for-profit legal service provider in Brooklyn, New York that concentrated on assisting individuals with bankruptcy, immigration and family law matters. She has also served as an Administrative Law Judge in New York adjudicating traffic violations.

attorneys.name: D. Clay Ward
attorneys.practice_type: Consumer Bankruptcy Lawyers in Augusta, GA
attorneys.bio:
D. Clay Ward, a founding member of Ward and Spires, LLC, practices in the areas of Consumer Bankruptcy, Student Loans, Criminal and Mediation. Clay is a native of Augusta, Georgia and graduated from Augusta College in 1993 with a Bachelor of Arts degree in history, with a minor in business. Following college he attended Augusta College for his M.B.A. and then attended John Marshall Law School in Atlanta, graduating with the degree of Juris Doctor in 1996. While in school, Clay was a member of the moot court board and competed in the national moot competition.

Clay served as an Assistant Solicitor for Richmond County beginning in 1996 under the Third Year Practice Act and continued working as a prosecutor after graduation. Clay then entered into practice as an Associate at the Hunter Firm with focus on criminal defense, domestic relations and personal injury.

He previously served as Chair for the Young Lawyers of Augusta and on the Board for several years. Clay was previously a board member for the State Bar of Georgia's Bankruptcy Section and served as Chair/Co-Chair for the Annual State Bar of Georgia Bankruptcy Seminar. He also served on the Richmond County Personnel Board, overseeing matters involving County employees.

Clay has counseled and represented individuals, professionals and small businesses in bankruptcy matters since becoming a founding Partner with Ward and Spires in 2000. Clay has diverse experience in both state and federal courts. He has tried cases in State Court, Superior Court, Federal Court, and before administrative agencies. In addition, Clay has successfully handled appeals before the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit.

Clay is involved with activities and organizations outside of work including Walton Foundation for Independence, which supports programs and services in the community for people with disabilities. He served as Chair of the Foundation for two years and remains active with the mission of the Foundation. Clay also coached youth soccer at the YMCA for many years, helping to teach young children about the game, personal growth and sportsmanship. Clay is a Board Member for the Augusta Arsenal Soccer Club and currently serves on the Executive Committee. He is an active member of the The Birdie Club, helping to support college golf at Augusta University. Clay has been a member of the Exchange Club of Augusta since 2005, another organization which supports various charitable organizations each year from funds raised at differing events hosted by the Exchange Club.

attorneys.name: David J. Ward Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Johns Creek, GA
attorneys.bio:
Dave is an experienced litigator who has focused most of his career on helping people successfully resolve family law issues, including divorce, alimony, custody, and child support matters. Dave graduated cum laude from the Norman Adriane Wiggins School of Law at Campbell University in 2004 having completed the requirements for their Advocacy track. He immediately opened his first practice in Raliegh, North Carolina, where he practiced for several years before relocating to the Atlanta area in 2010.

Dave has focused on litigation the entire time he has practiced and has focused on helping people navigate family law matters since 2010. Dave's undergraduate degree is in Finance, and he worked as a financial planner for several years before attending law school. He has been able to use the skills he acquired during that period to guide business owners and other high net worth individuals through complex family law situations.

Dave married his amazing wife, Aimee, in 2014. They have boxer mix fur baby named Cami. They share a passion for travel and have been fortunate to visit some of the most exotic locations in the world, including Antarctica. Dave is also an accomplished martial artist and self-defense instructor. He is also a true Disney fanatic.

Dave is admitted to practice in all state courts in Georgia, including the Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court of Georgia. He is also admitted to practice in all state courts in North Carolina.

attorneys.name: Lyle Griffin Warshauer
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Lyle Griffin Warshauer, (formerly Woodruff) brings a unique perspective to the practice of law. Prior to attending law school, she held a position as a paralegal with one of Atlanta's finest insurance defense firms. As a result, Lyle has a thorough understanding of the mindset of defense lawyers, and the large corporations and insurance companies they defend. She knows the direction in which the defendants are headed and strives to get there first. She is always prepared to respond to their strategies. While Lyle attended law school, she worked for a current justice of the Georgia Supreme Court, as well as one of the truly outstanding plaintiff's firms in the country.

Although she enjoys preparing cases for trial and utilizes her skills as an advocate to obtain full and just compensation from juries, she also understands that sometimes our client's best interest is to settle. Lyle measures our success by the results earned for the people who ask us to help them. It is this commitment to our clients that is always our first priority.

Lyle's strong academic background is evident in her research and writing skills. She enjoys the challenge of responding to the numerous complex legal challenges that can threaten the clients' cause.

In addition to her experience handling railroad cases, Lyle also has a particular interest in representing people who have been injured as a result of medical negligence. The intricacies of extensive and sometimes altered medical records, researching medical issues, as well as finding and working with expert witnesses can be challenging. Lyle accepts these challenges, as well as the challenges of helping victims through the emotional turmoil of litigation. She recognizes that catastrophic events change lives, and our clients need a powerful, yet compassionate advocate to represent their interests.

Lyle's professional commitment to helping people put their lives back together ensures that Warshauer Woodward Atkins never forgets our primary goal is to help people whose lives have been altered by the negligence of others.

attorneys.name: Michael J. Warshauer
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Michael J. Warshauer is a plaintiff's trial lawyer. Michael believes that in most cases serious injuries do not occur in the absence of some carelessness. He is dedicated to the pursuit of the highest possible compensation for people who are injured or killed through the fault of another.

Michael has helped people recover compensation, at the court house and in the office, in cases involving railroad employee injuries and crossing incidents, car and truck wrecks, false arrest, slip and fall incidents, malpractice by medical and legal professionals, and more. While Michael genuinely enjoys all types of cases, in addition to his vast knowledge of and love for railroad cases, he also enjoys tackling complicated product liability cases. These cases usually involve defective or poorly designed equipment or products that kill or maim consumers and workers. Michael enjoys sifting through intricate mechanical and scientific theories, detailed blueprints and other engineering matters to figure out a theory of recovery and how to explain that theory, in layman's terms, to his clients and to a jury.

Consistent with the firm's philosophy of keeping its clients informed about the law, Michael regularly teaches law to other lawyers as an invited speaker at continuing legal education seminars. He also frequently speaks at union meetings to educate railroad workers about the special laws which govern them. His knowledge of the special laws governing railroad workers has been published as a chapter in an encyclopedia of law.

Michael's continuous efforts to stay abreast of the law, to insist that clients are informed about their cases - the good parts and the bad, to properly prepare cases for trial - not settlement, and solid courtroom technique serve as the backbone of Warshauer Woodward Atkins.

Houston Washburn was raised in Gwinnett County, Georgia where his parents both practiced law. Houston went to the University of Georgia where he studied Public and International Affairs and graduated with a Bachelors of Science. After college, Houston studied law at Atlanta's John Marshall Law School where he met his wife Brooke Puglise Washburn. Brooke and Houston share two dogs a black lab Boone and a golden retriever Baier.

After being admitted to practice law, Houston opened his own general practice firm in Gwinnett County. Houston practices in most metro-Atlanta counties mainly in the areas of criminal law, traffic citations and DUI, personal injury, civil litigation, and family law.

Attorney James H. Webb, Jr., is a native of Atlanta, Georgia. He has devoted his career to the representation of injured persons in serious personal injury cases and concentrates in the area of medical malpractice. Mr. Webb insists that the lawyers and the other employees of the firm maintain a high level of professional and personal excellence. One of the few lawyers in the State of Georgia recognized as Board Certified in both Civil Trial Advocacy by the National Board of Trial Advocacy and in Pretrial Practice by the National Board of Civil Pretrial Advocacy, he has given many lectures and seminars to other lawyers in the areas of medical malpractice and trial advocacy. Attorney Webb is a former Chairman of the General Practice and Trial Section of the Georgia State Bar, which has approximately 3000 lawyer members. For many years, he was the organizer and moderator for a Georgia Bar sponsored medical malpractice winter seminar. He genuinely enjoys handling medical malpractice cases and commonly refers to them as the “last great Sherlock Holmes cases.”

attorneys.name: Michael G. Webb
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Mike Webb has spent nearly two decades litigating cases on behalf of Atlanta area clients. The legal profession is in Mike's DNA, as his father was also an attorney. In his words, personal injury law is fulfilling because “generally, when I meet a client, they are hurt, they are missing work, they are without an automobile. It is rewarding to help someone at a time when they need it most.”

New clients meet with Mike as early in the case process as possible, to develop a rapport and sense of trust in the relationship. And that relationship is a long-term one. Instead of looking for the quickest settlement, Mike approaches each case as if it is going to trial. This means he is committed to filing suit when necessary. One example of this was a motorcycle crash case for a Homeland Security Officer. The officer was severely injured when a truck driver ran a red light. In court, Mike was able to get a substantial verdict in the case after finding a 911 recording in which the truck driver implicated himself.

Mike's advice to prospective personal injury clients is “Help me help you. You can make your case much more valuable by working closely with me.”

Mike has deep roots in the Atlanta community. He has coached soccer, volleyball and basketball; chaired his school's annual fund, and served on its Development Committee. He is also a member of the Pastoral Care Ministry at his church. Mike devotes his free time to his wife and three daughters, but also remains a stalwart Braves and Falcons fan.

Witcher two years later. Nathaniel represents clients accused of crimes ranging from DUI to major felonies, and is experienced in all aspects of family law, including divorce, child custody, grandparents’ rights, adoptions, and juvenile court matters. Nat and his wife Christina reside in Carroll County. When not traveling to exotic places around the world (especially beaches!), they enjoy spending time with their adopted dogs and cats, grilling in the back yard, and rooting for the Georgia Bulldogs.

attorneys.name: Craig R. White
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Defense Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Craig R. White was born in Dallas, Texas in 1966. He moved to the Atlanta area in 1970 and currently resides in Marietta, Georgia. He earned his bachelor's degree in psychology (1988) and law degree (1991) both from the University of Georgia. He has been admitted to the Georgia Bar since 1991.

Craig practices general civil litigation with specialization in insurance defense, premises liability, commercial/common carrier litigation, bad faith litigation, commercial litigation, construction litigation, subrogation, medical malpractice, insurance coverage, product liability, collections, and workers' compensation. He serves as state-wide counsel for numerous large and small insurance companies as well as many private corporations. In addition, Craig also maintains a corporate, trusts and estates and business litigation practice. Craig is also admitted in state and federal courts located throughout Georgia. He is a member of the State Bar of Georgia, Atlanta Bar Association, the Defense Research Institute and Georgia Defense Lawyers Association.

In addition to being admitted in all Georgia Trial Courts, including Federal District Courts, Craig is also admitted to practice in the United States Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals, Georgia Supreme Court and Georgia Court of Appeals. Craig is also a member of the Georgia Defense Lawyers Association where he serves on its Automobile Liability and Premises Liability Committees. He is also one of the handful of Georgia attorneys invited to be a member of the Council on Ethical Billing.

As part of his law practice, Craig is actively involved in presenting seminars to his clients in an effort to keep them apprised of new developments in Georgia law on a wide range of topics including insurer bad faith, risk management, claim investigation, insurance coverage, trial practice and workers compensation issues. He has been approved by the Georgia Insurance Commissioner's Office to provide continuing education seminars to insurance adjusters for credit.

attorneys.name: Ivy R. White
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Ivy White practices workers' compensation law in Morgan & Morgan's Atlanta office. In addition to years of experience in civil litigation and workers' compensation, Ms. White gained personal experience with workers' compensation after a close family member was injured at work. Prior to joining Morgan and Morgan, she represented employers, insurers, self-insureds and third-party administrators in workers' compensation claims, giving her unique insight to both sides of workers' compensation claims. Now, Ms. White enjoys using her personal and professional experience to zealously advocate for injured workers and their families.

Ms. White was born in Atlanta, Georgia, but spent the majority of her childhood between Michigan, Georgia, and South Florida. She earned her associate's degree in Accounting from Florida Atlantic University in Boca Raton, Florida. She then attended Georgia State University, where she earned her bachelor's degree in Spanish, with a concentration in International Business. Prior to attending law school at Georgia State University College of Law, Ms. White worked as a paralegal in a boutique family law firm specializing in high asset and complex divorce and family law matters.

While in law school, Ms. White clerked for the Honorable John J. Goger and the Honorable Alford J. Dempsey in Fulton County Superior Court. She was a student attorney on the school's mock trial team, and by her third year of law school, Ms. White was already representing domestic violence victims in Cobb County. She was also a recipient of the Georgia Association of Black Women Attorneys (GABWA) Student Scholarship.

In addition to earning her JD, Ms. White also earned an MBA from Georgia State University J.Mack Robinson College of Business. She delivered the Student Commencement Address at Georgia State Law's 2016 Commencement Ceremonies, receiving the first standing ovation in the school's history.

attorneys.practice_type: Business and Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Joseph A. White is a trial lawyer who specializes in handling and effectively resolving business disputes, employment disputes, and personal injury litigation. Mr. White has been recognized multiple times as a “Georgia Super Lawyer Rising Star” and as a member of Georgia’s “Legal Elite”.

Mr. White joined Fried & Bonder in 2006, after spending five years training with one of Atlanta’s largest and most reputable law firms. Since joining Fried & Bonder, Mr. White has effectively and efficiently resolved dozens of business and employment disputes for companies large and small. Mr. White has also recovered millions of dollars on behalf of employees, personal injury victims, and other aggrieved clients. Mr. White prides himself on delivering excellent client service and achieving his clients’ objectives efficiently and cost-effectively.

Mr. White graduated with honors from Tulane Law School in 2001, where he was a member of the Order of the Coif and also served as managing editor of the Tulane Law Review. Mr. White is a native of Atlanta and attended college at Emory University where he studied philosophy and political science.

She specializes in all aspects of Social Security and disability law, which include SSI and Disability Insurance for adults, children, widows and widowers. She works with clients through all stages of the adjudicative process from the administrative to the appellate levels, including Federal District Court appeals. Although Ms. White has lived in Macon since 2002, she maintains ties to Douglas representing clients across South Georgia and also throughout the state. Furthermore, she represents clients throughout the Southeastern Region of the United States. Ms. White began specializing in Social Security law when she worked for the Social Security Administration in the Macon Office of Disability Adjudication and Review with Administrative Law Judges as an attorney decision writer. She remains active in the Macon Bar Association as well as in the Young Lawyers Division of the State Bar of Georgia as a member of the Board of Directors for the past two years.

attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Nathan Whittenburg founded First Class — The Atlanta Personal Injury Law Firm to create a more thoughtful and client-centered approach to legal representation.

After working within the traditional legal system, Nathan saw firsthand how clients were often left feeling unsupported and overlooked.

He established the firm to ensure that those injured in accidents receive the focused attention and respect they deserve.

The firm is built on the principle that injured clients should be fully informed, fully supported, and treated as individuals.

Nathan’s hands-on involvement in every case ensures that clients aren’t just guided through legal procedures, but also receive clear, honest communication at every stage.

By prioritizing transparency and careful attention to each client’s unique circumstances, the firm delivers personalized legal strategies that help clients recover both physically and financially.

Nathan Whittenburg’s approach is deliberate and detail-oriented, focusing on achieving meaningful outcomes rather than quick settlements.

Our law firm doesn’t just move cases forward — it takes the time to build strong cases, advocate effectively with insurers and opposing parties, and secure results that truly reflect the client’s needs and long-term well-being.

attorneys.name: Dylan Wilbanks
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Commerce, GA
attorneys.bio:
Dylan Wilbanks is the founder of Dylan Wilbanks LLC, a practice he built in his hometown. He litigates cases throughout the state and Southeast, and focuses his practice on three areas: helping people in his local courts with traffic and probate matters, assisting businesses and individuals in commercial litigation, such as contract or construction disputes or judgment collection, and helping those who have been injured through the negligence of another.

Born in Georgia, Dylan obtained his bachelor’s degree from the Georgia Institute of Technology, and received his law degree from the University of Georgia.

In addition to his legal practice, Dylan is actively engaged in his community and has served on the executive board of the Jackson County Area Chamber of Commerce, the board of Jackson County Water and Sewer Authority, and the board for the Commerce Downtown Development Authority. Dylan also has been President of the Commerce Kiwanis Club and the Commerce Area Business Association.

Dylan is admitted to practice in Georgia’s state and federal courts trial courts, the Georgia Court of Appeals, the Georgia Supreme Court, the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals, and the Federal Claims Court. He has been admitted pro hac vice to practice in the U.S. District Courts for the Eastern District of Kentucky and for Puerto Rico.

Dylan lives in Commerce with his wife, Lisa.

attorneys.bio:
A lifelong resident of Georgia and a member of the firm since 1971, Frank B. Wilensky has developed a strong reputation in the insolvency field. Although he has handled and managed all manner of cases in the Bankruptcy area, his current practice focuses primarily on high-profile debtor cases.

Remaining with the same firm for more than three decades, Mr. Wilensky has also contributed his time and expertise to a variety of professional activities and community concerns. He has served on the Board of Directors of the Bankruptcy Section of the Atlanta Bar Association, and is currently serving as the Chairman of the Creditors Rights Section of the State Bar of Georgia.

On the civic level, he has served as State President of the American Lung Association, and has chaired various committees dealing with refugee immigration, absorption and adoption for Jewish Family and Career Services.

Mr. Wilensky joined the firm as an associate in 1969 following military service, and he has served as Managing Partner since 1991.

attorneys.name: Jake Wilkes
attorneys.practice_type: Truck/Car Accidents Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
Jake Wilkes devotes his practice to helping individuals harmed by the negligence of others, in addition to assisting businesses and individuals in complex legal matters. Mr. Wilkes has assisted in catastrophic cases against hospitals, medical groups, and insurance companies.

Mr. Wilkes is a native of middle Georgia. Mr. Wilkes’ father and younger brother operate a septic tank manufacturing and installation company in middle Georgia, while his mother provides healthcare to veterans at a local Veterans Affairs facility. During his breaks in high school and undergraduate, Mr. Wilkes regularly assisted his father’s small business. Mr. Wilkes fondly remembers receiving his acceptance into Mercer Law School and notice of scholarship while laying drain lines in the summer of 2019. In addition to assisting the family business, Mr. Wilkes served as a bagger for a grocery store and served as a caddie at Reynolds Lake Oconee while pursuing his undergraduate degree. This broad experience allows Mr. Wilkes to relate to a variety of people, regardless of their background or station in life. Simultaneously, he demonstrates an ability to tackle the most complex legal issues, easily cooperating with members of the bench and bar.

Mr. Wilkes obtained his Juris Doctor, cum laude, from the Walter F. George School of Law at Mercer University in 2022. While in law school, Mr. Wilkes was awarded a spot on the President’s List in Fall 2019, Fall 2020, Spring 2021, and Fall 2021. In addition, he earned the Cali Award (highest grade in the class) for both the courses of Evidence and Secured Transactions. Mr. Wilkes was a member of both the Phi Delta Phi Honor Society and the Real Estate Law Society during his time at the Walter F. George School of Law.

Mr. Wilkes has prior experience interning for the Kight Firm, P.C. in his hometown of Dublin. At the Kight Firm, he assisted in commercial real estate closings and civil asset forfeiture cases.

In 2022, Mr. Wilkes joined Mayo Hill in Macon, Georgia. He expanded his practice to include criminal defense and assisting individuals and families suffering from the results of another’s negligence or medical malpractice.

In his spare time, Mr. Wilkes enjoys spending time with his family and friends, golfing, weightlifting, hunting, fishing, boating, traveling, and college football.

attorneys.name: Matthew M. Wilkins
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Marietta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Matthew M. Wilkins is a Partner in King, Yaklin & Wilkins, LLP. Matt’s practice focuses on general commercial, fiduciary, employment and construction litigation. His areas of expertise include shareholder disputes, restrictive covenant enforcement, and construction litigation.

Matt also acts as counsel to many private businesses and entrepreneurs, and has negotiated, prepared, and facilitated private mergers, purchases, design build contracts, government and construction contracts, output and requirements contracts, shareholder buy-outs, and asset purchases for companies ranging from start-ups to multinationals with millions of dollars in yearly revenues. Matt also advises many not-for-profit organizations, including charter schools, churches, private schools, and other tax exempt organizations.

Matt is an experienced trial lawyer, with experience in all types of litigation in state and federal court. Matt also routinely arbitrates matters before the American Arbitration Association, private arbitrators, and FINRA – the primary arbiter of disputes in the financial services and securities industry.

Matt serves clients everyday through his commercial and construction practice. Matt represents owners, general contractors, sub-contractors, and sureties in all facets of contract negotiation, project implementation, profit forecasting, and if necessary, litigation. Matt’s clientele consists of small, locally owned contractors to nationally recognized general contractors. The scope of projects negotiated and litigated range in size from a few thousand dollars to many millions. Because Matt acts both to negotiate contracts on front end and litigates disputes, many times through arbitration or trial, he has developed an expertise in identifying potential pitfalls in the contract documents. Matt’s goals in preparing and reviewing contracts are twofold: 1) to ensure the client’s objectives and intent are properly reflected, and 2) to avoid litigation or uncertainty should a dispute or unforeseen circumstance arise by including the appropriate provisions on the front end.

Matt routinely advises and counsels dentists and dental practices throughout the southeast in all areas of the business cycle to include corporate formation and governance, operations, mergers and acquisitions, restrictive covenant drafting and enforcement, shareholder disputes and break-ups, and, if necessary, litigation. Matt has prepared and negotiated lease agreements, loan documents, shareholder agreements, asset purchase agreements, and executive and provider agreements for practices, dentists, their associates, and their employees.

Matt is a 2002 summa cum laude graduate of the University of Georgia with a Bachelor of Business Administration degree in finance and international business. He attended the Regent University School of Law in Virginia where he graduated as the Valedictorian and summa cum laude in 2005. Matt joined King, Yaklin & Wilkins in 2007 and became a Partner in 2009.

Matt has been recognized by his peers with an AV Preeminent Rating on Martindale Hubbell.

Matt has been named a 2013 Georgia Super Lawyers Rising Star in the areas of business disputes and litigation. “Rising Stars” identifies the best attorneys who are under 40, and each year the honor is limited to no more than 2.5 percent of lawyers in the state.

Matt is an active member of the Cobb County Bar Association, Marietta Lawyer’s Club, Honorary Commander’s Association with the Cobb County Chamber of Commerce, and the Georgia Delta Sigma Phi Epsilon Alumni Board.

Matt and his wife, Kelly, are the proud parents of two girls. They attend North Point Community Church.

attorneys.name: Dierdra Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Dierdra Williams is a native of Winston-Salem, North Carolina. Dierdra graduated from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, School of Law, Juris Doctorate with Moot Court and Dean's List honors. She is also a graduate of North Carolina State University, where she attained a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science, Magna Cum Laude. There she made the Dean's List, became a Pi Sigma Alpha Honor Society member, was accepted into Golden Key National Honor Society, and the Phi Eta Sigma Honor Society.

As an experienced and passionate litigator with over 19 years of legal mastery, she brings a wealth of creative and pragmatic advocacy to safeguard the rights of injured Georgians. Dierdra has acted as lead counsel in numerous cases, specializing in motor vehicle accidents, work-related accidents, slip and falls, dangerous conditions at a premise, product liability, dog bites, general negligence, and property damage.

Dierdra has represented both plaintiffs and defendants and knows how to win fights (both with a smile and with a dagger). Most noteworthy, she was entrenched for six years in-house as a subrogation manager at Progressive Insurance Company, routinely handling litigation, discovery, mediations, arbitrations, and jury trials. Most recently, Dierdra was responsible for supervising litigation at a major company, which specializes in representing various insurance companies. This collective experience working with insurance companies gives her a unique and powerful road map in dealing with insurance companies, which translates to the best and highest settlements.

She is Member of State Bar of Georgia since November 2000 and was admitted to practice in the State Court of Georgia, Supreme Court of Georgia, Court of Appeals of the State of Georgia, Middle District of Georgia, and Northern District Court of Georgia. She is also a member of the State Bar of Tennessee.

When she is not zealously fighting for the rights of her injured clients, you will probably find her on the sidelines supporting her two sons who participate in several different sports.

attorneys.name: Jennifer Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Valdosta, GA
attorneys.bio:
The managing partner of Jennifer E. Williams, LLC, attorney Jennifer Williams possesses the knowledge and experience to assist clients with their civil or criminal matters. With over 15 years of experience, she has successfully handled cases in family law, criminal defense, personal injury and probate. She has extensive knowledge of the laws and legal procedures that will impact the outcome of your case.

Ms. Williams has achieved positive results for clients involved in divorce cases, including custody, support and property division matters. She has successfully defended her clients' rights in criminal cases involving both minor and major offenses. Additionally, she has secured just compensation for individuals who have suffered harm due to someone else's negligence.

Ms. Williams graduated with her Juris Doctor degree from the Barry University School of Law in Orlando, Florida, after completing her bachelor's degree in political science at the Valdosta State University in Valdosta, Georgia. She obtained her license to practice law in Georgia in 2008. She is also authorized to appear before the Georgia Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court of Georgia.

Ms. Williams is the former president of the Valdosta Bar Association, the Valdosta Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and the Valdosta Association of Women Lawyers.

attorneys.name: Joseph E. Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Macon, GA
attorneys.bio:
From their office in Macon, Georgia, Joseph E. Williams Jr. PC works with clients facing estate planning, personal injury and family law issues throughout Bibb County. Though the details of cases differ drastically, at the heart of each is someone who needs guidance. Mr. Williams has been practicing for over 40 years, advising people of how to meet their goals while working within the boundaries of the law.

We lead with compassion, whether the focus is on creating a will, going through probate or dividing property following a divorce. Past clients have been thankful for our sensitivity to their personal issues and ability to achieve results. For example, we recovered $300,000 in a case in which a car accident left a person with a broken jaw. In another situation, we guided a family through the adoption process, taking the stress off them as they welcomed a little girl into their home.

At Joseph E. Williams Jr. PC, we accept credit cards and work with clients to determine which approach best resolves their issues. If we cannot reach a settlement or otherwise find a solution outside the courtroom, the team at our law office is prepared to pursue litigation.

attorneys.name: Mary Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Atlanta, GA
attorneys.bio:
Mary prides herself on taking an individualized approach to every case and concentrates her practice on complex business disputes, first-party insurance litigation, and trial and appellate strategies. After serving as law clerk to the Honorable Blake A. Hewitt of the South Carolina Court of Appeals and as judicial extern to the Honorable Sherri A. Lydon of the U.S. District Court for the District of South Carolina, Mary practiced at AmLaw ranked firms in South Carolina and Georgia early in her career.

Mary is at home in the courtroom and has served as embedded complex motions and appellate counsel in multiple trials, including high-stakes talc, corporate fraud, and contractual dispute trials. She has also served as demand review committee counsel during shareholder derivative action litigation. Prior to attending law school, Mary worked within the Oregon Legislature as a legislative aide and later as a lobbyist, representing state health plan providers and building trades clients. She has substantial experience in regulatory and legislative affairs and in developing multi-pronged litigation and policy strategies.

The daughter of educators and whose family is proud Navy, in law school Mary served as Senior Articles Editor for the South Carolina Journal of Law and Education and was a student attorney with the Veterans Legal Clinic, where she represented service members before the Board of Veterans' Appeals and the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims. An ardent oral advocate, Mary was selected by the South Carolina Supreme Court as one of two winners of the J. Woodrow Lewis Moot Court Competition and was an invited student member of the John Belton O’Neall Inn of Court.

Mary’s most fulfilling career success was recently securing the maximum FEMA payments for her pro bono client who lost everything during Hurricane Helene and had previously been denied all federal assistance.

Mary is a classically trained ballet dancer, a lifelong artist, and loves the beach. She now lives in East Cobb with her family of all boys and Chesapeake Bay Retriever, “Stash.”
